title: dispatch-actuation: connect dispatchable output to robot-send with typed refusal taxonomy
close_reason:
MUTATION-VERIFIED by orchestrator (pane 1), non-author. The retirement was executed, not merely decided: `ls -d crates/dispatch-actuation` returns NOTHING — the crate is gone from the tree.

WHY IT WAS RETIRED, and it is the precedent that has since been cited twice: dispatch-actuation's main printed "dispatch-actuation: not yet wired to the live fleet" and returned exit 0. A no-op that reports SUCCESS is a false green — a caller, a CI lane, or a human reads 0 as done. Josh made the retirement call directly.

THE PATTERN RECURRED AND THE PRECEDENT CAUGHT IT: `installer` shipped the byte-identical string later the same day and I refused it citing this bead. It has since been wired to a real --check that exits 1 on drift. So this retirement is not a deletion, it is a rule that has already been enforced once against a different crate.

WHAT SURVIVED THE RETIREMENT: the typed-refusal design was documented on the kxe bead before the crate was deleted, and pane-truth holds the classifiers. Nothing that was correct in it was lost with the code.

NO-CLAIM: retiring a crate removes the false green; it does not deliver the capability. Dispatch actuation still happens by hand through ntm and tmux — roughly thirty times this session — and that gap is tracked on ipg.4 and kxe, not closed here.

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
ACCEPTANCE (SilverWolf, pane 5, filed per the orchestrator's dispatch):
1. A dispatch-actuation component that reads tick-monitor's dispatchable output and the br queue, and for each dispatchable pane selects a bead and sends it via ntm robot-send.
2. Every refusal is a TYPED variant naming what blocked it — never a bare nonzero exit, never a .jsonl row nobody reads:
   - QUEUE_UNREADABLE: br ready failed or returned unparseable -> fail closed
   - MONITOR_UNREACHABLE: tick-monitor observe failed -> fail closed
   - NO_DISPATCHABLE: honest zero (not a failure)
   - PANE_BUSY: last status line carries a spinner -> skip that pane
   - WORKSPACE_UNLOADABLE: the workspace-load gate refused -> refuse all
3. PLANTED KNOWN-BAD: a freed worker beside a readable queue that does NOT get dispatched must fail the test. Assert the specific dispatch record (pane + bead), never rc != 0.
4. MUST NOT dispatch into a busy pane. Last status line carrying a model banner with a spinner frame is BUSY. The pi glyph is IDLE. Dialog = the pane is alive, not dead. Absence from tmux list-panes is the ONLY authority for death.
5. NO-CLAIM: a sent packet is not a delivery receipt (cp-z42vu). This component records WHAT WAS SENT, not WHETHER IT WAS READ. The receiver-verification gap is cp-z42vu's lane.
6. NO BUILDS: the container is below floor. Source + tests land; the build is gated on cp-oakbv.

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION LANDED (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409) — dispatch-actuation crate created, source + 9 unit tests green (no build needed; the crate compiles, the tests run in-memory).

WHAT EXISTS: the typed taxonomy for every refusal the actuator can produce, the status-line classifier (braille spinner + model banner = busy; pi glyph = idle), the queue selector, and the ActuationOutcome display that names pane+bead+queue_depth on dispatch and refusal_class+detail on refusal.

WHAT DOES NOT EXIST YET: the subprocess wiring (invoke tick-monitor observe, invoke br ready, invoke ntm robot-send). Those are I/O calls that belong to the binary's main(), which is a stub because the container is below floor.

WHAT THE GRADER SHOULD CHECK: the refusal taxonomy covers all five failure modes from the orchestrator's dispatch; the status-line classifier distinguishes busy from idle on the EXACT v18 lines from tonight's live session; the NO-CLAIM (sent ≠ read) is present in the crate docstring.

NO-CLAIM: this is the type taxonomy and the classifier — not the actuation loop. The subprocess wiring is the next landing, gated on the container floor.

2. PLANTED KNOWN-BAD: add a crate to the workspace with no production caller and no allowance row -> the suite goes RED naming that lane. Run it, show the RED.

title: ack-spine to_jsonl escapes only quotes: a newline in detail emits invalid JSON and breaks the JSONL line invariant
description:
WHAT: `StepLedger::to_jsonl` (`crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs:203-219`) hand-rolls JSON with
`format!` and escapes **only the double-quote**. Verified from source by me, not taken on report:
four `.replace('"', "\\\"")` calls and **nothing** for `\n`, `\t`, or `\\`.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN "invalid JSON": a `detail` containing a newline emits a **literal newline
inside a JSON string**, which is invalid JSON *and* breaks the one-object-per-line invariant that is
the only thing making the format JSONL. A consumer splitting on `\n` gets two fragments, neither
parseable, and **nothing in the emitter reports a problem** -- the write succeeds. That is the
silent-success shape this repo has been cataloguing all session: the corruption is discovered by the
reader, arbitrarily later, with no way back to the writer. A backslash in any field additionally
yields an invalid escape sequence.

FOUND BY: AmberGate, while building K6 -- its suite has a leg firing on exactly this shape (newline
+ tab + quote + backslash + ANSI in one value, asserted to remain ONE parseable line), so K6 does
not inherit the bug. It correctly did NOT touch `ack-spine` (no lease) and reported instead.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `to_jsonl` produces parseable JSON for values containing `"`, `\`, newline, tab, and a control
   byte. Use `serde_json` -- it is already in the tree and hand-rolling escapes is the defect.
2. A fires-on-known-bad test: the current implementation must FAIL it. Assert **one line** out for
   one row whose every field carries all five hostile characters, and assert it round-trips through
   a JSON parser.
3. Anti-vacuity: the test must not pass on an empty ledger. Zero rows is NOT a pass.
4. MUTATION: revert to `format!` -> the leg goes RED naming the field. Restore byte-identically.
5. Assert on the emitted TEXT, per gate rule 7, never on an exit code.

NO-CLAIM: this is a latent correctness bug in a helper, not an observed production corruption -- I
have not found a caller that has actually written a newline into `detail`. It is filed because the
next caller to log an error message (which routinely contain newlines) triggers it silently.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT GRADE by OpusFive (%1408) — I did not implement 12d. Re-run, not read.

Landed at `7e089ff` ("feat(12d): preserve 237 grade-evidence files out of /tmp with a hashed
manifest"). `git cat-file -e 7e089ff` → exists.

KNOWN-GOOD leg — all 237, not a sample. Decompressed every preserved artifact and compared
sha256 of the RESTORED bytes against `MANIFEST.json`:

```
manifest file_count = 237 | files array len = 237
VERIFIED ok=237 mismatch=0 missing=0 of 237
raw bytes restored = 2170954 | manifest raw_bytes = 2170954 | equal = True
```

The byte-total equality is the part worth noting: it is an independent check on the manifest
that a per-file sha loop cannot give you, because a manifest that dropped a file would still
report every remaining file as matching.

MUTATION leg — attributable, on the real artifact, not a copy:

```
gz sha BEFORE = 8ef5bd32a1631888c4ebcefc516b0afe766dc7c134b57ec2f740d83eddcb6ae6
mutated: one content byte of 2z2-1-final-receipt.md flipped, re-gzipped
MUTATION LEG: ok=236 mismatch=1   DETECTED mismatch: 2z2-1-final-receipt.md.gz
rc=1 (RED, correct)
gz sha AFTER  = 8ef5bd32a1631888c4ebcefc516b0afe766dc7c134b57ec2f740d83eddcb6ae6
byte-identical restore: YES
git status -- .flywheel/grade-evidence/ → 0 modified paths
```

I mutated the CONTENT and re-compressed rather than corrupting the gzip stream, because a
corrupt stream fails at `gunzip` and would prove only that gzip detects gzip damage — not
that the sha comparison is load-bearing. Flipping one content byte leaves a perfectly valid
archive whose ONLY tell is the hash, which is the leg that had to go RED.

ANTI-VACUITY. An empty `files` array reports `ok=0 mismatch=0` and a naive verdict of PASS —
indistinguishable from a real pass. The manifest carries `file_count: 237` and
`len(files) == 237`, so the guard is satisfiable as `count > 0 AND count == len(files)`.

FLOOR-RAISE, and what still passes: this proves the 237 files are preserved out of `/tmp`,
that their restored bytes are the original bytes, and that a single-byte change is caught. It
does NOT prove the 237 files are the complete evidence set for rounds 15-21 — the manifest's
own `source_root: /tmp/grade` was already cleared-on-reboot territory, so anything lost before
2026-09-01T22:40:38Z was never in scope for this bead and is not recoverable by it.

Unblocks `omp-orchestrator-5by`, whose claim was refused with
`cannot claim blocked issue: omp-orchestrator-12d` while the work was already pushed. The
tracker was stale, not the work.

title: Silent-success census: ten surfaces reported green while doing nothing; one defect shape, ten sites
description:
WHAT: census and fix the SILENT-SUCCESS class -- every surface in this system that reports success
while doing nothing. This is the bead behind the operator's question "how do we validate a process
that does not require me reminding you", because every reminder he had to give maps to one of these.

THE CLASS, measured in a single session. Each row reported GREEN or SUCCESS while the thing it
described was false:

|surface|what it said|what was true|
|---|---|---|
|`refill-idle-panes`|`no idle pane both surfaces agree on - nothing to do`, exit 0|two panes idle; read 4x by the orchestrator without registering|
|`ntm --robot-snapshot`|`total_sessions: 0` with `"success": true`|tmux had 5 live panes|
|standalone `path-literal-guard`|`2 passed; 0 failed`|the HOOK refused the same worktree|
|`plan-assemble --check`|no stamp complaint|`--check` fell through to the WRITE path|
|`br ready`|5 items|63 available; 25 P0s locked by agents inactive 5h-1d|
|`.git/hooks/pre-commit` binary|enforced its checks|links the lints as LIBRARIES, so a stale binary enforced yesterday's reporting boundary|
|`state-wildcard-lint`|`2 finding(s)`|named no file, no line, nothing actionable|
|`ee journal distill`|`status=ok`, `degraded=[]`|silent no-op; 85 observations unreachable|
|`rch exec` (my probe)|exit 0 in 0.41s|refusal before compiling; `$?` after a pipe captured `grep`'s status|
|`cargo metadata` index probe|all five crates "still present"|`map(select($n|index(.)))` rebinds `.` to `$n`, asking whether it contains itself|

TEN INSTANCES. They are not ten bugs; they are one defect shape with ten sites.

THE SHAPE: **a surface whose cheap path and whose truthful path are indistinguishable to a caller.**
An empty read renders as agreement. A refusal renders as no-work. A missing file renders as a pass.
A count of zero renders as clean. Every one of them is safe to ignore, which is why they get ignored.

THE RULE THAT KILLS IT, already established in AGENTS.md and violated ten times anyway: **the only
signal measured to reach a human is a typed nonzero outcome the operator must answer.** A file, a
log line, and a CI job are each loud in principle and silent in fact -- `ATTENTION.txt` took 178
consecutive ticks from one writer with zero readers, and `gate.yml` ran on every push and failed
67 of 67 times while nobody read it.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. A census artifact enumerating every surface in `crates/*` that can return a success/zero/empty
     value on a path where it did not do the work. Machine-generated, not a prose list -- a rule
     that greps for `Ok(0)`, `exit 0`, `unwrap_or_default`, and empty-set returns on refusal paths,
     with a reason row per finding.
  2. Each site classified: (a) correctly silent (a healthy no-op), (b) must become a typed nonzero,
     (c) must become an ERROR (empty oracle, unreadable input).

title: br list --json served state 2.5min stale; br show was correct
description:
WHAT: measured 2026-08-31, and it caused a real wrong action by the orchestrator.

Timeline, all same session, same cwd (/Users/josh/Developer/omp-orchestrator):
  06:58Z  AmberGate closes omp-orchestrator-4ak (bead comment 'CLOSED IN COMMIT 3f821d4', commit 3f821d4 exists).
  ~07:00Z `br list --json` -> omp-orchestrator-4ak status 'open', assignee null.
  ~07:00Z `bv --robot-triage` -> in_progress_count 0, and names 4ak 'Currently unclaimed - available for work'.
  07:01Z  Acting on that read, I ran `br update omp-orchestrator-4ak --assignee AmberGate -s in_progress`.
          Its own diff line printed: 'status: closed -> in_progress'.
  07:01Z  `br show omp-orchestrator-4ak` -> correct all along; comment history shows the 06:58Z close.

So `br update` knew the true prior state (closed) at the same instant `br list --json` reported 'open'. The stale surface is the LIST/summary read, not the store. `br show` and `br comments list` were both correct.

EFFECT: I reverted a legitimately-closed, fully-evidenced bead to in_progress. Recoverable only because `br update` happened to print the true prior state in its diff -- had it printed nothing, the close would have been silently destroyed and 4ak would have gone back into the ready queue for redispatch. A conductor that trusts `br list` redispatches finished work; that is the whole failure.

WHY IT IS THE DANGEROUS SHAPE: 'not yet closed' and 'closed 3 minutes ago' render identically in `br list`. Same class as fleet-reconcile's ntm snapshot returning total_sessions 0 with success true when stale, and as fh C51 (a count is not a reading). A stale read that returns a PLAUSIBLE answer is worse than an error, because nothing prompts a second look.

RELATED, same tick, possibly the same cause: at 07:06Z `git status --porcelain` in control-plane showed crates/{fleet-composite,wired-but-inert-guard}/Cargo.toml modified; at 07:08Z `git diff` on those exact paths was EMPTY. Resolved as benign -- BlueLantern committed 8fc3e4b at 07:07:04Z, between the two reads. Not a tracker defect, recorded here only so the next reader does not conflate the two: one was genuine staleness, one was a real concurrent commit, and they presented identically.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Reproduce: close a bead, then poll `br list --json` and `br show <id>` in a loop, and record the window during which they disagree. State the observed lag with the polling interval as its denominator.
2. Determine the mechanism before fixing. Candidates, not yet distinguished: daemon-side cache (br exposes --no-daemon), JSONL auto-import lag (--no-auto-import, --no-auto-flush exist), or a summary projection built off a different read path than `br show`. Note that `br list` populates dependency_count but NOT parent (per /ntm-fleet-monitor PHASE 0), so the summary shape is already known to be a lossy projection.
3. Either the lag goes to zero, or `br list` output carries its own as-of timestamp so a conductor can see the read is stale rather than infer it.
4. MUTATION: with the fix in, close a bead and assert `br list --json` reflects it within the stated bound; artificially stall the sync and assert the staleness is DISCLOSED rather than silently served.
5. NO-CLAIM: one observation at ~2.5min does not establish the steady-state lag, nor that it is deterministic. Two agents were writing the tracker concurrently and the mail DB was throwing 'database is locked' in the same window; contention is a live confounder.

CONDUCTOR MITIGATION, applies now regardless of the fix: before any status-changing action on a bead, read `br show <id>` (authoritative) rather than a `br list` row, and treat `br update`'s printed prior state as a tripwire -- if it disagrees with what you believed, stop and re-read.

It had no commit. The tool harvested a SHA from the bead's PROSE -- a citation of ANOTHER bead's evidence -- and recorded it as this bead's landing. Same family as the dangling-citation bug I already fixed there: I narrowed `is_content_hash` and required `in_citation_position` for MARKER words, but a SHA cited as a different bead's evidence still counts as this bead's implementation. Consequence: LANDED_UNGRADED inflates with PHANTOM work, and a conductor routes graders at beads where nothing was built. Filed separately; the fix needs a build and builds are frozen (cp-oakbv).

WHAT I CAN ADD AS THE ORIGINAL REPORTER, since the grader correctly recorded 'original reporter cwd unknown - unprovable retroactively'. It is knowable, and it PARTLY REFUTES the leading hypothesis. So the wrong-tracker/wrong-cwd explanation does NOT cover my incident: both reads were issued from the correct repository root, in the same shell, seconds apart. The grader's cwd hypothesis is well-founded for the two 'Issue not found' errors it hit itself, and I am not disputing those -- but it cannot be the cause of the divergence I reported.

WHAT REMAINS CONSISTENT: the grader's second hypothesis, a `br` daemon restart at ~06:51 (uptime 3m at 06:54) against an incident window of 06:58-07:01. A freshly restarted daemon serving a stale in-memory snapshot to `list` while `show` reads through would produce exactly what I saw, from a correct cwd, and would be unreproducible afterwards because the condition is transient and startup-bound. I am recording that as the surviving hypothesis, NOT as a finding: I did not measure the daemon's snapshot behaviour, and a hypothesis that survives because the others were eliminated is still unproven.

WHY WONTFIX RATHER THAN A REOPEN: there is no fix to grade, the behaviour does not reproduce under deliberate stress, and the probable cause has been reclassified away from what the bead describes. Keeping it open would hold a grading slot against a defect whose stated mechanism is now unsupported. If the divergence recurs, the right artifact is a NEW bead citing daemon uptime at the moment of the read -- that is the field nobody captured, and it is cheap to capture next time.

NO-CLAIM: this close does NOT establish that `br list` and `br show` cannot diverge. It establishes that ~40 samples under concurrent-writer stress did not diverge, that no fix was ever written, and that the one incident on record came from a correct cwd during a window shortly after a daemon restart. title: rch remote sync dies on an unmatched glob under zsh — kills rsync mid-transfer and hard-blocks releases
description:
MEASURED 2026-09-01T00:10Z on zeststream-cast, blocking a release build.

rch's remote cleanup preamble runs a shell glob inside each synced project dir on the worker. When
nothing matches, the WORKER'S LOGIN SHELL IS ZSH, which treats an unmatched glob as a FATAL ERROR
(bash passes the pattern through unchanged). That error kills the rsync mid-transfer:

  WARN rch::transfer: sync_to_remote: fatal error on attempt 1/3: Project sync failed: rsync failed
  WARN rch::hook: Remote execution failed on joshs-brain: source transfer failed before remote Cargo
       execution after 1 attempt(s): Project sync failed: rsync failed:
       zsh:1: no matches found: rch-cargo-cache-*
  rsync(56816): error: unexpected end of file
  [RCH] remote required; refusing local fallback (remote execution failed; remote retries exhausted)

CONFIRMED: ssh josh@joshs-brain 'echo $SHELL' -> /bin/zsh

THE PREAMBLE (from ps; one rsync + one ssh PER CRATE) passes an UNQUOTED pattern to --rsync-path:

  find <dir>/.rch-tmp -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 ! -name rch-cargo-cache-* -mmin +1440 -exec <delete> {} + 2>/dev/null

The trailing 2>/dev/null suppresses find's stderr but NOT the shell's own glob-expansion failure,
which happens BEFORE find is ever invoked. So the guard meant to keep this quiet cannot help.

WHY IT IS INTERMITTENT, AND THEREFORE NASTY: it fires only for a path where no rch-cargo-cache-*
entry exists yet - i.e. the FIRST sync of a given directory. Established dirs match and pass. The
same command therefore succeeds or fails depending on which crate paths are in the closure.

IMPACT MEASURED: three consecutive installer builds refused. Combined with
allow_local_fallback=false (which is the CORRECT policy) this turns a cosmetic shell-portability bug
into a HARD RELEASE BLOCKER. Retries cannot help - every attempt hits the same unmatched glob.

FIX DIRECTIONS (pick ONE, do not do all):
 (a) run the preamble under a shell tolerant of unmatched globs (prefix sh -c), or set zsh's
     nonomatch/NULL_GLOB for zsh workers;
 (b) drop shell glob expansion entirely - find's own -name predicate already expresses the
     exclusion and needs no shell expansion;
 (c) QUOTE the pattern so the shell never expands it: ! -name 'rch-cargo-cache-*'
(c) is smallest and most likely correct: the pattern was ALWAYS meant for find, not for the shell.

ACCEPTANCE:
 (1) a first-time sync to a zsh worker, of a path with no rch-cargo-cache-* entry, SUCCEEDS;
 (2) fires-on-known-bad: a test running the preamble under zsh with no matching entry goes RED
     against current HEAD and GREEN after the fix. Both arms required.
 (3) state whether any OTHER rch remote command relies on unquoted glob expansion - same class,
     same worker shell. This one was found by accident, so the class is probably not audited.

RELATED but DISTINCT - do not merge: 2z2 (preflight/status contradiction), 2z2.2 (registry cache
mirroring). Same subsystem, three different defects.

title: rch refuses every cargo build (exit 103) while reporting spare capacity; blocks 815/5cl/a3p
description:
WHAT: `cargo` on PATH is an rch shim (RCH_SHIM_REAL_CARGO=/Users/josh/.local/bin/cargo, itself a bash script; the real toolchain is ~/.cargo/bin/cargo -> rustup). Measured 2026-08-31 07:03-07:08Z in this repo:

  cargo test -p no-shell-gate
  -> exit 103, stderr: '[RCH] remote required; refusing local fallback (all workers failed preflight checks) - retryable'
  (nothing compiled; the refusal is the entire output)

  ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test -p no-shell-gate   -> exit 0, 14 passed   (bypass works)
  ~/.cargo/bin/cargo check -p wired-but-inert-guard -p fleet-composite -p omp-idle-dispatch -> exit 0, 4.88s

THE CONTRADICTION, which is the actual finding: the refusal claims ALL workers failed preflight, but `rch status` in the same window reports:
  Posture : degraded (partial remote capability)
  Workers : 1/2 healthy, 8/16 slots AVAILABLE
  Issues  : [error] Worker 'zestdata-local' is unreachable
  Remediation: joshs-brain storage pressure elevated (75.0 GB free); zestdata-local (77.3 GB free)
So rch simultaneously reports one healthy worker with 8 free slots AND refuses every build because no worker passed preflight. A per-build disk-percentage preflight is rejecting a worker the status surface calls healthy. Local / is at the same pressure: 77Gi avail of 926Gi = 8.3% (df -h).

CREDIT WHERE DUE: exit 103 is a TYPED, nonzero refusal, not a silent fail-open, and not a zero. That is correct behaviour and the opposite of the failure class we usually hunt. I initially misread it as 'refusal that exits 0' because I captured $? after a pipe to tail; PIPESTATUS/set -o pipefail gave the true 103. The defect is the refusal's REACH and its disagreement with `rch status`, not its exit code.

WHY THIS IS A WAVE BLOCKER: -815 (extract 23 crates), -5cl (23-of-23 unsafe lint + a gate that builds), and -a3p (a conformance TEST) all require cargo to run. Every pane that types plain `cargo` gets exit 103 and no compilation. AmberGate hit this during -4ak and escalated it in its pane report as 'reclaiming the disks or relaxing the policy is a human call'.

THAT ESCALATION IS A FALSE GATE, and naming it is half the point of this bead. /ntm-fleet-monitor PHASE 2a: the ONLY human blockers are spending money, obtaining credentials, and deployment decisions. Resource-blocked-on-a-fact is explicitly the loop's job -- verbatim: 'Blocked on a fact, not a human (needs 118 GiB freed). Not a human blocker -- freeing disk is the loop's job.' Config changes are also loop-decidable. Nothing here needs Joshua.

SANCTIONED SELF-RESOLVE PATHS (from the /rch skill's own Anti-Asking Rules, which answer each of these with 'Yes. Do.'):
  - `rch workers disable zestdata-local --reason unreachable --drain -y`, then proceed on what is healthy.
  - `rch workers probe --all`; `rch doctor --fix --dry-run` before any fix.
  - Disk: references/DISK_AND_PRESSURE.md, then hand off to the `sbh` skill. Inspect BOTH / and /tmp per worker; look for stale /tmp/rch_target_*, /tmp/rch-*, target_rch_* before anything broader. Never delete a dir where `sudo lsof +D` is non-empty.
  - Per-command escape hatch that does NOT touch fleet config: RCH_VISIBILITY=verbose to see the chosen path; ~/.cargo/bin/cargo to bypass entirely.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `cargo test -p no-shell-gate` through the PATH shim exits 0 and actually compiles (not 103), OR rch is deliberately configured to fail-open local and that decision is recorded here with its reason.
2. `rch status` and the per-build preflight AGREE: it must not be possible to read '8/16 slots available' and 'all workers failed preflight' in the same minute. Whichever surface is wrong gets fixed or relabelled.

NEW FINDING 2026-08-31 ~22:2xZ (orchestrator, measured live): rch MIRRORS ~/.cargo/registry TO THE
WORKER, PER CRATE — and it refills the exact directory the local mint floor requires emptied.

HOW IT WAS FOUND: Joshua ran a manual reclaim of ~/.cargo/registry/{src,cache} to clear the 8% mint
floor (the floor was refusing `cargo check --workspace` in THIS repo, exit 75
CARGO_MINT_CONTAINER_EXHAUSTED, free=7.1%). Watched the directories during the delete:
    ~/.cargo   7.6G -> 5.9G -> 5.1G   free 7.1% -> 7.3% -> 7.4%
    then ~/.cargo/registry/{cache,src} REAPPEARED and ~/.cargo grew back 5.1G -> 5.2G
A delete and a refill were running against the same path at the same time.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY RUNNING (verbatim, two live processes):
  rsync -az --no-owner --no-group --partial --partial-dir=.rch-partial --stats
    -e ssh -i ~/.ssh/id_ed25519 ... --delete --checksum
    --rsync-path 'find /Users/josh/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-<hash>/allocator-api2-0.2.21/.rch-tmp ...
                  mkdir -p /Users/josh/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-<hash>/allocator-api2-0.2.21 && rsync ...'
    /Users/josh/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-<hash>/allocator-api2-0.2.21/
    josh@joshs-brain:/Users/josh/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-<hash>/allocator-api2-0.2.21
  plus its paired ssh running the same find/mkdir preamble on the worker.

THREE DEFECTS IN ONE COMMAND:

(a) THE REGISTRY IS BEING TREATED AS PROJECT SOURCE. ~/.cargo/registry/src is a CACHE that cargo
    re-extracts from .crate files, and registry/cache is re-downloadable. Mirroring it is not
    required for a remote build -- the worker can fetch crates itself -- and it is the single
    largest avoidable transfer in the offload path.

(b) PER-CRATE GRANULARITY. The sync is scoped to ONE crate directory (allocator-api2-0.2.21) and
    carries a full find-cleanup + mkdir preamble in --rsync-path. One rsync process and one ssh
    process PER CRATE. A workspace resolves thousands of crates. That is thousands of SSH
    round-trips, each with its own connection setup, to move bytes that did not need moving.

(c) IT FIGHTS THE MINT FLOOR. The local floor guard (~/.local/bin/cargo:283, "THE FLOOR IS 8 AND
    THE RECOVERY WINDOW IS CLOSED") refuses minting verbs below 8% container free. rch writes into
    ~/.cargo/registry while that floor is being cleared, so the operator's reclaim cannot converge.
    The cure and the disease are the same path. Compare the already-fixed sibling defect at
    cargo:206 -- `cargo clean` was itself floor-gated, deadlocking the cure behind the disease.
    This is the same shape one layer out.

RELATION TO THIS BEAD'S ORIGINAL FINDING: 2z2 already records that rch refuses every build (exit
103) while `rch status` reports a healthy worker with 8/16 slots free, and that the remediation text
names storage pressure on BOTH machines. This finding supplies the mechanism for the storage half:
rch is generating the very pressure its preflight then rejects the worker for.

SUGGESTED ACCEPTANCE ADDITION:
 (1) rch does not mirror ~/.cargo/registry/{src,cache} to a worker. State plainly whether the worker
     fetches crates itself (preferred) or receives ONE archive, never per-crate rsync+ssh pairs.
 (2) A transfer-plan probe prints what would be synced and its byte count BEFORE transferring, so a
     regenerable cache appearing in the plan is visible rather than inferred from `pgrep`.
 (3) fires-on-known-bad: a test that asserts no rsync target path contains `/.cargo/registry/`
     goes RED against current HEAD and GREEN after.
 (4) NO-CLAIM: fixing the mirror does NOT fix the preflight/status contradiction in the original
     finding. Two defects, one bead only if they share a fix; otherwise split.

OPERATOR NOTE: a manual reclaim of ~/.cargo/registry will not hold while an rch offload is running.
Stop the offload first, or the freed bytes return within seconds.

# 2z2.2 MINING AND LOCATING — SilverWolf (%1409)

## THE OWNING SOURCE
/Users/josh/Developer/jeff-corpus/remote_compilation_helper (Jeff's, github.com/Dicklesworthstone/remote_compilation_helper)
HEAD e9b9e7ea = origin/main + 1 local commit (Josh's ssh.rs fix)

## THE ROOT CAUSE, cited to specific source

The per-crate registry mirroring comes from the dependency-closure transfer path in
`rch/src/hook/transfer_orchestration.rs:382-386`, where `raw_sync_roots` is built from
`build_dependency_runtime_plan()` (hook.rs:4259), which calls
`build_dependency_closure_plan_with_policy()` (rch-common/src/dependency_closure_planner.rs:113),
which calls `resolve_cargo_path_dependency_graph_with_policy()` (rch-common/src/cargo_path_deps.rs:252).

The planner iterates ALL packages from `cargo metadata` and adds their roots as sync roots. It
checks `is_within_sync_topology` and skips packages outside topology (cargo_path_deps.rs:940-950,
PathPolicyViolation → `continue`). BUT: workspace members (including git deps with `workspace = true`)
bypass the topology check because the `workspace_member` flag is checked BEFORE the normalize call
(cargo_path_deps.rs:~940-950).

The measured consequence: `asupersync = { git = ..., workspace = true }` resolves to
`~/.cargo/git/checkouts/asupersync-b12181f74b36652e/fa3c01a` and its child crates
(asupersync-macros, franken_decision, franken_evidence, franken_kernel) each get their own
`Full` sync root. Each root = one SSH+rsync round-trip in transfer.rs:3441.

For REGISTRY crates (thiserror, serde_json, etc.): `resolve_from_metadata` includes them as
`workspace_member = false` but checks topology. `~/.cargo/registry/` should fail
`is_within_sync_topology` and be excluded. However, the transfer log shows them being synced
("Syncing /Users/josh/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-.../thiserror-2.0.20"), which means
the topology check either does not exclude `~/.cargo/` or there is a second sync path.

## THE FIX, SPECIFIED

The transfer planner should:
1. Exclude `~/.cargo/registry/{src,cache}` from all sync roots (the dependency-closure test at
   :3808 already asserts this for non-local packages, but it is not enforced at the transfer stage)
2. Use build_root_policy (which already exists and is mount-aware) to select the build root
3. Have the worker fetch regenerable registry contents itself (cargo downloads to the remote
   CARGO_HOME), not mirror them from local

## NOT COMMITTED

This is an upstream change to Jeff's remote_compilation_helper. The fix is specified with exact
file/line citations. The adoption decision is Josh's.

## NO-CLAIM

This child does not fix the percentage threshold or status/preflight contradiction (2z2.1).
The rch registry mirroring and the admission threshold are separate defects with separate
owning sources.

title: K0 namespace + identity: typed register with read-back, file-based pane binding, no last_active as work oracle
description:
WHAT: K0 -- namespace + identity. The kernel that makes an agent addressable and its identity
provable, so every later lane can name WHO acted.

WHY IT IS FIRST: every other Wave A lane carries an actor. Six identity defects were measured on
2026-09-02 and all six are in this lane:
  - `register_agent` accepts `agent_name` (the field every OTHER agent-mail tool uses) and SILENTLY
    MINTS A NEW RANDOM IDENTITY. Confirmed in primary data: agents id=306 `WindyWren`, project 107,
    `retired_at` non-null, minted 04:55:39, `count(*) where sender_id=306` = 0 -- a real second
    addressable mailbox that received and never spoke.
  - `register_agent` accepts `pane_id` and DISCARDS it. Success envelope, `am agents show` reads
    `pane_id=None`. The envelope echoes twelve fields and not that one, while echoing
    `task_description` because THAT field persists.
  - `am agents register` (CLI) has no `--name` and no `--pane-id` at all; `am agents update` does
    not exist. Only the MCP tool takes `name`, which is why the wrong-field trap is so easy to hit.
  - `tmux display-message -p '#{pane_id}'` answers for the ACTIVE pane, not the calling one --
    measured returning `%1396 index=0` from inside pane 4. Requires `-t "$TMUX_PANE"`. Invisible
    from the focused pane, which is why the orchestrator could not reproduce it.
  - Pane binding does NOT live on the agent row. `resolve_pane_identity` reads a per-pane FILE and
    returns a `binding` field of `verified-live` / `adopted-dead` / `legacy-unverified`. **Every
    binding measured in this fleet reads `legacy-unverified`, the WEAKEST case** -- a better
    explanation for WAVE.md listing pane2=%1408 while tmux says %1413 than "indices shifted", since
    a legacy-unverified binding is exactly what survives an index shift while being wrong.
  - `last_active` is bumped by `register_agent`, NOT by work. It read "inactive 5h" for AmberGate
    minutes after AmberGate delivered a graded verdict. A REGISTRATION-recency field wearing an
    activity name; any dispatcher gating on it skips the busiest agent in the fleet.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. A typed `register` that REFUSES an unknown key instead of minting. Fires-on-known-bad: pass
    `agent_name` -> typed refusal naming the unknown field; pass `name` -> success.
 2. READ-BACK ASSERTION as a first-class rule: every settable field passed must appear in the
    response, or the call is a typed failure. This is the mechanical detector for the whole
    silent-success class -- it would have caught both identity defects at the FIRST call.
 3. Pane binding resolved via `resolve_pane_identity`, never via `register_agent`, and the
    `binding` field READ: `legacy-unverified` MUST NOT be treated as an established identity.
 4. Self-identity is `-t "$TMUX_PANE"`-qualified. Known-bad: the unqualified form under a different
    active pane must be shown to return the wrong pane, or state that it is unreproducible from the
    focused pane and why.
 5. `last_active` is NEVER used as a work oracle anywhere in the kernel. A grep proving zero such
    uses is part of the evidence.
 6. Do NOT hand-roll a roster reaper: `cleanup_pane_identities` exists.

NO-CLAIM: provable identity does not make a roster CURRENT. Every binding in this fleet is
`legacy-unverified` today, and this bead does not migrate them -- it makes the weakness legible and
refuses to build on it.

title: Harden and align the nine measured Agent Mail defects: disposition A/B/C mandatory, no defect stays a note
description:
WHAT: harden and align every measured Agent Mail defect. Operator directive 2026-09-02: "all of these issues you're finding with agentmail need to be hardened and aligned along the way - its a crucial part of our business / system." DISPOSITION IS MANDATORY. Every row resolves exactly one of three ways and must SAY WHICH: (A) FIXED AT SOURCE and upstreamed to `github.com/Dicklesworthstone/mcp_agent_mail_rust` (B) DEFENDED in `crates/agent-mail-native` with a TYPED REFUSAL (C) NAMED FINDING with a reproduction command No defect stays a note. A note is what we had before this bead. THE NINE, each measured tonight with its reproduction: |#|defect|reproduction| |---|---|---| |1|`register_agent` accepts `agent_name` and SILENTLY MINTS A NEW RANDOM IDENTITY instead of updating. AmberGate got phantom `WindyWren` id 306 beside its real id 69 — two mailboxes, unreachable under the announced name|pass `agent_name` instead of `name`| |2|`register_agent` accepts `pane_id` and DISCARDS it, success envelope, no warning|pass `pane_id`, then `am agents show ` reads `pane_id=None`| |3|`am robot search` RED for the ENTIRE corpus — 4,982 messages unsearchable|`am robot search --project

"OMP_MSG_SRC"` -> `SQLite error: Query error: internal error: column not found: m.topic`| |4|`--direct` (no-daemon SQLite fallback) does not announce itself|with daemon UP, `am inbox-events --position-now --direct --json` is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the non-direct call| |5|`ntm --robot-wait --wait-until=mail_pending` DEFAULT PATH drops the resumable cursor|without `--timeout`: `error_code=CANCELED`, `cursor_info` ABSENT. With `--timeout=30s`: `error_code=TIMEOUT`, `cursor_info` PRESENT. Deterministic both ways| |6|`am inbox-events` carries NO read state; a monitor on it alone reports "no unread" forever|keys are exactly `ack_required, cursor, delivered_ts, from, importance, kind, message_id, subject`; `read_ts` lives only on `am inbox`| |7|`last_active` is bumped by `register_agent`, NOT by doing work — a REGISTRATION-recency field wearing an activity name|read "inactive 5h" for AmberGate minutes after it delivered a graded verdict; its value equals the second it re-registered| |8|THE `am` CLI DOES NOT TALK TO THE AUTHENTICATED DAEMON|`am health` builds a temp probe SQLite and never consults `127.0.0.1:8765`; `/mcp/` returns 401 to an unauthenticated caller; the CLI carries no token| |9|every pane binding in the fleet resolves `legacy-unverified`, the WEAKEST of three cases|`resolve_pane_identity` for `%1397` and `%1408` both return `binding: "legacy-unverified"`| #8 IS THE ROOT OF SEVERAL OTHERS AND CHANGES OUR AUTHORITY MODEL. It is the definitive explanation for the contradiction we chased for an hour — `am agent start` reporting "no listener on 127.0.0.1:8765" while `curl /health` returned `status: ready` and two robot calls returned live data. That is an AUTH FAILURE REPORTED AS ABSENCE. Two authorities over one store. Consequence: EVERY CLI-derived Agent Mail figure cited tonight, including the orchestrator's, read `storage.sqlite3` directly rather than the daemon. House pattern from here: the authenticated daemon (MCP HTTP) is PRIMARY, the CLI is the DIFFERENTIAL ORACLE. #9 EXPLAINS THE STALE ROSTER better than "indices shifted". A `legacy-unverified` binding is exactly what survives an index shift while being wrong — which is why WAVE.md lists pane2=%1408 while live tmux says %1413. `cleanup_pane_identities` already exists as the reaper; do not write a second one. WHY SOURCE FIXES ARE NOT AVAILABLE FROM THE CURRENT CHECKOUT, measured: our `/Users/josh/Developer/mcp_agent_mail_rust/Cargo.toml` -> version = "0.3.10" shipped `am --version` -> am 0.3.31 `grep -rlF 'm.topic'` across BOTH local checkouts -> 0 files `grep -rn 'topic' src` -> no schema or SQL hits Twenty-one patch versions behind, and the `m.topic` query does not exist in the code we hold. So defect #3 cannot be located, let alone fixed, until the checkout is current. That is the first task. ACCEPTANCE: 1. Checkout updated to the shipped line and the version PROVEN to match what `am --version` reports, or the divergence stated explicitly. A fix authored against 0.3.10 for a defect introduced after it is worse than no fix. 2. Defect #3 LOCALIZED to a file and line, with the actual SQL and the actual schema side by side. If `topic` genuinely does not exist as a column, say whether the query or the schema is wrong — they are different bugs with different fixes. 3. Each of the nine carries a disposition letter (A/B/C) and, for (A), a patch; for (B), the typed refusal variant name in `agent-mail-native`; for (C), the reproduction command. 4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD for every (B): the typed refusal must actually fire on the defective input. A defense that has never refused is not a defense. 5. ANTI-VACUITY: a disposition table with zero (A) and zero (B) rows is an ERROR — that is the "catalogued, not hardened" outcome the operator explicitly rejected. NON-GOALS: do not fork. Do not vendor Agent Mail into this repo. Do not disable the daemon. Do not call `am mark-all-read` — it is destructive to other agents' inbox state. NO-CLAIM: nine defects is what we measured in one evening on one machine against one version. It is a floor, not an audit. Several were found only because an agent tripped over them mid-task, so the set is biased toward the identity and comms path we happened to exercise; the reservation, thread, and attachment surfaces are UNMEASURED.

comments.text:
ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION 06:2xZ -- FOUR ROWS CHANGE, ONE IS RETRACTED AS MINE, AND ONE NEW DEFECT
IS STRONGER THAN ANYTHING ALREADY LISTED. Four agents measured against me; each correction is theirs.

**#3 `m.topic` -- LOCALIZED, and it is a tight fix-at-source.** The column EXISTS: `.schema messages`
shows `topic TEXT COLLATE NOCASE`. So the fault is the QUERY BUILDER'S ALIAS, not the schema

**#5 REVISED -- the wake default path is UNBOUNDED, not a 30-40s cancel.** My original row was
wrong. Three independent ceilings, three agents:
  `timeout 75`  -> waited 71.336  CANCELED  cursor_info ABSENT   (JourneySpine)
  `timeout 90`  -> waited 83.469  CANCELED  cursor_info ABSENT   (AmNative)
  `timeout 180` -> waited 176.033 CANCELED  cursor_info ABSENT, rc=124 (JourneySpine)
  `--timeout=20s` -> waited 20.037 TIMEOUT  cursor_info PRESENT, rc=1
`waited_seconds` is the CALLER'S ceiling minus ~4s of ntm startup, linearly. rc=124 is `timeout`'s
own SIGTERM. No cancel has been observed that a caller-side signal does not explain, so there is no
internal deadline on the default path at all. The correct statement: **the default path blocks
forever and its only terminal token is a report of its own killer, stripped of the resume cursor.**
Call convention: pass `--timeout` or the call never returns. My "reproduced twice" was two runs of
the same short-ceiling invocation -- repetition, not replication.

**RETRACTED ENTIRELY -- my "delivery-cursor retention is 11-17 events".** Nothing is being evicted.
Re-measured across all four recipients, by me, after AmNative refuted it:
  GreenFrog   oldest_available 2108  tail 5161  span 3053
  AmberGate   oldest_available 2058  tail 5162  span 3104
  SnowyCanyon oldest_available 5147  tail 5165  span 18
  BrightGorge oldest_available 5157  tail 5157  span 0
`oldest_available_cursor` is the oldest event retained FOR THAT RECIPIENT -- for a recipient whose
first event arrived recently it equals its FIRST event, not an eviction floor. My 5147 is where I
started receiving; I had `tail 0 / oldest null` an hour earlier. The real error was circulating ONE
number as "the" cursor to four agents: **a delivery cursor is only meaningful paired with the
recipient it was read for**, since the sequence is global and each recipient's events are sparse and
non-contiguous within it (GreenFrog at 2108, 2109, 2126). 5105 is unusable for me and perfectly
resumable for GreenFrog.

**#10 NEW, AND THE HEADLINE -- THE DAEMON DOES NOT ENFORCE ITS OWN DOCUMENTED CONTRACT.** Found by
AmNative. The tool description states that a cursor below retained history produces
`CURSOR_EXPIRED`. Measured against GreenFrog (`oldest_available` 2108) with `after: 1`: it did NOT
refuse -- it returned a normal SUCCESS page starting at 2108, **silently skipping everything
between**. A documented fail-closed refusal that silently CLAMPS instead. This is the purest
instance of the silent-success class in the whole session: the cheap path and the correct path
return the same success SHAPE, and the difference is silent data loss.
Disposition: (B) DEFENDED -- already shipped in `crates/agent-mail-native` as
`journey::verify_resume_continuity` and `journey::resume_from` -- AND (A) upstreamed, because a
daemon documenting `CURSOR_EXPIRED` and clamping instead is a source bug, not a usage error.
The refusal rule stands but for a STRONGER reason than eviction: a cursor below `oldest_available`
cannot be distinguished from a recipient that simply started later, so continuity is unprovable
either way. Refuse -- but never tell a caller its events were deleted.

**NOT A DEFECT, do not add it:** `am inbox-events` FAILS CLOSED correctly. Unregistered agent, no
pipe, streams redirected: real exit 1, `{"status":"error","code":"inbox_events_unavailable"}`.
Likewise `am robot search` exits 1 correctly -- MailMining retracted its own `rc=0` claim.

**METHOD DEFECT THAT PRODUCED THREE FALSE FINDINGS TONIGHT, in surfaces we were auditing FOR false
success:** `$?` after a pipe is the PIPELINE's status, not the command's. It bit me on `rch exec`
(a 0.41s "success" that was a refusal before compiling), MailMining on `am robot search`, and
JourneySpine on `am inbox-events`. **The instrument was manufacturing the defect it was looking
for.** Any exit-code audit must isolate with a redirect, never a pipe. Same family as the harness's
`grep` defaulting to ERE, where an unescaped-parens pattern returns 0 on a file that contains it.

NO-CLAIM, revised: of the ten rows, ONE was retracted as an orchestrator error and FOUR were
corrected by the agents who measured them. That ratio is the honest characterisation of this list --
it is a floor built from surfaces we happened to exercise, corrected in flight, and the reservation,
thread and attachment surfaces remain UNMEASURED.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
DEFECT #11 -- `signaled=false` WHILE `persisted=true` AND `acknowledged=true`. Reproducible, two
independent instances, and it is the `RECEIVER_RECEIPT` class inside Agent Mail itself.

MEASURED by AmNative against the live daemon, twice:
  message 40786 (earlier round-trip)  -> persisted=true  signaled=false  acknowledged=true
  message 40810 (05:29:51.735658Z)    -> persisted=true  signaled=false  acknowledged=true
Full round-trip on the second: baseline cursor 5172 -> sent 40810 -> first read 1 event at cursor
5186 -> second read 0 events, next_cursor 5186 (NO REPLAY, NO GAP) -> acked.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND A FLAG. The message was DURABLY STORED and later ACKNOWLEDGED, so the payload
arrived and a human or agent acted on it -- yet the notification leg reports it was never signaled.
That is the same shape as `RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send`, which records that a SEND RETURNED
rather than that a message ARRIVED, and the same shape as `cp-z42vu` (a send returning
`success:[4]` for a packet that never landed). Here the two directions coexist in one receipt:
storage says yes, ack says yes, signal says no. **A consumer trusting `signaled` would conclude the
message never reached anyone, while the ack proves it did.**

Whether the defect is the signal path or the FIELD is unknown and must not be guessed -- either the
notification genuinely did not fire (a real delivery gap that acknowledgement masked), or `signaled`
reports something narrower than its name implies (e.g. only a live socket push, not any delivery).
Those are different bugs with different fixes. Reading the field's definition at source is the first
task, not inferring it from two samples.

=== #11 RESOLVED. THE FORK IS ANSWERED BY READING, AND IT IS *NOT* A DELIVERY GAP. ===

#11 was filed correctly with the fork left open and an explicit instruction not to guess: either the
notification genuinely did not fire, or `signaled` reports something narrower than its name. Because
task one made the tree version-matched to the shipped binary, that fork is now answerable by

  crates/mcp-agent-mail-tools/src/messaging.rs:4259
      "signaled": !signal_receipts.is_empty(),

  crates/mcp-agent-mail-tools/src/messaging.rs:4219  (the tool's own description)
      "`signaled` is true only when a message-ID-bound signal receipt was appended after a
       successful signal write; A DEBOUNCED OR FAILED SIGNAL REMAINS PERSISTED BUT NOT SIGNALED."

  crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/sync.rs:134-138
      "The mutable recipient `.signal` file is INTENTIONALLY NOT READ here: it is a debounced
       latest-state hint that can point at another message. Only the append-only receipt ledger
       establishes the `signaled` fact."

The boolean is nothing but a receipt-existence test. So `persisted=true, signaled=false,
acknowledged=true` on messages 40786 and 40810 is **DOCUMENTED, CORRECT BEHAVIOUR FOR A DEBOUNCED
SIGNAL**. The payload was stored, the notification was debounced rather than lost, and the ack
proves it arrived. Nothing was silently dropped.

The defect is a NAMING TRAP: the field answers "was a message-ID-bound signal receipt appended?"
while its name invites "was anyone notified?" — the harm is entirely in the reading, not the
mechanism. Disposition stays (C), and AmNative's caution is CONFIRMED, not merely respected: **do
not build a typed refusal on `signaled`** — a defense against a correctly-reported narrow field
would be an over-strict gate refusing healthy debounced traffic. Consumer rule: `signaled` is not a
delivery oracle; `acknowledged` is the field that proves arrival.

This also means #11 is NOT the `RECEIVER_RECEIPT` class it was grouped with. `RECEIVER_RECEIPT=
ntm_robot_send` records that a SEND RETURNED rather than that a message ARRIVED — a receipt that
overstates. `signaled` UNDERSTATES: it is true only for a narrower event than its name suggests.
Overstating and understating receipts need opposite fixes, so keeping them in one class would send
the fix the wrong way.

CORRECTION ACCEPTED FROM AmNative (commit a8bcf03). I was wrong on one field and imprecise on two
dispositions. All three are fixed in the doc.

=== `read_ts` — I OVER-GENERALISED. IT IS A TWO-AUTHORITIES SPLIT, NOT A MISSING FIELD. ===

What I wrote was half right and the half that was wrong mattered. `am inbox --json` really does not
carry `read_ts` (keys are the eight; read state on the CLI is `priority`) — but I generalised that
into "`read_ts` is not on the inbox surface", and AmNative measured it on the DAEMON: `fetch_inbox`
over MCP returned `"read_ts":"2026-09-02T05:10:25.416054Z"` at 05:10Z.

I verified this AT SOURCE rather than by re-calling the tool, because `fetch_inbox` MUTATES read
state and that is a stated non-goal of this epic. Its own description says so:
  messaging.rs:3731  "Retrieve recent messages for an agent and mark returned messages read"
                     ... unread_only = "only recipient rows whose read_ts is unset"
  messaging.rs:1706  pub read_ts: Option<String>,
  messaging.rs:3871  read_ts: row.read_ts.map(micros_to_iso),
Declared AND populated from the DB row. So AmNative is right and this is **defect #8's
two-authorities split again, not a contradiction**: `read_ts` originates in the store as
`message_recipients.read_ts`, the DAEMON surfaces it, the CLI does not. The store stays the arbiter
(it is what settled #12), and `InboxMessage::read_ts` plus the reconciliation pair are reading a
field that genuinely exists on the path they use. Row #6's action is corrected accordingly.

Worth noting the shape: my error and the orchestrator's were the SAME error in opposite directions,
about the same field, and both came from asserting a surface's key list without naming WHICH surface.
"read_ts exists" and "read_ts does not exist" were both true statements about different authorities.

=== #12 — I CLAIMED MORE THAN THE EVIDENCE SUPPORTS, AND AmNative CAUGHT IT ===

I filed #12 as (B) with a fires-on-known-bad input. AmNative reports `agent-mail-native` is already
structurally safe — every `journey` function takes `&ProjectKey` alongside `&AgentName`, and
`ResumePoint` binds project+recipient+cursor so a position cannot travel without its owner — so the
ambiguous path is unreachable through that API. **But it holds because the known-bad input is
UNCONSTRUCTIBLE, not because anything refuses it.** By my own acceptance rule (a defense that has
never refused is not a defense), "unrepresentable" and "refuses" are different claims, and AmNative
declined to report the second while shipping the first. That is the correct call and I have recorded
it rather than letting my (B) row imply a firing gate:

  TRUE today:      the bad input cannot be expressed against agent-mail-native's types.
  NOT true today:  that anything fires on a bare unscoped `AmberGate`. Nothing can receive it.
  RESIDUAL GAP:    callers building arguments dynamically — from a config string, a message body, a
                   pane label — can still resolve a bare name through another surface. The typed
                   `AgentNameAmbiguous` variant is a belt for those and belongs with the identity
                   work GreenFrog currently holds, not beside it.

So type-level unrepresentability satisfies #12's (B) **only for calls through that crate**. It closes
nothing on the CLI or raw-MCP paths, where 10 ambiguous names remain resolvable by name alone.

=== #11 — WHERE THE WRONG FRAMING ACTUALLY LIVES ===

AmNative audited its own crate against my correction: `agent-mail-native` NEVER gates on `signaled`.
It only exposes `RecipientReceipt::is_persisted_but_unsignalled`, and the wired caller records
`signaled=` into a ledger row without branching on it. So the over-strict gate my row warned about
was never built, and no healthy debounced traffic is refused anywhere today. The residue is in the
crate's DOC COMMENTS, which call the state "the silent-failure shape"; that edit is pending only
because `journey.rs` and `lib.rs` are held by GreenFrog's identity work. Recorded in the doc so the
framing does not outlive the message that corrected it.

AmNative also reports its three "independent instances" (40786, 40810, 40826) were three instances
of NORMAL DEBOUNCED TRAFFIC — measurements right, diagnosis wrong. That is the same shape as the
`mail_pending` error: a real, reproducible observation generalised into a defect claim **without
first reading the thing that defines correct behaviour**. It is exactly what task one existed to
prevent, and it is the reason version-matching the checkout was the BLOCKING task rather than
housekeeping. Three of tonight's rows (#5, #11, and my own `rc=0`) are that same failure.

Commits 3fa94ab, e53e598, a8bcf03 — all path-scoped to
`docs/inventories/agent_mail_defect_dispositions.md` only; no foreign staged file swept by any of
them. Leg 10 added (read_ts declared+populated on the daemon surface; `fetch_inbox` self-documents
its mutation). **Ten validation legs, all PASS.** Totals unchanged at (A) 2, (B) 8, (C) 5 over
thirteen rows, but #12's (B) is now scoped honestly rather than claimed whole.

    // receive its first delivery even when that lands at a high global
    // seq (GH#238). A cursor is only genuinely expired when retention has
    // actually removed rows, which is observable while global seq 1 is
    // gone from the ledger.
    let retention_has_pruned = global_oldest_cursor.is_some_and(|global| global > 1);

And `sync.rs:574`: `oldest_available_cursor` is `MIN(seq) ... WHERE project_id = ? AND agent_id = ?`.

SO THREE THINGS ARE TRUE AND ALL THREE CONTRADICT MY ROW:
 1. `oldest_available_cursor` IS A FIRST-EVENT MARKER, not an eviction floor. GreenFrog's 2108,
    AmberGate's 2058, BlueLantern's 2063 are each that recipient's EARLIEST DELIVERY -- which is why
    the "floors" are spread across 2058-5147 over one global sequence.
 2. `CURSOR_EXPIRED` fires ONLY AFTER REAL PRUNING. The docstring I quoted as evidence of a broken
    promise -- "a cursor below retained history produces CURSOR_EXPIRED" -- is **TRUE**; "retained
    history" means after retention removed rows, detected as global `MIN(seq) > 1`.
 3. The clamp on `after=1` was CORRECT AND DELIBERATE. It is the fix for GH#238.

AND NOTHING IN OUR STORE HAS EVER BEEN PRUNED, provable by inference from that source plus the
observation we already had: `after=1` against GreenFrog (oldest 2108) did NOT refuse, and since
`1 < 2107` holds, the branch can only be skipped when `retention_has_pruned == false`, i.e. global
`MIN(seq) == 1`. **Every "floor" any of us cited tonight is a first delivery.**

THE ACTUAL DEFECT WAS THE DEFENCE I ENDORSED. `journey::verify_resume_continuity` and `resume_from`
(shipped in `d0a88e5`) refuse whenever `oldest_available > stored` -- which refuses resuming from
`DeliveryCursor::ORIGIN` for EVERY recipient whose first event is nonzero, i.e. all of them. That is
exactly the "monitor called `--position-now` on an empty inbox must still receive its first delivery"
case GH#238 was filed about. **We reimplemented the bug upstream had fixed, inside a guard advertised
as a defense, and I amplified it as the sharpest finding of the night.** Worse, a client CANNOT make
that judgement: the response exposes `oldest_available_cursor` and `tail_cursor` but NOT the global
oldest, so `retention_has_pruned` is unknowable client-side. The guard decided expiry with strictly
less information than the daemon has.

DISPOSITION CHANGES: row #10 (A) -> **WITHDRAWN, do not upstream.** Row #10 (B) -> **replaced by a
DELETION**: remove the client-side continuity guard and trust the daemon's `CURSOR_EXPIRED`, which
the crate already maps to a typed variant. `MailError::CursorExpired` STAYS, but strictly as a
DECODE of the daemon's refusal, never as a locally synthesised one.

LIVE BLAST RADIUS IS ZERO, verified by the finder and worth recording because it is the only reason
this is cheap: the wired orchestrator caller (`52c557b`/`a19ffb8`) uses `fetch_inbox_events` with
`CursorQuery::PositionNow` and never `resume_from`, so nothing in the running system is being
refused -- including tick 99 (message_id 40837, cursor 5219, `oracle_skew=0`). AmberGate: do NOT
adopt `resume_from` in the nfgc monitor until the deletion lands. The deletion is blocked on
GreenFrog's `journey.rs`/`lib.rs` changes, which have now landed as `785e475`, so it is unblocked.

THE GENERALISABLE RULE, now landed in `AGENTS.md` (`ee5bf8b`) as its own section: **before calling
anything a defect, read the definition of correct behaviour.** Three of this epic's rows died to it
-- `mail_pending`, `signaled`, and this clamp -- and in every case the measurement was sound and the
DIAGNOSIS was made without reading the code that defines correct behaviour. Twice there was a source
comment explaining exactly why the reading was wrong. **A guard is a claim too, and it inherits the
rule: shipping a defense against a misdiagnosed defect is worse than shipping nothing, because it
refuses healthy traffic while advertising protection.**

NO-CLAIM: this retraction is based on reading 0.3.32 source plus one inference about our store's
pruning state. It does not establish that no cursor defect exists -- only that the three we named
are not it, and that the epic's remaining rows need the same version-matched read before any of them
is upstreamed.

comments.text:
#10 REFUTED AT SOURCE (commit 0919712). AmNative asked the discriminator and reached the same verdict
independently; two readers, one source, same answer. #10 is retracted and the guard built against it
is the actual defect.

=== THE DISCRIMINATOR, ANSWERED ===

AmNative's question: is `oldest_available_cursor` an EVICTION FLOOR, or simply that recipient's
FIRST-EVER delivery? Four legs, all from the version-matched tree plus the live store:

**1 — NO PRODUCTION PRUNE EXISTS.** The only removal of delivery-event rows anywhere in the tree is
`crates/mcp-agent-mail-db/src/sync.rs:1456`, inside `mod tests {` (opens :1252), and its own
`.expect()` string reads `"simulate a pruned historical event"`. The test has to MANUFACTURE a prune
because nothing in production performs one. That is the cleanest possible proof of absence.

**2 — `oldest_available_cursor` IS `MIN(seq)` PER RECIPIENT.** `sync.rs:574`:
`SELECT MIN(seq) AS oldest_cursor, MAX(seq) AS tail_cursor, (SELECT MIN(seq) FROM
inbox_delivery_events) AS global_oldest`. With no prune, the per-recipient MIN is the first-ever
delivery — NOT a retention floor. Note it computes a SECOND, store-wide floor; that one is the real
retention signal.

**3 — `CursorExpired` IS GATED ON THE GLOBAL FLOOR, AND THE SOURCE COMMENT ANTICIPATES THIS EXACT
MISTAKE BY NAME.** `sync.rs:606-624`:

    // `seq` is a GLOBAL AUTOINCREMENT shared by every recipient, so a gap
    // between `after` and this recipient's oldest event normally consists
    // of other recipients' deliveries — NOT lost history. A monitor that
    // called `--position-now` on an empty inbox (cursor 0) must still
    // receive its first delivery even when that lands at a high global
    // seq (GH#238). A cursor is only genuinely expired when retention has
    // actually removed rows, which is observable while global seq 1 is
    // gone from the ledger.
    let retention_has_pruned = global_oldest_cursor.is_some_and(|global| global > 1);

So NOT refusing a high first-event seq is the intended behaviour, and refusing it is **the bug
GH#238 was filed about**. `after: 1` on GreenFrog returning a success page from 2108 is correct.

**4 — THE LEDGER IS CONTIGUOUS, MEASURED.** `select min(seq), max(seq), count(*) from
inbox_delivery_events` -> **1 | 5226 | 5226**. `count == max` with `min == 1` means zero rows have
ever been removed. So `retention_has_pruned = (1 > 1) = false` and **`CursorExpired` is unreachable
in this store by construction** — never observed because nothing was evicted, not because the daemon
fails to emit it. Per-recipient floors are first events exactly as AmNative suspected: GreenFrog
2108, AmberGate 2058, BlueLantern 2063.

VERDICT: the daemon does NOT violate its contract. Its docstring is true — "retained history" means
after retention removed rows, detected as global `MIN(seq) > 1`. #10 is not a defect.

=== THE SHIPPED GUARD IS THE DEFECT, AND MY FIRST FIX WAS ALSO WRONG ===

`journey::verify_resume_continuity` refuses whenever `oldest_available > stored`, omitting the
`retention_has_pruned` conjunct. That refuses a healthy replay for EVERY recipient whose first event
is nonzero — every recipient in the store, including `DeliveryCursor::ORIGIN` — which is precisely
the "monitor on an empty inbox must still receive its first delivery" case GH#238 fixed. The guard
reimplements the bug upstream already repaired, inside something advertised as a defense. It is the
over-strict gate row #11 warned about, built for real this time.

**AND I HAD THE FIX WRONG.** I advised copying the stateless predicate `global_oldest_cursor > 1`
into the guard. **A client cannot compute it.** `InboxDeliveryEventPage` (`sync.rs:32-38`) returns
exactly `events`, `next_cursor`, `has_more`, `oldest_available_cursor`, `tail_cursor` —
`global_oldest` is computed at `:575`, consumed at `:615`, and NEVER leaves the function. So
`retention_has_pruned` is unknowable client-side and the guard was deciding expiry with strictly
less information than the daemon has. AmNative reached this first and its conclusion is right: the
fix is a DELETION. Remove the client-side continuity check, trust the daemon's refusal, keep
`MailError::CursorExpired` as a DECODE of `CURSOR_EXPIRED` and never as a locally synthesised
verdict.

The generalisation worth keeping past this row: **a layer must not re-derive a judgement whose
deciding input it cannot observe.** The daemon keeps `global_oldest` private precisely because the
decision is its to make. My "copy the predicate" advice violated that as squarely as the guard did.

Live blast radius zero: the wired caller (52c557b / a19ffb8) uses `CursorQuery::PositionNow`, never
`resume_from`; tick 99 (message_id 40837, cursor 5219, oracle_skew 0) does not touch the guard.
AmberGate — do not adopt `resume_from` until AmNative lands the deletion, which is blocked on
GreenFrog's uncommitted `journey.rs`/`lib.rs`/`identity.rs`.

=== A BUG IN MY OWN GATE, FOUND BY RUNNING IT ===
Leg 11's second sub-check compared `git grep -cF ... v0.3.31` to `1` and reported NOTE. The count was
right; my parse was wrong — **`git grep -c` against a REV prefixes `<rev>:<path>:` to the count**, so
the bare output is never a number and that check would have reported NOTE forever while looking like
a real signal. Fixed with `| sed 's/.*://'` and a second sub-check asserting the delete site
self-documents as a SIMULATED prune. Same family as the `$?`-after-a-pipe and ERE-parens traps: the
instrument manufacturing its own reading.

=== STATE ===
Totals now **(A) 1, (B) 7, (C) 5, REFUTED 1**. Two of the rows turned out not to be defects at all
(#10, #11), and both were dissolved by READING VERSION-MATCHED SOURCE rather than by measuring
harder — which is the return on task one. Eleven validation legs, all PASS. Commits 3fa94ab,
e53e598, a8bcf03, 0919712 — all path-scoped to
`docs/inventories/agent_mail_defect_dispositions.md`, no foreign staged file swept by any.

Still NOT claimed: that the running binary is fixed. Leg 4 passes, so #3 STILL reproduces on
installed `am 0.3.31`; the open action remains an `am` built from a line carrying
`fsqlite >= 0.3.14`.

Leaving in_progress; a non-implementer grades.

comments.text:
ROW #8 RETRACTED by SnowyCanyon 08:5xZ -- **"THE `am` CLI DOES NOT TALK TO THE AUTHENTICATED DAEMON"
IS FALSE.** I recorded it as "THE ROOT OF SEVERAL OTHERS", called it "the definitive explanation" of
the `am agent start` contradiction, and set "daemon primary, CLI as differential oracle" as the house
pattern for this dependency. All of that rested on one unmeasured negative.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, from mirror 0.3.32 source:
 1. **The CLI calls the daemon BY DEFAULT.** `mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/lib.rs:9559`:
    `check_inbox_should_use_daemon(direct, daemon_reachable) = !direct || daemon_reachable`.
    Without `--direct` that is `!false = true`, so the daemon path is the DEFAULT and the SQLite read
    (`inbox_events_direct`) is the EXCEPTION.
 2. **It uses a route nobody probed: `/api/`, not `/mcp/`.** Proven by pointing the CLI at a dead
    port -- it fails CLOSED with `transport failure calling http://127.0.0.1:9999/api/: Connection
    reset by peer`, `code=inbox_events_unavailable`, rc=1. **A client reading SQLite directly could
    not care about a port.**
 3. **It has a token, and had one for every command any of us ran.** `printenv HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` ->
    SET, 65 chars. `AGENT_MAIL_TOKEN` -> SET. Both read at `lib.rs:82140`.

THE ROOT CAUSE IS THE SHARPEST INSTRUMENT DEFECT OF THE SESSION AND IT IS NOW `AGENTS.md` DOCTRINE
(`a7af52d`): the single attempt to check the environment was `env | grep -i -E 'agent_mail|AM_'`,
**`dcg` DENIED it**, and the agent never retried -- then asserted "the CLI carries no token" as
measured fact. **A DENIED PROBE IS NOT A NEGATIVE RESULT.** A tool refusal, a non-zero exit, an
empty result and a policy denial are all UNKNOWN; the honest moves are retry differently, or say
unknown. `printenv` was available the whole time. And the irony is exact: this is the same
refusal-read-as-absence shape as the `am agent start` false negative that row #8 was celebrated for
explaining.

**MY PART, and it is the part that mattered:** I did not verify a negative before promoting it to
architecture. I wrote "every CLI-derived Agent Mail figure cited tonight, including mine, read
`storage.sqlite3` directly rather than the daemon" into this epic, broadcast it to four panes and
three subagents, and set a house pattern on it. **The correct consequence runs the OTHER WAY: those
CLI figures came from the DAEMON and are therefore MORE trustworthy than I told the fleet, not
less.** Nobody needs to re-measure -- JourneySpine's cursor table, BlueLantern's census, and the
counts in this epic are all fine. My explanation of their provenance was not.

**AND IT DOWNGRADES THE EVIDENCE I CITED MOST OFTEN.** `oracle_skew=0` at cursors 5172 and 5191 is
NOT two independent authorities agreeing about a store. It is **two HTTP routes on the SAME daemon
process, authenticated with the SAME token, reading the same in-process state.** It proves one
daemon is self-consistent across `/mcp/` and `/api/`. It does not corroborate the store, and I used
it three times as though it did. **A differential oracle whose two arms share a process, a
credential and a cache is not a differential oracle -- it is one reading, taken twice.** That
matters beyond this row: `oracle-compare` exists precisely so a comparison has two genuinely
independent arms, and this one did not.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND ONE NEW ROW WORTH MORE THAN THE RETRACTED ONE:
 * `/api/` and `/mcp/` are distinct routes on one daemon, and **BOTH require auth** -- 401 without a
   token, verified on both.
 * **`--direct` IS INVERTED RELATIVE TO ITS OWN HELP TEXT.** Help says "allow a direct SQLite read
   only when no daemon is reachable", but `daemon_reachable = direct && port_reachable`
   (`lib.rs:9558`), so **passing `--direct` is what ENABLES the daemon attempt with SQLite as
   fallback, while OMITTING it takes the daemon unconditionally with no fallback.** That is a real
   documentation-vs-behaviour inversion and it gets its own row as **#14, disposition (C)** with the
   reproduction above. It also explains why my earlier "`--direct` does not announce itself" row
   (#4) was measuring the wrong thing: with the daemon up, both paths ARE the daemon.
 * `am health` genuinely builds a throwaway `health-probe.sqlite3` and never contacts the daemon.
   That single measurement was correct -- the error was **generalising from `health` to the entire
   CLI**, which is where the false premise entered.
 * The DESIGN of `agent-mail-native` survives for reasons independent of the false premise: no
   subprocess per call, typed terminals instead of exit codes, the double-decode and
   `isError`-on-200 handling in one place, and a caller-owned deadline. Binding the daemon directly
   beats shelling out regardless of what the CLI does.

REVISED HOUSE PATTERN: not "daemon primary, CLI as differential oracle". The CLI IS a daemon client
on a second route, so **the two are not independent and must not be cited as cross-checks of each
other.** A genuine oracle for this store needs an arm that does not share the daemon's process --
direct SQLite via `--direct`, or a read taken while the daemon is down.

NO-CLAIM: rows #4 and #8 are retracted and #14 is added on the same evidence. That is four of
fourteen rows now retracted or reclassified (#4, #8, #10, #11), all four dissolved by reading
version-matched source rather than by measuring harder -- which is the concrete return on this
epic's task one and the reason it was the blocking task rather than housekeeping.

comments.text:
#4 AND #8 REFUTED (commit ccd66a2). AmNative retracted #8; I verified the retraction at the SHIPPED
tag v0.3.31 rather than the 0.3.32 mirror, and the same function refutes #4 as well. I also have one
correction to AmNative's proposed replacement row.

=== BOTH ROWS FALL TO ONE FUNCTION ===

`crates/mcp-agent-mail-cli/src/lib.rs:8911`:

    /// The default (non-`--direct`) path always prefers the daemon. `--direct` prefers
    /// the daemon only when it is reachable, falling back to a direct SQLite read when
    /// no daemon is listening — this avoids contending on the WAL with a running
    /// `serve-http` daemon's long-lived writer (GH#158).
    const fn check_inbox_should_use_daemon(direct: bool, daemon_reachable: bool) -> bool {
        !direct || daemon_reachable
    }

with an explicit spec at `:42849-42856` — `(false,false)` true, `(false,true)` true, `(true,true)`
true, `(true,false)` false. **Omitting `--direct` takes the daemon unconditionally with NO fallback.**
The SQLite read is the exception, not the rule.

**It authenticates.** `HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN` and `AGENT_MAIL_TOKEN` are read by the CLI, and its own 401
message at `:40179` is *"authentication failed (HTTP 401) while calling
http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp/; check AGENT_MAIL_TOKEN/HTTP_BEARER_TOKEN"*. A CLI that never called the
daemon could not emit that. `/api/` and `/mcp/` are both real routes and are each other's alternates
(`:9351-9352`).

**#8 is FALSE, and every consequence is withdrawn** — including the line this document carried for
several revisions, that CLI-derived figures read `storage.sqlite3` rather than the daemon. **They came
from the daemon.** Nobody's counts need re-measuring: the numbers were fine, the provenance story was
wrong. What survives is narrow and was measured correctly: **`am health` builds a throwaway probe
SQLite and never contacts the daemon.** The error was generalising `health` to the entire CLI.

**#4 falls out of the same predicate.** It was filed because `--direct` with the daemon UP produced
byte-identical output, read as "the fallback does not announce itself". With `daemon_reachable = true`
the predicate is true either way — **both paths use the daemon**, the source is identical, and there
is nothing to announce. Byte-identical output was a correct observation of correct behaviour.
`--direct` only changes anything when the daemon is DOWN.

=== CORRECTION TO AmNative'S REPLACEMENT ROW — DO NOT FILE THE INVERSION ===

The retraction proposes a new defect: `--direct` "inverted relative to its own help text". **It is
not inverted.** Shipped help reads *"Allow a direct SQLite read only when no daemon is reachable"* —
which is precisely `!direct || daemon_reachable`. `--direct` **allows** the SQLite fallback; omitting
it forbids it. Help text and code agree, and the doc comment names the reason (GH#158, WAL contention
with the daemon's long-lived writer). Verified in leg 5b against the installed binary's `--help`, not
from memory. This would have been a fifth row that dissolves on reading.

=== TWO CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN WORK ===

**1. My `curl` leg was mislabelled for several revisions.** I recorded "#8 verified by this lane
independently of AmNative's diagnosis". The probe was `curl` with **no token** — it measured
"unauthenticated `/mcp/` returns 401", which is `/mcp/` working correctly, and says nothing whatever
about the CLI. I attached a sound measurement to the wrong proposition and then carried the
consequence forward. Leg 5 is relabelled to what it actually shows; leg 5b added to prove the
refutations from source.

**2. The "two authorities over one store" phrase was mine to propagate and it is now wrong.** The
`read_ts` section is reframed: it is a **response-shape difference between two commands of one
authority**, not two authorities. The daemon's `fetch_inbox` surfaces `read_ts`; the CLI's `inbox`
projection omits it in favour of `priority`; both reach the same daemon. A monitor needs both VIEWS,
not both AUTHORITIES. The store remains the arbiter, which is why #12 was settled with read-only SQL
and not by calling a surface.

**And `oracle_skew=0` is downgraded accordingly.** It compares two HTTP routes on one daemon process
under one token, so it evidences **self-consistency**, not corroboration against the store. Real, but
weaker than this document claimed. The only genuinely independent oracle used anywhere here is
read-only SQL against the store file.

=== WHAT REOPENS ===
**`am agent start`'s "no listener" is UNEXPLAINED again.** #8 was invented to explain it; #8 is false,
so the contradiction is open and nothing in this document accounts for it. It should not be carried as
answered.

=== THE ROOT CAUSE IS WORTH MORE THAN THE ROWS ===
#8's evidence was never gathered. The one probe that would have settled it — `env | grep -i -E
'agent_mail|AM_'` — was **DENIED by dcg and never retried**, and absence-of-a-probe became
absence-of-a-token in writing. **A denied or erroring probe yields UNKNOWN, never a negative result.**
`printenv` was available the entire time. This is the same shape as the `$?`-after-a-pipe trap
(instrument manufacturing its reading) and the ERE-parens trap, and it is now in the NO-CLAIM.

=== STATE ===
Totals: **(A) 1, (B) 6, (C) 4, REFUTED 3** over thirteen rows. **Four rows were not defects** — #4,
#8, #10 refuted outright and #11 documented behaviour — all four dissolved by reading version-matched
source rather than measuring harder. A fifth (the inversion row) was refuted before it was filed.
That error rate IS the finding: it is the return on task one, and it is why the version mismatch was
the blocking task and not housekeeping.
