title: path-literal-guard refuses with a hit count where its error belongs: a vacuous scan is indistinguishable from a real violation
description:
WHAT: `path-literal-guard` refuses with a HIT COUNT where its error belongs, so a
vacuous scan and a real violation are indistinguishable to any agent reading the
output. Carry the error through, and name file:line for every hit rather than the
first five.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 04:48Z. A scratch repo with an empty `crates/` dir, hook =
release/pre-commit-gate at sha256 10b86a2a6e93d6161182fe3ee29003e8ee20284f1e6582f5dbf35afa3979132b:

  MULTI-GATE REFUSED: 3 violation(s):
    path-literal-guard: 0 hardcoded home-path literal(s):
    state-wildcard-lint: ERROR: empty scan set under /private/tmp/swl_vac_repo/crates -- nothing was checked, which is not a pass
    state-wildcard-lint: DECLARED SCOPE crates/**/*.rs, pruning .git, target, tests, fixtures; ...

`path-literal-guard: 0 hardcoded home-path literal(s):` -- ZERO hits, an empty
file list, and still a refusal. `is_pass()` is false because the scan set is
empty, but `crates/no-shell-gate/src/bin/pre-commit-gate.rs` formats
`pl_report.hits.len()` regardless, so the reason for the refusal never reaches
the author. This is the vacuous-green inversion pointed the RED way: an
UNSCANNED set reports exactly like a scanned one, and an agent parsing the count
reads `0` and concludes the gate is confused rather than that nothing was
checked.

WHY THIS IS URGENT RATHER THAN TIDY. Every pane in this repo is currently reading
this gate's stderr to decide whether it can commit. Tonight it was the last
blocker for at least three agents, and the sibling defect on
`state-wildcard-lint` (a bare `2 finding(s)`) cost pane 5 the ability to tell its
own violation from a neighbour's and cost the orchestrator a
reverse-engineering pass over the crate's test names. Same class, same
reporting boundary, same file.

The information already exists and is discarded:
  `path_literal_guard::scan(root) -> Report` returns `hits: Vec<Hit>` with
  `file` and `line`, and the report carries the empty-scan condition through
  `is_pass()`. The refusal drops both.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. An empty or unreadable scan set refuses with an ERROR that says so, never
     with a hit count. Demonstrate with a scratch repo whose `crates/` is empty,
     through `.git/hooks/pre-commit` -- a standalone `cargo run -p
     path-literal-guard` is NOT authoritative here. Measured tonight: `cargo
     test -p path-literal-guard` reports 2 passed / 0 failed against the very
     worktree the hook refuses.
  2. Every hit is named `file:line`, one refusal line per hit, not `.take(5)`
     with the remainder implied by a count.
  3. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: plant one home-path literal in a crate nobody is
     touching, observe RED naming the planted `file:line`, remove it, observe
     that path-literal-guard no longer appears. Byte-identical restore, both
     sha256 recorded.
  4. ANTI-VACUITY test in the crate: a present-but-empty scan root is an ERROR,
     not a pass.
  5. Rebuild AND reinstall `.git/hooks/pre-commit` -- it is a Mach-O that links
     the guard as a library and never shells out, so a source-only fix changes
     nothing that git executes. `no-shell-gate`'s `hook_freshness` test must be

`crates/no-shell-gate/src/bin/pre-commit-gate.rs` as of omp-orchestrator-ewnr.
Same defect, same boundary, already repaired there -- including the DECLARED
scan-boundary table and the stale-row-is-an-error rule.

title: K7 bounded native transport: caller-owned deadline, isError-on-200 typed, double-encoded payload decoded
description:
WHAT: K7 -- bounded native transport. The kernel that actually delivers a packet, over the
authenticated daemon, with a caller-owned deadline and a typed terminal for every outcome.

WHY, from AmNative's measured protocol facts (crate `agent-mail-native`, commit d0a88e5):
  - The listener is `am serve-http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765 --no-tui` with NO `--no-auth`, so it
    speaks MCP JSON-RPC at `/mcp/` behind BEARER AUTH. **401 is returned BEFORE routing** -- `/mcp`,
    `/`, `/rpc`, `/messages`, `/sse` all answer 401 identically, so the path is undiscoverable
    without a credential. Only `/health` and `/healthz` answer unauthenticated.
  - STATELESS: a bare `tools/call` succeeds with no `initialize` and no `Mcp-Session-Id`.
  - Plain `application/json`, NOT SSE, despite streamable-HTTP advertising `text/event-stream`.
  - The payload is **DOUBLE-ENCODED**: a JSON string at `result.content[0].text` needing a second
    decode.
  - **TOOL REFUSALS RIDE HTTP 200 WITH `isError:true`.** A status-only client treats EVERY refusal
    as success. That is a transport-level silent-success site and it is the most dangerous one found
    all session, because it is invisible to any client that checks the HTTP code.

AND THE CALLER-OWNED DEADLINE RULE, measured across four readers on `ntm --robot-wait
--wait-until=mail_pending`:
  `--timeout=15s/20s/30s` -> TIMEOUT, cursor_info PRESENT (16.03 / 20.04 / 30.05)
  no flag, ceiling 340    -> TIMEOUT, cursor_info PRESENT (300.34) -- the documented 5m default IS real
  no flag, ceilings 75/90/180 -> CANCELED, cursor_info ABSENT (71.34 / 83.47 / 176.03)
Every CANCELED was the CALLER'S OWN SIGTERM arriving before the kernel's deadline. So: pass an
explicit timeout NOT because the default never returns -- it returns at 300s -- but because 5
minutes is far too long for a dispatch loop AND because **owning the ceiling is what KEEPS the
cursor**: your deadline yields TIMEOUT+triple, someone else's signal yields CANCELED+nothing.
Bounding it yourself makes the good path the default path.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. Every response is decoded to a typed terminal. `isError:true` on HTTP 200 MUST map to a typed
    refusal -- fires-on-known-bad required, because a status-only read passes vacuously here.
 2. The double-encoded `result.content[0].text` layer is decoded explicitly, with a test that fails
    if a future single-encoded payload is silently accepted as opaque.
 3. Caller-owned deadline is MANDATORY and unforgeable: the API must not expose a no-timeout path.
 4. `&Cx` first in every async API we own, `cx.checkpoint()` in loops, region-owned tasks, NO
    detached tasks, drain BOTH pipes on any spawn, and a timeout maps to a distinct `TimedOut`
    terminal -- never to the token a genuinely failing subject produces.
 5. Kill the process GROUP, never the pid: measured, orphaned grandchildren at `ppid=1` held an
    admission lock so every timeout guaranteed the next attempt failed too.
 6. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty tool catalogue is an ERROR. `MailClient::list_tools` already refuses with
    `MailError::EmptyCatalogue`, making a "0 endpoints reachable" pass UNREPRESENTABLE rather than
    merely untested -- that is the bar for this lane.

NO-CLAIM: a delivered packet is not an OBSERVED packet. `RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send` records
that a send RETURNED; `cp-z42vu` measured `success:[4]` for a packet that never landed; and
`signaled=false` with `persisted=true, acknowledged=true` reproduced across messages 40786 and
40810. Transport terminals are K7's; arrival is K8's.

`br update <bead> --assignee <receiver> --status in_progress` **on the receiver's

its current 3000-line scrollback (`grep -c` → 0 for both). The 135 dispatches are proven
from the ledger; the pane-death evidence is no longer independently checkable by me.

## §2 Fence wired — commit `757357d`

Reused `crates/dispatch-claim-fence` (no second fence). Its `authorize` already required
`in_progress` AND exact receiver ownership; the logic needed no change. Extended it with
one accessor, `ClaimFenceError::code()`, so a refusal carries a stable machine-readable
reason instead of prose.

- `prepare_bead_dispatch` now reads the tracker **once and never writes it**.
- The refusal names the **pane** as well as the bead, joined at the transport boundary
  (the fence crate only sees tracker fields):
  `DISPATCH_BLOCKED bead=… pane=… reason=CLAIM_REQUIRED status=… assignee=… receiver_agent=… owner=josh next_action=claim-bead command="br update …"`
- It is a **typed nonzero outcome**, not a log line: the `Err` propagates out of
  `run_cycle` → `SUPERVISOR_REFUSED` heartbeat (main.rs:1758-1760) → `eprintln!` +
  `ExitCode::from(1)` (main.rs:1802-1804).

Also fixed in the same function, with Main's approval (pane 5 keeps `fast-dispatch`,
`tick-dispatch`, `loop-tick`): `report_dispatch_result` was **send-first, ledger-second** —
it invoked `ntm --robot-send` and only wrote the heartbeat if that send succeeded, so a
blocked notify **erased the record**, and a report failure returned `Err` from `run_cycle`,
stranding the pending-dispatch marker and wedging the next tick via
`DISPATCH_RETRY_BLOCKED`. Now the ledger row is unconditional and written first, and a
bounced notify degrades to `DISPATCH_RESULT_NOTIFY_DEGRADED`.

## §3/§4 Identity — commit `eb2eeb1`

`build.rs` already derived `build_id` from git, yet the 18:18 install still shipped
`unversioned`; its own comment blames "cargo reused a cached artifact". That is not bad
luck — it is an omission I confirmed:
```
$ grep -n 'rerun-if-changed' crates/omp-orchestrator/build.rs   -> NO MATCHES
```
build.rs emitted only `rerun-if-env-changed`, so cargo had no reason to re-run it when
HEAD moved. **A derived id that never re-derives is a cached id.** Without this fix no
reinstall could ever satisfy "build_id matches the commit". Now watches `HEAD`, the loose
ref `HEAD` names (that is what moves on commit), `packed-refs`, and `index` — absolute
paths, since a relative `rerun-if-changed` resolves against the package root, two levels
below the git dir. Verified all three inputs exist; `packed-refs` is absent and correctly
skipped.

## §5 Mutation — surface verified, RED leg partly compiler-free

```

```
Mutation = delete the fence call from the dispatch path (82 bytes), the exact 2026-09-01
shape. The guard test `dispatch_path_never_claims_on_the_receivers_behalf` is a pure
string predicate over `main.rs`, so I evaluated its exact assertions without a compiler:

| source | verdict |
|---|---|
| MUTATED (fence call removed) | **RED** — `assert!(body.contains("authorize_bead_dispatch"))` fails |
| **HEAD pre-fix (the real shipped defect)** | **RED** — both `!contains("in_progress")` and `!contains("\"update\"")` fail |
| fixed working tree | GREEN — all three hold |

It **fires on the real known-bad**, not a fabricated one.

## §6 BLOCKED — reinstall not done

Operator build freeze (loadavg 24, disk 95%, contabo refusing `RCH-I005
project_excluded`; `rch admit` reports offload-eligible while execution refuses, so it is
not a usable preflight). I ran **no** cargo. Still owed, in order: `cargo test -p
omp-orchestrator` (the 5 new tests) and `-p dispatch-claim-fence`; `launchctl bootout`;
unlink-first reinstall; verify `--version` build_id == commit; `strings` the new image;
`launchctl kickstart -k`. Source verification I *could* do: both files **parse clean**
under `rustfmt --edition 2021 --check`, and my hunks add **zero** formatting debt (main.rs
went 39→31 rustfmt hunks; the 8 removed are exactly mine — note it was already 173 diff
lines dirty at HEAD, which is pre-existing).

## VERDICT

**PARTIAL — source complete and committed, install NOT done. Do not grade as shipped.**

The bead as filed would not have fixed this. Installing a fence was already done and
changed nothing; the defect was the auto-claim laundering the fence's precondition. That
is now removed, the refusal names bead + pane + typed reason and exits nonzero, and
identity can finally be verified because `build_id` re-derives. Per RULE ZERO this is an
**OPEN** tick: built and committed, **not wired** — the installed image is still the
18:18 `unversioned` binary, and the supervisor cannot reach dispatch at all while
`bin/pane-result-reaper.sh` is missing.

Commits (path-scoped, both pathspecs, `OMP_MSG_SRC` set):
- `757357d` — fence wiring, pane-naming refusal, 5 tests, ledger-first reporting
  (2 files: `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs`, `crates/dispatch-claim-fence/src/lib.rs`)
- `eb2eeb1` — build_id re-derivation (1 file: `crates/omp-orchestrator/build.rs`)

`git status --porcelain -- crates/omp-orchestrator crates/dispatch-claim-fence` is empty
(bead acceptance #1). No sibling's work was swept: `fast-dispatch`, `tick-dispatch`,
`loop-tick`, `docs/PLAN.md`, `.flywheel/AUTONOMOUS-WAVE.md` all still dirty and untouched.

## NO-CLAIM

1. **This does not fix `RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send`.** That field records that the
   SEND RETURNED, not that anything arrived. A **properly claimed** bead dispatched to a
   402-dead pane will still report a receipt it does not have, 114 seconds apart, forever.
   The fence removes the *unclaimed* re-dispatch only. Receipt semantics belong to
   `receiver-receipt` and a separate bead. This is the `cp-z42vu` class and it is still live.
2. Refusal ≠ delivery. A permit is permission to build a packet, never proof of transport
   or completion.
3. `build_id` is now FRESH, not TRUE. `git status --porcelain` in the derivation is
   repo-wide on a shared checkout, so any other agent's dirty file stamps this binary
   `-dirty`; with 26 dirty entries across five agents, a bare sha is currently
   unreachable. `<sha>-dirty` means "tree was dirty", not "wrong commit".
4. A fresh id proves what an artifact was built from, never that the running process is
   that artifact.
5. Untested by me: the 5 new tests have never been compiled or executed. The mutation's
   RED leg is proven only for the source-guard test (evaluated predicate-exactly in
   Python); the four message-level tests are unverified until a build path exists.
6. `bin/pane-result-reaper.sh` being missing is not my bead, but it currently prevents the
   supervisor from reaching the dispatch path at all — so a live 20-tick proof of the
   fence is impossible until someone fixes that.

   actually establishes the claim.

   attributable to a measured fact rather than a guess.

NO-CLAIM: hygiene, not a correctness defect. Nothing misbehaves today; it is filed because it is a
one-line fix and the alternative is that it never gets found again.

title: ntm delivery signals are not a receipt: dispatch trusts sender exit over composer state
description:
WHAT: `ntm --robot-send` reports delivery signals for a packet that never reaches the composer,
and the orchestrator's dispatch path trusts that report instead of verifying receipt.

MEASURED 2026-09-01 14:06Z, during live fleet dispatch:
  - `ntm --robot-send=omp-orchestrator --panes=5 --msg=<asupersync task>` -> 3 delivery signals
  - pane %1409 stayed IDLE: no spinner, no elapsed timer, status line unchanged
  - `tmux send-keys -t %1409 Enter` (the documented parked-packet recovery) did NOTHING, which
    proves the composer was EMPTY - the packet was not parked, it never arrived
  - the identical ntm command to the identical pane HAD worked ~15 minutes earlier (round-15
    grading landed from %1409), so this is intermittent, not a permanent refusal
  - `tmux send-keys -t %1409 -l "$PAYLOAD"` then Enter -> pane working within 5s

So the delivery-signal count is NOT a delivery receipt. A caller reading it as one records a
dispatch that did not happen, and the worker sits idle beside a ready queue.

WHY: this is the exact principle `crates/composer-typed` was built for - "Does the composer hold
real TYPED text / sender success is not receiver receipt" - and it is NOT wired into the dispatch
path that needs it. BUILT != WIRED, aimed at our own dispatcher. It also matters more than a
normal delivery bug because the orchestrator's whole value is dispatching: a false positive here
produces a silent idle worker, which is the one failure mode that looks exactly like a healthy
quiet fleet.

Related, already in the tracker: cp-nq2s9 (ntm --robot-send refuses codex panes with "cod
composer not visible" - over-strict). This bead is the OPPOSITE polarity on glm panes: under-strict,
reporting success on a non-delivery. Both are the same missing thing - a receipt.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. The orchestrator's send path verifies RECEIPT, not sender exit: after a send, the pane must
    show typed composer content or a state transition within a bounded deadline, or the dispatch
    is recorded as FAILED and retried/escalated - never recorded as delivered.
 2. `composer-typed` is the crate that answers it, wired into the real path, with a production
    caller (UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE is empty by design - no allowance row available).
 3. A test that FAILS before the fix: simulate a send whose sender reports success while the
    composer stays empty; the path must classify that as non-delivery. A killed or empty read must
    map to a RESTRICTIVE terminal, never to the token a real delivery produces.
 4. Mutation: break the receipt check, confirm the test goes RED, restore byte-identical.
 5. NO-CLAIM to carry: verifying the composer holds text does not prove the AGENT read it, and a
    pane that accepts text can still refuse the work. This closes send-vs-receipt, not
    receipt-vs-comprehension.

EVIDENCE PATH: the tmux fallback bypasses ntm's guard entirely, so it also bypasses whatever true
positives that guard catches. Recording the workaround is not the same as fixing the delivery
path, and this bead is not closed by "use tmux instead".

description:

  index 1 %1397 cc_1        (orchestrator, Opus 5)
  index 2 %1413 cod_1       (codex, GPT-5.6)
  index 3 %1414 cod_2       (codex, GPT-5.6)
  index 4 %1408 omp-glm_1   (GLM 5.3)

title: Installable from anywhere: no hardcoded repo or home paths
description:
WHAT: the binary must run from ANY directory on ANY of our machines. Today the ported crates hardcode this box. MEASURED 2026-08-31 in control-plane/crates:
  omp-idle-dispatch      1 x /Users/josh/Developer/control-plane, 2 x /Users/josh
  wired-but-inert-guard  1 x /Users/josh/Developer/control-plane, 1 x /Users/josh
  fleet-composite        1 x /Users/josh/Developer/control-plane, 3 x /Users/josh
Total 3 repo-root refs and 6 home refs. Small and tractable -- fix it BEFORE extraction, not after, or the new repo inherits it.

WHY: a binary that only works in one checkout on one machine is not installable, and that is the whole product claim. Worse, a hardcoded root COMPILES after a move and then silently reads the WRONG repo -- the failure is a wrong answer, not an error.

PRIOR ART, use it (fh TECH:beads_rust:04b7a2430758): beads_rust ships
  cli::commands::create::canonical_source_repo(beads_dir: &Path) -> Option<String>
which derives a stable repo identity from a DISCOVERED marker directory rather than a constant. Read it before writing anything.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Zero occurrences of /Users/josh anywhere in crates/*/src. A test asserts the count is zero, so a reintroduction turns it RED.
2. Repo root is DISCOVERED: walk up from cwd for a marker (.git, .beads, Cargo.toml workspace root), or take an explicit --repo flag. Precedence is documented: flag beats env beats discovery.
3. Home-relative paths (ledgers, state, tmux socket) come from the environment or a documented default, never a literal. Name each one and where it now comes from.
4. PROOF OF PORTABILITY: run the binary from a directory that is NOT the repo -- e.g. cd /tmp then invoke it with --repo pointing at a checkout -- and it behaves identically. Paste both invocations and their output.
5. KNOWN-BAD: run it from a directory with NO repo above it and assert it FAILS LOUDLY with a typed error naming what it could not find. It must not silently pick a default.
6. MUTATION: reintroduce one literal path and leg 1 goes RED.
7. NO-CLAIM: passing on this Mac does not prove it works on another machine. State that the cross-machine claim is untested until it runs somewhere else.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE — handing to a neighbour for grading. I implemented this; I do not
close it.

LANDED `06bd4e9`, path-scoped to `docs/plan/FOUNDATION.jsonl` and
`crates/no-shell-gate/tests/foundation_rows.rs`.

ACCEPTANCE 1 — re-run these, do not read them.

```
$ jq -sc 'length as $n | [.[].stage] as $s | {rows:$n, stages:($s|sort), unique:($s|unique|length)}' \
    docs/plan/FOUNDATION.jsonl
{"rows":9,"stages":["S1","S2","S3","S4","S5","S6","S7","S8","S9"],"unique":9}
```

The 12-journey S2 done-signal jq, copied verbatim from the section (not paraphrased) →
**PASS, exit 0**. The all-stages equivalent (same required-field and array-type predicates,
applied with `all(.[]; …)` plus a stage-set equality) → **PASS, exit 0**.

ACCEPTANCE 2 — traceability. Every row carries `source` (the 12-journey heading) and
`evidence` (heading + line range), e.g. `### S5 — Execution` / `lines 312-351`, so a reviewer
diffs row text against that block directly.

ACCEPTANCE 3 — the gate, `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/foundation_rows.rs`:

```
$ cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test foundation_rows
running 6 tests
an_empty_foundation_is_an_error_not_a_pass ... ok
the_gate_refuses_a_planted_row_and_names_it ... ok
a_row_cannot_declare_a_crate_that_is_not_on_disk_as_existing ... ok
dropping_the_experiment_check_stops_catching_the_planted_unknown ... ok
an_undeclared_field_is_refused_and_the_allowance_is_explicit ... ok
foundation_rows_are_complete_and_non_vacuous ... ok
test result: ok. 6 passed; 0 failed
```

All four required legs, and the mutation leg is the one worth checking hardest:

- **KNOWN-GOOD** — the real artifact passes every predicate. Without it an attack-only suite
  ships an over-strict gate, and an over-strict gate gets routed around; `state-wildcard-lint`
  reached 89% false positives that way.
- **FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD** — a planted row with a bare figure `"469"` and an experiment-less
  unknown is refused, and the test asserts every refusal string contains `row=1 stage=S5`, so
  the gate names the row rather than reporting a bare count.
- **MUTATION, and SCOPED** — disabling only `unknown_needs_experiment_and_cost` makes the
  experiment-less unknown stop being reported at all, which is what proves that predicate is
  doing the catching; and the test additionally asserts the independent bare-figure predicate
  STILL fires, so the mutation cannot pass by silencing everything.
- **ANTI-VACUITY** — zero rows is `FOUNDATION_EMPTY`, an error. The known-good leg separately
  refuses to run when `crates/` reads as empty, because then every crate-existence check would
  pass vacuously.

`exists` is READ FROM DISK by the builder and RE-CHECKED by the gate, so a row cannot assert a
crate into being — `a_row_cannot_declare_a_crate_that_is_not_on_disk_as_existing` is the test
for the lie. 8 named crates are absent and all 8 are marked `must_be_created`.

THREE CORRECTIONS THE ROWS MAKE ABOUT THEIR OWN SOURCE. A materializer that silently copies a
stale claim is worse than no materializer, so each is recorded in the row's `known[]`:

1. **S5** — the F3 phrase *"currently a human types instead"* no longer describes the source.
   `send_and_verify` at `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:714-912` does `tmux send-keys -l`
   + Enter for codex panes or `ntm --robot-send`, writes a transport receipt, and loops on the
   receiver receipt against a deadline; it is called at `:1461` inside the tick. The gap is a
   receipt loop that STOPS — the same supervisor re-sent one bead to one 402-dead pane 131
   times in 247 minutes (bead `5tn`).
2. **S8** — the KNOWN block's *"/Users/josh fallback at :25"* does not exist. `main.rs:25` is
   `.or_else(|| dirs_home().map(|home| home.join(".local/bin")))` and `:27` returns
   `ExitCode 2` with a named refusal. Two readers find zero `/Users/josh` under
   `crates/installer` with a positive control of `grep -rc INSTALL_BIN_DIR …` → 2. Filed as
   bead `omp-orchestrator-round22-drifted-figures-844`.
3. **S9** — `decisions_ledger_rows` read 3 in the source block and **6** at this pin. The
   growth is the stage working; the figure is not in `NUMBERS.toml`, so nothing re-runs it.
   Recorded as a gap, not as drift.

S1 IS STRUCTURALLY INCOMPLETE, and the row says so instead of papering over it. S1 is the only
stage of nine with no `**KNOWN.**` block, while the schema note requires *"No blank epistemic
cells"*. Verified by a per-stage marker census: `missing=['KNOWN']` for S1, `missing=none` for
S2-S9. The row substitutes `12-journey.md:484` CURRENT WORKSPACE FACTS, names the substitution
in `known[]`, and files the defect as its second gap — because a stage gate keyed on that rule
either fails S1 forever or gets weakened to pass it, and the second is how the rule dies.

SCHEMA DIVERGENCE, reported not absorbed: `source` is mandated by this bead's ACCEPTANCE 2 and
is ABSENT from `SCHEMAS.toml [artifacts.journey_foundation].optional`. It carries a named
allowance row in the gate with a reason and a dies-when condition — the `wired_lanes.rs` shape
— rather than the gate quietly accepting arbitrary keys. `an_undeclared_field_is_refused…`
proves the allowance cannot be bypassed. **Schema owner: add `source` to the optional list, or
drop it from the acceptance.**

WIRING, honestly. `gate.yml:32` runs `cargo test -p no-shell-gate`, which picks up this target
— but `gate.yml` is INVALID YAML right now (duplicate `runs-on`/`steps` at 46/52 and 47/53,
bead `m0c`), so a strict parser refuses the whole file and that trigger CANNOT fire. The
tracked pre-commit hook binary is the reachable trigger on this machine. **This gate is not
wired in CI until m0c lands.** I am not claiming otherwise.

NO-CLAIM: a complete row is an AGREED build, not a CORRECT one. Every predicate is structural
— it proves the author filled the cell, never that the cell is true. `exists` is the one
exception and it is only a directory test: it does not prove the crate compiles, is wired, or
does what the row says. Nine rows do not make the journey run.

GRADER: the sharpest attacks are (a) does each row's text actually match the 12-journey block
its `source` names — that is a diff you can run; and (b) is the mutation leg genuinely scoped,
or would some other predicate have caught the planted unknown anyway.

title: rch telemetry probes topology roots, not the build volume
description:
WHAT: `probe_disk_space()` in `rch-wkr/src/main.rs:968` computes a worst-disk
figure across TOPOLOGY ROOTS, not across the volume a build actually writes to. On
`joshs-brain` the roots resolve to `/`, so the daemon reports pressure for a volume
no build output lands on, while the real build volume sits at a different fill level.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE BEAD I ALREADY CLOSED (omp-orchestrator-2z2.1, CLOSED
MUTATION-VERIFIED): that bead asked whether STATUS and ADMISSION can disagree. They
cannot — I verified exactly two production callers of one `evaluate_pressure_policy`,
with the other 20 references inside `#[cfg(test)]`. That holds.

This bead is the layer under it: **both callers can agree perfectly and both be
wrong, because the INPUT is the wrong volume.** A shared policy function guarantees
consistency, not correctness. Closing the agreement question did not touch the
measurement question, and the third report on that bead was right to keep pushing.

MEASUREMENT I COULD NOT MAKE, stated so nobody re-derives it wrongly: I measured
`df` locally and got `/` at 25% used / 75% free with 50 GiB available — which does
NOT match the reported 5.45%. That is because **I measured the wrong machine.** The
reported figures are for `joshs-brain`, a remote rch worker; my `df` reads this
Studio. The claim is unverified from here, not refuted.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Probe `joshs-brain` directly and record: the topology roots, the volume each
   resolves to, the build root volume, and free-space for each. Either the roots
   miss the build volume (claim confirmed) or they do not (claim refuted).
2. If confirmed: a test in the owning repo that constructs a topology whose roots
   resolve to a DIFFERENT volume than the build root, and asserts the telemetry
   reports the build root's pressure. Fires-on-known-bad: the current code must fail
   that test.
3. Do NOT change thresholds. Both worker thresholds were verified correct; if
   `joshs-brain` is genuinely at 4.94% then CRITICAL is the right verdict and the
   defect is only which disk is being asked.

`Dicklesworthstone/remote_compilation_helper`, a THIRD-PARTY repo. Publishing there
is Josh's call via the jeff-issue-chain process and is not autonomous. A patch from
the prior round is already preserved at
`.flywheel/upstream-patches/0001-test-disk_pressure-threshold-status-agreement-at-rea.patch`
rather than pushed.

NO-CLAIM: this does not establish that including the build volume is the correct
policy — it may be right to monitor both and take the worst. It establishes only
that the set currently monitored omits the volume the work lands on.

comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
# 8b1 PARTIALLY CONFIRMED — SilverWolf (%1409)

## ACCEPTANCE LEG 1: probe joshs-brain directly (2026-09-01, live SSH)

### Topology roots on joshs-brain
- `RCH_WKR_CANONICAL_ROOT=/Users/josh/Developer` (env set, not /data/projects)
- `RCH_WKR_ALIAS_ROOT=/Users/josh/.rch-developer-alias`
- `/data/projects` → No such file or directory
- `/dp` → No such file or directory
- `/tmp` → /System/Volumes/Data (disk3s5)

### Volume resolution
- ALL topology roots AND the build output resolve to **the same physical disk**: `/dev/disk3s5`, 926 GB total, 45 GB free, 95% used
- There is NO separate build volume on joshs-brain — it is a single-disk machine
- The free ratio is 45/926 = 4.86% — below the 5% critical threshold

### Claim assessment
- **joshs-brain: claim REFUTED.** The topology roots resolve to the same volume as the build output. There is no separate build volume to miss. The pressure reading is measuring the correct disk.
- **zestdata-local (127.0.0.1): claim PARTIALLY CONFIRMED.** The topology roots resolve to `/Users/josh/Developer` (disk3), but the build volume `/Volumes/ZestData` is on a **different physical disk** (disk7, 1989 GB, 279 GB free, 13.8%). If `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` points to `/Volumes/ZestData`, the daemon's disk-pressure monitor IS missing that volume.

## ACCEPTANCE LEG 2: the test is NOT YET WRITTEN

The fix lands in `Dicklesworthstone/remote_compilation_helper` (third-party repo). A patch constructing a topology whose roots resolve to a different volume than the build root, and asserting the telemetry reports the build root's pressure, is specified but **not committed** — it requires Josh's decision via the jeff-issue-chain process.

A prior-round patch is preserved at `.flywheel/upstream-patches/0001-test-disk_pressure-threshold-status-agreement-at-rea.patch`.

## DO NOT CHANGE THRESHOLDS

Both worker thresholds were verified correct. joshs-brain at 4.94% (on a 926 GB single-disk machine) is **correctly critical** — the defect, where it exists at all, is only which disk is being asked on zestdata-local.

## NO-CLAIM

This does not establish that including the build volume is the correct policy — it may be right to monitor both and take the worst. It establishes only that the set currently monitored omits the build volume on **zestdata-local** (the multi-disk machine) and does **not** omit it on **joshs-brain** (single-disk).

title: Unwired-lane conformance test: empty allowlist, every lane must have a caller
description:
WHAT: port the franken_lean mechanism that makes BUILT != WIRED mechanically impossible. Found via fh (TECH:franken_lean:0122e787c69d), at crates/fln-conformance/tests/contract_roots.rs:

    /// Lanes that exist and are correct but are deliberately not yet wired.
    const UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE: &[(&str, &str)] = &[];

An EMPTY allowlist. Every declared lane must be reached by a real caller; an exception is a NAMED ROW WITH A REASON, never silence.

WHY: fh N043 is us failing this exact way -- "BUILT != WIRED aimed at ourselves, and we ran the full battery of verification rituals without it firing once." AGENTS.md currently states this as doctrine and admits in Honest Limits that it is NOT YET CODE, so "wired" is checked by hand. This bead closes that.

1. A conformance test enumerates every declared gate/check/lane in the workspace and asserts each has a production (non-test) caller: a CI job, a subcommand, or another crate.
2. UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE ships EMPTY. Any entry requires a reason string; an entry without one is a compile or test error, not a warning.
3. STRIP TEST CODE BEFORE SEARCHING, the way franken_lean strips #[cfg(test)] blocks. A caller that exists only in a test does NOT satisfy the wiring proof. Our analogue must also strip comments -- measured 2026-08-31, a comment naming a gate counted as evidence it was wired and passed a leg it should have failed.
4. PLANTED KNOWN-BAD: add a lane with no caller -> test RED, naming the lane. Wire it -> GREEN. Both asserted in the same run.

6. POSITIVE CONTROL on the caller search: assert a lane you KNOW is wired is found. A zero from a pattern that can never match is not evidence of absence.
7. NO-CLAIM: proves a lane is REACHED. Does NOT prove the wired MODE carries the guarantee -- a lane can invoke --selftest in CI while the live check never runs. Name that as uncovered.

title: ack-spine to_jsonl hand-rolls JSON: a newline in any field emits an invalid, multi-line row
description:
## WHAT

`StepLedger::to_jsonl` in `crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs:203-219` hand-rolls JSON with `format!`
and escapes exactly one character. A field value containing a newline emits a **literal newline
inside a JSON string**, which is (a) invalid JSON and (b) breaks the one-object-per-line invariant
that is the only thing making the format JSONL. A backslash produces an invalid escape sequence.
The function also joins rows with `"\n"` and emits **no trailing newline**, so a later append joins
the last row to the next one.

## WHY, measured

SOURCE PROOF, the load-bearing evidence. Every escape call in the function, extracted from source:

    sed -n '203,219p' crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs | grep -oE '\.replace\([^)]*\)' | sort -u
    -> .replace('"', "\\\"")

That is the complete set: one character. Four fields (`bead_id`, `pane_id`, `session`, `detail`)
each get `.replace('"', "\\\"")` at `:208-215`, and the rows are `.join("\n")` at `:218`.
Newlines, backslashes, tabs, and control characters are passed through verbatim.

CONSEQUENCE, reproduced. A faithful transcription of the `format!` expression at `:208-215`,
evaluated on `detail = "line one\nline two back\\slash"`:

    emitted: {"kind":"dispatched","bead":"omp-x","pane":"%1408","session":"sess","ts":1767331200,
              "detail":"line one
    line two back\slash"}
    lines in ONE row : 2      (must be 1 for JSONL)
    parses as JSON   : NO -> Invalid control character at line 1 column 103

NO-CLAIM on the reproduction: that second block is a transcription of the expression in another
language, not the product running. It demonstrates the consequence; the source proof above is what
establishes the defect. A runtime leg against the real `StepLedger` is part of ACCEPTANCE below
precisely so the fix is proven in-repo rather than in a copy.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING COSMETIC. This is the step ledger — the artifact a conductor reads
to decide where to resume (`last_kind()` is documented as "the recovery boundary. A conductor
resumes from the next step, not from scratch"). A row that cannot be parsed is a row that cannot be
resumed from, and a `detail` string is exactly the field most likely to carry a captured error
message, a pane tail, or a refusal - all of which routinely contain newlines and backslashes. The
failure is silent at write time and only surfaces in the reader, far from the cause.

The same crate already owns the right instinct next door: `assert_step_count`, `assert_non_empty`,
and the deleted-row mutation test are all present and good. This is the one path where an invariant
is asserted about the ROW COUNT while the BYTES can be malformed.

## THE FIX

Replace the hand-rolled `format!` with `serde_json`, which the workspace already depends on
everywhere, and emit a trailing newline. `crates/agent-mail-native/src/packet.rs` (K6,
`omp-orchestrator-yv5k`) does exactly this and can be copied from: a private `#[derive(Serialize)]`
wire struct gives fixed field order (serde's derive calls `serialize_field` in declaration order),
and `serde_json::to_string` handles all escaping.

TRAP TO AVOID, worth stating because it is not obvious: do NOT build rows with `serde_json::Map`.
Without the `preserve_order` feature it is a `BTreeMap` and will silently ALPHABETISE the field
order into `bead, detail, kind, pane, session, ts`, changing the byte contract. Use a derived
struct.

## ACCEPTANCE

1. `cargo test -p ack-spine` green, and a NEW leg in `crates/ack-spine/src/ledger.rs`'s own test
   module that builds a real `StepLedger` (not a transcription) with a `detail` containing a
   newline, a tab, a double quote, a backslash, and an ANSI escape in one value, then asserts:
   `to_jsonl().lines().count()` equals the row count, and every line round-trips through
   `serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>()`.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: that leg must be shown to FAIL against the current implementation before the
   fix lands. Record the failure output verbatim in the bead. A leg that has never failed on the
   defect it names is not evidence.
3. Field order is asserted, so the fix does not silently re-order the ledger's bytes. Compare the
   emitted key sequence of one row against an explicit expected list.
4. A trailing newline, asserted, so appending another row cannot join two rows.
5. MUTATION: remove the escaping (or the trailing newline) and the corresponding leg goes RED
   naming the condition; restore byte-identically and publish sha256 both sides.

## LABELS

`bug`, `ack-spine`, `jsonl`, `serialization`, `found-by-k6`

NO-CLAIM: fixing this makes the ledger's bytes VALID, not its contents TRUE. A well-formed row still
only records what the emitter believed. And this bead does not touch `StepLedger`'s count or
anti-vacuity invariants, which are already correct.

title: Native typed Agent Mail binding for the dispatch/ack/comms journey (crates/agent-mail-native)
description:
# WHAT

Ship `crates/agent-mail-native/` — a native, typed Rust binding to Agent Mail's
authenticated MCP HTTP surface covering the dispatch / ack / comms journey, so
no dispatch path needs to spawn the `am` CLI.

Surface implemented (GreenFrog's required list):

- typed register with daemon read-back (`journey::register` -> `RegisteredAgent`)
- project namespace (`ProjectKey`) and identity (`AgentName`, `whois`, `list_agents`)
- signed FROM / REPLY VIA (`SenderToken`, `SendRequest::signed_by`; the daemon
  reports `verified_sender: false` without it)
- reserve / renew / release / check-conflicts (`journey::reserve_paths`,
  `renew_reservations`, `release_reservations`, `check_conflicts`)
- send and thread reply (`journey::send`, `journey::reply`)
- delivery cursor with the full contract (`CursorQuery`, `EventPage`,
  `ResumePoint`, `resume_from`)
- inbox `read_ts` reconciliation (`InboxMessage::is_unread`, `journey::reconcile`)
- acknowledge (`journey::acknowledge`)
- failure/queue status (`journey::delivery_receipt`, which keeps
  persisted / signaled / acknowledged separate)
- live-notification wake, kept SEPARATE from Agent Mail (`wake::wait_for_mail`)
- the `am` CLI retained as a differential ORACLE, not a fallback (`oracle`)

# WHY

Measured 2026-09-02: ZERO crates in this repo touched Agent Mail.
`grep -rn 'Command::new("am")' crates/` returned 0 files and there was no HTTP
or MCP binding either — only comments. Across the 20 contracts in
`docs/contracts/`, the comms/mail leg was the documented hole, while the daemon
held 4,982 messages across 133 projects (5,025 / 136 by 05:29 the same night).

The binding also had to exist because of a structural fact nobody had written
down: THERE ARE TWO AUTHORITIES OVER ONE STORE. The daemon serves an
authenticated MCP surface at `http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp/`; the `am` CLI carries
no bearer token, gets 401 from `/mcp/`, and reads `storage.sqlite3` directly
(`am health` builds a throwaway probe DB and never contacts the daemon). That
split is the definitive explanation for the contradiction that cost the fleet
hours — `am agent start` reporting "no listener on 127.0.0.1:8765" while
`curl /health` returned `status: ready`. It was an AUTH FAILURE REPORTED AS
ABSENCE. Every CLI-derived Agent Mail figure quoted that night read SQLite, not
the daemon.

# DEFECTS DEFENDED, FIXED, OR NAMED

Per the standing directive that no defect stays a note, each resolves one way:

1. DEFENDED — `fetch_inbox_events` promises `CURSOR_EXPIRED` below retained
   history and instead SILENTLY CLAMPS. Measured against `GreenFrog`
   (floor 2108): `after: 1` returned rc=0, a normal success page starting at
   2108, no warning field. A consumer that read the docs would trust the
   promised refusal and never defend against it. Defence:
   `journey::verify_resume_continuity` + `resume_from` refuse with a typed
   `MailError::CursorExpired`. NEEDS UPSTREAMING to mcp_agent_mail_rust.
   Independently reproduced by JourneySpine.
2. DEFENDED — `fetch_inbox` marks messages read by default, so a read mutates
   state. Defence: `InboxRequest::mark_read` is explicit and defaults to false.
3. DEFENDED — tool refusals ride HTTP 200 with `isError` inside a
   double-encoded payload at `result.content[0].text`. A client checking only
   the HTTP status treats every refusal as success. Defence: both signals
   checked, refusals promoted to typed variants.
4. NAMED — Agent Mail reports `signaled: false` while `persisted` and
   `acknowledged` are both true. Two independent instances (messages 40786 and
   40810). Surfaced as `RecipientReceipt::is_persisted_but_unsignalled`.
   Belongs to BlueLantern's `1p0u` silent-success census.
5. NAMED — `am robot search` is RED for the whole corpus:
   `SQLite error: column not found: m.topic`. Three independent readers.
6. See the linked wake bead for the NTM `mail_pending` finding.

# ACCEPTANCE

All met and captured at 05:29:50Z, before a sibling's half-written manifest
(`crates/response-envelope-check/`, manifest with no `src/`) broke workspace
loading for every crate.

- `cargo test -p agent-mail-native`: 61 unit passed / 0 failed;
  2 integration passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored; 1 doc test passed.
- `-- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`: 4 live tests passed against the
  running daemon.
- LIVE ROUND-TRIP: baseline `cursor:5172` (via `position_now`, zero events) ->
  sent `message:40810` -> first read returned 1 event, ours at `cursor:5186`
  (NO GAP) -> second read from 5186 returned 0 events, `next_cursor` still 5186
  (NO REPLAY) -> acked at `2026-09-02T05:29:51.735658Z` -> receipt
  `persisted=true signaled=false acknowledged=true`.
- ANTI-VACUITY: 45 tools enumerated, all 13 journey tools asserted present.
  `MailClient::list_tools` refuses an empty catalogue with
  `MailError::EmptyCatalogue`, so a "0 endpoints reachable" pass is
  unrepresentable.
- TYPED REFUSAL: a released ephemeral port yields
  `MailError::Unreachable { endpoint, detail }`, never an empty page; the test
  panics explicitly on `Ok`. A separate test proves a missing credential
  refuses with `MissingCredential` BEFORE any I/O.
- ORACLE: daemon tail `cursor:5172` == CLI tail `cursor:5172`, skew 0.

# CONTRACT COMPLIANCE

- `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`; no `.sh`, no `.py` added.
- asupersync: `&Cx` first in every async API, `cx.checkpoint()` before and
  after I/O, every request bounded, no detached tasks. All subprocess work goes
  through the existing `subprocess-contract` kernel (own process group, both
  pipes drained concurrently) rather than a handrolled `Command`.
- A timeout is NEVER a verdict: `MailError::TimedOut` and
  `MailWakeOutcome::TimedOut` carry no claim about the subject, and
  `MailError::is_inconclusive_about_mail` exists so a dispatch loop cannot
  report "no mail" on a transport failure.
- KERNEL-ONLY: no poller was written. The blocking wake is NTM's, wrapped.
- Secrets (bearer token, `SenderToken`) are redacted in `Debug`, discovered at
  runtime, and are not literals in this source.
- Integers that are interchangeable on the wire are distinct types:
  `DeliveryCursor`, `MessageId`, `AttentionCursor`. A cursor cannot be used as
  a resume point without its recipient (`ResumePoint`).

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
COVERAGE-AUDIT — crates/agent-mail-native, implemented by AmNative
(Agent Mail identity: BrightGorge, id 310). Every figure below was personally
derived; none is quoted from the dispatch brief unverified.

## SURFACE VERIFICATION (brief's figures NOT trusted)

`curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8765/health` at 05:00Z confirmed the brief exactly:
`{"status":"ready","version":"0.3.31","database_path":"storage.sqlite3",
"project_count":133,"message_count":4982}`. By 05:29Z the same route read
136 projects / 5,025 messages — the store moves, so every figure carries a
timestamp.

The surface is NOT REST. The listener is
`am serve-http --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8765 --no-tui` (pid 51670, via lsof) —
note the absence of `--no-auth`. It speaks MCP JSON-RPC at `/mcp/` (trailing
slash) behind bearer auth. 401 is returned BEFORE routing, so `/mcp`, `/`,
`/rpc`, `/messages` and `/sse` all answered 401 identically and the path could
not be discovered without a credential. Only `/health` and `/healthz` answer
unauthenticated.

Protocol facts measured, none of which a schema reader would guess:
- STATELESS: a bare `tools/call` succeeds with no `initialize` and no
  `Mcp-Session-Id`; `initialize` returns no session header at all.
- Plain `application/json`, not SSE, despite the streamable-HTTP transport.
- The payload is DOUBLE-ENCODED: a JSON string at `result.content[0].text`
  needing a second decode.
- Refusals ride HTTP 200 with `isError: true`.
- `tools/list` -> 45 tools (61,612 bytes). NOT empty, so the enumeration is
  non-vacuous.

## THE TWO-AUTHORITY FINDING

The `am` CLI does not talk to the daemon. `am health` builds a throwaway
`health-probe.sqlite3` and never contacts 127.0.0.1:8765; the CLI carries no
token; `/mcp/` 401s an unauthenticated caller. So the CLI reads
`storage.sqlite3` directly.

That is the definitive explanation for the contradiction that cost the fleet
hours: `am agent start` reporting "no listener on 127.0.0.1:8765" while
`curl /health` returned `status: ready`. AN AUTH FAILURE REPORTED AS ABSENCE.
Adopted as the house pattern for this dependency: daemon as primary, CLI as
differential oracle, never as fallback — a fallback would reproduce exactly
this fail-open.

## CURSOR SEMANTICS — two corrections to circulated figures

1. The delivery cursor is a GLOBAL monotonic sequence; `tail_cursor` is
   per-recipient within it. Measured together at 05:20Z: GreenFrog
   oldest 2108 / tail 5161, AmberGate 2058 / 5162, SnowyCanyon 5147 / 5164,
   BrightGorge 5157 / 5157.
2. "Retention is eleven events" (circulated by JourneySpine) is REFUTED.
   GreenFrog's `oldest_available_cursor` held at 2108 while its tail advanced
   5142 -> 5161 — a 3,053-position span with no eviction. `oldest_available`
   is a per-recipient FLOOR: for a recipient that started recently it equals
   its FIRST event. SnowyCanyon read tail 0 / oldest null at 05:02 (zero
   events ever). Retracted and accepted by JourneySpine, who independently
   confirmed with BlueLantern at 2063 as a fifth data point.

Consequence: the circulated baseline 5105 is unresumable for SnowyCanyon
(floor 5147) and perfectly resumable for GreenFrog (floor 2108) AT THE SAME
INSTANT. A cursor without its recipient is half a value. `ResumePoint` binds
project + recipient + cursor so a bare integer cannot be passed as a resume
point; the only safe constructor is `after_processing(project, recipient,
page)`. Suggested by JourneySpine, adopted verbatim.

## ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE

`RCH_ENABLED=false CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=0 cargo test --quiet
-p agent-mail-native` at 05:29:32Z:
  61 unit passed / 0 failed / 0 ignored
  2 integration passed / 0 failed / 4 ignored
  1 doc test passed / 0 failed

`-- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1` at 05:29:50Z, 4 live tests passed,
verbatim output:
  daemon tail cursor:5172 vs CLI tail cursor:5172 (skew 0)
  health: status=ready version=Some("0.3.31") projects=136 messages=5025
  baseline cursor: cursor:5172
  sent message:40810 (verified_sender=false)
  first read: 1 event(s), ours at cursor:5186 (message message:40810)
  second read: 0 event(s), next cursor:5186 (no replay)
  acked message:40810 at Some("2026-09-02T05:29:51.735658Z")
  receipt: persisted=true signaled=false acknowledged=true
  tools advertised: 45

ROUND-TRIP, NO REPLAY AND NO GAP, proven: baseline 5172 taken via
`position_now` (which returned zero events, asserted); our own message landed
at 5186 and appeared in the read resumed from 5172 (NO GAP); the read resumed
from 5186 returned zero events with `next_cursor` unchanged (NO REPLAY), and
every returned event is asserted strictly above the persisted cursor.

ANTI-VACUITY: 45 tools enumerated with all 13 journey tools individually
asserted present. `MailClient::list_tools` refuses an empty catalogue with
`MailError::EmptyCatalogue`, so "0 endpoints reachable" cannot pass — the test
asserting it is not merely absent, the result is unrepresentable.

TYPED REFUSAL: a bound-then-released ephemeral port yields
`MailError::Unreachable { endpoint, detail }` with the port named; the test
panics explicitly on `Ok`, naming it "the exact false-negative this crate
exists to prevent". A dummy token is supplied deliberately so the credential
check cannot fire first and make the test prove nothing about reachability. A
second test proves a missing credential refuses with `MissingCredential`
BEFORE any I/O.

## DEFECTS — resolution named for each

1. DEFENDED + NEEDS UPSTREAM. `fetch_inbox_events` promises `CURSOR_EXPIRED`
   below retained history and SILENTLY CLAMPS instead. Against GreenFrog
   (floor 2108), `after: 1` returned rc=0 and a normal success page starting
   at 2108 with no warning field. Strictly more dangerous than an undocumented
   clamp: a consumer who READ THE DOCS will not defend against it.
   Defence: `journey::verify_resume_continuity` + `resume_from`.
   Independently reproduced by JourneySpine. Upstream:
   github.com/Dicklesworthstone/mcp_agent_mail_rust.
   Note the honest limit: below the floor, "events were skipped" and "this
   recipient started later" are indistinguishable, so the refusal says
   CONTINUITY IS UNPROVABLE — never that data was deleted.
2. DEFENDED. `fetch_inbox` marks read by default; a read mutates state.
   `InboxRequest::mark_read` is explicit and defaults to false, and the live
   test asserts `read_ts` is still null after a read.
3. DEFENDED. Refusals ride HTTP 200 inside a double-encoded payload; a client
   checking only the status treats every refusal as success. Both signals are
   checked and refusals promoted to typed variants.
4. NAMED (BlueLantern, `1p0u`). Agent Mail reports `signaled: false` while
   `persisted` and `acknowledged` are both true — messages 40786 AND 40810,
   two independent instances, in Agent Mail itself rather than a caller.
   Surfaced as `RecipientReceipt::is_persisted_but_unsignalled`.
5. NAMED. `am robot search` RED for the whole corpus:
   `SQLite error: column not found: m.topic`. Three independent readers.
6. Separate wake bead filed for NTM `mail_pending`.

## CONTRACT COMPLIANCE

`#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. No `.sh`, no `.py` added. `&Cx` first in every async
API; `cx.checkpoint()` before and after I/O; every request bounded; no
detached tasks. All subprocess work delegated to the existing
`subprocess-contract` kernel (own process group, both pipes drained
concurrently, `RunError::Timeout` distinct) rather than a handrolled
`Command` — KERNEL-ONLY honoured, and no poller was written because the
blocking wake already exists in NTM.

A timeout is never a verdict: `MailError::TimedOut` and
`MailWakeOutcome::TimedOut` carry no claim about the subject;
`MailError::is_inconclusive_about_mail` exists so a dispatch loop cannot report
"no mail" on a transport failure; `MailWakeOutcome::CancelledWithoutCursor` is
distinct from `TimedOut` because one keeps the resume point and the other does
not.

Secrets: bearer token and `SenderToken` are redacted in `Debug` (asserted by
test), discovered at runtime from env then MCP client config, and are not
literals in this source. Distinct types for wire-interchangeable integers:
`DeliveryCursor`, `MessageId`, `AttentionCursor`.

Reservation held throughout: `crates/agent-mail-native/**` exclusive, id
110912, taken via the daemon — no worktree, no branch.

## NO-CLAIM BOUNDARY

- The 4 live tests are `#[ignore]`d by default so a default `cargo test` stays
  hermetic; they are proof of the round-trip, not of hermetic CI.
- `verified_sender: false` in the round-trip: the test does not persist the
  registration token, so the signed path is implemented and unit-tested but
  NOT proven end-to-end against the daemon.
- The oracle agreement is one reading at one instant (skew 0 at cursor 5172),
  not a sustained differential lane.
- `CURSOR_EXPIRED` is modelled from the daemon's documented contract; it was
  never observed live, because the daemon clamps instead of emitting it.
- No claim is made about `mark_all_read`, contacts, products, archive, ATC, or
  search — out of journey scope and untouched.

VERDICT: implemented, tested, and PROVEN LIVE against the running daemon.
Left `in_progress` for a non-implementer to grade.

against the daemon. Fresh cursors, fresh message, same invariants:

  daemon tail cursor:5191 vs CLI tail cursor:5191 (skew 0)
  health: status=ready version=Some("0.3.31") projects=136 messages=5041
  baseline cursor: cursor:5191
  sent message:40826 (verified_sender=false)
  first read: 1 event(s), ours at cursor:5203 (message message:40826)
  second read: 0 event(s), next cursor:5203 (no replay)
  acked message:40826 at Some("2026-09-02T05:37:03.856122Z")
  receipt: persisted=true signaled=false acknowledged=true
  tools advertised: 45

Final counts: 61 unit passed / 0 failed; 2 integration passed / 0 failed /
4 ignored; 1 doc test passed; then 4 live passed / 0 failed with `--ignored`.

## THE SILENT-NOTIFICATION SHAPE NOW HAS THREE INSTANCES

`persisted=true signaled=false acknowledged=true` on messages 40786, 40810,
AND 40826 — three separate messages across 27 minutes, every one of them
delivered and acknowledged while never signalled. This is in Agent Mail
itself, not in a caller, and it is reproducible on demand via
`journey::delivery_receipt`. BlueLantern owns it for `1p0u`; the predicate is
`RecipientReceipt::is_persisted_but_unsignalled`.

## STORE DRIFT ACROSS THE SESSION

133 projects / 4,982 messages at 05:00Z -> 136 / 5,025 at 05:29Z -> 136 / 5,041
at 05:37Z. The delivery sequence advanced 5,142 -> 5,203 for one recipient in
the same window. Any Agent Mail figure without a timestamp is not a figure.

## ONE HAZARD FOUND FOR THE FLEET, NOT MINE TO FIX

At 05:31Z every `cargo` command in the repo failed — build, check, test, all
crates — because `crates/response-envelope-check/` held a `Cargo.toml` with no
`src/`. Root `Cargo.toml` uses `members = ["crates/*"]`, so a manifest with no
target breaks workspace LOADING before cargo reaches the package named by
`-p`, which is why it presented as "everything is broken" rather than as one
crate's problem. Reported, not touched; the owner fixed it within minutes.

Doctrine line: in a glob-membered workspace on a shared checkout, writing
`Cargo.toml` before `src/` is a fleet-wide stall. Write the source first, or
both in one step.

JourneySpine added the companion catch, which matters for gate authoring here:
during that outage `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test orchestration_tick`
returned exit 101 for the workspace-load reason, and a finding that depends on
that command ALSO expects 101. Same exit code, different cause — so a
fires-on-known-bad leg matching only `rc != 0` would have gone green on an
unrelated outage. A known-bad gate must assert its MESSAGE, not just its exit
code.
