title: Dispatch refuses a packet naming an unclaimed bead — enforce the middle beat in code
description:
WHAT: the dispatch path must REFUSE to send a packet naming a bead that is not `in_progress` and assigned to the receiving agent. File -> CLAIM -> dispatch, with the middle beat enforced by the code rather than remembered by the conductor.

WHY, measured 2026-08-31: `5rh` was dispatched to %1413 and never claimed. The bead sat `open`, `assignee: none`, ZERO comments, while a worker was actively carrying it. Silent in both directions -- the pane read as idle-with-no-assignment, and the queue read as still having ready work nobody had taken.

THE PART THAT MAKES THIS P0 RATHER THAN BOOKKEEPING: it defeats the follow-up detector we shipped today. `classify_followup` keys on (assigned + in_progress + no comment since dispatch). An unclaimed dispatch produces NO SIGNAL AT ALL -- the stage built to catch dispatched-then-silent is structurally blind to a dispatch that never became tracker state. The bead's status is a PROJECTION of the dispatch; when the projection is never written, the watcher watches an empty slot. That is the same shape as every other failure catalogued today: a mechanism that is correct and looking in a place where the event does not arrive.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: attempt a dispatch naming a bead that is `open`/unassigned -> REFUSED, with the bead id and its actual status in the refusal text. A refusal that does not name the bead sends the caller hunting.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, second form: attempt a dispatch naming a bead assigned to a DIFFERENT agent -> REFUSED. Two panes working one bead is the duplicate-work failure, and it nearly happened today when `br ready` offered a bead an agent had been building for 14 minutes while the tracker still read `unclaimed`.
3. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a correctly filed-claimed-dispatched packet passes untouched. A refuse-only gate is over-strict, gets routed around, and dies slower than no gate.
4. THE REFUSAL MUST BE ACTIONABLE, not just typed: name the exact `br update <id> --assignee <agent> --status in_progress` that would satisfy it. Measured today -- a supervisor emitted `DISPATCH_RETRY_BLOCKED owner=josh next_action=inspect-or-clear-pending-dispatch` 29 times and it worked precisely because it named the owner and the action.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: a dispatch with no bead id is an ERROR, never an unchecked pass. Broadcasts and corrections are a DIFFERENT operation and must be named as such rather than slipping through as bead-less dispatches.
6. MUTATION: remove the status check; leg 1 goes RED. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: claiming makes work VISIBLE, not DONE. A claimed bead with a silent pane is still a silent pane -- this closes the blind spot in the detector, not the silence itself. And `open`+unassigned is NOT by itself evidence of a skipped claim: it may simply be unstarted work. The discriminating signal is DISPATCHED-and-unclaimed, which means the DISPATCH LEDGER is the authority here, not the bead. A gate reading only bead status can prove the claim exists; only the ledger can prove a dispatch happened without one.

title: 01-idea:71 says dispatch DOES NOT EXIST; send_and_verify exists at main.rs:714 and is called at :1461
description:
## WHAT

`docs/plan/01-idea.md:71` states:

```
| actuate | dispatch | **DOES NOT EXIST** — a human types into panes |
```

That is false against the current tracked source. Correct the cell to
**`AVAILABLE, NOT VERIFIED`** — the category the same table already uses for the `complete` row —
and name the actual gap, which is runtime proof, not code.

## WHY

`crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:714-912` is a complete production actuator, `send_and_verify`:

- `:725-736` builds the dispatch packet and stages it to a temp file
- `:738` resolves the receiver kind (`receiver_is_codex`)
- `:740-760` for a codex pane: `tmux send-keys -t <pane> -l <packet>` then `send-keys Enter`
  — the exact two-step form `AUTONOMOUS-WAVE.md:229-231` says is the one that works
- `:768-776` otherwise: `ntm --robot-send=<session> --panes=<pane> --msg-file=<staged>`
- `:782` writes a transport receipt
- `:784-911` loops on receiver receipt against `RECEIPT_TIMEOUT`, with `cx.checkpoint()`

It is not dead code: `grep -rn 'send_and_verify' crates/omp-orchestrator/src` returns `:714`
(definition) and `:1461` (call site, inside the tick). The file is tracked
(`git ls-files -- crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs` → present). Positive control for the
greps: `grep -rc 'fn ' crates/omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs` → 79.

The crate's own header already carries the honest verdict, at `lib.rs:25-27`: the subprocess
wiring *"is designed but unverified at runtime."*

**Why this is a blocker and not a wording quibble.** `.flywheel/AUTONOMOUS-WAVE.md:44-49` elevates
this one line to the wave's ordering principle: *"That is the product. Everything else is
downstream of it. When you are choosing between two tasks, pick the one that gets the loop closer
to dispatching."* Four panes are prioritising against **"the actuator is missing"** when the
measured state is **"the actuator exists and is unproven."** Those are different tasks: one is
writing a dispatch path, the other is running the one that is there and reading its receipt. The
second is cheap and was never attempted; the first is the work the wave has been ordering itself
around.

The table's own vocabulary is what makes this a defect rather than a shorthand. Its seven rows
already distinguish existence from proof — `UNVERIFIED` twice, `FENCED`, `AVAILABLE, NOT WIRED` —
so `DOES NOT EXIST` is a deliberate and stronger claim, and it is the wrong one.

## ACCEPTANCE

1. `docs/plan/01-idea.md:71` reads `AVAILABLE, NOT VERIFIED` (or equivalent) and cites
   `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs:714` and the `:1461` call site.
2. `grep -rn 'DOES NOT EXIST' docs/plan/01-idea.md` → no match for the actuate row.
3. `.flywheel/AUTONOMOUS-WAVE.md` §1 is corrected in the same commit, since it quotes the line as
   the ordering fact. The corrected §1 must state what is actually missing.
4. The real gap gets a runnable acceptance, because renaming a cell ships nothing: one recorded
   run of `send_and_verify` against a live pane, with the transport receipt written by `:782` and
   the receiver receipt from the `:784-911` loop retained as evidence — or a named typed refusal
   explaining why it could not run. Expected result stated as `run X, expect Y` before the run,
   not after.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Whether the dispatch path is *correct*. This bead says the plan misdescribes it and that the gap
is verification. Proving the actuator delivers is milestone M3's job; this bead's job is to stop
the fleet from ordering work against a false absence.

## NO-CLAIM

Source existing and being called is not delivery. `AGENTS.md` is explicit that a sender's success
is not a receiver's receipt, and `cp-z42vu` recorded a send returning `success` while the packet
never arrived. Reclassifying the cell raises honesty, not capability; it may well turn out the
actuator has never successfully delivered once, which is exactly the measurement this unblocks.

(`section: 01-idea`).

title: Three dispatch renderers stage packets with no sender identity; 19 of 37 sites unidentified
description:
## WHAT

Three dispatch packet renderers stage a packet with NO sender identity, so a receiving pane learns
only the index it was sent to. Measured by `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/sender_identity.rs`, which
landed with this bead's sibling work and now refuses any new unidentified site.

The gate's own census, produced by the SAME `scan()` function leg 1 uses (not a grep handed to it):

| crate | dispatch sites | identity present |
|---|---:|---|
| `crates/omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs` | 7 | **NO** |
| `crates/omp-idle-dispatch/src/main.rs` | 2 | **NO** |
| `crates/refill-idle-panes/src/main.rs` | 2 | **NO** |
| `crates/fast-dispatch/src/main.rs` | 6 | yes |
| `crates/loop-tick/src/lib.rs` | 6 | yes |
| `crates/tick-dispatch/src/main.rs` | 6 | yes |
| `crates/kernel-only-operator-hook/src/lib.rs` | 8 | n/a — allowanced, see below |

Totals: 56 tracked crates, 129 source files scanned, **37 dispatch sites in 7 files, 19 of them
unidentified across 3 renderers**.

`kernel-only-operator-hook` is allowanced with a reason and is NOT part of this fix: it
pattern-matches the `--robot-send` argv to allow or deny a Bash event and constructs no packet, so
there is no packet for a FROM line to live in. Its 8 hits are the allowlist entry and its unit
fixtures.

## WHY

Operator directive, verbatim: *"make sure you all announce who you are when sending a message so a
pane can properly contact you back."*

The measured failure: every packet sent during the 2026-09-01/02 session went out as
`ntm send omp-orchestrator --panes=N` with no FROM line. `ntm send` names a session and an INDEX,
and **pane indices are not stable handles** — they shifted twice in one night. Two panes changed
MODEL mid-session (`%1408` GLM 5.3 -> Opus 5, `%1409` GLM 5.3 -> GPT-5.6-Luna) while their agent
NAMES held. So agent names are the durable handle and indices are not, and `WAVE.md`'s roster went
stale listing pane2=%1408 while live tmux said %1413. Three agents replied to the orchestrator only
because they happened to know it was pane 1.

Two traps that make a hand-written FROM line wrong, both measured, both of which the fix must avoid:

1. `tmux display-message -p '#{pane_id}'` answers for the **ACTIVE** pane, not the calling one.
   From pane 4 it returns `%1396 index=0`; with `-t "$TMUX_PANE"` it returns the truth,
   `pane_index=4 pane_id=%1408`. A renderer that builds its own FROM line with the unqualified form
   announces WHOEVER IS FOCUSED. Note the nasty part: it is INVISIBLE from the focused pane — run
   from pane 1 both forms agree, so the bug cannot be reproduced from where an orchestrator sits.
2. `register_agent`'s `pane_id` argument is silently DISCARDED — `whois` returns no `pane_id`
   field, and the success envelope omits it too. The pane binding lives in a per-pane identity FILE
   and has a kernel: `resolve_pane_identity {project_key, pane_id?}` reads
   `~/.config/agent-mail/identity/<project_hash>/<pane_id>` with two legacy fallbacks and a GH#252
   liveness predicate. Measured for AmberGate: `{"agent_name":"AmberGate","pane_id":"%1408",
   "binding":"legacy-unverified"}`. Use that kernel; do not add a second source of pane truth.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`, per renderer:

1. Each of the three renderers stages a packet whose first two lines are a FROM line naming the
   sending AGENT NAME plus its pane index AND pane_id, and a REPLY-VIA line naming both routes
   (`ntm --robot-send=<session> --panes=<index> --msg-file <path>` and Agent Mail to the agent
   name). Agent name first, because it is the handle that held all session.
2. `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test sender_identity` stays GREEN and the allowance shrinks from
   4 rows to 1 (`kernel-only-operator-hook` only). The gate FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS: a row naming
   a crate that now complies is an error, so the rows must be DELETED in the same commit as each
   fix. That asymmetry is the point — the list can only shrink.
3. The pane_id in the rendered FROM line comes from `resolve_pane_identity` or from
   `tmux display-message -t "$TMUX_PANE"`, never from an unqualified `display-message`. Assert it
   with a leg that feeds a multi-session `tmux list-panes -a` fixture and requires the CALLER's
   pane, with a negative control where the active pane differs from the caller's.
4. State in the commit which verdicts/paths still send unidentified packets, if any remain.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- `crates/fast-dispatch`, `crates/loop-tick`, `crates/tick-dispatch` — already identified, and
  another agent holds sender work on those three files.
- `crates/kernel-only-operator-hook` — allowanced with a reason; it renders no packet.
- Enforcing identity on the RECEIVING side. A FROM line makes a reply addressable; it does not
  prove the reply arrived.

## NO-CLAIM

A FROM line makes a packet ATTRIBUTABLE, not delivered. It does not fix
`RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send` recording that a send RETURNED rather than arrived, and it does
not make pane indices stable — it makes them unnecessary, by carrying the durable handle beside
them. The gate proves a from-marker is PRESENT in the file that dispatches; it cannot prove the
rendered value is CORRECT, which is why acceptance 3 pins the resolution source rather than the
string.

title: byte-exact dispatch journey mapping: S1-S9 stage to contract to kernel symbol, with the comms/mail hole named
description:
## WHAT

Author `docs/contracts/dispatch_journey_mapping_contract.md`: the byte-exact mapping layer
between the canonical S1-S9 journey (`docs/plan/12-journey.md`), the evidence map
(`docs/plan/11-lifecycle.md`), the 20 contracts in `docs/contracts/`, and the kernel symbols
that actually implement each stage. One row per operational stage:

  stage | parent S-stage | GOAL | governing contract | kernel crate | exact symbol/command | measured gap

Stages walked: observe, select, claim, dispatch, ack, receipt, verify, close, comms/mail.

Every stage GOAL is backed by >= 2 independent primary sources (arXiv abstracts read directly,
source + fetch-date cited). A single-source claim is labelled phantom doctrine inline.

## WHY

`docs/plan/12-journey.md` owns the dispatchable runbook (S1-S9, seven-field contract) and
`docs/plan/11-lifecycle.md` owns the evidence map (11.1 stage/crate ownership). Neither names a
single `docs/contracts/` file per stage, and neither names a callable symbol. The result is that
three separate stage vocabularies exist in one workspace with no bridge:

  loop_coverage::LoopLayer                    crates/loop-coverage/src/lib.rs:78            (10 members)
  tick_monitor::lifecycle::Stage              crates/tick-monitor/src/lifecycle.rs:35        (9 members)
  bead_lifecycle::model::LifecycleStatus      crates/ntm-fleet-monitor/src/bead_lifecycle/model.rs:75 (10 members)

Measured three-way intersection of their stable string labels: EMPTY. LoopLayer vs
lifecycle::Stage share ZERO labels. No enum has an `ack` member, a `receipt` member, or a
`mail`/`comms` member.

The comms/mail leg is the largest hole: `grep -ncE 'agent mail|agent-mail|inbox|mail_pending|robot-wait'
docs/plan/11-lifecycle.md` = 0, and repo-wide only two crate files mention Agent Mail at all,
both in comments/strings, never as a call. Meanwhile the kernel primitives are installed and live.

This bead is the MAPPING layer only. It does not author a rival spine; 12-journey.md remains
canonical and this document says so in its first paragraph.

## ACCEPTANCE

1. `test -f docs/contracts/dispatch_journey_mapping_contract.md`
2. `wc -c docs/contracts/dispatch_journey_mapping_contract.md` -> under 25000 bytes.
3. House shape present: a `Bead:` line and all of
   `## Purpose`, `## Contract Artifacts`, `## Validation`, `## Cross-References`,
   `## Non-Coverage`, `## NO-CLAIM`.
   Check: `grep -c '^## \(Purpose\|Contract Artifacts\|Validation\|Cross-References\|Non-Coverage\|NO-CLAIM\)$'` -> 6
4. `grep -oE 'DJ-[A-Z0-9-]+' ... | sort -u | wc -l` -> >= 8 distinct `DJ-*` stable IDs.
5. Every kernel claim in the mapping table resolves: for each named
   `crates/<crate>/src/<file>:<line>` anchor, the file exists in `git ls-tree -r HEAD` and the
   named symbol appears in it. A stage with NO implementing kernel states that explicitly
   rather than naming a plausible crate.
6. `## Non-Coverage` names the stages with weak or zero contract coverage by name and does not
   paper over them.
7. Every external/research claim carries >= 2 arXiv IDs with fetch-date, or is explicitly
   labelled single-source phantom doctrine.

## NON-GOALS

- Does not rewrite `docs/plan/12-journey.md` or `docs/plan/11-lifecycle.md`.
- Does not rewrite any of the 20 existing contracts in `docs/contracts/`.
- Does not touch `crates/`.
- Does not wire the mail leg; it names the missing kernel and the installed primitives it
  should call.

title: pane-truth: ExitCode::from(selftest(&rules) as u8) truncates -- a live twin of n34x, and undeclared AND unscanned
description:
WHAT: `crates/pane-truth/src/main.rs:49` is `return ExitCode::from(selftest(&rules) as u8);` while
`crates/pane-truth/src/lib.rs:695` is `pub fn selftest(rules: &PaneTruthRules) -> i32`. **Verified
live from source by SnowyCanyon, not taken on report.** A failure count of 256 truncates to **0** --
printing RED while exiting SUCCESS. Structurally identical to `omp-orchestrator-n34x`
(`cargo-lane-budget`), fixed at `dc617e2`.

WHY IT IS WORSE THAN THE ORIGINAL: the argument `selftest(&rules)` contains `(` and `&`, which
`passthrough_chain` (`exit_codes.rs:237-258`) rejects, so the site is **undeclared AND unscanned** --
the registry gate never demanded a row for it, and never will. The `cargo-lane-budget` instance was
at least *in* the scan set. This one is invisible to the mechanism built to catch exactly it.

**`pane-truth` IS THE FLEET'S GROUND-TRUTH ORACLE**, which is what makes the latency matter: a
selftest that prints RED and exits 0 is a broken oracle reporting itself healthy, and every
dispatch decision keyed on it inherits that.

ACCEPTANCE -- repeat the `n34x` proof, scoped, no new invention:
1. Apply the same remedy shape: a total `selftest_exit_code(i32) -> u8` returning `u8` LITERALS, so
   no numeric conversion remains on the path. Do NOT narrow `selftest`'s own signature if any test
   pins it -- check first and say which.
2. Reuse the existing RED code; add nothing to the closed 1-4 band. The count stays in the MESSAGE.
3. Known-bad FIRST, as an assertion of the mechanism before the fix: `assert_eq!(256_i32 as u8, 0)`,
   then refuse 256, 512, 65536, -1, `i32::MIN`.
4. An equivalence leg: the new conversion equals `reachable as u8` for `{0,1}`, so behaviour
   diverges ONLY where the old path was wrong.
5. **TWO MUTATIONS, and M2 is the one that matters** -- M1: restore `as u8` -> the truncation leg
   goes RED. M2: break ONLY the message half, leaving the code correct -> **exactly one leg fires**,
   proving the message assertion is independently load-bearing. Restore byte-identically both times
   and diff against recorded shas. An exit-code-only suite is blind to M2.
6. Assert on emitted TEXT per gate rule 7, never on an exit code alone.
7. Anti-vacuity: the suite must not pass on zero rules. An empty rule set is an ERROR.

NON-GOALS: do NOT sweep the other 20 census sites. Seven forward a value that could grow
(`tick-dispatch` x8, `verify-dispatch:54`, `loop-tick/main.rs:54`, `loop-driver` x2,
`loop-queue-filter:18`, `dispatcher-deadman:165`, `fleet-monitor:437`) and are UNEXAMINED beyond
reading the expression -- they are not claimed broken and are not in this bead.

NO-CLAIM: latent, not observed. `pane-truth`'s selftest would need to produce >=256 failures to
trigger it. Filed because the twin proves the class is not closed, and because this instance cannot
be caught by the registry gate at all.

title: state-wildcard-lint refuses without naming file:line, and its 2 pre-existing findings block every commit
description:
WHAT: (a) make `state-wildcard-lint`'s refusal NAME file and line, and (b) resolve its 2 findings,
which together with path-literal-guard are blocking EVERY commit in this repo.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 04:5xZ. `.git/hooks/pre-commit` -> exit 1:
  "MULTI-GATE REFUSED: 2 violation(s):
     path-literal-guard: 17 hardcoded home-path literal(s): crates/slb-guard-fail-closed/src/main.r
     state-wildcard-lint: 2 finding(s)"

DEFECT (a) -- THE REFUSAL IS NOT ACTIONABLE. path-literal-guard at least names a file (truncated).
state-wildcard-lint names NOTHING: "2 finding(s)" and no path, no line, no snippet. AGENTS.md's own
gate doctrine says a finding that does not name the replacement is not actionable, and this one does
not even name the offence. An agent hitting this cannot act, and pane 5 -- whose staged work is
clean and unrelated -- was left unable to distinguish its own violation from someone else's.
The crate already computes what is needed: `pub fn find_findings_in_source(source) ->
Vec<(usize, usize, String, Option<String>)>` at src/lib.rs:295 returns line/column data, and
`scan_source(file, source)` at :321 has the filename. The information exists and is discarded at
the reporting boundary.

DEFECT (b) -- THE 2 FINDINGS ARE UNATTRIBUTED AND PRE-EXISTING. What the lint forbids, from its own
tests (`state_wildcard_is_finding` / `primitive_wildcard_is_not_state_finding` at :394-400): a
wildcard `_ =>` arm in a `match` over a STATE ENUM. That is the right thing to forbid -- a `_` arm
silently swallows a newly added state, which is exactly the UNKNOWN-coercion class measured twice
tonight (ntm `state=UNKNOWN` treated as a busy claim; `safe_to_dispatch` derived from a non-answer).

A candidate scan (superset heuristic, NOT the lint's verdict) over `crates/*/src`:
  omp-inventory-map 7, tick-monitor 5, pane-dispatch-ready 4, ntm-fleet-monitor 4,
  state-wildcard-lint 3, finding 2, refill-idle-panes 1, receiver-receipt 1.
NONE of the six crates landed by extraction batch 1 appear. So this half of the commit block is
PRE-EXISTING and NOT extraction-caused -- that attribution is settled and pane 5 is cleared of it.

NOTE THE SELF-REFERENCE, which must be handled deliberately: state-wildcard-lint's OWN lib.rs
contains 3 candidates because its test fixtures embed the forbidden pattern as specimen data. If the
lint flags its own fixtures it is the seventh instance this session of a checker whose input
contains text about the thing it checks (kernel-bypass-gate has a specimen row of the string it
forbids; the gate census grepped a table naming every gate). Exclusion must be a DECLARED allowlist
with a reason, never inferred.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. The refusal names `file:line` and the offending arm for every finding. Verify by reading the
     hook's own output, `.git/hooks/pre-commit`, not a standalone run.
  2. The 2 findings resolved -- either fixed by making the match exhaustive over the state enum, or
     each one carrying a DECLARED allowlist row with a reason. A `_` arm that is genuinely correct
     (a non-state match, a primitive) is a lint false positive and should be reported as one.
  3. `.git/hooks/pre-commit` -> exit 0 for a commit touching only unrelated files. This is the
     bar that matters: the repo must be committable.
  4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: plant a `match state { X => (), _ => () }` over a state enum -> RED naming
     the planted file:line; remove it -> GREEN. Byte-identical restore, both sha256 recorded.
  5. KNOWN-GOOD leg: a primitive wildcard must NOT be flagged (the crate's existing
     `primitive_wildcard_is_not_state_finding` test is that leg -- keep it green).
  6. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty scan set is an ERROR, not a pass.

DO NOT touch crates/slb-guard-fail-closed or crates/zestgraph-hook-substrates -- pane 3 owns their
home-path repair under h71g, and a second agent editing them is how 889 lines were lost earlier
tonight. Do NOT bypass the hook; no --no-verify.

NO-CLAIM: the candidate counts above are a grep heuristic and are NOT the lint's verdict -- the lint
reports exactly 2, so most candidates are legitimate. Re-derive the real 2 from the crate's own API
rather than trusting my numbers; my probes have been wrong repeatedly tonight.

    oracle. There is no differential harness for it.
  - NOT that no other crate carries a wildcard-over-state arm the predicate misses.

    matches, struct fields and inferred bindings are invisible, and only surface at all
    when the scrutinee's NAME happens to end in one of eight state-like suffixes. False

    enumerate the space.

title: Exit 1 and exit 2 each carry three unrelated meanings
description:
## WHAT

Exit `1` carries **three unrelated meanings** across 32 crates and 89 literal sites, and exit `2`
carries three more across 34 crates and 118 sites. Split them so a caller can distinguish a
refusal from a broken tool without reading stderr.

Registered as `XC-001` and `XC-002` in `docs/error_codes/exit_code_registry.md`.

## WHY

Measured 2026-09-01. `crates/no-shell-gate/src/bin/pre-push-gate.rs` emits **exit 1** for both:

- `PRE_PUSH_GATE_REFUSED` at `:312, :321, :366, :375, :384, :402, :416, :434` — the gate WORKED
  and correctly refused.
- `PRE_PUSH_GATE_ERROR` at `:287, :303, :340, :427` — the gate DID NOT RUN: unknown flag,
  non-integer argument, unwritable receipt, and an empty `git ls-files` scan.

Same code, same file. A caller checking `$? -eq 1` cannot tell "your push is not allowed" from
"the thing that decides is broken", and on 2026-09-01 an agent read one as the other. Two of the
four session misreads reduce to this.

Exit 1 also serves as a usage error at 2 sites, and `ExitCode::FAILURE` (51 sites of
`SUCCESS`/`FAILURE` combined) folds into it.

Exit 2 is the mirror: dominantly a usage error (50 of 118 sites carry a `usage` message), but
`OracleCompareVerdict::Unmeasurable` maps to 2 at `crates/oracle-compare/src/lib.rs:103`,
`EXIT_USAGE = 2` at `crates/fleet-composite/src/main.rs:14`, and `PLAN_ASSEMBLE_ERROR` exits 2.
**It also collides with the `cargo` mint wrapper's own exit 2** (`CARGO_LANE_IDENTITY_UNSAFE`,
`CARGO_LANE_ISOLATED_TARGET_REQUIRED`, and 7 more markers at `~/.local/bin/cargo`), so a 2 from a
`cargo test` line has three possible owners.

`crates/oracle-compare/src/lib.rs:99-104` already shows the shape to copy —
`Agree`/`Disagree`/`Unmeasurable` as 0/1/2, a verdict and its absence given different codes.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes` stays at 7 passed with the new codes documented
   (the gate refuses any code lacking an `XC-*` row, so the registry must be edited in the same
   commit).
2. A leg proving separation, in whichever crate is split first: given an input that makes the gate
   REFUSE, expect the refusal code; given an input that makes the gate itself fail (unwritable
   receipt path), expect the DIFFERENT error code. Both arms asserted, so an all-one-code
   implementation fails.
3. `grep -c 'ExitCode::from(1)' crates/no-shell-gate/src/bin/pre-push-gate.rs` must fall, and the
   remaining sites must all be one meaning — stated in the commit which meaning.

New codes come from the **5..=63 unallocated band** named in the registry's §5 reservation table,
never from 64..=78 (`sysexits.h`) and never from 102..=125 (toolchain and wrappers).

## NOT IN SCOPE

Renumbering every crate. Take `pre-push-gate` first because it is the measured misread, then the
other gates as they are touched. A sweep across 32 crates in one commit is how a caller breaks
silently.

## NO-CLAIM

Splitting the code does not make any caller check it. Nothing here proves that a consumer reads
the new code rather than `!= 0`, and the marker prefixes remain the authoritative signal until
consumers are audited — a separate bead.

title: Corpus doc #13: exit code registry with enforced does-not-mean column
description:
## WHAT

Document #13 of 78 in `docs/plans/plan_to_write_the_document_corpus.md`, and the widest single gap
against the corpus: asupersync carries `docs/error_codes/` with 45 documents; we carried **zero**
while exit codes were scattered across 51 bin targets with nothing describing them.

Register every exit code this workspace **emits** (12 distinct) and every foreign code it
**receives**, one row per code with: code, emitting crates, what it MEANS, **what it does NOT
mean**, and the operator's next action. Reserve the number space. Name every code carrying two or
more meanings. Change no code — renumbering breaks callers and is a separate bead.

## WHY

Four exit codes were misread by agents on 2026-09-01, one of them by the pane that filed this:

- `103` read as a TEST RESULT because `0 passed 0 failed` printed beside it — a failure path
  emitting something shaped like data. The session's most expensive misread.
- `75` read as a build failure; it was `CARGO_MINT_CONTAINER_EXHAUSTED`, the disk-floor refusal.
- `127` read as "`bin/check.sh` is untracked", a repo defect that did not exist; the real cause was
  a stale worktree.
- `1` read as both "the gate is broken" and "the gate correctly refused" — and it is genuinely
  both, on different lines of the same file.

Before this document, `git grep -c --no-index -E '^//[/!].*\bexit' -- 'crates/*/src/*'` answered
**0 files** against a positive control of **102** files carrying `//!` docs at all. No crate
documented its own exits. The load-bearing column is therefore **does NOT mean**, not **means**.

## ACCEPTANCE

Re-run, do not read:

```
$ cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes -- --nocapture
```

Expect **7 passed**. The legs:

1. `every_emitted_exit_code_is_documented` — re-derives the emission set from all `.rs` files under
   `crates/*/src` and fails naming `file:line` for any code with no `XC-*` row.
2. `an_empty_scan_set_is_an_error_not_a_pass` — anti-vacuity; a zero-file scan returns a NAMED
   error, never an empty complaint list.
3. `a_planted_undocumented_code_is_caught` — fires-on-known-bad; a temp fixture emitting
   `ExitCode::from(213)` must be flagged.
4. `a_planted_documented_code_passes` — known-good; `ExitCode::from(2)` must pass. Without this leg
   an over-strict gate looks green, and an over-strict gate gets routed around.
5. `every_row_carries_a_does_not_mean` — refuses any row with an empty or placeholder
   `does NOT mean` cell, or fewer than 6 columns, or fewer than 12 emitted rows.
6. `the_scan_floors_seeded_from_this_suites_own_measurement_hold` — floors seeded from THIS
   suite's own scan (123 files, 12 codes, 18 pass-through sites), never from a neighbouring count.
7. `every_pass_through_site_is_declared` — every site forwarding a child's code must appear in §6.

Mutation leg, run at authoring time and reproducible: delete the `XC-004` row from the registry
(asserted to exist exactly once first) and leg 1 goes RED with
`EXIT_CODE_UNDOCUMENTED code=4 at crates/loop-switch/src/main.rs:75`; restore byte-identical
(sha256 `53ca7c5353cce9efdb3aa9da547b7f2d4efc917182aababc828e271d69732f9a`) and all 7 pass.

Structural bar, `docs/contracts/asupersync_process_grade.md`: all seven markers present, 32 stable
IDs, 19,142 bytes against a 25 KB ceiling, `## Non-Coverage` and `## NO-CLAIM` both present.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- **No renumbering, no code change.** Not one `ExitCode::from` was touched. The collisions are
  documented and filed separately.
- stderr marker registry (`PRE_PUSH_GATE_*`, `CARGO_MINT_*`, `RCH-Exxx`) — its own document.
- Emitters outside `crates/*/src`: test binaries, fixtures, build scripts, shell wrappers.

## NO-CLAIM

Documenting a code does not make any caller emit it correctly. The suite proves PRESENCE OF A ROW,
never truth of a row — a wrong `does NOT mean` cell passes every leg. It cannot tell a correct `1`
from a wrong `1`, because both are `1`; that is the defect the registry names and does not fix.
`XC-EXT-RCH`'s integer 103 is recorded as OBSERVED, not reproduced: two probes tonight returned 1
and 124 instead, and `rch schema export` ships 100 string codes with zero numeric exit mappings.

title: EXIT_CONFIG bound to two values; 78 bound to two names; 75 to five meanings
description:
## WHAT

Three constant/value collisions in the exit-code space, all measured, none inferred. Documented as
`XC-064`, `XC-075` and `XC-078` in `docs/error_codes/exit_code_registry.md`; this bead fixes them.

1. **`EXIT_CONFIG` is bound to two different values.**
   - `crates/fleet-composite/src/main.rs:16` — `const EXIT_CONFIG: u8 = 64;`
   - `crates/pane-dispatch-fence/src/main.rs:18` — `const EXIT_CONFIG: u8 = 78;`
   64 is `EX_USAGE` in `sysexits.h`; 78 is `EX_CONFIG`. One of the two is misnamed, and the
   `fleet-composite` one is the wrong one.

2. **`78` is bound to two unrelated names.**
   - `crates/fleet-monitor/src/lib.rs:413` — `pub const EXIT_CANNOT_OBSERVE: i32 = 78;`
   - `crates/pane-dispatch-fence/src/main.rs:18` — `EXIT_CONFIG = 78`
   "I could not observe the fleet" and "your configuration is wrong" are different operator
   actions from the same integer.

3. **`75` carries five meanings**, three ours and two foreign.
   - `crates/loop-driver/src/lib.rs:17` — `EXIT_CONCURRENT` (another instance holds the lock)
   - `crates/pane-dispatch-fence/src/main.rs:16` — `EXIT_BUSY` (the pane is busy)
   - `crates/installer/…` — `INSTALLER BLOCKED`
   - `~/.local/bin/cargo` — `CARGO_MINT_CONTAINER_EXHAUSTED` and
     `CARGO_MINT_PEAK_WOULD_BREACH_FLOOR`, both exit 75
   All five are honestly `EX_TEMPFAIL` "retry later", which is why 75 is the least harmful of the
   three — but `75` was misread as a build failure on 2026-09-01, so the retry semantics are not
   reaching the reader.

## WHY

Derived at commit `d48615c`:

```
git grep -n --no-index -E '^\s*(pub )?const EXIT_[A-Z_]+' -- 'crates/*/src/*'
```

A name bound to two values means a reader who has learned one crate is confidently wrong in the
next. A value bound to two names means a reader with only the integer cannot recover the meaning
at all. Both are the class the registry documents and this bead removes.

The precedent worth copying is foreign: `~/.local/bin/cargo:388` emits
`"exit_code":75,"is_gate_verdict":false` — the only emitter on this machine that ships the
refusal/failure disambiguation **in data** rather than in a prefix a human has to notice.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. `git grep -h --no-index -oE 'const EXIT_[A-Z_]+: [ui][0-9]+ = [0-9]+' -- 'crates/*/src/*' |
   sort -u` — every constant NAME appears exactly once with one value; no name has two values.
2. A new leg in `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/exit_codes.rs`:
   `no_exit_constant_name_is_bound_to_two_values` — the scanner already builds
   `consts: BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<u16>>`, so the assertion is that every set has len 1. The
   leg must be shown RED against today's tree (it will name `EXIT_CONFIG = {64, 78}`) before the
   fix lands, and GREEN after.
3. `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes` stays at 7+ passed, with the registry rows
   edited in the same commit — the gate refuses any code lacking a row.
4. Every renamed constant's call sites updated in the same commit, and the commit states which
   `sysexits.h` code each one now claims.

## NOT IN SCOPE

The 75 family is documented rather than renumbered here: three "retry later" meanings sharing
`EX_TEMPFAIL` is defensible, and the two foreign ones cannot be changed by us at all. The fix for
75 is the `is_gate_verdict` field in emitted JSON, not a new integer — file separately if wanted.

## NO-CLAIM

Fixing the names does not make any caller distinguish the codes; `!= 0` remains the dominant check
in the tree, and this bead does not audit consumers. And renaming `EXIT_CONFIG` in
`fleet-composite` changes an OBSERVABLE contract — anything scripting against 64 from that binary
breaks, which is why the acceptance requires the call-site sweep in the same commit.

title: 32 sites narrow an integer through an as cast on the exit path; the wrap can land on 0
description:
WHAT: 32 live sites across 13 crates narrow an integer through an `as` cast on the exit
path — `ExitCode::from(<expr> as u8)` or `process::exit(<expr> as i32)`. `as` WRAPS between
integers rather than refusing, so a value outside the target range emits a DIFFERENT code
than the source names, and the wrap can land on 0. Nothing gates it.

THE ACTIVATION IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL — IT ALREADY HAPPENED ONCE. `cargo-lane-budget` had
`ExitCode::from(selftest() as u8)` where `selftest() -> i32` accumulated a `failures`
counter and returned literal 0 or 1. Returning the counter instead of 1 — the obvious next
edit, since the count is computed and printed one line above the return — truncates 256 to
**0**: stdout reads `SELFTEST RED cargo-lane-budget failures=256` while the process exits
SUCCESS. ExtractTwo fixed that one site in `dc617e2` by introducing
`selftest_exit_code(failures) -> u8` returning `u8` LITERALS, so the narrowing is
inexpressible rather than merely absent. That is the pattern to copy.

CENSUS, derived 2026-09-02 by me (comment- and string-stripped, so prose does not count):

  crate                     sites  expression(s)
  tick-dispatch                 8  exit as u8
  crate-soundness-verify        5  EXIT_RED as u8
  loop-tick                     5  selftest_queue_guard() as u8, selftest_observe() as u8,
                                   selftest_cargo_lane() as u8, selftest_wait() as u8, code as u8
  fleet-monitor                 2  EXIT_CANNOT_OBSERVE as u8, rc as u8
  loop-driver                   2  output.code as u8
  pane-oracle-diff              2  v.exit_code() as u8
  pane-truth                    2  selftest(&rules) as u8, run_live(&session,&rules) as u8
  cargo-lane-budget             1  print_report(&check(&config)) as u8
  dispatcher-deadman            1  verdict.exit as u8
  fleet-reconcile               1  exit_for(&inner.verdict) as u8
  loop-queue-filter             1  output.code as u8
  omp-idle-dispatch             1  exit as i32
  verify-dispatch               1  out.code as u8
                             ----
                               32

NOTE THE FIGURE DISAGREEMENT, AND DO NOT AVERAGE IT. ExtractTwo reported 22 sites across 11
crates from a `grep -rnE` over `crates/`. I derive 32 across 13 using the exit_codes
scanner's own reader (balanced-paren argument extraction, comments and string literals
stripped). Two differently-shaped instruments, and the gap is the point of building the
gate: whoever takes this bead should re-derive rather than trust either number.

THREE CATEGORIES, and only the third is a defect:
 1. NAMED CONST WITH A CLOSED SPACE — `EXIT_RED` (`pub const EXIT_RED: i32 = 1`),
    `EXIT_CANNOT_OBSERVE`. The cast is lossless and provably so. 7 sites.
 2. DECLARED PASS-THROUGH OF A CHILD STATUS — `exit`, `rc`, `out.code`, `output.code`,
    `code`, `verdict.exit`, `v.exit_code()`. A child status is 0..=255, so `as u8` is
    identity over the real range. Each already carries an `XC-PT-*` row. ~17 sites.
 3. LOCAL `-> i32` FUNCTION RETURNING LITERALS — `pane-truth::selftest(&rules)`,
    `pane-truth::run_live(&session,&rules)`, `loop-tick::selftest_*()`. STRUCTURALLY
    IDENTICAL to the `cargo-lane-budget` defect: safe only while the return value happens
    to stay small, with no mechanism holding it there. ~8 sites.

THE LIVE INSTANCE WORTH FIXING FIRST: `crates/pane-truth/src/main.rs:49,51`.
`pane_truth::selftest` (`src/lib.rs:695`) is `-> i32`. Copy `dc617e2`'s shape.

WHY THE EXISTING GATE CANNOT SEE ANY OF THIS. `every_pass_through_site_is_declared` keys on
`passthrough_chain`, which rejects any argument still containing `(` or `&` after stripping
a trailing `()`. So `selftest(&rules)`, `exit_for(&inner.verdict)` and
`print_report(&check(&config))` are UNDECLARED AND UNRECOGNISED — never in the scan set, so
no row was ever demanded for them. Category 3 is invisible to the gate by construction.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. A leg in `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/exit_codes.rs` that derives the narrowing-cast
    sites and refuses any site with no reasoned allowance row, seeded from the leg's OWN
    scan — not from the census above and not from ExtractTwo's.
 2. BIDIRECTIONAL: an allowance row whose site no longer narrows must FAIL, so the list can
    only shrink. `no_declared_pass_through_row_outlives_its_site` in the same file is the
    shape to copy.
 3. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty narrowing-cast scan set is an ERROR, asserted IN the deciding leg
    rather than in a sibling floor leg.
 4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: plant a narrowing cast, observe RED naming file:line, remove,
    observe GREEN, byte-identical restore with both sha256 recorded.
 5. ASSERT THE MESSAGE, not the exit code (AGENTS.md gate rule 7).
 6. Category 3 sites either FIXED on `dc617e2`'s pattern or allowed with a reason that says
    they are DEBT rather than a decision. Say which per site.

NO-CLAIM: I did NOT audit the upstream range of any category-2 site, so "a child status is
0..=255" is the contract, not a measurement — a wrapper that returns a computed value rather
than a child's status would break it and this bead does not check that. I also did not verify
that every category-1 const is genuinely closed; I read `EXIT_RED` and inferred the rest from
the naming. The category boundaries are a starting hypothesis, not a finding.

a field access or a zero-argument call" — both are a bare identifier chain. So the
declaration for these rows must state a CLOSED code space rather than 0..=255, and the

 6. `refill-idle-panes` must KEEP the property omp-orchestrator-oe2 established: a
    confident two-surface contradiction exits NONZERO naming the panes. A registry
    declaration must not flatten a typed refusal back into a generic code.

`assembly_freshness` in this package is a COMPILE ERROR, not a registry problem —

NO-CLAIM: declaring these five rows does not make the pass-through leg semantically
correct. It proves PRESENCE OF A ROW, never truth of a row — the gate's own header says
so. It also does not fix `passthrough_chain`'s inability to distinguish a forwarded child
code from a local value, which is why two agents' honest instinct was to decline to
declare a site they did not write.

title: EXIT_DEADLINE=124 collides with timeout(1); 77 deviates from EX_NOPERM
description:
## WHAT

Two of our exit codes sit in bands owned by other tools, so their meaning is unrecoverable from the
integer. Documented as `XC-124` and `XC-077` in `docs/error_codes/exit_code_registry.md` §5.

1. **`124` collides with `timeout(1)`.** `crates/loop-driver/src/lib.rs:18` declares
   `pub const EXIT_DEADLINE: i32 = 124;`, which is exactly the code GNU/BSD `timeout` returns when
   IT kills a child. Our loops are routinely wrapped in `timeout`, so a 124 from a `loop-driver`
   line is ambiguous between "the driver self-limited at its deadline" and "the wrapper killed the
   driver before it decided anything".

2. **`77` deviates from `sysexits.h`.** We use it as **UNPROVEN** — the checker could not establish
   its verdict — in `crates/dispatcher-deadman/src/main.rs:130,134,138,159`,
   `crates/tick-dispatch/src/main.rs:146,153,245,370`, and `crates/fast-dispatch/src/main.rs:676`.
   In `sysexits.h`, 77 is `EX_NOPERM`. The semantics we assigned are the most valuable in the
   registry and the number advertises something else.

## WHY

Measured while writing the registry, and the first one is self-demonstrating: a probe of the `rch`
refusal path was wrapped in `timeout 90` and returned **124**. The reading "our binary hit its
deadline" was available and wrong — `timeout` produced it. That is the exact confusion `XC-124`
predicts, observed inside the session that documented it.

The reservation table the registry publishes:

| band | owner |
|---|---|
| `5`–`63` | UNALLOCATED, ours to claim |
| `64`–`78` | `sysexits.h` (`EX_*`) |
| `101` | Rust toolchain (panic) |
| `102`–`125` | toolchain and wrappers — `124` is `timeout`, `103` observed from `rch` |
| `126`, `127`, `128`+N | POSIX shell |

`124` is a standing violation of that table. `77` is a semantic conflict inside a band we share.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Move `EXIT_DEADLINE` out of `102..=125` into the unallocated `5..=63` band. Then:
   `git grep -c --no-index -E 'const EXIT_[A-Z_]+: [ui][0-9]+ = (1(0[2-9]|1[0-9]|2[0-5]))'
   -- 'crates/*/src/*'` returns **0**.
2. A new leg in `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/exit_codes.rs`:
   `no_code_is_emitted_in_a_foreign_band` — the scanner already derives the full code set, so the
   assertion is that no derived code falls in `101`, `102..=125`, `126..=127`, or `>=128`. Shown
   RED against today's tree (it will name 124) before the fix, GREEN after.
3. `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes` stays green with the registry's `XC-124` row
   edited in the same commit.
4. For `77`: EITHER move UNPROVEN to the unallocated band, OR record in the registry that we
   deliberately override `EX_NOPERM` and why. A decision either way, not silence. If it moves,
   every `emit_unproven` call site keeps its marker so the stderr signal is unchanged.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Auditing whether any consumer currently reads 124 from `loop-driver`. If one does, this becomes a
breaking change and needs its own migration note — check before landing.

## NO-CLAIM

Moving a code out of a foreign band removes the AMBIGUITY, not the failure. A `loop-driver` wrapped
in `timeout` will still return 124 when the wrapper wins — the point is only that 124 then means
exactly one thing. And nothing here makes a caller check the band; the registry's §5 is a rule for
authors, enforced by the proposed leg and by nothing else.

title: Delete the client-side continuity guard: it refuses healthy resumes because oldest_available_cursor is a per-recipient first-delivery marker, not an eviction floor
description:
WHAT: delete `verify_resume_continuity` (`crates/agent-mail-native/src/journey.rs:632-644`) and its
call site inside `resume_from` (`journey.rs:741`). **The fix is a deletion.** It is not a re-tune,
not a better predicate, and it must not be replaced by a client-side approximation.

WHY -- three independent measurements, all verified from version-matched source:
1. **The predicate is wrong about what it reads.** The guard refuses when
   `oldest.advanced_beyond(stored)`. But `oldest_available_cursor` is a **per-recipient
   FIRST-DELIVERY marker**, not an eviction floor: `mcp-agent-mail-db/src/sync.rs:574` is
   `oldest_available_cursor = MIN(seq) WHERE project_id=? AND agent_id=?`. So the guard refuses
   whenever a recipient's first event simply arrived later than the stored position -- **which is a
   healthy resume from origin.** Measured spread across four recipients: floors 2058-5147. A
   baseline of 5105 is simultaneously unresumable for one recipient and fine for another.
2. **The daemon's own refusal is gated on something the client cannot see.**
   `sync.rs:606-624`: `retention_has_pruned = global_oldest_cursor > 1`, and `CURSOR_EXPIRED` fires
   only when that holds -- i.e. only after REAL pruning. `global_oldest` **never leaves the
   daemon**. The client therefore decides expiry with strictly less information than the decider,
   which is the doctrine violation: **a layer must not re-derive a judgement whose deciding input it
   cannot observe.**
3. **The condition it guards against is currently unreachable.** The ledger is contiguous:
   `min(seq)=1, max=5226, count=5226`. `count == max` with `min == 1` proves **zero rows were ever
   removed**, so `retention_has_pruned` is false and `CursorExpired` cannot occur in this store by
   construction.

**THE DOC COMMENT ALREADY CONTAINS THE DEFECT, and this is the part worth reading before touching
the code.** It states the honest limit correctly -- "a cursor below `oldest_available_cursor` cannot
be distinguished from a recipient whose first event simply arrived later" -- and then concludes
**"Refusing is correct in both cases."** That conclusion is the bug. Refusing is correct in the rare
case and wrong in the common one, and the common one is *every first resume from origin*. A guard
that cannot distinguish healthy from expired must not refuse; it must abstain.

DO NOT: add a `global_oldest > 1` check client-side. That was proposed and refused -- the input is
unobservable there. The daemon already enforces it; trust the typed error when it arrives.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. `verify_resume_continuity` deleted. Its call in `resume_from` deleted. `resume_from` still
   returns the recipient-bound `ResumePoint` -- **do not weaken `ResumePoint`**, which is the part
   that works and makes a bare integer unrepresentable.
2. The six existing test assertions at `journey.rs:1215-1257` that exercise the guard: delete the
   ones asserting the refusal, and **replace with a leg asserting a first-resume-from-origin
   SUCCEEDS** where the recipient's floor is above the stored cursor. That leg must FAIL on today's
   code -- run it before deleting the guard and record that it fails. That is the fires-on-known-bad
   proof, and without it the deletion is unattributable.
3. Anti-vacuity: the replacement leg must not pass on an empty page. Zero events is an ERROR.
4. MUTATION: restore the guard -> the new leg goes RED. Restore the deletion byte-identically.
5. `cargo test -p agent-mail-native` green, and say how many legs you deleted vs added.
6. The `lib.rs:66` doc row promising `CURSOR_EXPIRED` behaviour must be corrected in the same
   commit -- it currently describes the client guard. **You hold `lib.rs`; nobody else can fix it.**

NO-CLAIM: deleting this removes a FALSE REFUSAL; it does not add resumability the daemon does not
already provide. When the daemon genuinely prunes, `CURSOR_EXPIRED` still arrives as a typed error
from the authority that can actually see `global_oldest` -- callers must still handle it. This bead
removes a second, wrong copy of that judgement, not the judgement.

title: commit-build-fence CI job cannot produce a verdict — wrong argv AND no registration store on a fresh checkout
description:
## WHAT

The `commit-build-fence` CI job cannot produce a verdict in EITHER direction, and never
could. `gate.yml` invokes:

    cargo run --quiet -p commit-build-fence -- .

`.` is a positional, and the binary's dispatcher only accepts a subcommand. Measured on
run 33583861505, job 100103746904, step "Run cargo run --quiet -p commit-build-fence -- .":

    COMMIT_FENCE_ERROR reason=unknown_command command=.
    usage: commit-build-fence [check|init|register|release] [options]
    Process completed with exit code 2

The obvious repair does NOT fix it. `commit-build-fence` takes its repo via `--repo`
(`crates/commit-build-fence/src/main.rs`, `fn repo_path`), never positionally, so the
corrected form is `check --repo .` — and that also exits 2, measured locally at HEAD:

    $ cargo run -q -p commit-build-fence -- check --repo .
    COMMIT_FENCE_ERROR path=/Users/josh/Developer/omp-orchestrator/.git/omp-build-registration.json reason=registration_store_missing
    exit=2

So the job has two independent defects: the wrong argv, and no registration store in a
fresh checkout. Fixing only the argv swaps one non-verdict for another while LOOKING like
progress — that is why this is a bead and not a one-line edit.

## WHY

This is the pass-1 pathology with a different mask. 67 consecutive CI runs were red
because `asupersync` could not compile on stable; that is now fixed (E0554 appears 0 times
in run 33583861505, and `porting-gate` went from dying at the compile to SUCCESS). But a
job that exits 2 on a usage error is not a gate — it is a red square that carries no
information, and its redness is indistinguishable from a real refusal. The sibling defect
in the same file was `cargo run -p no-shell-gate` with no `--bin`, exiting 101 with
"could not determine which binary to run" on every run since the package grew a second
bin; that one had an unambiguous correct form, was fixed in 5c7ff11, and the step is now
SUCCESS with the job failing at a LATER step on real test content. This one has no such
form, because the store lifecycle has to be designed.

Owner needed: whoever built the fence. The question is what `check` is supposed to mean in
CI, where no build has been registered — Clear, or refused-because-uninitialised. The
answer determines whether the job needs an `init` step, an explicit "no registration is
Clear" branch, or removal from CI.

## ACCEPTANCE

- [ ] Decide and document what `commit-build-fence check` means on a fresh checkout with
      no `.git/omp-build-registration.json`.
- [ ] `gate.yml`'s invocation matches the CLI contract, and the step exits 0 on a clean
      tree and nonzero on a genuinely fenced one.
- [ ] A fires-on-known-bad leg proves the CI-shaped invocation refuses when it should —
      the current job has never once refused for a fence reason, only for an argv reason.
- [ ] Closes with the run id where the step first produced a fence verdict rather than a
      usage error.

## NO-CLAIM

This bead does not claim the fence's LOGIC is wrong — its own suite passes
(`cargo test -p commit-build-fence` is green in run 33583861505; only the
`cargo run` step failed). The defect is the wiring and the fresh-checkout contract, not
the fence.

title: Corpus doc #10: finding_contract with FC-L1..L5 and a 12-leg invariant suite
description:
## WHAT

Document #10 of 78 in `docs/plans/plan_to_write_the_document_corpus.md`. Write
`docs/contracts/finding_contract.md`: the contract for `crates/finding`, stating laws
`FC-L1`..`FC-L5` and pinning, for each, whether the code enforces it TODAY. Ship the invariant
suite `crates/finding/tests/finding_contract.rs`.

Document what IS. Change no crate source; every defect the reading reveals becomes a bead named in
`## Non-Coverage`.

## WHY

`crates/finding` is the mechanism whose entire purpose is that an unfiled gap is impossible, and
`AGENTS.md` names it the sharpest self-indictment in the repo: *"crates/finding — which I wrote
thirty minutes earlier to make an unfiled gap impossible, then bypassed in the next tool call."*
Its five public types carried five laws stated in a header comment and enforced unevenly, with no
contract saying which was which.

Measured while writing it: `Finding::file` had **zero call sites anywhere including tests** and the
`Publisher` trait had **zero implementors**, so the crate's only law-bearing method was unreachable
and had never executed. Three of the five laws turned out to be unenforced.

## ACCEPTANCE

Re-run, do not read:

```
$ cargo test -p finding --test finding_contract
```

Expect **12 passed**. The suite is the first caller of `Finding::file` in the workspace. Legs:

1. `l1_the_only_disposals_are_file_and_waive_and_a_reasonless_waiver_is_refused` — plus a negative
   control refusing a third disposal path.
2. `l1_must_use_is_only_a_warning_and_does_not_survive_option` — pins the measured enforcement
   floor, with a positive control (`unsafe_code = "forbid"` found in 51 manifests) so the zero for
   `unused_must_use` is not a broken reader.
3. `l2_filed_carries_whatever_the_publisher_returned_including_an_empty_id` — PINNED DEFECT.
4. `l2_a_real_bead_shaped_id_round_trips_into_filed_and_retires_the_spool_row` — known-good arm.
5. `l3_the_durable_row_is_on_disk_before_the_publisher_runs` — the ordering PROVED: the test
   publisher reads the spool directory at the moment it is invoked and must see exactly 1 row.
6. `l3_a_publisher_failure_leaves_the_row_recoverable_not_lost` — a failure is DEFERRED, not lost.
7. `l3_respooling_the_same_finding_does_not_duplicate_the_row` — recovery is idempotent.
8. `l3_an_unreadable_spool_dir_is_an_error_not_an_empty_sweep` — anti-vacuity, with a positive
   control on the same reader.
9. `l4_a_finding_cannot_name_a_replacement_today` — PINNED DEFECT with positive control.
10. `l5_a_waiver_carries_no_expiry_so_it_is_permanent_today` — PINNED DEFECT with positive control.
11. `a_planted_incomplete_finding_is_refused_field_by_field` — fires-on-known-bad, 5 arms.
12. `a_complete_finding_is_accepted_and_its_body_carries_the_standard_shape` — known-good.

Mutation leg, run at authoring time and reproducible: in `Finding::file`, swap the publish ahead of
the spool (asserted to exist as exactly one block first). Leg 5 goes RED with "the publisher saw 0
pending row(s); FC-L3 requires exactly 1", and the three other `file()`-exercising legs fail with
it — 8 passed / 4 failed. Restore byte-identical
(sha256 `d8b1e865a1da493755983c1f0dfe0d6d376380da53b414711b189cd88be8bf10`) and all 12 pass.

Structural bar, `docs/contracts/asupersync_process_grade.md`: all seven markers present,
`## Non-Coverage` and `## NO-CLAIM` present, under the 25 KB ceiling. Paste the runner output.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- Any change to `crates/finding/src`. The only manifest change is ONE dev-dependency
  (`asupersync`, same pin) because an integration test cannot see a crate's normal dependencies
  and `file()` takes `&Cx`.
- Fixing the three unenforced laws, or wiring the crate: five separate beads,
  `finding-l1-bypassable-py3`, `finding-l2-unvalidated-id-3j8`, `finding-l4-no-replacement-jz2`,
  `finding-l5-waiver-no-expiry-jex`, `finding-crate-unrouted-ca9q`.

## NO-CLAIM

This contract does not make any caller route through the crate — the zero-caller fact is stated in
`## Non-Coverage` and owned by `finding-crate-unrouted-ca9q`. Three of five laws are documented as
UNENFORCED rather than claimed; a reader who takes `FC-L2`, `FC-L4` or `FC-L5` as a guarantee has
misread the contract, which is why each carries its bead id inline. And the suite proves the laws
for the TYPE, never for its consumers: there are none.

title: The finding crate is unrouted: file() had zero callers and Publisher zero implementors
description:
## WHAT

The `finding` crate is not routed through by anything, and the specific facts are sharper than the
summary. Measured 2026-09-01 via `cargo metadata` (authoritative) and literal greps:

| claim | measured |
|---|---|
| `Finding::file` call sites, whole workspace incl. tests | **0** |
| `Publisher` implementors | **0** — the trait had no implementor, so `file()` was unreachable |
| `Finding::waive` call sites outside the crate's own tests | **0** |
| `pending()` (the recovery sweep) production callers | **0** |
| crates depending on `finding` | **2** — `ack-spine`, `finding-dispatch` |
| of those, crates that IMPORT it | **1** — `finding-dispatch/src/lib.rs:10` |
| `finding-dispatch` dependents | **0** |
| callers of `finding_dispatch::finding_for` | **0** |

So the whole chain is inert: a producer with no caller, feeding a filing path with no
implementation, guarded by a sweep with no operator. `ack-spine/Cargo.toml:22` declares
`finding = { path = "../finding" }` and never imports it — the dependency edge that made this look
wired is an unused dep.

**Correction to the standing account.** The repo's framing is "ZERO production callers", and that
is wrong in one direction and understated in another: there ARE two dependency edges, and the
law-bearing method had zero exercises of any kind, including tests, until
`crates/finding/tests/finding_contract.rs` landed.

## WHY

`AGENTS.md` names this the sharpest self-indictment in the repo: *"crates/finding — which I wrote
thirty minutes earlier to make an unfiled gap impossible, then bypassed in the next tool call."*
BUILT != WIRED, aimed at the mechanism whose entire purpose is to stop gaps from going unfiled. A
crate that exists so an unfiled gap is impossible, and that nothing calls, is itself the unfiled
gap.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. One real caller, end to end. `finding_dispatch::finding_for` already builds complete findings
   from `SupervisorDecision`; wire the supervisor to call it and to `file()` the result through a
   `Publisher` that shells `br create` via `subprocess_contract::run_output`. Then:
   `git grep -c --no-index -F '.file(' -- 'crates/*/src/*'` returns at least 1 outside
   `crates/finding/`.
2. A `Publisher` implementation exists and is tested against a real `br` invocation in a scratch
   `.beads`, expecting a created id that matches the `br` id shape.
3. `cargo test -p finding --test finding_contract` stays at 12 passed — the suite's test publisher
   must keep working alongside the production one.
4. Remove the unused dep: delete `finding = { path = "../finding" }` from
   `crates/ack-spine/Cargo.toml:22`, then `cargo metadata --no-deps` shows `finding` dependents as
   exactly the crates that import it. Do this in its own commit; a manifest edit inside a wiring
   commit hides which change broke the build.
5. The recovery sweep gets an operator: something must call `pending()` on a schedule and finish
   deferred rows, or `FC-L3`'s guarantee is a durable row nobody collects. Name the caller.

## NOT IN SCOPE

The three unenforced laws — `FC-L2` (unvalidated id), `FC-L4` (no replacement), `FC-L5` (no
expiry) — are separate beads. Wiring a crate with three known gaps is still worth more than an
unwired crate with none, so this bead does not wait on them.

## NO-CLAIM

One caller is not adoption. A single wired path proves the mechanism RUNS; it does not prove that
agents route findings through it rather than writing prose, which is the behaviour the crate exists
to change and which no test can assert. That gap closes by measurement over time — count
prose-only gaps per session — not by this bead.

title: FC-L1: must_use does not survive Option<Finding> and unused_must_use is denied nowhere
description:
## WHAT

`FC-L1` — "a gap observed is a gap filed" — rests on `#[must_use]` on `Finding`, and that
enforcement fails in two measured ways. Close both so the obligation cannot be dropped.

1. **`#[must_use]` does not survive `Option<Finding>`, which is the only producer's signature.**
   `finding_dispatch::finding_for(&SupervisorDecision, u32) -> Option<Finding>`
   (`crates/finding-dispatch/src/lib.rs:22`) is the one function in the tree that builds a
   `Finding`. Measured with rustc directly on 2026-09-01:

   ```
   direct();            -> warning: unused `Finding` that must be used
   returns_option();    -> NO WARNING          (fn returns Option<Finding>)
   ```

   So the compiler does not object when a caller of `finding_for` drops the result. The one
   mechanism protecting the obligation is bypassed by the one signature that creates it.

2. **`unused_must_use` is denied nowhere.** No `[workspace.lints]` table exists in the root
   `Cargo.toml`, and no crate manifest sets it. Positive control on the same reader:
   `unsafe_code = "forbid"` is found in **51** manifests. Even the case that DOES fire is a
   warning a build can ignore.

## WHY

The crate's own header says the compiler is the enforcement: *"You cannot have a finding and drop
it — the compiler objects."* Measured, it objects only for a bare `Finding`, only as a warning,
and never through the wrapper the real producer returns. `AGENTS.md` records the author bypassing
this crate in the next tool call after writing it; the type-level guard would not have stopped
that, and now we know why.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Deny the lint: add `[workspace.lints.rust] unused_must_use = "deny"` at the root and inherit it
   in `crates/finding`. Then `cargo test -p finding --test finding_contract` — the leg
   `l1_must_use_is_only_a_warning_and_does_not_survive_option` goes RED naming the manifest count,
   and `docs/contracts/finding_contract.md` §FC-L1 must be updated in the same commit. That leg is
   a PINNED DEFECT: its failure is the signal the fix landed.
2. Close the `Option` hole. Either change the producer to `Result<Finding, NotYet>` /
   `#[must_use] pub enum MaybeFinding { … }`, or have `finding_for` file/waive internally so no
   bare `Finding` crosses the boundary. Then, with a probe of the same shape as the measurement
   above, `rustc` must warn for the producer's return: run
   `rustc --edition 2024 --crate-type lib` over a two-line probe and expect ONE warning per
   dropped result, not zero.
3. A negative leg: a caller that DOES dispose (files or waives) must produce no warning — an
   over-strict lint that fires on correct code gets `#[allow]`-ed and dies.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Routing production code through the crate — that is the unrouted-crate bead. This bead is only
about the obligation being non-bypassable once a `Finding` exists.

## NO-CLAIM

Denying the lint makes dropping a `Finding` a build error in THIS workspace only; a downstream
consumer can still `let _ = …`. And a warning-free build does not prove any gap was filed — it
proves no `Finding` VALUE was dropped, which is a strictly weaker statement than `FC-L1`.

title: FC-L2: Filed accepts any publisher string as a bead id, including empty
description:
## WHAT

`FC-L2` — "`Filed` must name the bead id; a Finding that cannot produce one is unconstructible" —
is **not enforced**. `Finding::file` copies whatever the publisher returns straight into
`Filed { id }` with no validation (`crates/finding/src/lib.rs:219-224`), so a publisher returning
`""` yields a `Filed` claiming a bead that does not exist.

Measured by the contract suite, which asserts today's behaviour so the fix cannot land silently:
`l2_filed_carries_whatever_the_publisher_returned_including_an_empty_id` passes with
`filed.id().is_empty() == true`.

## WHY

`Filed` is the proof object. Every downstream consumer that trusts it — a close-evidence gate, a
grade, a reconciliation ledger — reads the id as "this gap became schedulable work". An empty or
malformed id makes `Filed` a receipt with no referent, which is the same class as this repo's
close-evidence defect where a bead cited a path that never existed. A proof object that can be
constructed around nothing is worse than no proof object, because a reader stops looking.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Add a validated id at the `Filed` boundary — a `BeadId` newtype or a check inside `file` that
   refuses an id which is empty or does not match `<prefix>-<slug>-<suffix>`. Then
   `cargo test -p finding --test finding_contract`: the pinned leg above goes RED and must be
   rewritten to `expect_err`, with §FC-L2 of the contract updated in the same commit.
2. A known-GOOD arm must stay green: the existing
   `l2_a_real_bead_shaped_id_round_trips_into_filed_and_retires_the_spool_row` files
   `omp-orchestrator-finding-contract-abc` and must continue to succeed. An id validator strict
   enough to refuse a real `br` id is a worse defect than the one being fixed.
3. Decide and state what happens to the spool row when the id is refused: it must remain
   `.pending` (a DEFERRED finding), never be marked published. Assert it with a leg of the same
   shape as `l3_a_publisher_failure_leaves_the_row_recoverable_not_lost`.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Verifying the bead EXISTS in the tracker. Shape validation is local and cheap; existence requires
a tracker round-trip and belongs with the publisher implementation.

## NO-CLAIM

A well-shaped id does not prove a bead exists, is open, or is reachable by `bv`. `Filed` will
still be a claim — just one that can no longer be built around an empty string.

title: FC-L4: a Finding cannot name its replacement
description:
## WHAT

`FC-L4` — "a Finding names its REPLACEMENT when it reports something missing" — has **no
representation in the type**. `Finding` carries `what`, `why`, `acceptance`, `labels`, `priority`
and nothing else (`crates/finding/src/lib.rs:106-112`). A finding that reports an absence cannot
name what should be used instead, so the reader must re-derive it.

Measured by `l4_a_finding_cannot_name_a_replacement_today`, which asserts that `replacement`,
`instead_use` and `supersedes` are all absent from the source, with a positive control that
`acceptance`, `labels` and `priority` ARE found.

## WHY

`fh N040`: a replacement claim needs a smoke check at BOTH ends — the new thing works AND the old
caller is gone. This repo's own doctrine states the narrower rule: `AGENTS.md` requires a gate's
output to name "the kernel that should have been used", because "a finding that does not name the
replacement is not actionable". The `finding` crate enforces the bead standard
(WHAT/WHY/ACCEPTANCE/labels) as a type precondition and then omits the field its own repo's rule
requires.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Add the field. It must be OPTIONAL in the type and REQUIRED conditionally: a finding whose
   `what` reports an absence must carry a replacement. Choose the discriminator explicitly — a
   `FindingKind::Missing { replacement: String }` variant is preferable to a free-text sniff,
   because a keyword scan over `what` will misfire.
2. `cargo test -p finding --test finding_contract`: the pinned leg goes RED (its absence
   assertions fail) and must be rewritten to assert presence, with §FC-L4 updated in the same
   commit.
3. Two arms, both asserted: a `Missing`-kind finding built WITHOUT a replacement is refused with a
   named error (`FindingError::MissingField("REPLACEMENT")`); a non-`Missing` finding with no
   replacement is still accepted. Without the second arm the change makes every finding carry
   ceremony it does not need.
4. `finding_dispatch::finding_for` must compile unchanged or be updated in the same commit — it
   is the only producer, and a new required field breaks it silently otherwise.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Checking that the named replacement exists or works. That is the both-ends smoke check `fh N040`
describes, and it belongs to whoever acts on the finding.

## NO-CLAIM

A replacement field does not make the named replacement correct, reachable, or better than what it
replaces. It only makes the finding actionable without a second investigation.

title: FC-L5: a waiver carries no expiry, so it is a permanent silent exemption
description:
## WHAT

`FC-L5` — "WAIVED IS NOT CLOSED: a waiver carries an expiry or it is a silent permanent exemption"
— is **not enforced**. `Waived` carries `body` and `reason` only
(`crates/finding/src/lib.rs:284-287`), and `Finding::waive` requires a reason and nothing else. A
waiver written once is permanent and never resurfaces.

Measured by `l5_a_waiver_carries_no_expiry_so_it_is_permanent_today`, which asserts `expiry`,
`expires`, `revisit_by` and `until` are all absent from the source, with a positive control on
`WaiverNeedsReason` and `pub fn reason`.

## WHY

This repo has already paid for exactly this defect in a neighbouring mechanism.
`crates/no-shell-gate/tests/wired_lanes.rs` records it verbatim: *"An allowance that outlives its
reason is worse than no allowance, because it reads as a considered exception when it is only an
un-revisited one."* Five `UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE` rows sat unchanged while all five acquired
production callers; the gate caught the drift by accounting, not by any row failing.

`Waived` is the same shape with none of the accounting: a reason, no expiry, no sweep, and nothing
that ever asks whether the reason still holds. `waive()` is currently reachable only from the
crate's own tests, so the exemption pile is empty — which makes this the cheapest possible moment
to fix it.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Add an expiry to `Waived`. It must be REQUIRED, not optional — an optional expiry defaults to
   permanent, which is the state being removed. Prefer a `revisit_by` deadline plus a
   `WaiverError::Expired` on read, so a stale waiver is loud rather than silent.
2. `cargo test -p finding --test finding_contract`: the pinned leg goes RED and must be rewritten
   to assert presence, with §FC-L5 updated in the same commit.
3. A sweep, mirroring `pending()`: `expired(waiver_dir) -> Result<Vec<PathBuf>, FindingError>`
   with the SAME anti-vacuity rule — an unreadable directory is an ERROR, never an empty sweep.
   Assert both arms, exactly as `l3_an_unreadable_spool_dir_is_an_error_not_an_empty_sweep` does.
4. Waivers must be durable at all: today `Waived` is an in-memory value that nothing writes to
   disk, so an expiry with no persistence expires nothing. State where a waiver is stored and
   assert a written waiver survives a process boundary, as `SpooledFinding` already does.

## NOT IN SCOPE

Choosing a default window. Name one in the contract when it lands; picking it here would be a
guess with no data.

## NO-CLAIM

An expiry does not make anyone revisit the waiver — it makes the waiver LOUD at a known date. The
sweep still needs a caller, which is the same unrouted-crate problem tracked separately, and
adding an expiry to a mechanism nothing calls raises no floor by itself.

title: 32 pid-only child.kill() sites: a deadline that spares grandchildren poisons the NEXT attempt too
description:
WHAT: ~32 pid-only `child.kill()` sites across 15 crates. A deadline that signals one pid leaves
that child's grandchildren running, reparented to init.

MEASURED 2026-09-01 by crates/no-shell-gate/tests/group_kill.rs (production source only, tests
and subprocess-contract excluded, comments stripped): 32 sites.

WHY IT IS EXPENSIVE, and it is not the obvious reason. AGENTS.md records the measurement:
"orphaned grandchildren (ppid=1, 0.0% CPU) held the admission lock, so every timeout guaranteed
the next attempt also failed - the failure created the condition for its own repetition." The
orphan OUTLIVES the timeout that created it, so the next attempt inherits a poisoned lock and
times out too. A single pid-kill does not cost one failure; it costs every subsequent one until
someone kills the orphan by hand.

WORSE THAN A UNIFORM GAP: several crates signal a GROUP in one function and pid-kill in another
- fast-dispatch, oracle-compare and omp-idle-dispatch all appear in both lists. The
inconsistency is intra-crate, so a reader who checks one call site learns nothing about the next.

THE REFERENCE FIX IS ALREADY IN THE TREE: crates/loop-tick/src/lib.rs. Two halves, and neither
works alone:
  1. process_group(0) at the SPAWN site so the child leads its own group. Without it, `-pid`
     names a group we do not own and the signal goes nowhere useful.
  2. TERM then a graced KILL on `-pid` in the reaper, matching subprocess-contract's
     bounded_output so both paths behave identically, plus a direct child.kill() fallback for
     when the group signal cannot be delivered.

THE TEST THAT PROVES IT, and why the existing suites did not: loop-tick had ELEVEN tests and all
eleven passed both BEFORE and AFTER the fix, because none spawned a grandchild. The new test has
the child spawn a grandchild that touches a marker at t+2s, then sleep 30s; a 200ms deadline must
leave that marker absent. It also asserts the fixture actually timed out, so it cannot pass by
never reaching the deadline. Copy that shape.

ACCEPTANCE, per converted site:
 1. process_group(0) at the spawn site AND a group signal in the reaper. Both, or neither counts.
 2. A grandchild-survival test for the crate, modelled on loop-tick's.
 3. Mutation: revert to child.kill(), confirm the test goes RED naming the marker, restore
    byte-identical.
 4. Lower PID_KILL_CEILING in group_kill.rs by exactly the number of sites converted, in the
    same commit. Never raise it.

NO-CLAIM: the gate counts a TEXTUAL pattern, not cancel-correctness. A site that signals the
group can still be wrong (no deadline, undrained pipes, a child that was never a group leader),
and a child.kill() used as a fallback AFTER a group signal is legitimate - the gate cannot tell
those apart, which is why it ratchets a count rather than asserting a property. Converting all 32
does not by itself make the fleet cancel-correct.

comments.text:
PROGRESS 2026-09-01: 32 -> 31 sites, and the FIRST conversion is done as the reference.

loop-tick converted: run_child now calls subprocess_contract::bounded_status, and the private
64-line wait_deadline duplicate is DELETED (commit 5520f42). spawn_contract 16 -> 15 crates.

THE PATTERN TO COPY, in order:
  1. Read the crate's spawn site AND its wait/kill path together. They are one change.
  2. If it redirects to files, bounded_status is still correct - it sets NO stdio, so caller
     redirects survive. I wrongly believed it "inherits" and nearly skipped this conversion.
  3. Delete the local duplicate. Do not leave it beside the kernel call.
  4. Map TimedOut to a distinct outcome. A killed child has NO exit status.
  5. Test the EXPORTED function, never the private helper - the helper is what you are deleting.
  6. Mutation: break bounded_status's -pid signal upstream; your crate's grandchild test must
     go RED. That is what proves you route through the kernel instead of resembling it.
  7. Lower PID_KILL_CEILING in the SAME commit by exactly the number you converted.

title: Flagship no-shell gate is wired to a workflow that can never run (no git remote)
description:
WHAT: the repo's FIRST hard gate -- no tracked .sh/.py -- is invoked only from .github/workflows/gate.yml (cargo run -p no-shell-gate; cargo test -p no-shell-gate). `git remote -v` RETURNS EMPTY. There is no remote, so the workflow can NEVER EXECUTE. The gate has no runner.

MEASURED 2026-08-31: the gate binary itself is CORRECT. Run by hand it exits 1, names both offending files, and prints 'the exemption list is empty by design; there is no check.sh carve-out'. So this is not a detector defect -- the detector is right and unreachable.

WHAT IT COST, same day: two .sh files were committed into the tree the gate forbids -- scripts/ack-detector.sh (7187210, 12:36) and scripts/heartbeat-check.sh (298afbf, 11:30) -- while README.md hard gate 1 says the gate 'lands BEFORE the first crate is copied' precisely so the mess cannot accumulate. It accumulated anyway, in the repo whose ONE RULE is 'No .sh. No .py. Not in bin/, not in scripts/, not just for testing.'

WHY THIS IS THE MOST EXPENSIVE INSTANCE: AGENTS.md exists to prevent exactly this -- 'A mechanism that is written, tested, adversarially hardened, and invoked by nothing is worth zero.' This session hit BUILT != WIRED twelve times; this is the twelfth and the worst, because this gate defines the repository.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. The gate runs on a trigger THAT EXISTS ON THIS MACHINE, with no remote and no CI service. A pre-commit hook is the candidate; per hook-certification it must be Rust, asupersync-backed, cancel-correct, and registered in hooks_certified.toml. It must NOT be auto-registered -- a hook error reads as DENY and can brick every Write/Edit/Bash fleet-wide.
2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD through the real trigger, not by hand: stage a .sh, attempt the commit, assert refusal. Running the binary directly is what we already had and it did not stop anything.
3. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: a normal Rust-only commit is NOT refused. An over-strict commit gate gets bypassed with --no-verify and then protects nothing.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty scan set is an ERROR. Zero tracked files must not read as a pass.
5. MUTATION: break the extension match, the known-bad leg goes RED; restore byte-identically and report the sha both sides.
6. THE WIRING TEST IS THE DELIVERABLE: assert a live trigger reaches the gate. AGENTS.md prescribes the shape -- an UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE that is EMPTY, where an exception is a named row with a reason, not silence.

NO-CLAIM: a pre-commit hook is bypassable with --no-verify by design. This raises the floor from 'nothing runs the gate' to 'skipping it is an explicit act'. It does not make committing shell impossible, and saying otherwise would be the overclaim this repo refuses.
