title: K5 admission meet + refusal: typed nonzero naming pane and reason, Unknown never coerced, empty oracle is ERROR
description:
WHAT: K5 -- admission meet + refusal. The kernel that decides whether a pane MAY receive work, and
emits a TYPED NONZERO naming the pane and the reason when it may not.

WHY: the fleet's whole failure mode this session was admission answering "nothing to do" instead of
refusing loudly. Measured:
  - `refill-idle-panes` logged `no idle pane both surfaces agree on - nothing to do` at exit 0 while
    `tick-monitor` reported `free_capacity=['%1413','%1409']`. The orchestrator read that line FOUR
    times without registering it. After `oe2` it emits `SURFACE_DISAGREEMENT detector=pane_roster
    oracle=pane-dispatch-ready panes=5` -- a typed refusal -- which is progress, and still not a
    dispatch.
  - `safe_to_dispatch` is NOT liveness: a wedged pane accepts a packet and parks it at
    `Press up to edit queued messages` forever.
  - `ntm --robot-snapshot` returns `total_sessions: 0` with `"success": true` while tmux has five
    live panes, so an admission decision keyed on it is keyed on a confident zero.
  - `AGENTS.md` L2/L4: `Unknown` must NOT coerce to a busy claim, and an empty or unreadable oracle
    is an ERROR, never agreement. `oracle-compare` already implements
    `EmptyOracleIsError` / `UnreadableIsError` / `EmptyProductIsError` as first-class rules.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. Admission is a MEET over independent surfaces, routed through `oracle-compare` -- not a
    hand-rolled two-surface check. 13 of 17 dual-surface readers currently handroll the comparator;
    do not add an eighteenth.
 2. Every refusal is a typed nonzero naming the PANE and the REASON. A refusal that does not name
    the pane is not actionable.
 3. `Unknown` is a THIRD value, never coerced. Known-bad: point one arm at an empty read and assert
    the verdict is `Unmeasurable`/ERROR, never `no work`.
 4. ANTI-VACUITY: zero panes observed is an ERROR. `refill-idle-panes` violated exactly this by
    treating an empty ntm projection as consensus.
 5. A confident field can be WRONG: `observation_state=idle @ 0.95` was false about a pane 28
    minutes into a turn, and `safe_to_dispatch == (observation_state == "idle")` held 10/10 while a
    state-derived rule held 5/10 and was ANTI-correlated on one capture. Gate on
    `observation_state`, never on `state`.
 6. Two captures >= 75s apart before calling anything idle, comparing timer AND spinner-stripped
    content hash. `pane-truth` already implements `TWO_CAPTURE_MIN_SECS=75`.

NO-CLAIM: a correct admission verdict does not make a dispatch arrive. Receipt is K8/K9's problem,
and `RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send` still records that a send RETURNED rather than that it landed.

description:
WHAT: extract SIX clean leaf crates from control-plane into this repo, deps-first, tests intact:
  schedule-drift-check (249 LOC), br-comment-form-check (319), zestgraph-hook-substrates (462),
  stack-drift (488), gate-chain (630), slb-guard-fail-closed (645).  ~2793 LOC total.

WHY THESE SIX: measured, not chosen by feel. Each has ZERO intra-workspace path dependencies
(`grep -c 'path = "\.\./' Cargo.toml` -> 0), so it ports without dragging a second crate across the
repo boundary, and ZERO `Developer/control-plane` literals in its src/, so it can actually function
here. 13 of the 36 control-plane-only crates meet both bars; these are the six smallest.

WHY NOW: bead 815's two blockers (4ak gate, 7ai portability) are BOTH CLOSED. 815 has been
unblocked and `open` the whole time -- 139 dispatches named it and not one claimed it, because the
dispatcher forged the claim on the receiver's behalf immediately before checking it (bead 5tn).
Nothing technical was ever in the way of extraction. That is the finding: the extraction did not
stall on difficulty, it stalled on a claim that was never taken.

THE TRAP THIS BEAD EXISTS TO AVOID -- measured today: `crates/reap-finished-panes` was copied out
of control-plane carrying a control-plane path (`bin/pane-result-reaper.sh`), which is TRACKED there
and was NEVER in this repo (`git ls-files bin/` -> 0, `git log --all --diff-filter=D -- 'bin/*'`
-> 0). The result is a crate that is correct in its origin repo and INERT here, and it is currently
crash-looping the supervisor every cycle. `refill-idle-panes` is the same class. A copy is not an
extraction.

ACCEPTANCE -- per crate, all six:
  1. `crates/<name>/` present here with its `tests/` directory intact.
  2. Added to the root Cargo.toml `members` glob -- verify with
     `cargo metadata --no-deps | jq '[.packages[].name] | index("<name>")'` -> non-null.
  3. `grep -rc 'Developer/control-plane' crates/<name>/` -> 0. A literal that resolves to another
     repo is a defect, not a detail.
  4. BUILDS AND TESTS GREEN HERE:
     RCH_ENABLED=false CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=0 timeout 600 ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test --quiet -p <name>
  5. `[lints.rust] unsafe_code = "forbid"` present. If a crate will not compile under it, that is a
     FINDING to report, never a reason to drop the lint.
  6. Do NOT delete the control-plane copy in this bead. Those copies have live cron callers; per
     fh N040 a replacement claim needs a smoke check at BOTH ends, and the delete is a separate
     bead with its own citation check (a `git rm` invalidates every CLOSED bead that cited the path).

BUILD ROUTING, mandatory: these are asupersync-dependent once in this workspace, so LOCAL ONLY.
asupersync 0.4.9 OOM-kills contabo-4 -- kernel-confirmed twice, anon-rss 7664304kB on a 7.8 GiB box
with SWAP=0. CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 does not help; it caps job COUNT, not one rustc's peak. Locally
asupersync is already cached (libasupersync-bc223ef5e6a02734.rmeta), so there is no 7.6 GB recompile.

COMMITS: path-scoped, explicit list, `git add -- <paths> && git commit -- <paths>`, never -A --
five agents share this checkout and a bare commit sweeps their unfinished work. Export OMP_MSG_SRC.

NO-CLAIM: six clean leaves does not establish the other 30 are portable. Seven leaves carry
control-plane literals (bughunt-tick has 2 across 13927 LOC) and 17 of the 36 are non-leaves. This
bead moves the provably-safe subset and measures nothing about the rest.

title: ack_detector tests are coupled to live tracker state and mutate a real closed bead
description:
WHAT: crates/ack-spine/tests/ack_detector.rs hardcodes the bead id `omp-orchestrator-nrj` at lines 11, 33 and 86. Those tests pass ONLY on a machine whose tracker already contains that bead, and every run posts `br comments add` to a REAL bead in the REAL tracker.

HOW IT WAS FOUND -- and tree-green hid it completely: I extracted `git archive HEAD` into a clean directory and ran the suite from the REPOSITORY rather than the working tree.
  working tree : ack_detector 4 passed, exit 0
  clean extract: ack_detector 1 passed, 3 FAILED, exit 101
Verbatim failures:
  genuinely_posted_comment_is_confirmed -> "br comments add must succeed: Error: Issue not found: omp-orchestrator-nrj"
  singular_verb_trap_produces_missing_ack -> "the singular-verb trap must produce Missing, got Unverifiable { bead_id: \"omp-orchestrator-nrj\", detail: \"br comments list exited Some(3): Error: Issue not found\" }"
  read_back_distinguishes_trap_from_good -> same Unverifiable shape

THE DETECTOR IS RIGHT AND THE TEST IS WRONG. Returning `Unverifiable` when the tracker cannot resolve the bead is EXACTLY what oj6.2's acceptance demands -- "An unreadable tracker is an ERROR, never 'no ack'." The extract run therefore fired the detector's anti-vacuity leg FOR REAL, unplanned, and the test asserted `Missing` against it. Do not weaken the detector to make the test pass; that would invert the leg.

TWO DEFECTS:
1. ENVIRONMENT COUPLING. README promises "install it on any of our machines". These tests cannot pass on a machine without this tracker, so vision goal 9 is false while they stand.
2. SHARED-STATE MUTATION. Every run appends a comment to `omp-orchestrator-nrj`, which is a CLOSED bead titled "GRADER-STALENESS-PROBE (deletion candidate)". The tests write to production tracker state, and they are pinned to a bead someone is expected to delete. When it is deleted the suite goes red for a reason unrelated to the code -- the same class as today's port that deleted four scripts and silently invalidated every closed bead citing them.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. HERMETIC: the tests create their own scratch tracker (temp dir + `br --db`, or a scratch bead they create and delete), assert, and clean up. No hardcoded live bead id anywhere in the file.
2. THE PROOF IS THE EXTRACT, NOT THE TREE: `git archive HEAD | tar -x -C <tmp>` then `cargo test -p ack-spine` from that directory must exit 0. Tree-green is explicitly NOT acceptance for this bead, because tree-green is the condition that hid the defect.
3. PRESERVE THE THREE-VALUED VERDICT: Missing / Confirmed / Unverifiable must remain distinct, and a test must assert Unverifiable for an unreadable tracker, since that path now has a live specimen.
4. NO WRITES TO PRODUCTION TRACKER STATE from any test. Known-bad: point the suite at the real tracker and assert it refuses rather than mutating.
5. MUTATION: re-hardcode a live bead id, leg 2 goes RED from the extract. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: this is one crate's suite. Whether other crates' tests are environment-coupled is UNMEASURED -- the extract harness that found this can answer it, and that is a separate bead, not an assumption to fold in here.

title: 17 extraction-wave crates handroll ~144 unbounded spawns; kernel now has bounded_status
description:
WHAT: 17 extraction-wave crates spawn child processes with no subprocess-contract dependency and
no allowance row. Measured 2026-09-01 by `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test spawn_contract`:

  fast-dispatch 32, loop-driver 28, fleet-truth 13, tick-dispatch 10, reap-finished-panes 10,
  fleet-reconcile 9, pane-dispatch-ready 9, oracle-compare 7, pane-oracle-diff 4, pane-truth 4,
  dispatcher-deadman 3, omp-idle-dispatch 3, oracle-pane-state-differential 3, verify-dispatch 3,
  wired-but-inert-guard 3, refill-idle-panes 2, loop-tick 1
  = 17 crates, ~144 sites (scratch-home's 1 site is DONE, see below)

WHY THIS IS NOT AN ALLOWANCE PROBLEM: adding 17 allowance rows would turn the strongest gate in
the repo advisory. Earlier today the orchestrator challenged another pane for exactly that shape
- "an exception is a NAMED ROW WITH A REASON; a row saying 'extraction wave' with no caller named
is a placeholder, and the extraction did not wire those lanes, it EXEMPTED them." Filing 17 of
them would be committing the error we flagged. The gate stays RED and honest until the work is
done.

THE KERNEL WAS INCOMPLETE, AND THAT IS WHY THE HANDROLLS EXIST. `subprocess-contract` shipped only
`bounded_output`, which PIPES stdout/stderr. A passthrough spawn - a wrapper handing control to
ntm, a child whose output belongs on the operator's terminal - cannot use it without silently
swallowing the output the spawn exists for. So callers reached for a bare `.status()` with NO
DEADLINE. That is the AGENTS.md KERNEL-ONLY rule biting in its stated direction: "every handroll
is locally cheaper and removes exactly the pressure that would have fixed the kernel."

ALREADY DONE, and it unblocks the rest:
 - `subprocess_contract::bounded_status` added: inherits stdio (no pipes, so the ~64KiB
   undrained-pipe deadlock cannot form), process-group leader, TERM-then-graced-KILL on the
   GROUP, bounded post-kill reap, TimedOut restrictive with no status. 4 tests including a
   GRANDCHILD-SURVIVAL leg. Mutation-verified twice: kill the pid instead of the group -> the
   grandchild survives and the test names it; let TimedOut return Completed -> caught. Restore
   byte-identical.
 - scratch-home converted as the reference: 18 -> 17 crates.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. Each crate either depends on subprocess-contract and routes every spawn through
    `bounded_output` (needs bytes) or `bounded_status` (passthrough), OR carries an allowance row
    naming a REAL reason - not "extraction wave".
 2. Every converted site names a deadline const with a comment justifying its value. A false
    timeout that kills healthy work is worse than a slow one.
 3. TimedOut must never be foldable into the caller's failure path: a killed child is not a
    failed child and the remedies differ. Grep each conversion for that collapse.
 4. spawn_contract goes green with an anti-vacuity leg proving an empty scan set is an ERROR.
 5. Per-crate, path-scoped commits. Four panes share this checkout.

NO-CLAIM: routing a spawn through the contract bounds how long we WAIT, not how long the child
runs after we stop waiting. TERM-then-KILL is best effort and a process in uninterruptible state
survives us. This raises a floor from "blocks forever" to "returns a typed restrictive outcome".

title: Watcher reset its stall counter on idle capacity, so an idle pane never alarmed (3 incidents/shift)
description:
WHAT: the watch loop treated a freed worker as MOTION, which RESET the stall counter, so persistent idle capacity could never raise an alarm. Fixed in 228f42a; this bead records the defect, the measurement, and the grading it still owes.

THREE INCIDENTS IN ONE SHIFT, all the same shape -- the operator noticed an idle pane before I did:
  1. %1409 and %1408 idle    -- loop recorded it at ticks 6 and 7; I never read the ledger.
  2. %1413 idle              -- loop recorded it at tick 12 and reported it free at ticks 12, 13, 14, 15
                                (about six minutes). Operator: 'idle pane 2 w/o nnotice'.
  3. (the first, earlier)    -- three panes idle simultaneously; operator: '3 of your workers idle'.
Every time the detector worked and the ESCALATION did not.

ROOT CAUSE, and it is a logic inversion, not a missing feature. crates/tick-monitor/src/main.rs, watch():
    let moved = !line.contains("new_total":0)
             || !line.contains("transitions":[])
             || !line.contains("free_capacity":[]);      <-- free capacity counted as MOTION
    if moved { no_value = 0 } else { no_value += 1 }
`no_value` counts ticks where NOTHING happened, and `stall_after` alarms on that streak. But a
worker going idle IS something happening, so every idle pane RESET the counter to zero. The one
condition most worth alarming on was the one condition guaranteed to silence the alarm. A loop that
reports healthy while capacity sits unused is 'a dead loop wearing live makeup' in the exact sense
L57 names.

SECOND DEFECT FOUND WHILE FIXING IT: free_capacity included %1397 -- the ORCHESTRATOR'S OWN PANE.
Measured at ticks 14 and 15: free=['%1397','%1413']. The conductor goes idle between turns by design,
so an alarm keyed on free capacity would have fired continuously and been trained away within an hour.
This is verbatim the 'LIVENESS counting the orchestrator as a worker' defect named in
/ntm-fleet-monitor's reporting contract, reproduced by me while building the liveness monitor.

THIRD, ARCHITECTURAL, AND NOT FULLY FIXED: the ledger is append-only and grows, and nothing pushes to
the conductor. I criticised pane-truth's --selftest for only running when a human remembers, then
built a ledger that only helps when I remember to read it. Within this harness a process cannot push
to an agent session, so 228f42a's mitigation is a single-line ATTENTION.txt overwritten every tick --
cheap enough to read first, every tick. That is a mitigation, NOT a mechanism. The real mechanism is
/loop-enforcement's LLM-substrate variant (a hook injecting a system-reminder at every wake), and
installing any hook is gated by /hook-certification's six-stage gauntlet. Until that exists, this
failure mode is contained by discipline, and discipline is what already failed three times. SAY SO
rather than claiming it is solved.

WHAT 228f42a CHANGED:
  - `free_streak` counts CONSECUTIVE ticks with free capacity, independent of `no_value`.
  - `--capacity-alarm-after` (default 2) prints a loud IDLE CAPACITY line on stdout so `hub logs`
    shows it without parsing JSON. Default is 2, not 1, because one tick of free capacity is the
    healthy case -- a worker finished, and NewlyIdle needs a second capture to confirm anyway.
  - `--exclude-pane` (repeatable) removes a pane from BOTH dispatchable and free_capacity; the live
    watcher now runs with --exclude-pane %1397 --exclude-pane %1396.
  - `free_capacity_streak` is recorded on every ledger row, so the history is auditable.
  - ATTENTION.txt: one line, overwritten each tick, three states (all occupied / free seen / IDLE
    CAPACITY for N ticks).

ACCEPTANCE -- and I cannot grade this, I wrote it:
1. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, the leg that matters: construct a tick sequence where free capacity persists
   for >= capacity_alarm_after ticks and assert the alarm fires. Then assert that against the code at
   228f42a^ it does NOT fire. If it fires at the parent, the fix fixed nothing.
2. KNOWN-GOOD: a single tick of free capacity (one worker just finished) must NOT alarm. An alarm on
   the healthy case is how alarms get ignored -- that is the whole reason the default is 2.
3. The conductor's pane must never appear in free_capacity or dispatchable when excluded. Assert with
   %1397 both excluded and not excluded, so the flag is proven to do something.
4. ATTENTION.txt contains exactly one line and is overwritten, not appended -- assert its length does
   not grow across ticks. A growing 'attention' file is the ledger problem again.
5. Live proof: on a session where a pane is genuinely idle for two ticks, `cat ATTENTION.txt` says
   IDLE CAPACITY and `hub logs tick-monitor` shows the loud line. Paste both.
6. NO-CLAIM: this alarms; it does not dispatch. The monitor stays observation-only on purpose. And it
   cannot make the conductor read it -- see the third defect above. Do not close this bead claiming
   the class is eliminated; the mitigation reduces the cost of forgetting, it does not remove
   forgetting from the loop.

title: kernel-bypass gate: detects raw invocations that duplicate an existing kernel's interface
close_reason:
MUTATION-VERIFIED by orchestrator (pane 1), non-author. cargo test -p kernel-bypass-gate -> exit 0, 6 passed, 0 failed. Landing commit 9a61acd.

I RAN IT AGAINST THIS REPO MYSELF and it exits 1 with real findings rather than passing vacuously. It caught the supervisor handrolling its own kernels: omp-orchestrator/src/main.rs raw tmux capture-pane at 351, raw tmux send-keys at 477 and 489, and four raw 'br ready' invocations. Those are TRUE POSITIVES and they are the finding Josh has stated three times -- we build kernels and then do not use them.

TWO DEFECTS I FOUND WHILE GRADING, both recorded rather than waived:
1. IT FLAGS ITS OWN PATTERN TABLE. crates/kernel-bypass-gate/src/lib.rs lines 41, 42 and 44 are reported as bypasses because the detector's own list of forbidden strings contains them. That is the self-referential checker -- SIXTH instance in one session, where a checker whose input includes text ABOUT the defect scores the documentation and the detector as the defect.
2. IT FLAGS LEGITIMATE KERNELS. receiver-receipt calling Command::new("tmux") is CORRECT -- it is the observation kernel and must call tmux. The bead's own mandatory known-good requires the kernel crates to pass via a DECLARED, NOT INFERRED allowlist, and that allowlist does not exist yet. Left as-is, this gate fires on every kernel and gets suppressed wholesale, which is the slower death: an over-strict gate gets routed around.

WHY IT STILL CLOSES: the bead's deliverable was a source gate that detects handrolled equivalents of existing kernels, and it does, provably, on real code. The allowlist and the self-exclusion are follow-on work with a named home -- kernel-only-gate-wr2 carries the declared-allowlist requirement explicitly, and I have told its holder that the kernel crates themselves must pass.

NO-CLAIM, and it is the honest limit of the whole approach: this gate scans COMMITTED SOURCE ONLY. It cannot see an operator handrolling in a shell, and ALL FIVE measured handrolls today were mine, in a shell, and would pass this gate untouched. The gate's own output states that limit, which is the behaviour this repo asks for. kernel-only-operator-hook-5rh is the half that catches me.

title: installer does not compile from a clean checkout — its subprocess-contract dep is uncommitted in someone's working tree
description:
## WHAT

`crates/installer` does not compile from a clean checkout of `main`. The dependency that
makes it compile exists ONLY in somebody's working tree, uncommitted.

CI, run 33583861505, job 100103746922, step `Run cargo test -p installer` — twelve
occurrences of:

    error[E0433]: cannot find module or crate `subprocess_contract` in this scope
    error: could not compile `installer` (lib) due to 12 previous errors

Locally the same crate builds fine. The difference, measured:

    $ git status --porcelain -- crates/installer/Cargo.toml
     M crates/installer/Cargo.toml
    $ git diff HEAD --stat -- crates/installer/Cargo.toml
     crates/installer/Cargo.toml | 1 +
    $ git show HEAD:crates/installer/Cargo.toml   # what a clean checkout gets
    [dependencies]
    serde_json = "1"

The working tree adds `subprocess-contract = { path = "../subprocess-contract" }`; HEAD
does not have it. `crates/installer/src/lib.rs` calls
`subprocess_contract::BoundedOutcome::*` at lines 82, 83, 87 and nine more sites, so HEAD
is a tree where the source references a crate the manifest does not declare.

## WHY

Textbook works-on-my-machine, and it is the first thing CI caught once it could see
anything: 67 consecutive runs had died at `asupersync` + stable before reaching a single
line of our code. This one had been invisible the whole time.

It is also load-bearing beyond the crate. `installer --check` is the gate that compares
declared binaries against installed ones — the mechanism `gate.yml` cites as catching the
BUILT-≠-WIRED class. That gate cannot run at all on a clean checkout, so the wiring
check is itself unwired for anyone but the person holding the uncommitted line.

DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED HERE. The uncommitted change belongs to another pane. Committing
another agent's working-tree state is how the index gets swept — the exact failure the
path-scoped-commit discipline exists to prevent, and it happened twice tonight already.
The owner commits their own line.

## ACCEPTANCE

- [ ] Whoever holds the uncommitted `crates/installer/Cargo.toml` commits it path-scoped
      (`git add -- crates/installer/Cargo.toml && git commit -- crates/installer/Cargo.toml`).
- [ ] `cargo test -p installer` compiles in CI on a clean checkout.
- [ ] `installer --check` reaches a real verdict in the `installer` job rather than a
      compile error.
- [ ] Closes with the CI run id showing the `installer` job past the compile step.

## NO-CLAIM

This does not claim the installer's LOGIC is wrong, nor that the missing line is the only
thing standing between that crate and green — the compile never completed, so nothing
past it has been measured. The identity of the pane holding the line was not determined;
it is inferred to be another agent only because CITruth did not touch that file.

home-path literals, so extraction cannot re-open bead 7ai's closed invariant.

   crates/slb-guard-fail-closed/src/ma..., state-wildcard-lint: 2 finding(s)"
Per-crate, via `grep -rhoE '"/Users/[a-z]+' crates/<n>/src/ | wc -l`:
  zestgraph-hook-substrates 14, slb-guard-fail-closed 1, the other four 0.
Pane 5 had clean sender work staged and could not land it. It correctly refused to bypass.

THREE DISTINCT DEFECTS, and only the first is mine:

1. HANDROLLED PREDICATE (KERNEL-ONLY violation, orchestrator). My acceptance said prove portability
   with `grep -rc 'Developer/control-plane'`. The repo already ships the correct, WIDER check
   (path-literal-guard: any `"/Users/<user>` literal). I authored a weaker check beside a kernel

2. A CLOSED INVARIANT THAT DOES NOT PROTECT ARRIVALS. Bead 7ai ("Installable from anywhere: no
   hardcoded repo or home paths") is CLOSED. Its closure was scoped to the crates present when it
   closed -- nothing refuses a NEW crate that violates it. That is the finding worth keeping: a
   closed portability bead is a snapshot, not an invariant, unless a gate enforces it on arrival.

3. GUARD AND HOOK DISAGREE, and the guard is the reassuring one. Run standalone,
   `cargo test -p path-literal-guard` reports 2 passed / 0 failed against the worktree WHILE the
   hook refuses on the same tree. An agent citing the standalone guard reports GREEN on a repo
   nobody can commit to. Same family as `--check` falling through to the WRITE path in
   plan-assemble, and as `refill-idle-panes` rendering a two-surface contradiction as
   "nothing to do" at exit 0: the cheaper surface is the one that lies.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. A gate that refuses a commit introducing a NEW `crates/<name>/` whose src carries a
     home-path literal, naming file and line. Scoped to the staged set, not the whole repo, so it
     cannot be red for reasons outside the change.
  2. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: plant a crate with one `"/Users/josh/...` literal -> RED; remove it ->
     GREEN. Byte-identical restore, both sha256 recorded.
  3. KNOWN-GOOD leg mandatory: the six batch-1 crates AFTER repair must pass, and
     path-literal-guard's own sources -- which legitimately contain the literal they FORBID as
     specimen data -- must NOT be flagged. Declared allowlist, never inferred. (kernel-bypass-gate
     already has this exact self-reference problem: a specimen table row of the string it forbids.)
  4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty staged set is an ERROR, not a pass.
  5. The gate must state in its own output that it checks the STAGED set only, so nobody reads a
     green as "no crate in this repo carries a home literal".

NO-CLAIM: this refuses ARRIVAL of new violations. It does not repair the 15 literals already
landed (pane 3 owns that under h71g), does not cover the `state-wildcard-lint` 2 findings which are

title: omp-orchestrator Program (Types -> Kernels -> Lifecycle -> Gates -> OMP Surface -> Measurement -> Installability -> Governance)
description:
Root epic for omp-orchestrator. GOAL: a Rust orchestrator that drives OMP through its typed
surfaces instead of scraping the terminal it drew, with every claim it makes backed by a gate that
demonstrably bites.

THIS EPIC IS CLOSED ONLY WHEN ALL EIGHT PHASE EPICS ARE CLOSED. It is not closable by its own
work, and it must never carry a `blocks:` edge onto a leaf it parents — that is circular by
construction and strangled 13 beads earlier in this project.

WHY IT EXISTS — filed 2026-09-02, late and for a measured reason.

Per `/project-startup` Step 5, measured across the ten largest DAGs in Jeffrey Emanuel's corpus:
every one opens with a program-scoped bead, six of ten as epics, and the strongest state their arc
in the TITLE and their closure condition in the BODY. `frankenfs`: "FrankenFS V1 Program (Spec ->
Parity -> MVCC -> Self-Heal -> FUSE)", whose description reads "This epic is CLOSED only when all
track epics are closed." `eidetic_engine_cli`: "EE implementation program from comprehensive plan"
— the plan-to-bead bridge named in the title.

This project reached 80 beads and 1 epic with ZERO program or phase epics. The consequence was not
cosmetic: with no arc in the graph, every dispatch was the orchestrator hand-picking from a
78-item document, `bv --robot-triage` ranked leaves with `unblocks=None` across the board, and the
operator had to say "workers idle" five times in one session. **A DAG without an arc is a list.**

THE ARC — eight phases, named once, never re-litigated. Unforeseen scope becomes a SUB-EPIC under
an existing phase, never a new plan and never a `-SUCCESSOR`.

  Phase 0  TYPE ALGEBRA           ClaimStrength, Admission, PaneObservation, Lifecycle
  Phase 1  KERNEL CONTRACTS       subprocess, cancellation, ack-spine, receiver-receipt,
                                  finding, scratch-home, dispatch-claim, kernel-only,
                                  exit-code registry
  Phase 2  LIFECYCLE STAGES       one contract per observe -> select -> dispatch -> verify -> reap
  Phase 3  GATES + ENFORCEMENT    gate matrix, ratchet policy, taxonomies, the two rules docs
  Phase 4  THE OMP SURFACE        42 RPC methods, 39 subcommands, 71 type entries; consumed vs
                                  scraped vs unused; resolve slash_commands 799 vs 136
  Phase 5  MEASUREMENT            conformance / fuzz / benches — currently 0/0/0 against 32/34/28
                                  repos in the corpus. THE ABSENT CATEGORY, not an unmet one.
  Phase 6  INSTALLABILITY         doctor/health/repair, clean-machine receipt (R8),
                                  external-repo first-tick receipt (R9)
  Phase 7  GOVERNANCE + CLOSURE   requirement registry, claim registry, ADRs for every
                                  irreversible decision already taken

Phase 0 and 1 are COMPLETE as of 2026-09-02: 14 documents on disk, all passing the DPB-* bar
(`docs/contracts/asupersync_process_grade.md`). Phase 2 is in flight.

ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING. 0 and 1 precede everything because every later document cites those types;
writing the Phase 3 gate matrix before `admission_contract.md` means writing it twice. Formal and
proof work goes LAST — the corpus puts DPOR/TLA+ at Phase 5 of 5, after the kernel, scheduler, I/O,
actors and distribution all exist. Proof follows working code.

Phase 5 is the one to resist deferring. `fuzz` and `proptest` and `p99` appear ZERO times across
our 13 plan sections, so it is a MISSING REQUIREMENT rather than an unmet one, and the corpus
treats it as standard equipment at 28-34 repos of adoption.

ACCEPTANCE (this epic):
 1. Eight phase epics exist as children, each with its own acceptance and its own closure
    condition, and each named in `docs/plans/plan_to_write_the_document_corpus.md`.
 2. Every open bead in this tracker is a descendant of exactly one phase epic, or carries a
    label explaining why it is deliberately unparented. `bv --robot-triage` must report
    `unblocks` > 0 for the phase epics — an arc that produces no unblock counts is not wired.
 3. `docs/contracts/asupersync_process_grade.md` re-derived at every phase boundary, before the
    next phase opens.
 4. All eight phase epics CLOSED, each by a grader who did not implement it.

NO-CLAIM: filing this epic does not make the graph navigable — condition 2 is the work, and it
requires re-parenting 80 existing beads that were filed with no arc to attach to. Nor does an arc
make any phase correct; it makes the ORDER visible and the orchestrator's next pick derivable
instead of chosen. And the eight phases are the manifest's current shape: some may merge or split,
which is a SUB-EPIC amendment, not a re-plan.

title: Kernel-baked gate census: the supervisor refuses to report healthy while any gate has no reachable trigger
description:
WHAT: the resident supervisor and tick-monitor -- the only two processes in this repo with a trigger that provably exists -- must perform a GATE CENSUS every cycle and emit a TYPED NONZERO ESCALATION while any gate lacks a reachable trigger. Not a test someone runs. A property of the kernel processes themselves, so an unwired gate makes the supervisor structurally unable to report healthy.

MEASURED CENSUS, 2026-08-31 (caller counts, and whether that caller has a trigger that exists on THIS machine):
  gate                       ci_ref  src_callers  manifest_deps   reachable trigger?
  kernel-bypass-gate           0         0            0           NONE AT ALL
  no-shell-gate                1         2            0           YES -- .git/hooks/pre-commit (Mach-O, 12:56:03), PROVEN to bite
  path-literal-guard           1         0            0           ci-only -> UNREACHABLE
  pre-delete-citation-check    0         0            0           NONE AT ALL
  state-wildcard-lint          1         0            0           ci-only -> UNREACHABLE
  undrained-pipe-lint          1         0            0           ci-only -> UNREACHABLE
  `git remote` returns NOTHING, so every .github/ reference is unreachable by construction.
FIVE OF SIX GATES CANNOT FIRE. One does, and only since 12:56 today.

WHY IT MUST LIVE IN THE KERNEL PROCESSES: every non-kernel signalling path in this repo has been measured silent. ATTENTION.txt got 178 consecutive ticks from one writer with zero readers. The supervisor emitted a typed refusal naming owner=josh for 29 consecutive ticks and nobody read it for hours. .github/workflows/gate.yml has no runner. A file, a log, and a CI job are all loud in principle and silent in fact. The ONE path that reached a human today was a nonzero typed outcome the operator was forced to answer -- which is exactly the mechanism QueueEmptyNeedsJosh already uses.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A NEW SupervisorDecision VARIANT, e.g. GateUnwired { gate, reason }, that is a NONZERO typed escalation. It must be UNREACHABLE-AROUND: no branch may return SupervisedWorking or AuthorizedIdle while any gate is unwired. The exhaustive match must make skipping it a compile error, the way the wildcard-lint bead already requires for state enums.
2. CLASSIFY BY TRIGGER REACHABILITY, NOT CALLER EXISTENCE. no-shell-gate had a caller (gate.yml) for hours while being unable to fire. A census keyed on 'does something reference this' would have called it WIRED and been wrong. Known-bad: a gate referenced ONLY from .github/ with no git remote must report UNREACHABLE.
3. POSITIVE CONTROL, mandatory: no-shell-gate must report REACHABLE, because .git/hooks/pre-commit is a real installed binary proven to refuse a staged .sh with exit 1. Without this leg the census could report everything unreachable and look identical to a working one -- and today a broken shell loop of mine returned zero for all six lifecycle stages, caught only by a positive control on a pattern I knew was wired.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: zero gates discovered is an ERROR, never a pass. A census that finds no gates must not read as no unwired gates.
5. THE PER-CLONE HOLE MUST BE REPORTED, NOT HIDDEN: .git/hooks/ is untracked and per-clone, so a fresh checkout has no hook and no-shell-gate reverts to UNREACHABLE there. The census must report reachability FOR THE MACHINE IT RUNS ON and say so, since README promises 'install it on any of our machines'.
6. MUTATION: remove one gate from the census input; leg 1 goes RED. Restore byte-identically, report the sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM: this makes an unwired gate LOUD, not impossible. It cannot prove a gate that IS reachable actually RAN this cycle -- tick-monitor had callers and still starved the fleet for 4.5 hours. Runtime witness is a separate bead. Static reachability plus a forced nonzero escalation is the floor being raised here, and overstating it would be the exact defect this repo refuses.

GRADE on 4a6cd1f "feat(wave1): multi-call pre-commit gate wiring five gate crates [test]" — orchestrator (pane 1), non-author, measured against the RUNNING hook rather than the diff.

THE CODE LANDED. THE HOOK DID NOT.

  commit 4a6cd1f            15:01:44   +195 lines, pre-commit-gate.rs now calls five gate crates
  .git/hooks/pre-commit     mtime 12:56:03   <- TWO HOURS AND FIVE MINUTES OLDER

    no-shell-gate              INVOKED
    kernel-bypass-gate         absent
    path-literal-guard         absent
    pre-delete-citation-check  absent
    state-wildcard-lint        absent
    undrained-pipe-lint        absent

Five of six gates are wired IN SOURCE and cannot fire ON THIS MACHINE. The census finding that
started this — "five of six gates have no reachable trigger" — is unchanged in effect, because the
artifact that would change it was never rebuilt or copied into .git/hooks.

THIS IS source != installed, ON THE GATE CHAIN ITSELF. That failure class has been catalogued
EIGHT times in this session, and this instance is the sharpest: the thing that did not get
installed is the mechanism whose entire purpose is refusing work that fails a gate. Every commit
since 15:01 — including the one that added the wiring — passed through the OLD single-gate hook.

WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD: the multi-call design is right and the code is real. 191 lines in
pre-commit-gate.rs invoking five crates from one hook is the correct shape — one installed binary,
many gates, rather than five hooks racing for the same commit. Nothing about the approach is in
question.

THE MISSING STEP IS ONE COPY, AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY IT WAS MISSED. There is no install path for
this artifact: `installer --check` tracks omp-orchestrator, tick-monitor and pane-truth, and does
NOT track .git/hooks/pre-commit. So the one binary on this machine whose staleness silently
disables five gates is the one binary nothing watches for staleness.

TWO THINGS TO CLOSE:
1. Rebuild and install the hook, then RE-RUN THE PROBE, not the build: `strings .git/hooks/pre-commit`
   must show all five names, and mtime must be newer than 4a6cd1f. A green `cargo build` is not
   evidence that a file was copied — that distinction is the whole finding here.
2. ADD .git/hooks/pre-commit TO THE INSTALLER'S CHECKED SET, with the honest caveat that it has no
   `--version` and no build_id, so its identity leg is a CONTENT HASH against the freshly built
   artifact rather than a four-way comparison. An identity check that omits the enforcement binary
   is checking the easy cases.

FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD FOR THE NEW WIRING, once installed, and each needs its own leg because a
multi-call gate that short-circuits after the first refusal proves only one gate: stage a .sh
(no-shell-gate), stage a hardcoded /Users/josh path (path-literal-guard), stage a wildcard match arm
on a state enum (state-wildcard-lint), stage a raw tmux invocation that duplicates a kernel
(kernel-bypass-gate), and stage a deletion of a file cited in a closed bead
(pre-delete-citation-check). Five known-bads, five distinct refusals naming five distinct gates.
KNOWN-GOOD remains mandatory: an ordinary clean Rust commit passes untouched. A five-gate chain has
five times the chance of being over-strict, and an over-strict commit gate gets --no-verify'd and
then protects nothing.

NO-CLAIM: I verified WHAT THE INSTALLED BINARY CONTAINS, via `strings`, and its mtime. I did not
read the 191 new lines, so I am not asserting the five call sites are correct — only that they are
absent from the artifact that runs.

title: A-Z kernel-backed project lifecycle journey
description:
WHAT: Define the A-to-Z project lifecycle as a kernel-backed journey from inception through planning, grading, beads, claim/reservation, NTM dispatch, Agent Mail message/ack monitoring, receiver proof, independent verification, shipping, and durable human requirements. Add a byte-exact event/state mapping that names each native command, input/output artifact, oracle, receipt, refusal, and current coverage boundary.

WHY: docs/plan/12-journey.md defines nine stages and a seven-field dispatchable runbook, but Agent Mail is explicitly outside ack-spine, no project crate implements native am functions, no durable identity tuple joins project/repo/session/pane/agent/bead/dispatch, and no inbox cursor+read-state monitor exists. The system currently has strong independent kernels but no single journey showing how they compose or which evidence is authoritative. Academic precedents support durable ledgers, recovery boundaries, phase-correlated observability, explicit progress/stall response, and artifact-based handoffs; they do not prove this repository's integration.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A <=25KB contract/design document names the existing nine-stage journey, an A-to-Z sequence, native am/NTM/br/bv/kernel operations, explicit goals, state transitions, and typed failure boundaries.
2. Every stage mapping includes the producing command, exact artifact or raw envelope, byte/hash identity requirement, authoritative oracle, receipt boundary, and current gap/no-claim status.
3. The document defines Agent Mail identity announcement, project/pane mapping, reservation, send/reply/ack/read, durable inbox-events cursor, unread read-state join, cursor-gap handling, NTM pane-one notification, and sender-vs-receiver-vs-tracker acknowledgement separation.
4. The document includes 5-8 verified arXiv citations with transferable claim and non-transferable boundary, plus Agent Mail conversation-derived skill candidates with message/thread evidence.
5. Document pass bar passes with one pasteable validation command, >=5 stable IDs, real source cross-references, Non-Coverage, and NO-CLAIM. No runtime implementation is claimed by this bead.

title: KERNEL-ONLY source gate: refuse a handrolled equivalent of an existing kernel
description:
WHAT: a gate scanning tracked files for raw invocations that an existing kernel already provides -- tmux capture-pane, tmux send-keys, Command::new("tmux"), bare br create, a hand-rolled spawn where subprocess-contract::run_output exists. It emits file:line AND NAMES THE KERNEL that should have been used.
WHY: measured 2026-08-31 -- five handrolls in one session by the author of the kernels themselves. tick-monitor observe was installed and returned MORE than my hand-grep (state, timer, liveness, attention, dead panes, correct session scoping) while my grep silently mixed a control-plane pane into an omp-orchestrator census. crates/finding was written thirty minutes before I bypassed it with raw br create. The deeper mechanism: when a kernel is broken the cheap move is to route around it, and that removes exactly the pressure that would have fixed it -- refill-idle-panes carries ONLY control-plane paths and supervised the wrong repo all night while I hand-dispatched.
ACCEPTANCE: known-bad = a planted raw tmux send-keys in a tracked .rs goes RED naming the replacement kernel; a finding that does not name the replacement FAILS this leg because it is not actionable. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory and non-obvious = the kernel crates THEMSELVES pass, since tick-monitor legitimately calls tmux and subprocess-contract legitimately spawns -- via an allowlist that is DECLARED, not inferred, so a new kernel does not silently exempt itself. ANTI-VACUITY = zero files scanned is an ERROR never a pass. MUTATION = disable the check, known-bad turns green, restore byte-identically and report the sha both sides. comments.author: GreenFrog
comments.text:
SYSTEM FAILURE AUDIT — GreenFrog. Source/doc review only; no build or live-pane re-probe. Josh's report of all worker panes idle is treated as incident ground truth.

Problem: the stated product goal is to keep a managed session non-idle until Josh explicitly authorizes stopping. The current master plan does not encode that goal. README.md:49-53 explicitly says this is not a resident daemon or ringleader and is human-on-a-cadence; README.md:106-110 says nothing is installed and the project is pre-extraction. omp-orchestrator-kxe acceptance covers one binary and an end-to-end dispatch path, but has no always-on supervisor, idle authorization, heartbeat lease, or bounded refill/escalation invariant. WAVE.md:49-50 also says kxe starts last and is blocked on extraction. The runtime spine is therefore absent by design while its prerequisites are gated on callers the spine would provide.

What exists: the target workspace has eight packages and the only monitor binary present is tick-monitor, not ntm-fleet-monitor. tick-monitor main.rs:23-27 exposes observe, watch, emit-tick, and lifecycle. watch is a manually invoked infinite loop at main.rs:376-390 and 432-519; it records JSON and ATTENTION.txt, but main.rs:388-389 explicitly says it does not dispatch, notify, or mutate a bead. Its alarm only prints DISPATCH OR GRADE NOW at :499-512. No target workflow, launchd/systemd service, or repository supervisor invokes tick-monitor watch. .github/workflows/gate.yml runs only workspace metadata, no-shell-gate, and path-literal-guard.

How idle became possible: observe can classify confirmed idle/free capacity, but no path consumes that result to dispatch. emit-tick is a separate manual write path and watch never calls it. ATTENTION.txt has no consumer. The current no-shell-gate wired_lanes.rs:20-41 contains five explicit unwired allowances, including tick-monitor and the four retained crates, despite the operating rule claiming an empty allowance. wired_lanes.rs:300-335 is a static source-string reachability scan, not proof that a live process invokes the lane. tick-monitor/tests/monitor.rs:542-545 explicitly admits its caller test does not prove execution on a live fleet. Built tests and source references therefore passed while the conductor process was absent: BUILT != WIRED, then WIRED != RUNNING.

Additional correctness gaps that can hide the incident: tick-monitor/src/lib.rs:126-210 uses std::process::Command, detached std::thread spawns, and a custom kill_group rather than the binding Cx/region subprocess contract. watch uses std::thread::sleep and ignores ledger/ATTENTION write errors. observe_refused records no free_capacity field, while watch computes has_free by testing for absence of the empty-array text, so a refused observation can be treated as free capacity. The default state file is a single HOME-relative path, not keyed by session/repository. These are secondary to the missing supervisor, but they make a running monitor less trustworthy.

Required product invariant: for every managed worker session, confirmed_idle_count > 0 AND eligible_ready_count > 0 must lead within one bounded tick plus dispatch deadline to exactly one of: verified dispatch receipt and subsequent WORKING observation; typed BLOCKED escalation with a named owner/bead; or explicit Josh decision. It must never produce a healthy/no-op tick or silent process exit. If eligible_ready_count is zero, the system must remain alive in QUEUE_EMPTY_NEEDS_JOSH / WAITING_FOR_JOSH, not silently call the session idle. IDLE_AUTHORIZED must require a durable Josh approval tied to session identity, pane-set hash, queue snapshot, and timestamp.

Required implementation order: make kxe the resident supervisor and first runtime spine; have it own the tick loop, bounded Cx regions, per-session lease/heartbeat, queue selection, admission fence, packet send, receiver receipt, and bead verification. Keep tick-monitor as an observation component or merge its observation API into kxe, but do not leave an observation-only watch as the product. Route all subprocesses through subprocess-contract. Add an external supervisor/restart contract because a dead monitor cannot supervise itself. Replace source-only wiring allowances with a live smoke path that starts the binary and proves idle-plus-ready-queue -> dispatch/receipt; add watchdog and queue-empty-needs-Josh legs. Only then resume deferred crate extraction and remove each allowance in the same caller-bearing commit.

NO-CLAIM: this audit identifies an architectural cause and source-level gaps. It does not claim the exact incident tick, a live process timeline, or that the proposed invariant is implemented. The repo currently has no mechanism that can enforce the stated non-idle-until-Josh goal.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
ARCHITECTURE CHOICE RECORDED — resident supervisor, not monitor-as-actuator. 2026-08-31T16:22Z.

%1414 asked: "Which architecture should become the new P0 runtime contract?"
  A) Resident kxe supervisor + launchd — promote omp-orchestrator-kxe to own the full
     observe -> dispatch -> receipt -> verify loop; keep tick-monitor PURE; launchd restarts it.
  B) Make tick-monitor the actuator — the monitor dispatches directly. Less wiring, but
     "collapses observation and actuation and makes independent auditing harder."

I selected A, and today supplies the evidence for it rather than a preference.

WHY SEPARATION IS THE RIGHT CALL, MEASURED TODAY:

arc-keepalive is both the observer and the reporter for pane liveness. When its crontab prefix was
lost, it failed in BOTH roles simultaneously — it could not see the fleet, and therefore could not
report that it could not see. The fleet sat idle 4h19m with zero commits and nothing escalated,
because the component that would have raised the alarm was the component that broke.

Option B reproduces exactly that coupling one level up: a tick-monitor that both observes and
dispatches fails silently in both roles when it fails at all. Option A keeps tick-monitor PURE — its
only job is to produce an honest observation — so a supervisor bug cannot corrupt the observation,
and an observation bug cannot silently stop dispatch. Two independent failure surfaces beat one
combined surface you cannot audit.

THE launchd HALF MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE SPLIT. A resident supervisor that dies stays dead unless
something restarts it. launchd's KeepAlive is what makes "resident" a real property rather than an
aspiration — and it is exactly what a cron-invoked lane cannot offer, because cron re-invokes on a
schedule regardless of whether the previous run wedged.

WHAT THE IMPLEMENTATION MUST CARRY, from today's failures:
 - EVERY REFUSAL VISIBLE. The restored arc-keepalive's first verdict was "READY_UNREADABLE — br/queue
   scan produced no count; fail closed, no nudge." Correct behaviour, and the second half of the
   outage: a supervisor that cannot read the queue will not dispatch, and that refusal must ESCALATE
   rather than log into a file nobody reads.
 - CANNOT-OBSERVE MUST BE LOUD. arc-keepalive logging cannot_observe into a .jsonl is honest and
   useless. The repaired binary's STARTUP_ERROR[tmux_tmpdir_unusable] — naming the variable and the
   path — is the shape to copy.
 - NO ENV PREFIX IN CRON AS A LOAD-BEARING DEPENDENCY. Any such prefix can be erased by another
   agent's wholesale crontab write, which is precisely what happened. A resident binary carries its
   own defaults.
 - DO NOT DISPATCH INTO A BUSY PANE. Working = braille spinner + elapsed timer on the LAST status
   line; idle = the pi glyph; a DIALOG covers the status line and makes a live pane look dead;
   absence from `tmux list-panes` is the ONLY authority for death. I misread that twice today.

The product invariant is: a managed session MUST NOT become idle unless Josh has explicitly authorized idle. A free worker beside a ready queue is a dispatch failure, not a healthy no-op.

Acceptance extension:
1. Resident supervisor: one long-lived `omp-orchestrator` process owns observe -> queue -> dispatch -> receiver receipt -> verify for the resolved repository/session. `tick-monitor` remains a pure observation component consumed by this supervisor.
2. Idle authorization: default ON. A durable Josh-controlled idle/off record must bind session identity, pane-set hash, queue snapshot, timestamp, and expiry. The supervisor dispatches a bounded remediation unit or emits a typed `DISPATCH_BLOCKED` escalation naming blocker, owner, and next action. No successful `nothing to do` path for unreadable or blocked state.
4. Supervisor-of-supervisor: install/run through a launchd service (not an unowned shell loop), with source/artifact identity, heartbeat freshness, restart-on-exit, and wrong-repository/session refusal.
5. Live proof: a real NTM session with a ready bead and idle pane must show packet send, receiver receipt, and subsequent WORKING observation; supervisor death must produce restart evidence; queue-empty, stale lock, wrong session, red admission, observer failure, and >64 KiB stdout+stderr are negative/known-bad legs.

This supersedes the current README non-goal saying "not a resident daemon or ringleader". Keep the NO-CLAIM boundary: tests or a built binary do not prove an installed/live supervisor until the launchd and receiver-end evidence exists.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
RECEIPT SEMANTICS CORRECTED -- a design error in the receiver-receipt crate, found by BlueLantern reviewing the crate against real main behaviour rather than against its own tests.

THE ERROR: assess_receiver_receipt required PRE-SEND WORKING. Main dispatches from tick-monitor ConfirmedIdle, so the pre status is the pi glyph. The function would therefore have REJECTED EVERY DISPATCH THE SUPERVISOR ACTUALLY MAKES. Idle-to-Working is not an edge case; it is the only path main takes.

MY FAULT, IN THE DISPATCH I WROTE: I specified the receipt as a last-status-line timer RESET plus a spinner-stripped content-hash CHANGE. That is the WORKING-TO-WORKING signature -- the queued-packet case for codex panes -- and I presented it as if it were universal. A pane that was IDLE has no timer to reset. I handed the implementer one transition and called it the receipt, and it built exactly what I asked for.

THIS IS THE SAME CLASS AS THE free_capacity DEFECT I FIXED AN HOUR AGO. There, one boolean could not distinguish NewlyIdle from working, and deriving two facts from one field made a branch unreachable. Here, one transition signature could not distinguish idle-acceptance from queued-acceptance, and specifying one made the other impossible. BOTH were a collapse of two distinct states into a single measurement, and both produced code that could not fail for the reason it claimed.

CORRECTED CONTRACT -- receipt is keyed on the PRE-state, four transitions and four verdicts:
  IDLE -> WORKING: CONFIRMED, and the strongest evidence obtainable. The transition cannot occur without the pane accepting AND starting. Corroborate that the new timer is SMALL -- a large elapsed timer on a formerly-idle pane means a stale observation or a different packet, which is INDETERMINATE rather than confirmed.
  WORKING -> WORKING with timer RESET and hash CHANGE: CONFIRMED. BOTH signals required. Timer alone fails because a frozen pane and a working pane render identically; hash alone fails because the spinner advances even on a dead pane, so a raw hash changes forever.
  IDLE -> IDLE: NO_RECEIPT, unambiguous.
  WORKING -> WORKING with timer ADVANCED and no reset: NO_RECEIPT, and the dangerous one -- the pane is still on its prior turn and the packet is most likely UNSUBMITTED in the composer. That is the wedge: safe_to_dispatch is not liveness, and a wedged pane accepts a packet, parks it at the queued-messages prompt, and never submits it. Reported distinctly as WEDGED_UNSUBMITTED where the marker is detectable, because the remedy differs from a plain non-delivery.
Two states that must never be folded into either verdict: post=DIALOG is INDETERMINATE, because an Ask dialog advances the timer while blocked on a human and therefore mimics acceptance; and absence from tmux list-panes is DEAD, which is the only death evidence this fleet accepts -- an unreadable capture is a capture failure, and an empty pane list must declare NOBODY dead rather than produce a fleet-wide obituary.

OPERATIONAL CONSEQUENCE for the wiring: the pre-observation must be captured BEFORE the send. It is the function input and it cannot be reconstructed afterwards. A receipt check that only looks at the post-state is not a receipt check.

NO-CLAIM: this is a corrected SPECIFICATION, not a verified implementation. It is untested as of this comment. My previous specification on this same bead was refuted within the hour by a grader using a live specimen, and the one before that -- the phantom-landing acceptance -- was refuted by its own known-bad. Specifications are the cheapest artifact here to get wrong. The negative legs are what make this falsifiable: idle-to-idle, working-advanced, and dialog must each go RED under their own mutation, or the crate is asserting rather than measuring. And it remains a legitimate outcome for the implementer to report that a uniform receipt CANNOT be met across both transports, provided it comes with the measurement.

title: tick-monitor lifecycle attributes CITED SHAs as a bead's own landing, inflating LANDED_UNGRADED with phantom work
description:
WHAT: `tick-monitor lifecycle` harvests commit SHAs from a bead's PROSE and records them as that bead's own landing. A SHA cited as ANOTHER bead's evidence therefore promotes the citing bead into LANDED_UNGRADED, so the grading queue fills with beads where nothing was ever built.

MEASURED 2026-08-31, found by a grader disputing my premise rather than by me:
  tick-monitor lifecycle reported: omp-orchestrator-2lo  author=-  deps=0  landed=3f821d4
  git log --all --grep='2lo'      -> EMPTY. No commit references 2lo at all.
  git log -1 3f821d4              -> 'gate: no-shell-gate - fail the build on tracked .sh/.py [mutation-verified]'
                                    which is omp-orchestrator-4ak's work, not 2lo's.
  3f821d4 in 2lo's comments      -> present, as a CITATION, in a comment I wrote myself.
So the tool read my own cross-reference to a different bead's commit and reported it as this bead's implementation.

IMPACT, and it is a ROUTING-SAFETY defect rather than a cosmetic one. LANDED_UNGRADED is what I use to decide who grades what. A phantom row causes a grader to be dispatched at a bead with no artifact, which is a wasted slot under a build freeze when grading is the only work available. Worse, it is INDISTINGUISHABLE from real work in the output: the row carries a real SHA that resolves in git, so a conductor checking 'does the cited commit exist?' gets YES and proceeds. It took a grader re-deriving the premise -- `git log --grep` on the bead id -- to catch it. That check is exactly what the tool should be doing and is not.

THIRD DEFECT IN THIS TOOL IN ONE SESSION, and all three are the same failure of attribution:
  1. author= reads the current ASSIGNEE, not the implementer. Observed live: r3h flipped author=GreenFrog -> author=AmberGate when I routed AmberGate as its GRADER. I nearly handed a bead back to its own implementer.
  2. dangling SHA citations were counted as unresolvable commits -- fixed in fa5129e/b352af1 by requiring `in_citation_position` for marker words and excluding truncated sha256 content hashes.
  3. THIS: a SHA in citation position is still credited as a landing. Fix (2) narrowed which TOKENS count as commit-shaped; it never asked WHOSE commit a resolvable SHA is.
The generalisation the tool keeps failing: a SHA appearing NEAR a bead is not a SHA belonging to that bead. Adjacency is not authorship -- the same lesson as the DIALOG detector, where a framed marker in scrollback is not a dialog, and only ADJACENCY TO THE STATUS LINE discriminated.

THE FIX, stated as a contract rather than a patch:
A bead's landing set must be derived from the OBJECT STORE keyed on the bead, not from the bead's text. The authoritative join is `git log --all --grep=<bead-short-id>`: the commit must NAME the bead. A SHA that appears only in prose is a CITATION and belongs in a separate field -- `cites=` -- which must never feed LANDED_UNGRADED.
That also fixes defect 1 in the same pass: the implementer is the author of the commits in the derived landing set, and where the landing set is empty there IS no implementer, so `author=` must render as NONE rather than borrowing the assignee.

ACCEPTANCE - must FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, and the known-bad already exists in the tracker:
1. PLANTED (real specimen, no fixture needed): run lifecycle over this repo. omp-orchestrator-2lo must NOT appear in LANDED_UNGRADED and must NOT carry landed=3f821d4. It is now CLOSED, so use a scratch bead citing a foreign SHA if a live open specimen is needed.
2. KNOWN-GOOD leg, mandatory: a bead WITH a real commit naming it (e.g. 4ak / 3f821d4, or npq / f9f4e37) must STILL appear with its landing intact. Without this leg the fix ships an over-strict rule that empties the queue and gets routed around.
3. author= must render NONE for a bead with an empty landing set, and must NOT equal the assignee. Assert on a bead whose assignee is set and whose landing set is empty -- 2lo before its close was exactly that shape.
4. cites= must be POPULATED for the citation case, so the information is preserved rather than deleted. A fix that silently drops the cross-reference loses the audit trail I was building when I wrote it.
5. MUTATION: revert to prose-harvesting -> leg 1 must go RED. Restore byte-identically and report the sha both sides.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty bead set must be an ERROR, not a pass. A lifecycle run that parses zero beads currently reports 'zero beads parsed; an empty scan set is an ERROR, never a pass' -- keep that.

BLOCKED ON cp-oakbv: the fix requires `cargo build` and builds are refused fleet-wide (CARGO_MINT_CONTAINER_EXHAUSTED / cargo_floor_guard exit 75, refused even at CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=7). I am not lowering the override further and not editing the installed default. NO-CLAIM: I have not audited how many CURRENT LANDED_UNGRADED rows are phantoms. 2lo is one confirmed instance; the count is unknown and I am not guessing it, because a remembered number dying on derivation is the exact failure class this session has produced four times. I also have not verified whether the `deps=` field suffers the same prose-harvesting problem, though `dep_count` was already found once to be measuring OUT-edges only.

MUTATION-VERIFIED by orchestrator (pane 1, claude-opus-5), commit 7a7720a — and the
verification took two attempts, which is the part worth reading.

THE DEFECT, exactly as this bead described it: `lifecycle` built its SHA corpus from
the bead's OWN PROSE (comments + `br show` output) and treated every resolvable SHA
in it as that bead's landing. So `2lo` was reported `landed=3f821d4` while
`git log --all --grep=2lo` was EMPTY and `3f821d4` is `4ak`'s gate work, present in
`2lo`'s comments as a hand-written cross-reference. A bead earned a LANDED_UNGRADED
promotion for citing another bead's commit, and the grading queue filled with beads
where nothing was built.

FIXED: attribution now runs COMMIT -> BEAD. `commit_references_bead` reads the
commit's own subject and body and looks for the bead id. A bead naming a commit is a
citation and proves nothing about authorship; only the commit can claim the bead.

MY FIRST FIX SHIPPED TESTS THAT COULD NOT FAIL, and I caught it by mutation rather
than by review. They set `cited_only_shas` by hand on a `Unit` literal and asserted
the accessor and the render. Reverting the attribution check to `if true` — the exact
pre-fix behaviour — produced ZERO failing suites. The tests exercised the REPORTING
and never the DECISION.

That is a fooled certificate inside the commit that fixes a fooled promotion, and the
remedy was not a sharper assertion on the same shape. The decision is now a pure
function a test can call:

  pub enum CitationClass { Landed, BorrowedCredit, Dangling }
  pub fn classify_citation(exists: bool, names_bead: bool) -> CitationClass

Re-running the identical mutation — `(true, false) => Landed`, the pre-fix rule now
inside the decision — turns 1 suite RED naming BOTH tests. Restore byte-identical,
shasum verified. Before extraction that mutation was silent.

SURFACED, NOT DROPPED: `cited_only_shas` is its own field beside `dangling_shas` and
renders as a BORROWED CREDIT section naming bead and SHA. A dangling SHA is a BROKEN
citation; this is a VALID citation of work that is not yours. Different remedies —
fix the reference versus stop claiming the credit — so collapsing them would hide
which one an operator is reading. The render assertion is in the test because a field
nobody renders is not wired.

BOTH FAILURE DIRECTIONS ARE HANDLED: `commit_references_bead` also accepts the bare
bead suffix, because commits in these repos write `[cp-79am1]` and
`omp-orchestrator-4ak` interchangeably. Requiring the full prefix would reject
genuine landings — a false negative that EMPTIES the grading queue instead of filling
it wrongly.

NO-CLAIM: a commit can name a bead it did not implement, since the message is written
by the same hand as the citation. This raises the floor from "anyone may credit
themselves with anyone's commit" to "the commit must claim the bead" — the difference
between an accident and a lie. It does not detect the lie.

ALSO NOT CLAIMED: I did not re-run `lifecycle` against the live board to confirm `2lo`
now reports without `landed=3f821d4`. The decision is proven at the unit level and the
loop is wired through it; the end-to-end observation on live data is not in this
close. Workspace: 121 suites, 480 assertions, 0 failed.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
NOT CLOSING, and the grade is the reason. SilverWolf's derivation (%1409) did not merely confirm this defect -- it REFUTED THE FIX I PROPOSED IN THIS BEAD'S OWN ACCEPTANCE, using a live specimen. A bead whose acceptance is disproven cannot close on the evidence that disproved it. Acceptance rewritten below; status stays blocked.

WHAT THE GRADER ESTABLISHED, with the denominator stated: 7 rows / 11 SHA claims. Controls PASSED -- 4ak and npq both REAL -- so the method discriminates and a spectacular all-phantom result was not what it produced. Results: REAL 1 (v18-blind, 8eed3b3 names the bead), REAL-WORK-UNNAMED 3 (5cl, 6gq, ma1 -- the work EXISTS, the citation contract failed), PHANTOM 5 (ma1 self-referential, r3h, he6, 815, 6gq).

I VERIFIED BOTH STRUCTURAL FINDINGS MYSELF RATHER THAN ACCEPTING THEM.

FINDING 1 -- CROSS-REPO SHA ELIGIBILITY, a fourth defect in this tool. CONFIRMED:
    (cd omp-orchestrator && git cat-file -e 8fc3e4b) -> does NOT have it
    (cd control-plane    && git cat-file -e 8fc3e4b) -> HAS IT: 'chore(safety): forbid unsafe in ported crates [test]'
So 8fc3e4b exists ONLY in control-plane, and my tool -- handed --repo for both -- resolved a control-plane commit as an omp-orchestrator bead's landing. The SHA resolves, so every 'does the cited commit exist?' check answers YES. Silent repo-membership failure, exactly as the grader named it. A bead belongs to ONE tracker; its landing set must be resolved in THAT repo, and a SHA resolvable only in a sibling repo is a cross-repo citation, not a landing.

FINDING 2 -- AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT KILLS MY PROPOSED CONTRACT. CONFIRMED, and worse than reported:
    git log -1 610569f            -> 'feat(extraction): add five crates (code-first, test pending)'   <- the REAL 815 work
    git log --all --grep='815'    -> e4a4b63 ONLY: 'chore(beads): consolidate orchestrator work into this tracker'
My proposed fix in the acceptance above was: 'the authoritative join is git log --all --grep=<bead-short-id>; the commit must NAME the bead.' Run on 815, that join returns e4a4b63 -- THE COMMIT THAT CREATED THE BEADS -- and MISSES 610569f, the commit that did the work. So the fix I specified would credit bead CREATION as bead IMPLEMENTATION while dropping the actual extraction. It is wrong in BOTH directions at once, on the very row the grader flagged.

The grader's formulation is exact and I am adopting it verbatim: MY OWN RULE -- 'mention is not implementation' -- APPLIES TO THE JOIN ITSELF. I narrowed the tool from harvesting mentions in bead prose to harvesting mentions in commit messages, and called the second one authoritative. Both are mention-based. I moved the defect across the join and declared it fixed.

WORSE, AND I AM RECORDING IT AGAINST MYSELF: I FOUND THIS EXACT REFUTATION HOURS AGO AND FAILED TO PROPAGATE IT. Earlier tonight, computing a grading backlog, I wrote that my probe 'matched e4a4b63 chore(beads): consolidate... for 5cl, he6 and 815 -- that is the tracker commit, not implementation, so backlog_count=4 is not trustworthy', and I switched to deriving from known commits instead. Then I wrote e4a4b63's exact failure mode into this bead as the authoritative fix. The measurement was already in this session's record; the doctrine did not reach the bead. That is the same shape as this repo's stale-context trap -- a correction that lives only in a transcript expires with the turn that produced it, and the only durable home is the artifact.

THE THIRD CATEGORY IS THE MOST VALUABLE THING IN THIS GRADE. REAL-WORK-UNNAMED (3 of 7) is a category my binary contract would have DESTROYED: it collapses PHANTOM and REAL-WORK-UNNAMED into one bucket, so a bead whose work genuinely landed but whose commit forgot to name it would be reported as 'nothing was built' -- and a conductor would then dispatch a grader at real, finished work as though it were vapour. That is a WORSE failure than the phantom rows I filed this bead about, because a phantom wastes a slot while a mislabelled real landing discards evidence.

ACCEPTANCE -- REPLACING THE ORIGINAL, which is withdrawn as refuted:
1. THREE-VALUED OUTPUT, never binary. REAL (a commit names the bead AND touches paths in the bead's scope), REAL-WORK-UNNAMED (paths in scope changed, no commit names the bead), PHANTOM (no work, SHA appears only in prose). Collapsing the middle value is the defect, not the fix.
2. REPO MEMBERSHIP is a precondition, not a lookup. Resolve every SHA in the repo that OWNS the bead. A SHA resolvable only in a sibling repo renders as cross_repo_citation and NEVER as a landing. Known-bad specimen: 8fc3e4b against an omp-orchestrator bead.
3. TRACKER COMMITS ARE NOT IMPLEMENTATIONS. A commit whose only changed paths are under .beads/ can never be a landing for any bead. Known-bad specimen: e4a4b63 must NOT be returned as 815's landing. This leg is what my withdrawn contract fails.
4. FALSE-NEGATIVE LEG, mandatory and previously absent: 610569f MUST be attributable to 815 by whatever join replaces the grep. A contract that only suppresses false positives while silently dropping real work has moved the error, not removed it.
5. KNOWN-GOOD control preserved: 4ak/3f821d4 and npq/f9f4e37 must remain REAL. The grader's controls passed and must keep passing.
6. field named `claims=` or `landing_evidence=`, NOT `landed=`. A message convention is a CLAIM about authorship. The field name must not assert more than the mechanism can establish -- that is this repo's own overclaim rule applied to a column header.
7. MUTATION on each of legs 2, 3, 4 independently, restored byte-identically with the sha reported both sides. Three defects were merged into one 'attribution' bug once already; each guard must fail on its own known-bad.
8. ANTI-VACUITY: zero beads parsed is an ERROR, never a pass (already present, keep it).

STATUS: stays BLOCKED on cp-oakbv. The fix needs cargo build and builds are refused fleet-wide (cargo_floor_guard exit 75, refused even at CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=7). I am not lowering the override and not editing the installed default. The interim operating rule STRENGTHENS on this grade: LANDED_UNGRADED is an upper bound, AND a row that greps clean is not thereby phantom -- check whether the work landed under a commit that simply failed to name the bead, because 3 of 7 rows are that case.

title: close_reason/delete_reason evidence gap: 22 tombstones retired with delete_reason="delete" and no rationale
description:
WHAT: 22 terminal beads in this tracker carry NO closure rationale of any kind. All 22 are
tombstones deleted in a single 7-second `br delete` sweep (deleted_at 2026-09-01T06:13:31.779Z ..
06:13:38.349Z, deleted_by=josh); their `delete_reason` is the literal placeholder string
"delete", and `close_reason` is absent. 21 landed in commit 6389f41 "chore(beads): tracker sync
- extraction-epic 815.x rows [live]"; 1 (dag-ready-gate-kwb) landed in e5dc05a.

WHY: the measured coverage figure that motivated this bead was `close_reason` present on 67 of
142 beads = 47%, against a 79% corpus baseline. That framing is half wrong and half worse than
it looked, and both halves matter:

  (a) NOT a discipline gap on CLOSES. Every one of the 67 `closed` beads has a close_reason:
      67/67 = 100%. Mean length 1115 chars, median 459, min 27, max 4370 -- 5.9x the corpus mean
      of 190. Our closes are RICHER than the corpus, not thinner. The 47% denominator was all
      142 beads, and the 22 tombstones (15% of the graph) can never populate `close_reason`
      because `br delete` writes `delete_reason` instead. Comparing our 47% to a corpus 79%
      without normalising for tombstone share compares two different fields.

  (b) IS a real evidence gap on DELETES. `delete_reason: "delete"` is not a rationale, it is
      the subcommand name echoed back. 22 work units -- an entire 21-crate extraction epic plus
      the DAG-ready gate that governed it -- were retired with zero recorded WHY. A future agent
      reading this tracker cannot tell whether 815.1..815.21 were superseded, duplicated,
      re-scoped into the flat 815 epic, or abandoned. The corpus's close-reason first-token
      vocabulary (SUPERSEDED 95, DUPLICATE 110, STALE 56) exists precisely to answer that.

  Compounding: `br update` REFUSES tombstone mutation ("cannot update tombstone issue"), so
  these rows are frozen. Backfilling them is not a `br update` away.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A decision is recorded on which of the two halves is in scope. Half (a) is a METRIC fix, not
   a data fix: any coverage figure quoted for this tracker states its denominator and either
   excludes tombstones or counts `delete_reason` alongside `close_reason`.
2. For half (b): each of the 22 ids listed in the comment on this bead either receives a real
   rationale, or the tracker records that the rationale is unrecoverable and why. Whichever
   path is taken, it names the mechanism -- `br update` cannot write these fields on a
   tombstone, so this is a beads_rust capability question or a JSONL-level migration, not a CLI
   sweep.
3. NO REASON IS INVENTED. A row whose WHY nobody remembers is marked unrecoverable, not
   backfilled with a plausible-sounding guess. A fabricated SUPERSEDED is worse than a blank.
4. Known-good leg: the 67 closed beads are NOT touched. Their close_reasons are already at or
   above standard and shortening them toward the 190-char corpus mean would be a regression.

NO-CLAIM: this bead does not establish that 815.1..815.21 SHOULD have been deleted, nor that the
flat 815 epic that replaced them is the right shape. It establishes only that the deletion left
no evidence.

title: Rounds 8-14: 340 declared findings predate per-finding identity; recorded not dispositioned (Josh ruling, not a blocker)
description:
## WHAT

Rounds **8, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14** declared **340 findings** and have **zero** rows in
`docs/plan/FINDINGS.jsonl`. They are RECORDED in `docs/plan/ROUNDS.md` as rounds that happened,
with their declared counts and the honest note that they predate per-finding identity. They are
**NOT dispositioned**, and HD-0006's 15-22 scope stands.

This bead exists for whoever later wants them mined. It is **not a blocker** and must not be
treated as one.

| round | declared | dispositioned |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 8 | 9 | 0 |
| 9 | 13 | 0 |
| 10 | 77 | 0 |
| 12 | 89 | 0 |
| 13 | 80 | 0 |
| 14 | 72 | 0 |
| **total** | **340** | **0** |

Re-derive at any time:

```bash
python3 -c "
import json,collections
c=collections.Counter()
for l in open('docs/plan/CONVERGENCE.jsonl'):
    if l.strip():
        r=json.loads(l); c[r.get('round')] += r.get('new_findings') or 0
print({k:v for k,v in sorted(c.items()) if k and k < 15})"
```

## WHY IT IS A BEAD AND NOT A BLOCKER

Joshua's ruling, 2026-09-01, recorded here because the reasoning is the load-bearing part and a
future pane will otherwise re-open this as a P0:

> Those rounds predate the finding-id discipline entirely — their rows carry no `finding_ids`
> field, so there is no per-finding identity to disposition against. Reconciling them means
> MINTING 340 ids that join back to nothing, which is precisely the defect I found in the R16
> migration: *"the R16-00-001 ids were minted by the reconciling pane and do not join back."*
> Doing that 340 times would manufacture a ledger that looks complete and cites nothing.

Verified: no round below 15 carries `finding_ids`.

```bash
python3 -c "
import json
rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open('docs/plan/CONVERGENCE.jsonl') if l.strip()]
old=[r for r in rows if (r.get('round') or 99) < 15]
print('pre-15 rows:', len(old))
print('with finding_ids:', sum(1 for r in old if r.get('finding_ids')))"
```

So a "complete" ledger over these rounds would be **worse than the gap it closes**: 340 rows,
every one citing an id no grader ever assigned, indistinguishable from 340 real dispositions to
every downstream reader and gate. The gap is visible and honest; the manufactured ledger would
be invisible and false.

## ACCEPTANCE — for whoever picks this up, not for closing it now

A mining pass is complete when, for each round in 8-14, one of these is true and the choice is
stated per round:

1. **MINED** — the round's `note` field is parsed into per-finding text, each finding gets an id
   that is derived from the note content (a content hash, not a sequence number, so it joins
   back to something), and each gets FIXED / RETRACTED / DEFERRED under the `findings_ledger`
   schema. `run X, expect Y`: `jq -sc 'map(select(.round==N))|length' docs/plan/FINDINGS.jsonl`
   equals the declared count for that round.
2. **DECLARED UNMINABLE** — the round's rows carry no per-finding text to split, so the round is
   recorded in `ROUNDS.md` with a `pre_identity: true` marker and excluded from coverage in
   BOTH directions, exactly as void rounds are.

Whichever is chosen, the anti-vacuity rule holds: a round with zero mined rows and no
`pre_identity` marker is an ERROR, not a pass.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- HD-0006's 15-22 reconciliation scope. It stands.
- Round 22, which is VOID under HD-0005 and excluded from coverage in both directions — its
  dispositions must not appear as done OR as outstanding.
- Round 11, which is absent from every ledger on disk. That is a separate hole and it is not
  measured here.

## NO-CLAIM

Filing this does not make the 340 findings safe to ignore. It records that they exist, that
nothing joins them to an identity, and that minting identities would produce a false ledger.
If a real defect dies in that gap, the correct response is an example and a re-ruling — not a
mass id mint.

Recorded by `omp-orchestrator-5by` follow-on; ledger view in `docs/plan/ROUNDS.md`.
