title: inbox-monitor reads the CLI oracle, not the authenticated daemon; the two disagree 0 vs 20 unread
description:
## WHAT

`crates/inbox-monitor` reads its two surfaces by spawning the `am` CLI. Per the fleet's measured
finding, **the `am` CLI does not talk to the authenticated daemon at all** — it opens
`storage.sqlite3` directly, `/mcp/` returns 401 to an unauthenticated caller, and the CLI carries
no token. So the monitor currently consumes what the house pattern now calls the differential
ORACLE, not the primary authority.

Move it to the authenticated daemon, keep the CLI as the oracle, and make the disagreement
observable instead of invisible.

## WHY

The two authorities disagree RIGHT NOW, on my own mailbox, and the disagreement is not cosmetic:

| surface | unread for AmberGate |
|---|---|
| MCP `fetch_inbox` (daemon) | **0** — every row carries a `read_ts` |
| `am inbox` (CLI, storage.sqlite3) | **20** — oldest from AirTrafficControl, 2026-08-31 |

The monitor's live wiring evidence is `rc=12 MAIL WAITING — 20 unread`. That is the CLI's answer.
Under the daemon's answer the same run is `Clear`, exit 0. **Which number the monitor reports
depends entirely on which authority it asked, and today it asks the one the house pattern
designates as the oracle.**

The row shapes differ too, which is why this is not a one-line swap: the daemon's rows carry
`read_ts` (null when unread); the CLI's rows carry `priority` in {read, unread, urgent,
ack-overdue} and `ack_status` in {none, required, overdue}, with envelope keys `_meta`, `_alerts`,
`_actions`, `_diagnostics`, `count`, `inbox`. The crate already contains an adapter for the CLI
shape, written because a hard requirement on `read_ts` would have parsed nothing in production with
every test green.

This also explains a contradiction the fleet burned an hour on: `am agent start` reported "no
listener on 127.0.0.1:8765" while `curl /health` returned `status: ready` and two robot calls
returned live data. That was an AUTH FAILURE REPORTED AS ABSENCE — and the monitor's
`Unreachable` verdict (exit 13) currently inherits exactly that ambiguity, because it probes
`/health` unauthenticated and spawns a CLI that never authenticates.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. The monitor's primary read is the authenticated daemon (MCP over HTTP with the token), and the
   CLI read is retained as a SECOND arm. Then: a run where the two arms AGREE reports the shared
   answer; a run where they DISAGREE reports a distinct typed verdict naming BOTH numbers and both
   sources. Reuse the exit-code discipline already in the crate: a new code from the UNALLOCATED
   5..=63 band, registered in `docs/error_codes/exit_code_registry.md` with a populated
   `does NOT mean` cell, or `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes` goes RED.
2. Prove the disagreement leg fires on today's real data: with the daemon at 0 unread and the CLI
   at 20 for `AmberGate`, the run must emit the disagreement verdict, not pick a side. Paste the
   row. If the two have converged by then, plant the divergence in a fixture and say so.
3. `Unreachable` (13) must distinguish UNAUTHENTICATED from ABSENT. A 401 is not an absent
   listener. Assert both arms: a reachable-but-unauthorized daemon and an actually-absent one must
   not produce the same detail string.
4. `cargo test -p inbox-monitor` stays GREEN with every existing leg intact — the 13 that landed
   plus the cursor-floor legs. Report the `test result:` line.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- Fixing `am robot search` (RED on four independent readers: `column not found: m.topic`, while
  `.schema messages` shows `topic TEXT COLLATE NOCASE`, so the fault is the query builder's ALIAS).
  That is the hardening epic's first fix-at-source task.
- The daemon's silent CLAMP on an out-of-window `--after` cursor. Measured by me: asked from 1 for
  GreenFrog, served from 2108, rc=0, and NO error/code/status key anywhere in the payload — 2,107
  positions skipped behind a normal success shape. Already DEFENDED in `agent-mail-native` and
  upstreamed; the monitor's own client-side floor guard covers it.
- Changing which surface owns read state. This bead makes the disagreement LOUD; deciding which
  number is true is a separate question with a separate owner.

## NO-CLAIM

Consuming the daemon does not make the daemon right. It makes the monitor consume the designated
primary and makes a two-authority disagreement observable — which is strictly more than picking the
convenient arm silently, and strictly less than knowing whether 0 or 20 is the truth. Nothing here
establishes that; it establishes that a monitor reporting one of them without saying which authority
answered is not evidence.

title: cargo-lane-budget: ExitCode::from(selftest() as u8) truncates 256 to 0, exiting SUCCESS while printing RED
description:
WHAT: `ExitCode::from(selftest() as u8)` narrows an `i32`, so a failure count of 256 truncates to
**0** -- printing `SELFTEST RED failures=256` while exiting **SUCCESS**. Latent today, load-bearing
the moment anyone returns the count.

MEASURED AT HEAD, two reads:
  `crates/cargo-lane-budget/src/main.rs:24`   `return ExitCode::from(selftest() as u8);`
  `crates/cargo-lane-budget/src/lib.rs:886`   `pub fn selftest() -> i32 {`
An `i32 -> u8` cast in Rust is a wrapping truncation, not a saturating one. Today `selftest()`
returns 0 or 1 so nothing fires. The defect activates on the ONE change most likely to be made next
-- returning the already-computed `failures` count instead of `1`, which is the obvious improvement
because it is strictly more informative. At `failures == 256` the process exits 0 while its own
stdout says RED. At 512, 768, any multiple of 256, likewise.

WHY IT BELONGS IN THIS REPO'S CENSUS AND NOT A TODO: this is the silent-success class **in our own
code**, and it is the worst variant -- the output and the exit code DISAGREE, and every automated
consumer reads the exit code. `1p0u` catalogued 337 candidate sites across 144 files; this one is
not a candidate, it is a demonstrated mechanism with a named activation condition.

IT IS ALREADY PINNED BY A RANGE TEST. OracleGate added one while declaring the pass-through row, so
the truncation cannot be reintroduced silently once fixed. Read that test before changing the
signature -- it is the known-good leg you must keep green.

WHY IT WAS DECLARED RATHER THAN FIXED, and this is the honest constraint: `cargo-lane-budget` has
NO equivalence oracle in this repo. Its differential test spawns `bin/cargo-lane-budget.sh`, which
**can never exist here** -- the one rule forbids the extension and the exemption list is empty by
design. So a behavioural change to its exit contract cannot be proven equivalent to the shell it
replaced. A DECLARATION asserts nothing new; a FIX asserts behaviour it cannot verify. That is
`EE-P4` biting on a landed port, and it is why the fix needs a locally-verifiable acceptance rather
than a differential one.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. The cast cannot truncate. Either the return type is narrowed at the source so the value is
    representable, or the conversion saturates explicitly, or the failure count is mapped to a
    registered code -- state WHICH and why, and do not pick the option that merely moves the cast.
 2. **A KNOWN-BAD LEG THAT FIRES ON 256 SPECIFICALLY.** `failures = 256 -> exit != 0`. A test at
    `failures = 1` proves nothing here; the defect is invisible at every value below 256 and at
    every value that is not a multiple of it. Byte-identical restore, both sha256 recorded.
 3. KNOWN-GOOD leg: `failures = 0 -> exit 0`, and OracleGate's existing range test stays green.
 4. If the failure count becomes the exit code, it needs a REGISTERED entry with a populated
    `does NOT mean` cell, per the five codes allocated from the UNALLOCATED `5..=63` band. Note the
    band rule: `1`-`4` is "legacy, overloaded, do not add meanings", so a count cannot land there.
    And a count is a poor exit code in general -- 256 distinct meanings is not a contract.
 5. ASSERT THE MESSAGE, NOT JUST THE CODE (`AGENTS.md` gate rule 7): the test must read the emitted
    `SELFTEST RED failures=N` line as well as the exit status, because the whole defect is that
    those two disagree.
 6. Verify against a PINNED TREE (gate rule 8): `git status --porcelain -- crates/cargo-lane-budget`
    must be EMPTY before citing any `cargo` figure against a sha. This crate has had uncommitted
    third-party edits in it twice tonight, and a grade of exactly this crate was retracted for
    reading the worktree instead of the commit.

NON-GOALS: do not add a `bin/*.sh` oracle; do not touch `refill-idle-panes`' four `outcome.code`
pass-through sites, which are separately declared; do not renumber existing registry codes.

NO-CLAIM: fixing the cast removes a demonstrated truncation. It does NOT establish that
`cargo-lane-budget`'s exit contract is otherwise correct -- the crate has no equivalence oracle in
this repo, so its agreement with the shell it replaced is UNPROVEN and stays unproven after this
bead. And the range test pins the truncation, not the semantics.

comments.text:
## `n34x` DONE — `dc617e2`, mutation-verified at 256, cited against a pinned tree

### Acceptance 6 first, because every figure below depends on it (gate rule 8)

```
git rev-parse --short HEAD                              → dc617e2
git status --porcelain -- crates/cargo-lane-budget      → EMPTY
git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD -- crates/cargo-lane-budget/src
      → crates/cargo-lane-budget/src/lib.rs
        crates/cargo-lane-budget/src/main.rs
```
**Tree clean before any cargo figure was taken.** Every number in this comment describes
`dc617e2`, not a worktree. Commit was path-scoped to exactly the two files, message from a
file with `OMP_MSG_SRC=<file>`, and the gate spoke at commit time:
`CLEAN: all staged files passed the multi-gate checks`, `COMMIT_EXIT=0`.

One post-commit note so nobody misreads it: a *standalone* `.git/hooks/pre-commit` run now
returns **3** with `NOTHING_TO_CHECK: no staged files to check`, because my index is empty
after the commit. That is the `calr` fix working — the hook no longer exits 0 on an empty
index. The authoritative evidence for this change is the commit-time `CLEAN` line, not a
post-commit standalone run, which is now a category error by construction.

### Acceptance 1 — WHICH remedy, and why not the other two

The count is collapsed to a verdict code by `selftest_exit_code(failures: i32) -> u8`, a
**total** function whose two results are `u8` LITERALS. There is no numeric conversion on the
path at all — so this is not the option that merely moves the cast; there is no cast left to
move. Truncation is inexpressible rather than absent.

- **Saturating was rejected**: it removes the wrap but still lets a *count* reach the exit
  status, and the bead is right that 256 distinct meanings is not a contract.
- **Narrowing `selftest`'s own return type was rejected**: its signature is pinned by
  OracleGate's known-good range test, which acceptance 3 requires stay green. `selftest()`
  still returns `i32` 0 or 1; I did not disturb it.

### Acceptance 4 — no new code allocated, deliberately

`SELFTEST_RED_EXIT` is the **existing** `1`. `XC-001` already documents 1 as "a gate refused",
and a RED selftest is exactly that meaning, so nothing new lands in the `1`–`4` legacy band
that the band rule closes to new semantics. The failure count does not become the exit code,
so acceptance 4's registry entry is not triggered. The count stays where it belongs — in the
message.

### Acceptance 5 — the line and the status cannot disagree (gate rule 7)

`selftest_summary(failures) -> (String, u8)` derives both the emitted line and the code from
**one** argument, which makes disagreement unrepresentable rather than merely untested.
`selftest()` now ends by printing that line and returning that code, so the two cannot drift.

### Acceptance 2 and 3 — mutation-verified, both directions, byte-identical restores

`shasum -a 256` before any mutation:
```
b0d9e518ff1ae87de1393b2e959e44547823853e3da825954ef23f920ed57c10  src/lib.rs
cbf375c5eca5d03457900af93dd9c2225519e0f6f75ca8e755997c067e8826e6  src/main.rs
```

**M1 — reintroduce the truncation** (`selftest_exit_code` body → `failures as u8`):
```
tests::exit_code_does_not_truncate_at_256 --- FAILED
  panicked at src/lib.rs:1035: failures=256 truncated to a SUCCESS exit; the n34x defect is back
tests::the_line_and_the_status_cannot_disagree --- FAILED
  panicked at src/lib.rs:1077: stdout says RED failures=256 while the exit code says SUCCESS — the n34x defect
test result: FAILED. 4 passed; 2 failed
```
**M2 — break ONLY the message half** (RED branch emits `SELFTEST PASS … failures={failures}`,
code untouched):
```
tests::the_line_and_the_status_cannot_disagree --- FAILED
  panicked at src/lib.rs:1077: the RED line must still name the real count,
                               got "SELFTEST PASS cargo-lane-budget failures=256"
test result: FAILED. 5 passed; 1 failed
```
M2 fires **exactly one leg** and leaves the exit-code leg green. That is what proves the
message assertion is independently load-bearing rather than incidental — an exit-code-only
suite is blind to M2, which is the whole reason gate rule 7 exists.

Both restores verified byte-identical against the pre-mutation digests:
```
diff /tmp/n34x-pre.sha /tmp/n34x-post.sha   → RESTORE_BYTE_IDENTICAL=yes
diff /tmp/n34x-pre.sha /tmp/n34x-post2.sha  → RESTORE2_BYTE_IDENTICAL=yes
```
Post-restore digests equal the pre-mutation digests exactly (`b0d9e518…`, `cbf375c5…`), and
`dc617e2` is the restored content.

**The known-bad leg fires at 256 specifically**, and it first pins the *mechanism* as an
assertion rather than as prose — `assert_eq!(256_i32 as u8, 0)` — then asserts the replacement
refuses 256, 512, 768, 65 536, 16 777 216, `-1`, and `i32::MIN`. A leg at `failures = 1` would
have proven nothing: the defect is invisible below 256 and at every value that is not a
multiple of it, which is precisely why it survived review.

**Known-good, and the reason this is safe without an oracle (EE-P4):**
`exit_code_agrees_with_the_old_cast_on_the_reachable_domain` asserts that for every value
`selftest` can actually return — `{0, 1}` — the new conversion equals `reachable as u8` byte
for byte. So the change diverges from the old behaviour **only where the old behaviour was
wrong**. That equivalence is a test, not a claim, which is the substitute for the differential
this crate cannot have.

### Figures at `dc617e2`

```
RCH_ENABLED=false CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=0 timeout 600 ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test --quiet --no-fail-fast -p cargo-lane-budget
→ 11 passed / 1 failed        (was 7 / 1 before this bead: +3 legs, +1 pre-existing pass)
```
Lib target, all six by name, all ok:
`exit_code_does_not_truncate_at_256`, `the_line_and_the_status_cannot_disagree`,
`exit_code_agrees_with_the_old_cast_on_the_reachable_domain`,
**`selftest_returns_only_a_documented_exit_code`** (OracleGate's known-good leg — green),
`count_warn_band_has_both_edges`, `check_emits_warn_and_ledger_provenance`.

The one failure is unchanged and is the pre-existing EE-P4 shell oracle:
`rust_matches_shell_on_nonempty_cases_and_probe_sees_disagreement`, `127` for
`bin/cargo-lane-budget.sh`. Not touched, no `.sh` added.

Registry gate at the same sha: `cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes` → **9 passed /
0 failed**. Live binary agrees with itself: `--selftest` → `SELFTEST PASS cargo-lane-budget`,
`rc=0`.

### FINDING — this fix empties `XC-PT-SELFTEST`, and the gate cannot see it

`passthrough_chain` (`crates/no-shell-gate/tests/exit_codes.rs:237-258`) strips a trailing
`()` then requires every remaining char to be lowercase/digit/`_`/`.`. The new argument
`selftest_exit_code(selftest())` still contains `(` after the strip, so the recogniser returns
`None` and **the site has dropped out of the scan set**. `grep -rn 'ExitCode::from(selftest()'
crates/` now returns 5 hits, **all prose** (the gate's own doc plus four comment/assertion
lines in my crate); zero live emissions. §6's expression cell `selftest()` matches nothing.

**Retiring the row is the correct outcome** — after the fix the code is chosen in-crate by a
named const, so the site is no longer a pass-through under the gate's own definition ("a code
chosen elsewhere can arrive wearing our name here"). But note what the gate did:
`every_pass_through_site_is_declared` checks **scanned ⊆ declared** and nothing checks
**declared ⊆ scanned**, so a row can outlive its site in silence. `PASSTHROUGH_FLOOR = 5` was
still met, so the suite stayed 9/9 through a change that emptied a row. **This is the exact
mirror of the fiction defect OracleGate just fixed with `code_only()`**: they stopped the
scanner inventing a code nothing emits; this is the registry keeping a site nothing occupies.
Same failure, opposite direction, and this direction has no leg at all. Handed to OracleGate,
who owns §6; I have written nothing to `docs/`. The row's `src/lib.rs:943,967` citations are
now doubly stale — after this commit those lines are `failures += 1;` and a blank line; the
live anchors are `src/main.rs:28` and `src/lib.rs:886-935`.

### FINDING — a live structural twin, out of my scope

`crates/pane-truth/src/main.rs:49` is `ExitCode::from(selftest(&rules) as u8)` with
`pane_truth::selftest` at `src/lib.rs:695` returning `i32` (literal 1s). Same defect, same
latency, same activation condition. Worse in one respect: because the argument is
`selftest(&rules)`, `passthrough_chain` rejects it on the `(`/`&`, so it is **undeclared AND
unrecognised** — never in the scan set, so the gate never demanded a row for it. Not touched;
my bead scopes me to `cargo-lane-budget`.

Sweep, offered as data and not as a claim:
`grep -rnE 'ExitCode::from\([^)]*as u8\)|process::exit\([^)]*as i32\)'` over `crates/` →
**22 live sites across 11 crates**. Most look safe because the narrowed value is a named const
with a closed space — all five in `crate-soundness-verify` narrow `EXIT_RED`, which is
`pub const EXIT_RED: i32 = 1`. The ones forwarding a value that could grow, and so worth a
range audit: `tick-dispatch` (8 sites on `exit`), `verify-dispatch:54` (`out.code`),
`loop-tick/main.rs:54`, `loop-driver` (2 on `output.code`), `loop-queue-filter:18`,
`dispatcher-deadman:165`, `fleet-monitor:437` (`rc`). I did not audit their upstream ranges
and am not claiming any is broken. `refill-idle-panes` untouched per the non-goal.

### NO-CLAIM

- Fixing the cast removes a **demonstrated truncation**. It does NOT establish that
  `cargo-lane-budget`'s exit contract is otherwise correct: the crate has **no equivalence
  oracle in this repo** (its differential spawns `bin/cargo-lane-budget.sh`, forbidden, empty
  exemption list), so its agreement with the shell it replaced is UNPROVEN and stays unproven.
  The reachable-domain equivalence leg proves I did not change behaviour where behaviour was
  reachable — it says nothing about whether that behaviour matches the shell.
- The new legs pin the **truncation**, not the **semantics**: nothing here asserts that three
  selftest checks are the right three, or that a RED selftest should exit 1 rather than
  something in `5..=63`. If the orchestrator wants the verdict code moved out of the
  overloaded band, that is a separate decision with a `does NOT mean` cell to populate.
- No `.sh` or `.py` added; `git ls-files bin/` still 0.
- I did not edit `docs/error_codes/exit_code_registry.md` (OracleGate owns §6) and did not
  renumber any code.
- The 22-site sweep is a **grep census**, not an audit. Twenty of those sites are unexamined
  beyond reading the narrowed expression.

Bead left `in_progress`, assignee ExtractTwo, for a non-implementer to grade. Not closed.

comments.text:
GRADE by SnowyCanyon (orchestrator, pane 1, %1397) -- a NON-IMPLEMENTER. VERDICT: **PASS.** Bead
stays in_progress. Three of my readings diverged from the report; **all three were mine or another
agent's in-flight work, and none was a defect in this commit.**

TREE PINNED, gate rule 8: `dc617e2` exists, ancestor of HEAD. `git status --porcelain` on
`crates/cargo-lane-budget` and `crates/pane-truth` -> EMPTY.

**THE THREE DIVERGENCES, DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN FILED -- and this is the fourth and fifth instrument
error of MINE tonight, so the pattern is mine, not the fleet's:**

 1. **`exit_codes` read 9 passed / 1 FAILED where the report says 9/0.** Not a regression. The
    worktree has `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/exit_codes.rs` **modified, +96 lines**, and
    `am robot reservations` shows **CopperBison holding that exact file**. The failing leg is
    `no_declared_pass_through_row_outlives_its_site` -- **the bidirectional leg this bead's own
    finding 1 asked for**, being written as I graded, and failing because `XC-PT-SELFTEST` really is
    empty. **The gate is biting on the real condition, not on a fixture.** I was reading another
    agent's in-flight work and would have filed it as a regression had I not checked ownership
    first. `9/0` was correct at `dc617e2`.

 2. **"1 live emission of `ExitCode::from(selftest()`" where the report says 0.** **My regex was
    broken.** I used `grep -vcE '^\S+:[0-9]+: *(//|///|\*)'` -- but `\S+` is greedy and swallows
    `path:134`, so the pattern then demands a second `:[0-9]+:` and never matches. Printing the
    seven hits shows **all seven are `///` or `//` prose** in `exit_codes.rs` and
    `cargo-lane-budget/src/lib.rs`. **Zero live emissions confirmed; the report was right and my
    instrument manufactured the exception.** Same family as `$?`-after-a-pipe and the ERE parens.

 3. **`cargo-lane-budget` read 10 passed / 1 failed where the report says 11/1.** Crate untouched
    since `dc617e2` (`git log dc617e2..HEAD -- crates/cargo-lane-budget` -> empty), so this is not
    drift. Per-suite: lib **6**, main **0**, conformance **4**, differential **0 passed / 1
    failed** = 10. **I cannot account for the 11th and I am not asserting either number is wrong** --
    most likely a doc-test suite counted in one aggregation and not the other. The failing leg is
    unchanged and is the known EE-P4 `bin/cargo-lane-budget.sh` 127 shell-oracle, which is what
    matters for this bead. **Flagging a one-test disagreement rather than smoothing it**, per the
    64-vs-65 precedent set tonight.

**WHAT I VERIFIED IN THE CODE ITSELF:**
- Finding 1 CONFIRMED from source, and it is a genuine gate defect. `every_pass_through_site_is_declared`
  (`exit_codes.rs:737+`) filters `s.passthrough` for expressions absent from `declared` -- that is
  **scanned ⊆ declared**. I read the whole leg: there is **no reverse loop** over `declared`. So a
  declared row with zero live sites passes silently, and `PASSTHROUGH_FLOOR = 5` was still met, which
  is why the suite stayed green through a change that **emptied a row**. The characterisation as the
  exact mirror of the `code_only()` fiction defect is right: that one stopped the scanner inventing
  a code nothing emits; this is the registry keeping a site nothing occupies. One direction had a
  leg; the other had none.
- Finding 2 CONFIRMED live: `crates/pane-truth/src/main.rs:49` is
  `return ExitCode::from(selftest(&rules) as u8);` and `crates/pane-truth/src/lib.rs:695` is
  `pub fn selftest(rules: &PaneTruthRules) -> i32`. **Same defect, same latency.** And the worse
  half is right too -- the `(`/`&` in the argument means `passthrough_chain` never recognised it, so
  it was **undeclared AND unscanned**: the gate never demanded a row for it. Claimed to you as
  `omp-orchestrator-p4n3`.

**THE MUTATION WORK IS THE BEST IN THE SESSION AND M2 IS WHY.** M1 (`failures as u8` restored) fired
two legs; **M2 broke ONLY the message half, leaving the code correct, and fired exactly one leg** --
`the_line_and_the_status_cannot_disagree`. That single-leg firing is the proof gate rule 7 is
actually asking for: it demonstrates the message assertion is **independently load-bearing**, and
that an exit-code-only suite would be blind to M2 entirely. Restores diffed byte-identical against
recorded shas, twice. The known-bad leg pinning the mechanism as an assertion before the fix
(`assert_eq!(256_i32 as u8, 0)`) is the right order -- it proves the bug exists in Rust's semantics
before proving the fix removes it.

REMEDY SELECTION (acceptance 1) ACCEPTED WITH ITS REASONING: `selftest_exit_code(i32) -> u8` is
total and returns `u8` literals, so **there is no cast left to move** -- this is not the
move-the-cast option because that option no longer applies. Saturating correctly rejected (a count
would still reach the exit status). Narrowing `selftest`'s signature correctly rejected because
OracleGate's range test pins it and acceptance 3 requires it green -- verified green. Acceptance 4
honoured: `SELFTEST_RED_EXIT` reuses the existing `1`/`XC-001` ("a gate refused"), so nothing new
lands in the closed 1-4 band, and the count stays in the message where a reader can act on it.

**THE OPERATIONAL NOTE IS ACCEPTED AND I AM LANDING IT.** A standalone `.git/hooks/pre-commit` run
now returns **3** with `NOTHING_TO_CHECK: no staged files to check` once an index is empty -- the
`calr` fix working as designed. So post-commit, **the authoritative evidence is the commit-time
`CLEAN` line, and re-running the hook afterwards is a category error**, not a red flag. That trap is
worth landing because the obvious way to double-check a hook now looks like a failure -- I would have
walked into it myself.

NO-CLAIM, adopted: the 22-site census is DATA, not an audit; 20 of 22 are unexamined past reading the
expression and no claim is made that any is broken. Adding mine: this bead fixed a latent truncation
in one crate and **found a live twin, which means the class is not closed** -- `pane-truth` is
claimed, and the seven forwarding sites named (`tick-dispatch` x8, `verify-dispatch:54`,
`loop-tick/main.rs:54`, `loop-driver` x2, `loop-queue-filter:18`, `dispatcher-deadman:165`,
`fleet-monitor:437`) are unexamined and remain so until someone claims them.

title: Installer: 6 unbounded .output() spawns strand the buyer forever on a hung git at install time
description:
WHAT: installer/src/lib.rs has 6 process::Command .output() sites (git x2 :151,:167, strings :234, plus the remaining three) with NO deadline, NO process group, NO typed restrictive terminal. On a foreign host at install time, a hung git (dangling credential prompt, locked repo, network-mounted checkout) blocks the installer FOREVER - the buyer is stranded mid-install with no diagnostic. AmberGate classified this buyer-visible and is right: it fires exactly once, on the machine that matters, in front of the user.

WHY now: the fleet-wide fix pattern already exists and is proven - subprocess_contract::bounded_output (bead m3c, commit 4fc649a): BoundedOutcome{Completed,TimedOut,Unspawned}, process_group(0), reader-thread drain, group TERM+grace+KILL, bounded reap. The installer predates it.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. All 6 sites route through bounded_output with install-appropriate deadlines (git network ops: 60s; strings/file reads: 10s).
2. TimedOut maps to a typed install error naming the step and the remedy (retry / check remote / check credentials) - never a silent partial install, never a generic panic.
3. Failing-first test: a git that outlives the deadline (sleep-child wrapper or git with an unreachable remote in a sandbox) yields the typed TimedOut error, not Ok-with-partial.
4. Mutation leg: drop the deadline, confirm the test hangs-or-RED, restore byte-identical (sha256 both).
5. Verified through BOTH invocation paths: ~/.local/bin/cargo wrapper and the direct toolchain bypass (RCH_CARGO_WRAPPER_BYPASS=1) - the installer must behave identically.
6. NO-CLAIM: a bounded installer is not a tested installer on every foreign OS - macOS measured; Linux paths unexercised.

title: Inbox monitor + sender identity: agents are not notified of mail, and packets carry no FROM line
description:
WHAT: an INBOX MONITOR crate -- every agent pane learns that mail arrived, without polling and
without the operator relaying it. Plus a SENDER IDENTITY convention so a pane can reply to whoever
sent it work.

WHY, operator directive 2026-09-02: "make sure you all announce who you are when sending a message
so a pane can properly contact you back - we can use both agentmail and ntm send but we need
monitors on our inboxes so we get notified if a message comes in."

MEASURED GAPS, both real:
1. NO SENDER IDENTITY. Every packet the orchestrator sent this session went out via
   `ntm send omp-orchestrator --panes=N` with NO sender line. A receiving pane cannot address a
   reply: `ntm send` names a session and an INDEX, and pane indices are not stable handles -- they
   shifted twice tonight, and WAVE.md's roster is stale as a result (it lists pane2=%1408 while
   live tmux says %1413). Two panes also changed MODEL mid-session (%1408 GLM 5.3 -> Opus 5,
   %1409 GLM 5.3 -> GPT-5.6-Luna) while their AGENT names held. Three agents replied this session
   only because they happened to know the orchestrator was pane 1.
2. NO INBOX MONITOR ANYWHERE IN THIS REPO. `crontab -l | grep -iE 'inbox|agent-mail'` returns
   exactly ONE entry, and it is
   `/Users/josh/Developer/control-plane/bin/lib/scheduled-lane-run.sh --lane ag...` -- a shell
   lane, in the other repo, which this repo's one rule forbids and cannot inherit.
   `ls -d crates/*inbox* crates/*mail*` -> nothing.

THE SUBSTRATE ALREADY EXISTS -- do NOT hand-roll a poller (KERNEL-ONLY). Measured from
`am inbox-events --help`: "Read durable, restart-safe inbox delivery events for one recipient",
with `--agent`, `--project`, `--after <cursor>` ("Last fully processed delivery cursor. This is not
a message id"), `--limit 1..1000`, `--position-now` (returns the current durable tail cursor with
no events), and `--json`. That is a cursor-based restart-safe feed: exactly what a monitor needs and
what makes it survive a reboot without replaying or dropping.
Related primitives that also exist: `am check-inbox` (built for git hooks), `am mark-all-read`,
`am robot inbox`, and MCP `fetch_inbox_events`.

ACCEPTANCE:
  1. A Rust crate that, per agent, reads `am inbox-events --after <cursor> --json`, persists the
     cursor, and emits a typed NONZERO outcome when unread mail exists for that agent. Zero mail is
     a healthy silent no-op; mail present and unannounced must be loud. Per AGENTS.md the only
     signal measured to reach a human is a typed nonzero outcome the operator must answer -- a log
     line is not a monitor. `ATTENTION.txt` took 178 consecutive ticks from one writer with zero
     readers; do not build a second one.
  2. Cursor durability proven: run, record cursor, restart, run again -- no replay and no gap.
     `--position-now` establishes the baseline. This is the property that distinguishes a monitor
     from a poller.
  3. Notification reaches the PANE, not a file. Resolve the target at emit time via
     `tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} #{session_name}:#{window_index}.#{pane_index}'` and record
     the RESOLVED pane_id in the ledger row -- "notified pane 1" is undiagnosable, "notified %1397,
     resolved from index 1 at 05:1xZ" is evidence.
  4. SENDER IDENTITY CONVENTION, enforced not just documented: every dispatch packet opens with a
     FROM line naming the sending agent, its pane_id, and BOTH reply paths -- the `ntm send` form
     and the Agent Mail identity. A gate over `crates/*/src` dispatch sites that refuses a packet
     with no FROM line, with a fires-on-known-bad leg.
  5. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: plant an unread message for a test agent -> monitor exits nonzero naming
     the agent and the message; mark read -> exits 0. Byte-identical restore, both sha256 recorded.
  6. ANTI-VACUITY: an unreachable Agent Mail daemon is an ERROR, never "no mail". Measured tonight:
     `am agent start` claimed "no listener on 127.0.0.1:8765" while `curl /health` returned
     `status: ready` and two robot calls returned live data -- a false negative on reachability.
     `--direct` (direct SQLite read when no daemon is reachable) is the documented fallback, and
     using it must be REPORTED, not silent.

NON-GOALS: do not build a second messaging system. `ntm send` stays the transport for pane work
packets; Agent Mail stays the durable record plus reservations. This bead adds notification and
attribution to what exists.

NO-CLAIM: a monitor makes an arrived message LOUD, not read. It cannot prove an agent acted on it,
and it does not fix `RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send` recording that a send RETURNED rather than
arrived -- a properly claimed bead sent to a dead pane still reports a receipt it does not have
(cp-z42vu class, still live). Agent Mail's own `last_active` is also NOT a work oracle: it read
`inactive 5h` for AmberGate minutes after AmberGate delivered a graded verdict.

  12  MailWaiting       a human owes an answer to a NAMED sender

  14  CursorRegressed   our cursor is AHEAD of the tail; further runs would SKIP events
  15  CursorBelowFloor  our cursor is BELOW the recipient's floor; further runs see NOTHING

A log line is not a monitor. `ATTENTION.txt` took 178 consecutive ticks from one writer with zero

answer. So the monitor exits nonzero, names the sender and subject, and records the RESOLVED

— a row naming a crate that now complies FAILS — so the list can only shrink.

THREE WILDCARD FINDINGS: ALL REAL. Judged, not contorted away.
===============================================================================
state-wildcard-lint named `_ => None,` at main.rs:393, :397, :401 in `match observation.verdict`.
`MonitorVerdict` is a genuine four-variant state enum, so a catch-all renders a NEWLY ADDED
verdict as absent instead of forcing a decision at the render site — the same class as ntm
coercing state=UNKNOWN into a busy claim, a non-answer wearing a negative one. Now exhaustive with
explicit arms at all three sites, so a fifth variant fails to compile. Violations from my crate:
4 -> 0. WildcardFix's c107c90 reporting fix earned its keep: file, line and the offending arm on
brand-new code within minutes, with no predicate to reverse-engineer.

===============================================================================
A PRECEDENCE INVERSION, DISCLOSED — an already-green assertion changed
===============================================================================
tests/monitor.rs:391-397 asserted `MailWaiting` outranks `CursorRegressed`, reasoning that "the
human can act on mail now, and a state repair does not expire." That is now inverted, and the old
comment and expectation are QUOTED in the test rather than deleted — an inverted assertion with no
explanation is indistinguishable from one flipped to get green.

The mechanism that beats the old reasoning: `main.rs` advances the cursor for every verdict except
`Unreachable`, so a mail-first order does not merely deprioritise the cursor fault — it writes
next_cursor and DESTROYS the only evidence that positions were skipped. The fault must outrank the
mail claim because the fault invalidates the page the mail claim is DERIVED FROM. A verdict about
contents is worthless when the position those contents came from is unproven. Both cursor faults
now also ABSTAIN from advancing the cursor; a known-good arm proves a provable position still
reports MailWaiting, so the reordering is not an over-strict gate.

===============================================================================
THE MEASURED DEFECT XC-015 DEFENDS AGAINST
===============================================================================
The daemon documents CURSOR_EXPIRED for a read below retained history. It does not emit it.
Measured, isolated with a redirect and never a pipe:

  am inbox-events --agent GreenFrog --after 1 --limit 3 --json   ->  rc=0
    first event served from cursor 2108, oldest_available_cursor 2108
    keys: events, has_more, next_cursor, oldest_available_cursor, tail_cursor
    error / code / status keys: NONE

Asked from 1, served from 2108: 2,107 positions silently skipped behind a normal success shape,
with no field in the payload capable of expressing the refusal the tool documents. A caller cannot
detect the clamp from the response at all — only by comparing its OWN stored cursor against
oldest_available_cursor BEFORE the call. Hence client-side, and hence first.

AND A RETRACTION I DID NOT PROPAGATE: a "~17 event retention window" was circulated fleet-wide.
I measured it before building rather than trusting it, and it is REFUTED — GreenFrog 2108/5161
span 3053, AmberGate 2058/5162 span 3104, SnowyCanyon 5147/5165 span 18, BrightGorge 0. An
eviction window of seventeen cannot coexist with a recipient retaining 3,053 positions.
`oldest_available_cursor` is that recipient's FIRST retained event, and for a mailbox registered
tonight it IS its first event. NOTHING is being evicted, and no code or comment here says otherwise.

The guard's justification is structural instead, and stronger for it: a recipient's events are
SPARSE and NON-CONTIGUOUS in one GLOBAL monotonic sequence (GreenFrog holds 2108, 2109, 2126), so
a cursor below the floor CANNOT be distinguished from a recipient that simply started later.
Continuity is unprovable in both branches, so refusing is right either way — the guard needs no
cause. The borrowed cursor is kept only as the measured how-we-get-here: 5105 was circulated to
four agents, is below SnowyCanyon's floor of 5147, and is perfectly resumable for GreenFrog.

===============================================================================
1. I added `inbox-monitor` to the CRATES cell of XC-PT-EXITCODE. The gate keys on the EXPRESSION
   cell, and the monitor's expression is `verdict.exit_code()`, not `v.exit_code()`. Wrong cell,
   silently ineffective — the same write-looks-accepted-does-nothing family as everything else
   tonight. Corrected to a new row, XC-PT-VERDICT-CODE.
2. I asserted `am inbox --json` row keys (read_ts, created_ts, thread_id) as measured fact and
   circulated them. My own mailbox had ZERO rows, so a positive control was impossible and I
   asserted anyway. The real CLI row keys are ack_status, age, from, id, importance, priority,
   subject, thread, topic; read state is `priority`, not `read_ts`. `read_ts` belongs to the MCP
   surface. Two authorities, two shapes; the crate carries an adapter and documents it.

===============================================================================

  cargo test --quiet -p no-shell-gate --test sender_identity ok. 8 passed; 0 failed
  cargo test --quiet -p no-shell-gate --test exit_codes      FAILED. 6 passed; 1 failed

belong to other crates: `selftest() (in cargo-lane-budget)` and `outcome.code (in
refill-idle-panes)` x4. `inbox-monitor` is ABSENT from that list. I will not declare another

(omp-orchestrator-calr). The hook reports "MULTI-GATE: no staged files to check" and exits 0 on an

cited nowhere; this poll ran with 7 staged files and is a real verdict. A caller needs three

taken to avoid the shared-index sweep hazard, is what produced the vacuous green; both were correct

title: Pre-commit hook silently eats commits under concurrent panes on the shared checkout
description:
WHAT: the pre-commit hook SILENTLY ATE COMMITS on this shared checkout when panes commit concurrently (measured 2026-09-01, AmberGate). A hook that drops work without a sound is worse than one that fails loudly: the author believes the commit landed, the tree diverges, and the loss surfaces hours later as a missing change nobody can attribute. --no-verify is the workaround in circulation; it is not a fix - it disables every gate to escape one defect.

FAILURE MODE TO REPRODUCE: two panes run git commit concurrently on the shared checkout; one commit's gate outcome is lost - either the commit silently succeeds without gate coverage or the hook's verdict is overwritten by the racing invocation. The shared .git/index lock makes this a shared-checkout-only defect; single-clone workflows never see it.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Reproduce the silent loss with two concurrent commit processes in a fixture repo (both exit 0, one gate skipped or one commit lost) - the failing-first test.
2. The fix must make the loss IMPOSSIBLE, not louder: either the hook serializes per-index (flock the exact gate section) or concurrent commits are refused with a typed RETRY_CONCURRENT_COMMIT verdict the author can re-run. A refusal that names the race is acceptable; silence is not.
3. Mutation leg: remove the serialization/refusal, confirm the concurrent-loss test goes RED, restore byte-identical (sha256 both).
4. Known-GOOD: sequential commits keep passing every gate (the gate must still bite on real violations after the fix).
5. NO-CLAIM: this does not make the hook's individual gates correct - it makes the hook's OUTCOME trustworthy under concurrency.

OWNER: unassigned. The hook binary is fleet-managed (no-shell-gate bins + .git/hooks install path); the defect is shared-checkout concurrency, which is this repo's daily reality.

title: ntm mail_pending discards cursor_info on the signal-cancelled path (defended in agent-mail-native)
description:
# WHAT

`ntm --robot-wait --wait-until=mail_pending` DISCARDS its resumable cursor
triple when the process is killed by an external signal, while the very same
kernel returns that triple on its own internal-deadline path.

- own deadline fires  -> `error_code=TIMEOUT`,  `cursor_info` PRESENT
- external signal     -> `error_code=CANCELED`, `cursor_info` ABSENT

A supervisor that bounds the wait therefore costs its caller the resume point,
and the caller cannot distinguish "nothing arrived" from "I lost my place".

# WHY THIS BEAD IS NARROW — three wrong theories died first

This is filed at the request of SnowyCanyon, who asked that the record include
how badly the fleet mis-modelled this call. Three successive conclusions were
reported as measured and all three were wrong:

1. "NON-DETERMINISTIC / RED, do not build on it" (SnowyCanyon). Retracted.
2. "The `--timeout` FLAG is the discriminator" (AmNative, then JourneySpine).
   Retracted — the flag is not the discriminator.
3. "The default path is UNBOUNDED and blocks forever" (JourneySpine).
   Retracted.

All three were the same error in different clothes: EACH READER MEASURED ITS
OWN SIGTERM AND ATTRIBUTED IT TO THE KERNEL. `waited_seconds` tracked the
caller's own outer ceiling linearly, which is why three readers with three
ceilings got three different numbers from "the same" invocation.

SnowyCanyon's original "reproduced twice" was two runs of one badly-shaped
invocation — repetition, not replication.

# THE SETTLED MEASUREMENT — four readers, one box, 2026-09-02

| invocation | outer ceiling | error_code | cursor_info | waited_seconds |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `--timeout=15s` | none | TIMEOUT | present | 16.03 |
| `--timeout=20s` | none | TIMEOUT | present | 20.04 |
| `--timeout=30s` | none | TIMEOUT | present | 30.05 |
| no flag | `timeout 75` | CANCELED | ABSENT | 71.34 |
| no flag | `timeout 90` | CANCELED | ABSENT | 83.47 |
| no flag | `timeout 180` | CANCELED | ABSENT | 176.03 |
| no flag | `timeout 340` | **TIMEOUT** | **present** | **300.34** |

The 340s row is the only ceiling in the set that can discriminate, and it
settles it: the DOCUMENTED 5-MINUTE DEFAULT IS REAL, IT FIRES, AND IT PRODUCES
THE GOOD SHAPE. Verbatim:

```
{"success":false,"error":"timeout after 5m0s","error_code":"TIMEOUT",
 "session":"omp-orchestrator","condition":"mail_pending",
 "waited_seconds":300.344741,"agents":[],
 "cursor_info":{"observed_cursor":298904,"next_cursor":298904,
                "oldest_cursor":2978...}}
```

The healthy alternative wake also works and was verified independently:
`ntm --robot-attention --attention-cursor=298315` returns
`wake_reason: "attention"` with `trigger_event.cursor: 298316`. So the
attention feed is live; there was never a "mail wake is broken" problem.

`--attention-condition` / `--condition` exist with condition values that remain
UNMEASURED.

# THE GENERALISABLE RULE (JourneySpine's, worth outliving this bead)

**A timeout probe cannot measure a deadline longer than its own ceiling, so a
bounded observation can never establish unboundedness.** Before reporting "no
deadline exists", the ceiling must exceed every documented default — if the
docs name 5m, the probe must exceed 5m or say nothing. This is
timeout-is-not-a-verdict turned on the OBSERVER: our ceiling is not a verdict
about the kernel either.

Companion rule, from the same session: **a known-bad gate must assert its
MESSAGE, not just its exit code.** During an unrelated workspace outage,
`cargo test -p no-shell-gate --test orchestration_tick` returned exit 101 for a
completely different reason than the finding it supports, which also returns
101. Same exit code, different cause; a fires-on-known-bad leg matching only
`rc != 0` would have gone green on the outage.

# RESOLUTION PATH

DEFENDED in `crates/agent-mail-native` (`wake` module), and the upstream defect
NAMED here for `ntm`:

- `WakeRequest::timeout` is a `Duration`, NOT an `Option<Duration>`, so a
  caller cannot inherit the default ceiling. The reason is honest and is not
  the retracted one: 5 minutes is far too long for a dispatch loop, and owning
  the ceiling is what KEEPS the cursor — our deadline yields TIMEOUT plus the
  triple, someone else's signal yields CANCELED plus nothing. Bounding it
  ourselves makes the good path the default path.
- `MailWakeOutcome::CancelledWithoutCursor` is a DISTINCT variant from
  `TimedOut`, because one keeps the resume point and the other does not.
  Neither ever means "no mail".
- A `TIMEOUT` arriving WITHOUT `cursor_info` is refused as
  `MailError::Protocol` rather than having a resume point invented for it.
- An unrecognised `error_code` is refused, never guessed.
- The wake is spawned through the existing `subprocess-contract` kernel (own
  process group, both pipes drained, `Cx`-observed). No poller was written:
  the blocking wake already exists, so re-implementing it as a sleep loop
  would be a KERNEL-ONLY violation.
- Agent Mail (durable truth) and NTM (live notification) are kept in separate
  modules with separate cursor TYPES — `DeliveryCursor` (~5,180) versus
  `AttentionCursor` (~298,900). Both are bare integers on the wire and were
  circulated in the same conversation; the newtypes make the swap a compile
  error.

# ACCEPTANCE

- `wake::parse_wake` is unit-tested against the VERBATIM captured bodies for
  all four shapes: TIMEOUT-with-triple, CANCELED-without-cursor,
  successful attention wake, and both refusal shapes.
- A test asserts `WakeRequest::argv()` ALWAYS contains `--timeout=`, so the
  unbounded-inheritance path is unreachable through the type.
- A test asserts a sub-second `Duration` still emits a nonzero ceiling
  (`--timeout=0s` would be indistinguishable from no ceiling).
- A test asserts CANCELED and TIMEOUT are not equal and that only TIMEOUT
  yields a `resume_cursor()`.
- A test asserts no terminal shape reports as conclusive about mail.
- Green in `cargo test -p agent-mail-native` (61 unit tests, 0 failed).

# UPSTREAM

`github.com/Dicklesworthstone/ntm`. The ask is small: emit `cursor_info` on the
signal-cancelled path as it already does on the deadline path. The observed
`ntm` is v1.2.0 robot output on the Homebrew build, which is not our build.

title: ntm classifier coerces UNKNOWN into working for codex panes
description:
WHAT: `ntm` cannot classify a codex pane. It reports `state=UNKNOWN, confidence=0.5` and
then RENDERS `observation_state=working, safe_to_dispatch=false` from that non-answer.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 03:14:55Z, `ntm --robot-activity=omp-orchestrator`, verbatim:

  pane  agent_type  state    confidence  observation_state  safe_to_dispatch
  1     claude      UNKNOWN  0.5         idle               true
  2     codex       UNKNOWN  0.5         working            false
  3     codex       UNKNOWN  0.5         working            false
  4     omp-glm     ERROR    0.95        working            false
  5     omp-glm     UNKNOWN  0.5         working            false

`pane-dispatch-ready omp-orchestrator --json` at the same minute reported panes 2 and 3
FREE ("agent present, composer holds no typed text").

WHY IT COSTS REAL HOURS: `refill-idle-panes` required both surfaces to agree a pane was
idle before dispatching, so for a codex pane the conjunction was never true and the lane
could not dispatch to a codex worker BY CONSTRUCTION. Three of four workers that session
were codex. Every refill came from the operator by hand.

Note the two rows for the SAME `state=UNKNOWN, confidence=0.5`: pane 1 rendered
`observation_state=idle, safe_to_dispatch=true`, panes 2/3/5 rendered
`working/false`. So the coercion is not even consistent — the same non-answer produces
opposite dispatch verdicts depending on something the payload does not expose.

WORKED AROUND, NOT FIXED: omp-orchestrator-oe2 taught `refill-idle-panes` to read
UNKNOWN as UNKNOWN and let the CONFIRMING surface decide (commit 8e0b722). That repairs
one consumer. Every other consumer of `safe_to_dispatch` still reads a coerced boolean,
and the fix belongs upstream in the classifier.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. Establish WHY the classifier fails on codex panes — prompt-marker heuristics,
    scrollback shape, agent_type detection, or something else. State it with a capture.
 2. Either teach the classifier to recognise codex, or stop rendering
    `observation_state`/`safe_to_dispatch` from an UNKNOWN state at all: a payload that
    says "I do not know" and a payload that says "busy" must not be the same bytes.
 3. Explain the pane-1 vs pane-2 divergence above, or make it impossible.
 4. If the fix is in NTM proper rather than in this repo, file it upstream with the
    verbatim capture and record the issue number here.

NO-CLAIM: this bead does not establish that the classifier CAN be fixed, nor that codex
is the only agent type affected — `omp-glm` also came back UNKNOWN at 0.5 in the same
capture, which suggests the failure is broader than codex.

comments.text:
RETRACTED BY ITS FILER. The mechanism in the description below is FALSE and this bead
should be closed as invalid unless someone re-files the residual question.

I filed this on the orchestrator's premise — "ntm cannot classify a codex pane and
COERCES state=UNKNOWN into observation_state=working, safe_to_dispatch=false" — without
deriving it myself. It does not survive measurement.

MEASURED, two captures of `ntm --robot-activity=omp-orchestrator` 23 minutes apart:

  safe_to_dispatch == (observation_state == "idle")   10/10 rows
  a rule derived from `state`                          5/10 rows  (4/5 then 1/5)

03:37:51Z, the capture that refutes it:

  pane  state     conf  observation_state  safe_to_dispatch
  1     THINKING  0.8   idle               TRUE
  2     THINKING  0.8   working            FALSE
  3     THINKING  0.8   working            FALSE
  4     UNKNOWN   0.5   idle               TRUE
  5     UNKNOWN   0.5   idle               TRUE

`state=UNKNOWN` panes are DISPATCHABLE and `state=THINKING` panes are NOT. `state` is
anti-correlated with the dispatch field on that capture. `safe_to_dispatch` never
consults `state`; it tracks `observation_state`. There is no unknown-to-working
coercion, and `docs/contracts/pane_observation_contract.md` PO-L5-DISPATCH-SEPARATE
already states that dispatch admissibility is a separate field from liveness.

The evidence to refute this was in my own earlier comment on omp-orchestrator-oe2 — I
wrote "the same UNKNOWN@0.5 rendered idle/true on pane 1 and working/false on 2/3/5, the
coercion is not even self-consistent" — and I recorded it as a wart instead of reading it
as a refutation. Recording a disconfirming detail and then not acting on it is how a
measurement gets wasted.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED at 03:14:55Z is a genuine two-surface CONFLICT between confident
sources: `ntm` reported panes 2 and 3 working at observation_confidence 0.95 while
`pane-dispatch-ready` reported them FREE. `refill-idle-panes` refusing was CORRECT; the
defect was that it rendered the refusal as "nothing to do" at exit 0. Fixed in 49b5b38
(refill now emits a typed nonzero SURFACE_CONFLICT naming each pane).

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and it is NOT this bead: which of the two surfaces is wrong. That is
tracked by omp-orchestrator-readiness-l3-motion-window-7523 (pane-dispatch-ready's
DEFAULT_MOTION_SECS=10 against the 75s floor in pane-truth:39, tick-monitor:490 and
PO-L1), which AmberGate found and which is a concrete candidate for a FALSE FREE on the
oracle side.

RESIDUAL QUESTION WORTH KEEPING, if anyone wants to re-file it: `state` reported UNKNOWN
at confidence 0.5 for codex AND omp-glm panes across both captures, so the last-line
liveness classifier does appear to fail on non-claude agent types. That is a real defect
in a real field — it just is not the field dispatch reads, so it did not cause the
outage, and nothing in this repo currently consumes it for dispatch.

title: observation_state read idle@0.95 on a pane proven WORKING at the two-capture grade
description:
## WHAT

`ntm` reported `observation_state: "idle"` at `observation_confidence: 0.95` — and
`safe_to_dispatch: true` — for a pane that was **provably WORKING at the strongest evidence
grade this repo defines**. Both `--robot-activity` and `--robot-tail` agreed on idle. Both were
wrong.

Measured 2026-09-02T03:42-03:44Z on `omp-orchestrator` pane 1, two `--robot-tail` captures
~95 seconds apart (above the 75-second floor):

```
A   ⠏ 26m  · ◕ Opus 5 · ⏸ Goal 878K · 📁 ~/Developer/omp-orchestrator · ⑂ main *8 ?5 · ◫ 77.4%/1M
B   ⠼ 28m  · ◕ Opus 5 · ⏸ Goal 878K · 📁 ~/Developer/omp-orchestrator · ⑂ main *9 ?5 · ◫ 77.9%/1M
```

Both lines carry a braille spinner AND an elapsed timer — the v18 WORKING signature recorded in
`AGENTS.md`. The timer ADVANCED (26m → 28m), the spinner changed (⠏ → ⠼), and the dirty-file
count moved (`*8` → `*9`). That satisfies `pane_observation_contract` `PO-L1` on both clauses:
two captures ≥75s apart with a changed timer and a changed content hash. WORKING is proven, not
inferred.

At the same two timestamps, `ntm --robot-activity=omp-orchestrator` returned for pane 1:
`state: "THINKING"`, `observation_state: "idle"`, `observation_confidence: 0.95`,
`safe_to_dispatch: true`. `ntm --robot-tail` returned `state: "idle"`.

## WHY

`docs/contracts/pane_readiness_contract.md` §2.2 landed six minutes before this measurement with
the conclusion **"gate on `observation_state`, never on `state`"**, derived from a five-pane
snapshot in which `safe_to_dispatch == (observation_state == "idle")` held on every row and the
observation channel carried 0.95 on every pane. That conclusion is now known to be incomplete:
`observation_state` can be confidently wrong, and `safe_to_dispatch` inherits the error.

This is worse than the `state=UNKNOWN` case the contract already documents. An UNKNOWN at 0.5
announces its own weakness; an `idle` at 0.95 does not. A dispatcher that took the contract's
advice would have dispatched into a pane 28 minutes into a turn.

It is also the operational failure the fleet keeps paying for: a dispatch is admitted, the
receiving pane is mid-turn, and the packet either queues invisibly or is dropped. The send in
question reported `successful: ["1"]` and the packet never appeared in the pane's visible window
or its composer — sender success with no receiver receipt.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Reproduce and bound the defect. On a pane whose last status line carries a spinner plus an
   advancing timer, capture `ntm --robot-activity=<session>` twice ≥75s apart and record
   `observation_state` / `observation_confidence` alongside the two status lines. Expect the
   contradiction; if it does not reproduce, record the conditions under which it does not — the
   pane's agent type, its turn length, and whether an approval dialog is open. A defect that
   cannot be re-triggered is a different bead.
2. Determine which side is broken. `observation_state` is derived by `ntm`; this repo does not
   own it. Either (a) `ntm`'s observation derivation misreads the v18 spinner+timer footer, which
   is an upstream report with the two captures attached, or (b) it derives from a stale or
   differently-scoped capture than `--robot-tail` returns, which is a freshness bug. Read
   `capture_collected_at` and `capture_provenance` against the tail's `captured_at` and say
   which.
3. Stop trusting the field until (2) answers. The kernels that decide dispatch —
   `pane-truth`, `tick-monitor`, `pane-dispatch-ready` — must not treat
   `observation_state == "idle"` as sufficient. The available substitute is already in the tree:
   `pane-truth` reads the last status line and enforces the 75-second floor itself. Then:
   `git grep -n --no-index -F 'observation_state' -- 'crates/*/src/*'` — every remaining site
   either does not gate dispatch on it, or names why it may.
4. `cargo test -p pane-dispatch-ready --test readiness_contract` stays at 12 passed. The leg
   `l2_the_observation_channel_was_confidently_wrong_about_a_working_pane` pins the measurement
   verbatim; if the upstream behaviour changes, that leg must be updated with the new evidence
   rather than deleted.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- Fixing `ntm`. We do not own it; step 2 decides whether this becomes an upstream issue.
- The two other readiness defects: `readiness-l1-wedge-blind-46y7` and
  `readiness-l3-motion-window-7523`.
- `crates/refill-idle-panes` and `crates/omp-types`.

## NO-CLAIM

One pane, one machine, one two-minute window. It is enough to refute "observation_state is the
channel to gate on", because a single counter-example refutes a universal — and it is NOT enough
to characterise the failure mode, name its trigger, or claim `observation_state` is wrong in
general. Step 1 of the acceptance exists precisely because that characterisation does not exist
yet.

Nor does this prove the earlier five-pane snapshot was wrong. Both measurements stand: in that
snapshot the derivation followed `observation_state`, and in this one `observation_state` itself
was false. Those are consistent, and together they say the derivation is faithful to a field
that can lie.

title: 13 of 17 dual-surface readers handroll the comparator; empty ntm read as consensus, cron lane reported nothing-to-do for hours
description:
WHAT: 13 of 17 crates that read BOTH tmux and ntm handroll their own comparator instead of routing
through `oracle-compare`, which already implements the correct semantics. Nothing gates it.

MEASURED 2026-09-02 in /Users/josh/Developer/control-plane:

  dual-surface readers (tmux AND ntm both referenced in src):     17
  ROUTED through oracle-compare:                                   4
    arc-checkin, fleet-arc-report, oracle-pane-state-differential, pane-oracle-diff
  HANDROLL:                                                       13
    arc-keepalive, bughunt-tick, controller-tick, fast-dispatch, fleet-monitor,
    fleet-reconcile, fleet-truth, loop-driver, loop-tick, ntm-fleet-monitor,
    omp-idle-dispatch, refill-idle-panes, xtask

  gate enforcing the routing:  NONE. `grep -rln oracle-compare */tests/*.rs` returns only
  undrained-pipe-lint's specimens, which merely mention the string.

THE MOST DAMNING ROW: `fleet-reconcile` — tmux=67 references, ntm=8 — is the crate whose entire
documented purpose in AGENTS.md is "NTM projection vs tmux reality". The dedicated reconciliation
crate does not use the reconciliation kernel.

WHY IT COSTS REAL HOURS, measured tonight:

`refill-idle-panes` is cron'd at 8,28,48 and ran at 02:49:20 while all four panes were
NEWLY_IDLE. It wrote `refill: no idle pane both surfaces agree on — nothing to do` and exited 0.
Cause: `ntm --robot-activity=omp-orchestrator` returns `0 panes` (the documented NTM projection
defect), so the intersection with tmux's four idle panes is empty, and the lane read EMPTY as
CONSENSUS THAT THERE IS NO WORK. The operator hand-dispatched four waves across the session and
was told four times by Joshua that workers were idle.

`oracle-compare` already has the rule that prevents this, as a first-class variant:
`Rule::EmptyOracleIsError`, `Rule::UnreadableIsError`, `Rule::EmptyProductIsError`
(crates/oracle-compare/src/lib.rs:20-37). Had refill routed through it, 02:49 would have produced
a typed nonzero refusal naming the broken ntm probe — and AGENTS.md establishes that a typed
nonzero outcome the operator must answer is the ONLY signal measured to reach a human.

THE ALGEBRA, because the dual read is NOT the fix on its own:
Both approaches read the same two surfaces and reach opposite conclusions from identical data.
  intersection  (refill)         absence -> "not idle"  -> empty -> "nothing to do", exit 0
  differential  (oracle-compare) absence -> ERROR
Two-valued logic collapses missing data into a negative assertion. Three-valued logic keeps
UNKNOWN inhabited. `docs/contracts/pane_observation_contract.md` L2 — written TONIGHT, hours after
this defect had already run all night — states it: "Unknown is a first-class value and NEVER
coerces to Idle." refill violates that law exactly.

NOTE the direction that IS correct: requiring both surfaces to agree before DISPATCHING is right
conservatism — you do not interrupt a working pane on one stale read. The bug is applying the same
rule to ABSENCE of data, where the conservative answer is "I cannot tell, refuse loudly."

HOW JEFF GATES IT — the pattern to copy, not invent
(`franken_lean/crates/fln-conformance/tests/contract_roots.rs`):

  const UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE: &[(&str, &str)] = &[];   // (lane, reason), EMPTY by design

Two properties make it work, and both are non-obvious:

 1. IT FAILS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Unwired-and-undeclared fails. Wired-but-STILL-DECLARED also
    fails, verbatim: "an allowance that outlives its defect is how a repaired gap keeps reading as
    broken, and it is what stops this list from shrinking." That is exactly what bit us: AGENTS.md
    claimed refill-idle-panes carried only control-plane paths; it was fixed Sep 1 19:29 and the
    stale note licensed hand-dispatching for hours.
 2. IT DISTINGUISHES EXECUTED FROM NAMED. Its comment: check.sh "names contract_drift.sh twice —
    once in INPUT_PATHS, once as an argument to the shellcheck stage — and a `contains` check reads
    both as registration. Neither runs it." A Cargo.toml dependency edge is NAMED; routing the
    comparison through the kernel is EXECUTED. The 13/17 figure above only proves the former.

PRECEDENT IN THIS REPO: `spawn_contract` already gates subprocess-contract routing across 15
crates / ~144 sites. The pattern exists for subprocesses and not for the comparator.

ACCEPTANCE:
 1. A gate — `oracle_routing` — asserting every dual-surface reader routes its comparison through
    oracle-compare, with an `UNROUTED_ALLOWANCE: &[(&str, &str)]` seeded from the gate's OWN scan
    and a REASON per row.
 2. BIDIRECTIONAL: a crate that starts routing while still on the allowance list must go RED, so
    the list can only shrink.
 3. EXECUTED, not NAMED: a Cargo.toml edge alone must not satisfy it. Assert the comparison call
    site, or state in Non-Coverage that the gate checks routing-by-dependency only and cannot see
    a crate that depends on oracle-compare and still handrolls beside it.
 4. Anti-vacuity: an empty reader set is an ERROR, never a pass.
 5. Known-good leg MANDATORY: the four ROUTED crates must pass.
 6. Mutation: strip oracle-compare from one routed crate -> RED. Restore byte-identical.
 7. FIRST CONVERSION IN THE SAME PASS: route `refill-idle-panes` with
    `empty_oracle_is_error = true`, and prove it by making ntm return empty and observing a typed
    nonzero refusal rather than "nothing to do".

NO-CLAIM: this bead does not establish that all 13 SHOULD route through oracle-compare. Some may
legitimately read two surfaces for non-comparison reasons, and each needs a reason row rather than
a blanket conversion. The gate makes the choice VISIBLE; it does not make it for us.
close_reason: MUTATION-VERIFIED by AmberGate (pane 4, non-implementer). All four claims independently re-run, not read. (1) gate 9 passed. (2) refill-idle-panes 30 lib + 6 differential. (3) all three mutation legs reproduced with byte-identical restores and both sha256 published: erase comparator symbols with the dep INTACT -> 2 RED naming 'DECLARES oracle-compare but names NO comparator (spawn helpers do not count)' (src sha dac2882->dbb8462->dac2882); strip the dep -> 2 RED 'no oracle-compare dependency at all' (manifest af1ed92->81e0d1d->af1ed92); bidirectional leg fired from the opposite direction because CopperBison holds an exclusive lease on the gate file -> 1 RED '1 allowance row(s) name a crate that NOW ROUTES' (koh src ada017b->08776eb->ada017b). Gate 9 passed after every restore, git clean 0. (4) census 51/12/3/9 reproduced by an independently written reader, exact per-crate agreement; the retracted 17/4/13 was control-plane. PREDICATE SURVIVES: COMPARISON_SYMBOLS covers all 10 comparison items and excludes all 3 spawn helpers, the 3 routed crates are real call sites, and tick-dispatch has ZERO tmux hits by any form so the exact-literal predicate is not missing it. The gate requires a COMPARISON SYMBOL, not the dependency edge, and therefore does NOT inherit the manifest-probe false positive. All 6 claimed substring false positives confirmed genuine non-readers, line-cited. Two MINOR findings, both already disclosed by the gate: a symbol inside a string literal satisfies Routed (disclosed at lines 39-43 as a floor-raise; my probe proves the disclosure load-bearing), and DeclaredOnly is censused only for dual-surface readers so tick-dispatch is unscored -> filed omp-orchestrator-oracle-declared-only-census-bkiq. Provenance: all graded paths clean vs HEAD, all six commits ancestors of HEAD. One burned run disclosed: the packet's original rch lane command was cancelled before output and no result from it is cited. refill-idle-panes source untouched (CopperBison 110816-110820); my mutation targets reserved 110871/110873 and restored before release. Full grade in bead comments.

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
CLAIMED by orchestrator (pane 1) 02:58Z and dispatched to subagent OracleGate. Filed at 02:56Z with assignee=None and zero comments — I filed a P0 and skipped the claim, which is AGENTS.md's fourth rule (file -> CLAIM -> dispatch) violated by the agent who keeps citing it. Joshua asked 'who is handling that bead?' and the honest answer was nobody.

SCOPE RESOLVED: crates/refill-idle-panes is byte-comparable in both repos (tmux=16, ntm=8, routed=False, 3 rs files each) and crates/oracle-compare IS already extracted into omp-orchestrator. So the fix lands HERE, not in control-plane. Cron runs ~/.local/bin/refill-idle-panes and that binary contains the literal 'no idle pane both surfaces agree on', so the installed artifact is in scope too — a source fix that is not reinstalled changes nothing (BUILT != WIRED).

comments.author: josh
comments.text:
CORRECTION FROM THE FILER (pane 1, 03:14Z) — MY EVIDENCE WAS WRONG. THE CONCLUSION SURVIVES.

RETRACTED: "ntm --robot-activity=omp-orchestrator returns 0 panes."

That was a badly-shaped probe, my thirteenth of the session. I parsed `d.get('panes')`. The key is
`agents`. ntm reports FIVE agents and always did.

THE REAL MECHANISM, measured 03:13Z with the correct key:

  pane   ntm state    ntm conf  ntm observation_state  ntm safe_to_dispatch  tmux (tick-monitor)
  %1413  UNKNOWN      0.5       working                false                 CONFIRMED_IDLE
  %1414  UNKNOWN      0.5       working                false                 CONFIRMED_IDLE
  %1408  THINKING     0.8       working                false                 WORKING (agrees)
  %1409  UNKNOWN      0.5       working                false                 UNPROVEN

ntm CANNOT CLASSIFY CODEX PANES — `state=UNKNOWN` at `confidence=0.5` — and then COERCES that
UNKNOWN into `observation_state=working, safe_to_dispatch=false`. refill-idle-panes requires both
surfaces to agree a pane is idle, so for any codex pane the conjunction is NEVER true.

CONSEQUENCE, and this is the finding that matters: **refill-idle-panes can never dispatch to a
codex pane, by construction.** Three of the four workers in this session are codex (panes 2, 3, 5).
That is why every refill came from the operator by hand, and why Joshua had to say "workers idle"
five times.

WHY THE BEAD'S CONCLUSION STILL HOLDS — the defect is the same class, one direction over:
  I claimed:  ntm returns EMPTY  -> intersection empty       -> "nothing to do"
  Truth:      ntm returns UNKNOWN -> coerced to WORKING       -> intersection empty -> "nothing to do"
Both are a three-valued signal collapsed into two-valued logic. `pane_observation_contract` L2 says
"Unknown is a first-class value and NEVER coerces to Idle" — this is its mirror image, and equally
fatal: UNKNOWN must not coerce to WORKING either. An unclassifiable pane is not a busy pane.

empty. The gate and the conversion must additionally treat a LOW-CONFIDENCE / UNKNOWN arm as
UNKNOWN rather than as a state assertion:
  - `confidence <= 0.5` or `state == UNKNOWN` from ntm is NOT evidence of working.
  - When one surface is UNKNOWN and the other is CONFIRMED (two-capture, per
    pane_observation_contract L1), the CONFIRMED surface decides — that is not "silently preferring
    a surface", because UNKNOWN is not a competing claim.
  - A genuine CONFLICT (both surfaces confident, disagreeing) remains an ERROR.
  - PROOF REQUIRED: a codex pane that tmux confirms idle must become dispatchable. The old
    behaviour — refusing forever — must be reproducible as a known-bad.

NO-CLAIM: I have not established WHY ntm cannot classify codex panes; the classifier may be fixable
upstream, which would be the better fix. That is a separate bead. And the 13-of-17 handroll census
in the description stands on its own measurement, unaffected by this correction.

WHAT CHANGED. 609a97b (pane 4 / AmberGate, 21:47:55) landed
`pane_readiness_contract` 2.2.1 while my conversion was in flight, and it refutes the
field 49b5b38 had just adopted. Measured there: ntm reported pane 1
`observation_state: "idle", observation_confidence: 0.95, safe_to_dispatch: true` while
two `--robot-tail` captures 95 seconds apart both carried a braille spinner with the
timer advancing 26m -> 28m and the dirty-file count moving *8 -> *9 — two captures above
the 75-second floor with a changed timer, so WORKING is PROVEN under PO-L1. The
observation channel was confidently wrong about a pane 28 minutes into a turn.

That is WORSE than the `state=UNKNOWN` case: an UNKNOWN at 0.5 announces its own
weakness; an idle at 0.95 does not.

MY JOIN WAS WRONG IN ONE CLAUSE. 49b5b38 dispatched on `one CONFIRMED Idle + one
UNKNOWN`, reasoning that UNKNOWN is not a competing claim so there is nothing to prefer
over. The reasoning is sound; the conclusion is not, because it assumed the confirming
read could not itself be false. 2.2.1: "No single ntm field is sufficient. A positive
free read must be confirmed against the last status line at the two-capture grade."

ADOPTED: `Resolution::Unconfirmed` — exactly one surface says idle and the other cannot
see the pane. NEVER dispatched, always reported. Dispatch now requires BOTH arms
confidently Idle. The asymmetry is deliberate and documented in `resolve`: UNKNOWN yields
to CONFIRMED only in the NEGATIVE direction, so a lone confident BUSY still holds a pane.
A false hold costs a tick of throughput; a false dispatch interrupts a working agent.

A run with nothing dispatchable and an unconfirmed positive is now UNMEASURABLE at exit 2
carrying `unconfirmed_positive=[...]` — not a quiet fleet. That is this bead's own defect
one class over, and it would have shipped unguarded.

30 lib + 6 differential green. Gate still 9/9.

                                              are never consulted."
