title: Type inventory: 51 enums, 79 structs, 4 collisions, 6 Verdict dialects, 4 types asupersync already has
description:
WHAT: the type inventory — a gated, generated list of every public type each crate owns, the collisions between them, and the types we are missing. Josh: "where is our list of types that we are managing, suggesting, and building, for all of the crates per our crate inventory ecosystem — gated in."

IT DID NOT EXIST. We gate the OMP surface per crate (OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml) and the eight asupersync properties per crate (ASUPERSYNC-CONFORMANCE.md). Nothing has ever enumerated the TYPES, which is the layer where "typed, logged, observable" is actually delivered or not.

MEASURED 2026-08-31: 51 public enums, 79 public structs, across 22 of 24 crates.
Two crates own NO public type at all: finding-dispatch and pane-dispatch-fence — both already flagged elsewhere, finding-dispatch as a zero-caller library that is nevertheless omp-orchestrator's only manifest caller.

FINDING 1 — FOUR COLLIDING TYPE NAMES, and one of them is dangerous:
    Finding        finding, state-wildcard-lint
    LintReport     state-wildcard-lint, undrained-pipe-lint
    Violation      no-shell-gate, undrained-pipe-lint
    Observation    omp-orchestrator, tick-monitor      <-- THIS ONE
`Observation` is not a coincidental name clash. tick-monitor PRODUCES the observation that omp-orchestrator's `decide()` CONSUMES, and each defines its own incompatible struct. There is no shared type across the seam, so the producer and the consumer agree only by convention. That is exactly the seam where free_capacity was derived from the wrong filter and where a NewlyIdle pane became invisible as capacity — a defect that would have been a compile error if one type crossed the boundary.

FINDING 2 — SIX VERDICT TYPES, NO SHARED TRAIT:
    AckVerdict, FenceVerdict, FollowUpVerdict, ReceiptVerdict, SilenceVerdict, Verdict
Six independent answers to "what happened", none composable, none countable. This is precisely why grading is prose: there is no type a grade can BE, so a grade cannot be counted, queried, or required. Twelve beads currently sit in_progress with no verdict and nothing noticed, because nothing could.

FINDING 3 — SEVENTEEN TYPES IN THE ACK/RECEIPT VOCABULARY, SPLIT ACROSS TWO INCOMPATIBLE DIALECTS:
    ack-spine speaks AUTHORITY: TransportAuthority, DeliveryAuthority, AckAuthority, AckEvidence, AckSummary
    ack-stage speaks RECEIPT:   TransportReceipt, TransportReceiptError, AckReadback, AckStageInput/Result
    receiver-receipt speaks a third: ReceiptVerdict, ReceiptReason, PostSendObservation
Three crates, three vocabularies, one problem. They were written days apart by different agents against the same gap and never reconciled.

FINDING 4 — THE TYPES WE ARE MISSING, checked by name:
    Grade             ABSENT   <- the gap that makes grading prose
    DeliveryClass     ABSENT   <- asupersync has it: EphemeralInteractive/DurableOrdered/
                                  ObligationBacked/MobilitySafe/ForensicReplayable
    AckKind           ABSENT   <- asupersync has it: "acknowledgement boundary reached"
    ObligationLedger  ABSENT   <- asupersync has it: reserve, then commit or abort
    Budget            ABSENT
    Outcome           PRESENT, but only in tick-monitor and unrelated to asupersync's Outcome
Four of the six absent types ALREADY EXIST in asupersync at the rev we pin (fa3c01aec, v0.4.9). We invented three ack dialects for a vocabulary we already depend on.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. GENERATED, NEVER DRAWN. omp-inventory-map already exists and already models InventoryRow/Node/Edge — extend it to emit the type inventory rather than writing a second scanner. One command, output pasted beside it.
2. COLLISION DETECTION IS A GATE, NOT A REPORT: two crates declaring the same public type name FAILS, unless the row carries a named reason. Same shape as UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE — the allowance starts with the four measured entries above and each states why the duplication is acceptable or when it dies.
3. THE `Observation` COLLISION GETS A DECISION, not an allowance row: one shared type across the tick-monitor -> omp-orchestrator seam, or a stated reason why the producer and consumer must diverge. This is the highest-value single row in the inventory.
4. POSITIVE CONTROL: a crate with a unique, well-formed type set must PASS. A gate that flags all 22 is indistinguishable from a broken one.
5. ANTI-VACUITY: zero types discovered is an ERROR, never a clean inventory. Two crates legitimately own no public type; that must be reported as a NAMED ZERO, not silence.
6. THE MISSING-TYPE LIST IS PART OF THE OUTPUT. An inventory that lists only what exists cannot show a gap, and the gap is the point of this bead.
7. MUTATION: rename a type to collide deliberately; leg 2 goes RED and names both crates. Restore byte-identically, sha both sides.

NO-CLAIM 1: a type inventory proves SHAPE, not SEMANTICS. Two crates can own identically-named types that mean different things (Violation in no-shell-gate vs undrained-pipe-lint may be legitimately distinct), and two differently-named types can mean the same thing — which is exactly the ack/receipt case. The gate catches name collisions; a human decides whether the vocabulary is actually split.
NO-CLAIM 2: "ABSENT" was checked by exact name. A crate could implement DeliveryClass semantics under another name and this scan would call it absent. The four asupersync types are named from that codebase; adopting them is a separate decision, and mapping a surface is not adopting it.

title: Five-leg conformance gate: make every per-crate declaration something cargo test refuses
description:
WHAT: one conformance test with five legs, so every per-crate declaration this repo has written becomes something `cargo test` REFUSES rather than something a document asserts.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT MAKES THIS P0, taken 2026-08-31: we have written four per-crate declarations and THREE OF THEM ARE READ BY NOTHING.

  ENFORCES (something refuses on violation):
    crates/no-shell-gate/tests/wired_lanes.rs   RED right now on "UNWIRED LANE: installer"
    .git/hooks/commit-msg                        Mach-O, MSG_SRC x5, refused the orchestrator's
                                                 own commit at 16:00
    .git/hooks/pre-commit                        enforces no-shell-gate ONLY
  DECLARES (no reader, no refusal):
    OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml         consumed_by_code = 1
    ASUPERSYNC-CONFORMANCE.md    consumed_by_code = 0
    omp-types                    depended_on_by   = 0 of 25 crates

The canonical vocabulary shipped with ZERO dependents forty minutes after being written, by the orchestrator, in the session where that is the cardinal sin. It is available and mandatory nowhere. That is the twentieth BUILT != WIRED here and the reason this bead exists rather than a fifth document.

THE PATTERN TO COPY IS ALREADY IN THE TREE. `wired_lanes.rs` is the only proven enforcement in this repo and it has the right shape:
    fn every_declared_lane_has_a_production_caller()          <- the substantive leg
    fn every_allowance_row_names_a_lane_and_carries_a_reason() <- validates the EXCEPTIONS
The second function is the one most gates omit. Without it an allowance list degrades into a place to put things you do not want to fix.

THE FIVE LEGS, each with an allowance list that starts EMPTY and whose rows carry reasons:

  LEG 1  WIRED — exists, red on `installer`. Do not touch it; extend beside it.
  LEG 2  SURFACE DECLARED — every workspace crate has a [crates.x] block in OMP-SURFACE-MAP.toml.
         UNDECLARED (crate present, no block) and GHOST (block present, no crate) both FAIL.
         The input is validated 21/21 and already ships ONE DELIBERATE GHOST specimen
         (crates.ack-spine-collab-gap) so the GHOST leg fires on an in-tree case permanently.
  LEG 3  ASUPERSYNC CONFORMANCE — the eight properties. forbid(unsafe_code) is mandatory; six
         crates lack it today, and two of those (pane-dispatch-fence, subprocess-contract) carry
         the asupersync dependency while omitting the lint, which is the least defensible pair on
         the board. Every Command::new routes through subprocess-contract or carries a stated
         deadlock-safe reason: 29 raw sites exist against 4 compliant crates.
  LEG 4  CANONICAL TYPES — a crate declaring a public type that duplicates one re-exported by
         omp-types FAILS. This is the leg that makes the vocabulary mandatory instead of
         available, and without it omp-types stays furniture.
  LEG 5  NO COLLISIONS — two crates declaring the same public type name FAILS. Allowance seeded
         with the four measured rows: Finding, LintReport, Violation, Observation. `Observation`
         requires a DECISION, not an allowance row — tick-monitor produces what omp-orchestrator
         consumes and each declares its own incompatible struct, which is the seam where
         free_capacity was derived from the wrong filter and a NewlyIdle pane went invisible as
         capacity. One shared type makes that a compile error.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. All five legs live in ONE test target that runs under plain `cargo test`. Not a binary someone
   remembers to invoke — the distinguishing property of leg 1 is not that it is better written, it
   is that cargo refuses.
2. EVERY LEG HAS ITS OWN ALLOWANCE VALIDATOR, mirroring
   `every_allowance_row_names_a_lane_and_carries_a_reason`. An entry with an empty reason must fail
   the validator, so nobody can silence a leg with a bare path.
3. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD, one specimen per leg, all IN-TREE: an unwired crate (have it), an undeclared
   crate, a crate missing forbid(unsafe_code), a crate redeclaring a canonical type, and a name
   collision. An external apply-patch harness silently no-ops when its index hash misses HEAD.
4. KNOWN-GOOD IS MANDATORY PER LEG: a conforming crate passes every leg untouched. Five legs is
   five times the chance of being over-strict, and an over-strict gate gets routed around, which
   is a slower death than no gate.
5. ANTI-VACUITY PER LEG: zero crates scanned is an ERROR for every leg independently. A shared
   scan that returns empty must not let five legs pass together.
6. MUTATION: break each leg's predicate in turn; that leg goes RED and the other four stay GREEN.
   If breaking one turns several red they share a defect and are not five legs.

NO-CLAIM 1: this makes nonconformance FAIL THE SUITE. It does not make it impossible — a leg can
be deleted, an allowance row added, or the suite skipped. It raises the floor from "a document
says so" to "removing the check is an explicit, reviewable act."
NO-CLAIM 2: legs 2 through 5 are CANDIDATE — specified, inputs measured, not built. Only leg 1 is
banked, and it is banked because it fired unprompted on a real lane. Do not describe this bead as
"the conformance gate" until at least one new leg has gone red on its own specimen.
NO-CLAIM 3: five green legs prove SHAPE, never BEHAVIOUR. A crate can satisfy all five and still
leak a detached task, kill a pid instead of a process group, or map a timeout to the token a
genuinely failing subject produces. Those three cost real time this session and none is greppable.

title: Typed completion signal: the worker says done — nothing infers it
description:
WHAT: two missing mechanisms in the dispatch loop, measured together at 22:39:30Z from one tick-monitor payload. Josh named both: "why isn't our crate substrate finding that pane 4 is idle and why isn't pane 4 letting you know when they are done."

FAILURE 1 — THE OBSERVER FINDS IT AND THEN DISCARDS IT. This is worse than blindness.

  raw tmux, %1408:  the pi glyph        -> idle
  tick-monitor, same instant:
      %1408 state=IDLE t=0                              <- the kernel KNOWS
      idle_panes: {dispatchable: [], count: 0, free_capacity: []}   <- and throws it away

The STATE field is correct. The ACTIONABLE field is empty. Any consumer reading `idle_panes` — which is the field a dispatcher would consume — sees no capacity while a pane sits idle. The information exists and is destroyed one layer up.

ROOT CAUSE, already documented in this repo as a FIXED bug: `free_capacity` is derived from the same `is_dispatchable` filter as `dispatchable`, and `dispatchable` requires CONFIRMED idle (two captures >=75s apart). A pane at t=0 is NEWLY idle, so it is excluded from BOTH lists. omp-orchestrator/src/lib.rs:163-166 records the identical defect verbatim: "an earlier version derived both from one filter, which made the NewlyIdle branch of decide unreachable ... the exact shape that let the fleet sit idle while every watchdog reported healthy."

THE FIX LANDED IN omp-orchestrator AND NOT IN tick-monitor — the observer kept the bug the decider removed. Filed as tickmonitor-free-capacity-blind-vgf, still open. This is its THIRD live occurrence today: the 178-tick capacity failure, panes 4 and 5 at 19:22, and %1408 now.

FAILURE 2 — NO COMPLETION SIGNAL EXISTS AT ALL. This one has no bead until now.

%1408 finished its work somewhere between 22:35 and 22:39 and NOTHING TOLD THE CONDUCTOR. There is no worker->conductor "done" path in this system. Every completion this session was discovered by the conductor happening to look, or by a human saying so in chat.

AND THE FOLLOW-UP STAGE DOES NOT CLOSE THIS. `classify_followup` (ack-spine, closed today) detects SILENCE past a deadline — "this pane went quiet and owes a verdict." That is the pathological case. It does not detect COMPLETION — "this worker finished, here is the verdict, the pane is free." A healthy finish and a hang look identical to a silence detector until the deadline expires, which means every clean completion costs a full deadline of idle time before anything notices.

THE CHAIN, AND WHERE EACH LINK STANDS:
  observe        tick-monitor        WORKS (state is correct)
  actionable     idle_panes          BROKEN (vgf) — discards NewlyIdle
  consumer       supervisor decide() FENCED — 162 refused ticks, owner=josh
  actuator       the conductor       A HUMAN-DRIVEN LOOP, ~30 hand dispatches today
  completion     nothing             DOES NOT EXIST
Four links, one works.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A TYPED COMPLETION SIGNAL, emitted BY THE WORKER, not inferred by a watcher. It carries: bead id, terminal verdict, evidence reference, and the pane's freed-capacity claim. Inference is what we have; it costs a deadline and cannot distinguish finished from wedged.
2. IT MUST SURVIVE PANE DEATH. Per the measured ack analysis, the only artifact that survives a pane dying, a context compaction, and a daemon restart is a durable tracker row. A message is not a completion record. Signal via the bead; the pane may be gone by the time anyone reads it.
3. COMPLETION AND SILENCE ARE DISTINCT OUTCOMES and must not collapse into one enum arm. `Finished{verdict}` and `SilentPastDeadline{minutes}` are different facts with different responses — refill versus investigate. A single "not working" state is the free_capacity defect repeating at a higher layer.
4. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-GOOD: a worker completing normally produces a completion row WITHOUT the conductor polling. Assert the row exists after a real finish. This is the leg that proves the signal is pushed rather than discovered.
5. FIRES-ON-KNOWN-BAD: a worker that dies mid-task produces NO completion row, and the silence detector — not this mechanism — is what fires. Assert the two paths do not overlap.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: zero completions observed in a window where a bead moved to closed is an ERROR. A completion mechanism that never fires is indistinguishable from a fleet that never finishes anything.

DEPENDENCY, STATED HONESTLY: this composes with vgf but does not replace it. Even a perfect completion signal leaves `free_capacity` wrong for panes that go idle WITHOUT completing a bead — an interrupted worker, a cleared pane, a fresh start. Both are needed; neither subsumes the other.

NO-CLAIM 1: a completion signal makes a finish VISIBLE, not VERIFIED. The worker asserts it finished; the conductor still re-runs the cited command before closing. Nine beads today were closed on re-run evidence and two were REFUSED after their author reported success.
NO-CLAIM 2: this closes the notification gap, not the actuation gap. Something must still consume the signal and dispatch. Today that consumer is a human, the supervisor is fenced, and an accurate signal nobody reads is the 178-tick failure with better data.

title: Wave BEADS: task, commands, slash-commands
description:
SURFACES: task, commands, slash-commands (136 commands). Governing skill /beads-workflow -- every bead self-contained with testable acceptance: run X, expect Y.
MEASURED TODAY: a P0 at the head of the ready queue had NO ACCEPTANCE SECTION AT ALL and two agents in a row triaged it and idled rather than shipping. A bead you cannot write acceptance for is not granular enough.
PER-CRATE CONTRACT (all 8 clauses, from the epic): asupersync-native (&Cx first, cx.checkpoint in loops, region-owned tasks, kill the process GROUP); unsafe_code=forbid; cancel-correct (a timeout is not a verdict; drain BOTH pipes -- try_wait past ~64KiB deadlocks, tell is 0% CPU with no children); typed (exhaustive match so a new variant is a compile error); logged (one typed row per step, step count ASSERTED); observable (every field its OWN predicate plus explicit UNKNOWN -- never derive one field from another's filter); robot-reachable (doctor/health/repair, versioned JSON envelope, namespaced probe ids, one command answers 'what is true now'); WIRED (a caller exists and a conformance test proves it, UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE empty).

Category (b) rows MUST name the OMP alternative that exists today. Positive control: at least one surface in this wave reports FULLY COVERED, or the scan is broken. comments.author: SilverWolf
comments.text:
WAVE .4 DISPATCH — MEASURED VERDICT (SilverWolf, pane 5, %1409). Zero builds. Every claim re-derived from the installed binary at runtime.

THE DECIDING QUESTION ANSWERED: does --mode=rpc expose a send-with-receipt for a pane we do not own? **NO.** OMP's --mode=rpc is a SINGLE-SESSION transport — it speaks to the OMP instance in the current process, not to other panes or sessions. Measured: get_state returns structured model data, but there is no pane management, no cross-session dispatch, and no send-to-third-party capability. The mux* methods (muxConnect/muxPing/muxRestartServer) are for the TUI multiplexing layer, not accessible from --mode=rpc.

CLASSIFICATION CORRECTED FROM THE ORCHESTRATOR'S ORIGINAL:
  pane state      (b)→ MIXED: --mode=rpc get_state provides structured model/session state for OUR OWN session — category (b) is correct for single-session state queries. Cross-pane state still requires tmux capture-pane because OMP's RPC cannot see other sessions. So: (b) for same-session state, (a) for cross-pane state.
  dispatch        (b)→ CORRECTED TO (a): OMP's RPC cannot address a third-party pane. tmux send-keys and ntm robot-send are the ONLY mechanisms that work for cross-pane dispatch. Scraping is correct here — there is no OMP alternative to switch to.
  health check    (b)→ MIXED: omp/muxPing exists but is not accessible from --mode=rpc (the mux* layer is TUI-only). The heartbeat file we write IS the correct mechanism. Category (a) for cross-pane, (b) for own-session state.
  session         (b)→ CONFIRMED: OMP's --continue/--resume/--session-dir are real capabilities we should use instead of pane-id tracking. This is the strongest (b) finding.
  receipt         (b)→ NOT CONFIRMED: OMP's --mode=rpc does not provide a delivery receipt for a sent message. The receiver-verification gap (cp-z42vu) cannot be closed by OMP's RPC layer.

THE 42 HANDLER METHODS CLAIM: I probed the --mode=rpc transport and found it accepts input commands (text, get_state, and others) but I could not enumerate the full method registry. The "42 handler methods" figure from the orchestrator's census is plausible but I could not independently derive the complete list. The RPC mode responds to unknown commands with a typed error, so the method set is discoverable by probing — but a comprehensive enumeration requires running a live OMP session with real work, which is beyond this grading pass.

WAVE .4 SURFACES CLASSIFIED:
  irc          (a) genuinely not ours
  collab       (c) capability we should use — multi-agent coordination in OMP
  jsonrpc      (a) genuinely not ours — LSP/DAP message framing, not orchestration
  mcp          (a) genuinely not ours
  launch       (c) capability we should use — OMP's launch/launchd integration
  exec         (b) we reimplemented via subprocess — OMP's exec surface provides structured tool execution
  subprocess   (a) genuinely not ours — OMP internal subprocess management

NO-CLAIM: the --mode=rpc probes ran against a no-session, no-tools, no-lsp, no-extensions instance. A production OMP session with extensions and LSP would expose a different (likely larger) RPC surface. The classification is correct for the launched configuration tested.

title: oracle_routing censuses DeclaredOnly only for dual-surface readers; tick-dispatch is unscored
description:
## WHAT

`oracle_routing`'s `Routing::DeclaredOnly` variant is computed correctly and evaluated for
**only the 12 dual-surface readers**. A crate that declares `oracle-compare`, calls no
comparator, and reads ONE surface is scored by nothing.

`tick-dispatch` is that crate today, measured 2026-09-02 during the oe2 grade:

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| manifest declares `oracle-compare` | **true** |
| comparison symbols in `src/**/*.rs` | **NONE** |
| `oracle_compare` symbols actually used | `spawn_timeout`, `spawn_timeout_stdin` |
| `tmux` by ANY form, case-insensitive, whole src | **0 hits** |
| `ntm` invocation | `src/main.rs:360` `which("ntm")`, `:514` |

So it is genuinely single-surface, correctly outside the dual-surface census — and therefore
outside every assertion in the gate.

## WHY

This is the exact shape of the false positive the oe2 bead was filed about. Its own header
table names three crates that declare the kernel and call zero comparators —
`fleet-arc-report`, `arc-checkin` (control-plane) and `tick-dispatch` (here) — and records
`fleet-arc-report` as "the damning row: it reads both surfaces, handrolls the comparison, and
a manifest probe certified it as fixed."

The gate closes that hole for dual-surface readers: with the dependency edge intact and the
comparator symbols erased, `pane-oracle-diff` goes RED naming
*"DECLARES oracle-compare but names NO comparator (spawn helpers do not count)"* — verified
by mutation during the grade. But the census that selects which crates get examined is keyed
on reading BOTH surfaces. **A green `oracle_routing` is therefore not evidence that no crate
in this repo declares the kernel while handrolling beside it — only that no dual-surface
crate does.**

`control-plane` reportedly carries 12 declare-but-never-compare crates repo-wide. A gate
scoped to dual-surface readers would not have caught the row that motivated it, in the repo
where it happened.

## ACCEPTANCE

`run X, expect Y`:

1. Add one leg to `crates/no-shell-gate/tests/oracle_routing.rs`:
   `every_crate_declaring_oracle_compare_names_a_comparator`. Scope: **all 51 tracked
   crates**, not the dual-surface subset. It reuses `routing_of` and `crate_sources`
   unchanged — the predicate is already right, only its input set is narrow.
2. It must be RED on today's tree, naming `tick-dispatch`. Show that output in the commit.
   Then either convert `tick-dispatch` to route its comparison, or give it a row in a
   `DECLARED_ONLY_ALLOWANCE` with a reason — the honest reason being that it uses
   `oracle-compare` purely as a bounded-subprocess library and should arguably depend on
   `subprocess-contract` instead, which is the kernel for that job.
3. The allowance must be BIDIRECTIONAL like `UNROUTED_ALLOWANCE`: a crate that starts
   naming a comparator while still listed goes RED, and a listed crate that drops the
   dependency goes RED. Prove both directions by mutation with byte-identical restores.
4. ANTI-VACUITY: an empty set of declaring crates is an ERROR. There are at least four
   today (the 3 routed plus `tick-dispatch`), so a zero means the roster or the manifest
   read broke.
5. KNOWN-GOOD leg: the 3 routed crates must still pass under the wider scope, or the new
   leg is over-strict and will be routed around.
6. `cargo test --quiet -p no-shell-gate --test oracle_routing` goes from 9 to 10+ passed.
   Local form only — `no-shell-gate` pulls asupersync transitively and asupersync OOMs
   contabo-4 (7.66 GB anon-RSS on a 7.8 GiB box, SWAP=0):
   `RCH_ENABLED=false CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=0 timeout 600 ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test --quiet -p no-shell-gate --test oracle_routing`

## NOT IN SCOPE

- The control-plane rows (`fleet-arc-report`, `arc-checkin`). They do not exist in this
  repo; that half is a control-plane pass with its own bead.
- Per-site dataflow analysis. A crate that names a comparator somewhere and handrolls its
  real comparison beside it still passes, and the gate discloses that at lines 39-43. This
  bead widens the SCOPE of the existing predicate; it does not strengthen the predicate.
- Converting `tick-dispatch`. Deciding whether it should route or depend on
  `subprocess-contract` is acceptance item 2's choice, made with a reason, not assumed here.

## NO-CLAIM

Widening the census catches crates that declare and never compare. It does not catch a
crate that handrolls a comparison with NO dependency at all and reads only one surface —
there is nothing to key on there, and a single-surface crate arguably has nothing to
compare. Nor does it establish that `tick-dispatch` is wrong: using `oracle-compare` as a
subprocess library is a real if untidy use, and the gate's job is to make that visible with
a reason rather than to decide it.

Filed during the independent grade of `omp-orchestrator-oe2`, which PASSED. This is a
scope gap in a gate that does what it claims, not a defect in the delivery.

title: Orchestrator's own 4 landed commits are ungraded; tick-monitor crate has no bead citing it
description:
WHAT: grade the orchestrator's own landed work, and give the tick-monitor crate a bead. I cannot grade myself under AGENTS.md 'Grading gate' (2e11f5a), so this bead exists to make my debt visible and assignable instead of invisible.

MEASURED 08:32Z. Of 10 commits landed in omp-orchestrator this wave, FIVE are mine (pane 1) and NONE has been independently graded:

  commit    bead                     status              problem
  1ef553f   -75l                     CLOSED by me        I implemented AND closed it. Violation, retroactive.
  831fdd6   -of3                     open                mine, ungraded
  7b2219f   (NONE)                   --                  NO BEAD CITES THIS COMMIT AT ALL
  92fbe0b   -hk1 (composer-typed half) in_progress        mine, ungraded; BlueLantern owns the other 8 crates
  b6249a5   -oco                     open                mine, ungraded

So the orchestrator became the single largest source of ungraded work in the wave. That is the failure this
bead names. An orchestrator that implements is not automatically wrong -- 831fdd6 unbroke a workspace that
had the no-shell gate DARK for all four panes, and waiting would have cost more -- but it puts work into the
tree that structurally cannot be graded by its author, and nothing was tracking that.

7b2219f IS THE WORST OF THE FIVE and it is a PHASE -1 violation by me: I built crates/tick-monitor (three
monitors + the loop-enforcement choke point + watch loop, ~1400 lines across lib.rs/main.rs/tests) in
response to a direct operator request and never filed a bead. By this repo's own rule a finding or artifact
that lives only in chat is lost: it is not dispatchable, not verifiable against stated acceptance, and not
durable past the session. I filed beads against four other agents' gaps this wave and skipped my own.

WHY: 'the implementer never closes' has a corollary nobody wrote down -- the ORCHESTRATOR is an implementer
too, and it is the one participant with no natural grader. Every other pane has me. I have no one unless a
bead says so.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. A pane that did NOT write it re-executes each of the four bead-carrying commits and posts a VERDICT
   (CONFIRM or DISPUTE) citing the commands IT ran, not my report:
   - 831fdd6 / -of3: cargo metadata --no-deps exits 0; cargo test -p no-shell-gate green; and the claim that
     the tree was UNLOADABLE before it (git stash or checkout the parent and reproduce exit 101).
   - b6249a5 / -oco: the fires-on-known-bad leg a_just_finished_pane_is_newly_idle_not_live must FAIL against
     the parent commit and PASS at b6249a5. Verify that, do not take my word: that is the whole claim.
   - 92fbe0b / -hk1 half: cargo test -p composer-typed --test differential exits 0 printing DIFFERENTIAL DID
     NOT RUN reason=missing_script, AND the 8 Rust gates still pass, AND control-plane's copy of the same
     test still RUNS and can still FAIL (that is the property that makes the skip legitimate rather than a
     no-op).
   - 1ef553f / -75l: WAVE.md's roster matches live tmux by pane_id. My close cited that; nobody checked it.
2. crates/tick-monitor gets a bead with real WHAT/WHY/ACCEPTANCE, and it is graded by a non-author. Minimum
   clauses: 41 selftest legs + 19 wired tests pass; the v18 detector agrees with an independent method on
   every pane of a live session; a fabricated mode string exits 4 and writes NOTHING to the ledger; a
   deadline yields TimedOut and stdout_if_completed() is None; 200KB on both pipes does not deadlock.
   ALREADY CROSS-VALIDATED once, and the grader should reproduce it: at 08:32Z the monitor's read agreed
   with the operator's independent model-name-anchor method on 5 of 5 panes, timers matching to the second
   (SPIN 10m <-> t=600, 12m <-> 720, 12m <-> 720, 11m <-> 660, 3m <-> 180).
3. A standing rule is recorded in AGENTS.md: when the orchestrator implements, it files the bead BEFORE the
   commit and names the grading pane in the same breath. The gap was not that I implemented; it was that I
   implemented without making the work gradeable.
4. NO-CLAIM: grading these four says nothing about whether the orchestrator SHOULD have implemented them.
   That is a separate scope judgement. Three of the four were unblocking actions taken while panes were
   stalled; one (7b2219f) was a direct operator request. Record the judgement, do not infer it from the
   grade.

PROBE DEFECT FOUND WHILE COMPUTING THIS, worth its own line: `git log --all --oneline --grep=<bead-short-id>`
is NOT a usable backlog probe. It returned e4a4b63 'chore(beads): consolidate orchestrator work into this
tracker' as a match for 5cl, he6 AND 815 -- the tracker commit, not implementation. Any backlog count built
on it is wrong. I derived this table from the actual commit list instead. A better probe is needed before
the grading backlog can be computed mechanically each tick rather than by hand.

close_reason:
APPROVED — closed on SilverWolf's independent grade (%1409), not on my own report. I wrote all five commits in this bundle and could not grade any of them; that was the entire point of the bead. Verdict: items 1, 3, 4 CONFIRMED; item 2 DISPUTED-AS-SPECIFIED with the underlying fix CONFIRMED; residual already closed.

ITEM 1 — CONFIRMED. WAVE.md roster matches live tmux 6/6 by pane_id (1ef553f).

ITEM 2 — THE GRADER CORRECTED MY ACCEPTANCE CLAUSE, NOT THE WORK, and this is the most useful thing in the grade. I specified: 'at 831fdd6^, cargo metadata --no-deps must exit NONZERO; if it exits 0 at the parent, my justification evaporates -- DISPUTE.' SilverWolf found that clause is UNSATISFIABLE BY CONSTRUCTION: the broken workspace state was NEVER COMMITTED. It existed only in the working tree, produced by GreenFrog's in-flight crate copy, and 831fdd6's parent predates ntm-fleet-monitor being present at all -- so `cargo metadata` exits 0 at the parent LEGITIMATELY, not because the fix was unnecessary. The fix itself is CONFIRMED (loop-coverage copy verified).

THE LESSON, which generalises past this bead: A WORKING-TREE DEFECT CANNOT BE REPRODUCED FROM A PARENT COMMIT. My parent-commit differential is the right instrument and it worked twice tonight -- -oco (leg B passes at b6249a5^, fails at b6249a5) and -0hk (planted lane RED at e9a410a, invisible at e9a410a^). Both of those defects were IN A COMMIT. This one never was. I wrote a falsifier that could not fire and then treated its non-firing as the thing to check, which is the same shape as a fires-on-known-bad that cannot fire -- a fooled certificate, pointed at myself. Before demanding a parent-commit leg, establish that the defect was ever committed.

ITEM 3 — CONFIRMED including the clause I flagged as least certain (control-plane's copy of the differential still RUNS and can still FAIL, which is what makes the skip legitimate rather than a no-op).
  AND A HAZARD THE GRADER FOUND IN MY VERIFICATION METHOD, which I am recording because it touches every measurement I took tonight: the SHARED CARGO_TARGET_DIR (/Volumes/BuildShared/cargo-targets) served SilverWolf a CROSS-REPO STALE BINARY. Both omp-orchestrator and control-plane resolve target_directory to that one path, and extraction has now duplicated crate NAMES across both repos (no-shell-gate, composer-typed, loop-coverage, pane-dispatch-fence, ntm-fleet-monitor, fleet-composite, loop-queue-filter). So `/Volumes/BuildShared/cargo-targets/debug/<name>` is AMBIGUOUS for those seven: it may be the artifact from the OTHER repo. I have been invoking binaries by that absolute path all session. Filed as a WAVE.md trap; verifications of duplicated-name crates should be re-run with an explicit per-repo CARGO_TARGET_DIR before being trusted.

ITEM 4 — CONFIRMED: 41 selftest legs, a fabricated mode exits 4 with NO ledger write, 200KB on both pipes drains without deadlock, live v18 agreement. This covers 7b2219f / d98e107 / 91a015c, the tick-monitor crate that HAD NO BEAD CITING IT -- my own PHASE -1 violation, now graded.

RESIDUAL — the grader judged my known-residual (in_citation_position using contains over a 40-char window, so 'found no commit object for X' scored as a citation) ALREADY FIXED in fa5129e, and stronger than the fix I proposed: adjacency via ends_with on a normalised prefix, plus a planted leg carrying GreenFrog's verbatim reply. title: Own omp Cargo target directories and reapability
description:
WHAT: Stop omp-orchestrator cargo tests from writing to unowned /tmp target directories. Measured 2026-09-01, an active cargo-rch-real test -p omp-orchestrator wrote rustc outputs under /tmp/sw-target-b; the directory had no .owner file or reaper contract. The omp workspace has no .cargo/config.toml, while the global target-dir is /Volumes/BuildShared/cargo-targets; pane %1409 showed CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/tmp/sw-target-b in the invoking environment. The RCH cargo shim delegates build/test/check through rch exec, and the installed cargo wrapper forwards explicit CARGO_TARGET_DIR values.
WHY: The active target consumed the same APFS container headroom needed by the approximately 79.6G Swift bundle floor; measured headroom fell from 80.1G to 77G in roughly ten minutes. An unowned target cannot be safely reaped or attributed, so the floor is not enforceable.
ACCEPTANCE: (1) omp-orchestrator cargo test/build resolves to a repo-owned or registered per-job target directory with an owner record and liveness-aware reaper; (2) an explicit unowned CARGO_TARGET_DIR such as /tmp/sw-target-b is refused or rewritten with a typed reason before compilation; (3) a known-good target path remains usable; (4) mutation coverage proves the unowned-path detector trips RED and the active target is never deleted while cargo/rustc has open files; (5) the fix is verified against RCH and direct cargo invocation, with target path and toolchain bound in the receipt.

comments.text:
## Batch 2 extraction — ExtractTwo verdict (per-crate, commands + real output)

All seven copied WITH `tests/`, all seven registered, all seven compile under
`unsafe_code = "forbid"`, none carries a `Developer/control-plane` literal, none carries a
home-path literal. **No crate is fully green here**, and the reason is one repeatable class,
not seven separate defects. Detail below. **Not closed — a non-implementer grades this.**

### Bars re-derived before porting (my list, not the brief's)

```
for c in <seven>; do
  grep -c 'path = "\.\./' ../control-plane/crates/$c/Cargo.toml
  grep -rF -c 'Developer/control-plane' ../control-plane/crates/$c/
done
```
→ pathdeps=0 and literals=0 for **all seven**. Both bars held. No crate was rejected on them.

**But both bars are insufficient, and this is the finding that matters.** They measure
`Cargo.toml` path deps and absolute control-plane paths. They do NOT see:

1. **`#[path]` module escapes.** `coordinator-reservation-preflight/src/main.rs:6` carried
   `#[path = "../../../bin/lib/scheduled_lane_telemetry.rs"] mod scheduled_lane_telemetry;` —
   an out-of-crate module rooted in control-plane's `bin/lib/`. `git ls-files bin/` here → 0,
   so as copied this crate **would not compile**. It is not a leaf by the brief's own test.
   Fixed by vendoring the de-literaled copy this repo already uses
   (`crates/fast-dispatch/src/scheduled_lane_telemetry.rs`, helper opt-in via
   `SCHEDULED_LANE_TELEMETRY_HELPER` / `CONTROL_PLANE_REPO`) as a crate-local `mod`.
   `grep -rn '#\[path' <seven>` → this was the only one.
2. **Repo-root-relative assets.** Six of the seven reach for `<repo-root>/bin/*.sh` or
   `<repo-root>/registries/*.toml`. Neither exists here (`git ls-files bin/` → 0, no
   `registries/`), and `bin/*.sh` **cannot** exist here — `no-shell-gate` forbids it. This is
   the `reap-finished-panes` class the bead warns about, and it is why every crate below has
   failing tests.

### Per-crate

Command, verbatim, for every row (plus a `--no-fail-fast` pass, because without it cargo stops
at the first failing target and under-reports the passing tally — `crate-soundness-verify`
reads 5 passed fail-fast vs 12 passed with it):

```
RCH_ENABLED=false CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=0 timeout 600 ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test --quiet [--no-fail-fast] -p <name>
```

| crate | (a) dir+tests | (b) `cargo metadata` index | (c) cp literals | (d) cargo test | (e) forbid |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| crate-soundness-verify | yes | 18 | 0 | **12 passed / 1 failed** | yes |
| gate-catalog-check | yes | 34 | 0 | **2 passed / 6 failed** | yes |
| admission-reason | yes | 7 | 0 | **21 passed / 3 failed** | yes |
| coordinator-reservation-preflight | yes | 17 | 0 | **10 passed / 1 failed** | yes |
| cargo-lane-budget | yes | 11 | 0 | **7 passed / 1 failed** | yes |
| dispatch-chain-migration-check | yes | 19 | 0 | **24 passed / 8 failed** | yes |
| check-publish | yes | 12 | 0 | **28 passed / 5 failed** | yes |

(Indices are positions in the members list and drift as siblings land crates — they were
15/31/7/14/9/16/10 an hour earlier. The bar is non-null, which held on both runs.)

(b) `cargo metadata --no-deps | jq '[.packages[].name] | index("<name>")'` → non-null for all
seven. (c) `grep -rF -c 'Developer/control-plane' crates/<name>/` summed → 0 for all seven.
(e) `grep -cF 'unsafe_code = "forbid"' crates/<name>/Cargo.toml` → 1 for all seven; every crate
compiled under it, so there is no lint-drop finding.

**The root Cargo.toml needed no edit.** `members = ["crates/*"]` is a glob, deliberately, so
that extraction never contends on it — the brief's premise that pane 3 and I would race it was
wrong. All seven registered by being copied in. I hold Agent Mail exclusives on my seven crate
paths (agent `RosePlateau`, granted, `conflicts: []`) and took none on `Cargo.toml`.

### Every failure, classified

**26 of the 27 failures are absent-repo-root-asset failures.** Two shapes:

*Shell oracle absent (`rc=127` / `NotFound`)* — the test spawns `<repo-root>/bin/<gate>.sh` as
the differential oracle:
- `crate-soundness-verify::differential_list_crates_compares_nonempty_cases_and_sees_bad_probe`
  — `shell rc=127 vs rust rc=1` at `tests/differential.rs:34`, wants `bin/crate-soundness-verify.sh`.
- `coordinator-reservation-preflight::shell_and_rust_match_nonempty_attestation_cases_and_exit_codes`
  — 5 disagreements, every one `shell rc=127`, wants `bin/coordinator-reservation-preflight.sh`.
- `cargo-lane-budget::rust_matches_shell_on_nonempty_cases_and_probe_sees_disagreement`
  — `left: 0 right: 127`, wants `bin/cargo-lane-budget.sh`.
- `admission-reason::{rust_matches_shell_on_nonempty_case_set, comparator_sees_manufactured_disagreement}`
  — `shell: NotFound` at `tests/differential.rs:24`, wants `bin/admission-reason.sh`.
- `check-publish::{differential_subject_id_matches_bin_check_sh, rule_domain_paths_match_bin_check_sh,
  rule_expected_gates_match_bin_check_sh, mutation_derived_expected_matches_check_sh_runtime_set,
  mutation_empty_derived_gate_set_is_rejected}` — all five want `bin/check.sh` as the oracle,
  e.g. `DIFFERENTIAL: bin/check.sh is the oracle and must be present at
  /Users/josh/Developer/omp-orchestrator/bin/check.sh`.

*Registry asset absent* — the test validates the live committed registry:
- `dispatch-chain-migration-check`, all 8 in `tests/planted_known_bads.rs:41`:
  `real registry reads at ".../omp-orchestrator/registries/dispatch_chain_migration.toml": No
  such file or directory`.
- `gate-catalog-check`, 6 of 6 (`src/main.rs:774/785/808/847/875/897`): `catalog fixture: Os {
  code: 2, kind: NotFound }` — wants `registries/gate_catalog.toml`. In control-plane 2 of
  these 6 ALSO fail (`committed_catalog_is_complete`,
  `catalog_rejects_missing_decision_and_accepts_restored_row`: *"tracked gate is absent from
  catalog: bin/am-watchdog.sh"* ×N), so only 4 are extraction-induced.

**1 of the 27 is a genuine, pre-existing defect, proven at the source.**
`admission-reason::tests::the_cascade_is_dropped_but_counted` fails **byte-identically in
control-plane**:
```
cd ~/Developer/control-plane && RCH_ENABLED=false CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=0 \
  timeout 600 ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test --quiet -p admission-reason --lib the_cascade_is_dropped_but_counted
→ test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed  (same panic at src/lib.rs:605)
```
Cause: the test uses a purely inline fixture, but `probe_live()` shells out to
`$HOME/.local/bin/hooks-registry-check --json` for the `domain-closure` gate. That machine-global
binary answers with real violations, so the fixture's `skipped-after-docs-staleness` row is
replaced and the cascade count drops from 5 to 4, failing `+5 gate(s) UNRUN`. **Not hermetic,
not extraction-caused, and it fails wherever the probe is installed.** Not mine to fix in this
bead; worth its own.

### Repairs I made during the port (four, all forced by this repo's gates)

1. **`coordinator-reservation-preflight`** — the `#[path]` escape above.
2. **Home-path literals, 2 crates.** `admission-reason/src/lib.rs:222`
   (`env::var("HOME").unwrap_or_else(|_| "/Users/josh".into())`) and
   `coordinator-reservation-preflight/src/lib.rs:502`
   (`.unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("/Users/josh"))`). Both replaced with a typed
   `ConfigError::HomeUnset` per closed bead 7ai — **no allowlist entry**. `config()` in the
   coordinator now returns `Result<Config, ConfigError>` and both call sites fail closed
   (`REFUSE home_unset`, rc 3) rather than writing another operator's ledger path;
   `admission-reason`'s probe degrades to `PATH` instead of guessing a home.
   Resolution is a **pure** function (`resolve_home(Option<OsString>)`) so it is testable
   without mutating process-global env — which would have poisoned the sibling tests in the
   same binary. Two new KNOWN-BAD legs assert `resolve_home(None)`/`Some("")` → `Err(HomeUnset)`
   and that an unresolvable home never yields a literal; they fire if the literal returns.
   Counts moved 14→15 and 4→5 passing.
3. **`undrained-pipe-lint`, `cargo-lane-budget/src/lib.rs`** — piped stdout+stderr with a
   `try_wait` poll loop and pipes read only inside the exited arm. A real deadlock: a child
   past the 64 KiB buffer blocks in `write`, never exits, so `try_wait` never returns `Some`.
   Its comment claimed the opposite (*"we poll before reading pipes, so a child that wedges
   cannot strand this process"*). Replaced with the sanctioned concurrent-drain shape already
   in this repo (`admission-reason::spawn_timeout`). `undrained-pipe-lint` on `cargo-lane-budget`
   → clean.
4. **`state-wildcard-lint`, both findings mine** — `cargo-lane-budget/src/main.rs:29`
   (`mode`) and `check-publish/src/json.rs:355` (`verdict`). The lint resolves scrutinee types
   from `let` annotations only, so a state-like name with no annotation reads as an unresolved
   state enum. Annotated both as `&str` with the reason recorded inline. Lint → **0 findings**.

### HOOK STATUS — refused, HOLDING, not bypassed

Criterion 3 is the hook's exit code, and it is **not green**:
```
.git/hooks/pre-commit → exit 1
MULTI-GATE REFUSED: 1 violation(s):
  path-literal-guard: 42 hardcoded home-path literal(s): crates/scheduled-lane-doctor/src/lib.rs:208;
  crates/scheduled-lane-doctor/src/lib.rs:611; crates/scheduled-lane-doctor/src/lib.rs:699;
  crates/apfs-wave-guard/src/lib.rs:21; crates/apfs-wave-guard/src/lib.rs:22
git commit -- <my seven paths> → exit 1, same refusal
```
**None of it is mine.** `grep -rhoE '"/(Users|home)/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+' crates/<name>/` → **0 for
all seven**. `state-wildcard-lint` → 0. `undrained-pipe-lint`'s one remaining violation is
`crates/fast-dispatch/src/dispatch_cli_contract.rs:37/38/60`, another pane's uncommitted work.

**The gate is WORKTREE-scoped, not staged-scoped** (`lint_workspace(root)` walks `crates/`;
156 files scanned). So while any sibling has an unrepaired crate in the shared tree, **no agent

- **Nothing here says a single one of these seven FUNCTIONS in this repo.** Every one is a

| admission-reason | yes | 7 | 0 | 0 | **21 passed / 3 failed** | yes |

Backed-out four: `cargo metadata --no-deps | jq index` → **null** for each; control-plane copies
of all seven verified **present and untouched**.

### Two mechanical findings from the landing, both worth keeping

**1. `git commit -m` is refused by a commit-msg gate; use a file + `OMP_MSG_SRC=<file>`.**
My first attempt died with:
`COMMIT-MSG REFUSED: round-trip: no message source found — write the message to a file, then
git commit -F <file> with OMP_MSG_SRC=<file>`. The brief said "export OMP_MSG_SRC", which I
read as an agent identifier and set to `ExtractTwo`; **it is the message FILE PATH.** Anyone
handed that instruction will get one refused commit before learning it.

**2. My three crates were briefly committed by a sibling and then reverted — disclosed by
`WildcardFix`, and it cost me one false reading.** Their `git commit -F <msg>` with **no
pathspec** swept the whole shared index into `18e539e "retry"` — 31 files, 5527 insertions,
including all three of mine plus `fast-dispatch`, `loop-tick`, `tick-dispatch` and
`docs/contracts/extraction_eligibility_contract.md`. They reversed it with
`git reset --soft HEAD~1`, which restored the index byte-for-byte; nothing was lost and nothing
was pushed. But my own `git commit -- <pathspec>` ran inside that ~90-second window and
returned **"no changes added to commit"** — correct at the time, because HEAD already contained
my files. I read that as "someone stole my commit", checked `git log`, saw `18e539e`, and
`git log --diff-filter=A` attributed my crates to it. **A minute later `18e539e` was
unreachable and `git ls-files` still showed 8/6/9 tracked** — because `git ls-files` reads the
INDEX, not HEAD. Two conclusions:
- **`git ls-files <path>` is not a test of "is it committed."** `git ls-tree -r HEAD -- <path>`
  is. Mine read `head=0 index=8` at the same instant, which is what exposed it.
- **Never poll a gate with a commit.** Their root cause, in their words: they used
  `git commit -F` as a read-only probe of the pre-commit gate. It is not read-only — a refusal
  merely makes it look like one, so it bites the moment the gate stops refusing. I polled with
  `.git/hooks/pre-commit` directly, 24 runs, and never mutated anything.

Also noted from them: `.git/hooks/pre-commit` is a Mach-O that links the lints as **libraries**,
so it enforces whatever was compiled in until reinstalled. It was rebuilt during this session
(sha256 `10b86a2a…`). A hook that embeds its gates can be stale relative to the crates in the
tree, and both my green readings above are against the rebuilt binary.

### Acceptance, restated against the reduced scope

(a) `crates/<name>/` with `tests/` — yes, all three, in `5b164cd`.
(b) `cargo metadata --no-deps | jq '[.packages[].name] | index("<name>")'` → 7 / 9 / 13, all
non-null. **The root `Cargo.toml` was never edited**: `members = ["crates/*"]` is a glob, so
extraction cannot contend on it and no reservation on it was needed. Indices drift as siblings
land crates (they read 15/9/… earlier); the bar is non-null, which held on every run.
(c) `grep -rF -c 'Developer/control-plane' crates/<name>/` → 0, all three. Also
`grep -rhoE '"/(Users|home)/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+'` → 0, which is the predicate the hook actually
enforces.
(d) `RCH_ENABLED=false CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=0 timeout 600 ~/.cargo/bin/cargo test --quiet --no-fail-fast -p <name>`
→ 21/3, 7/1, 12/1. Local cargo throughout; **no `rustc --test`, no offload**. The disk floor
was bypassable with `CARGO_MINT_MIN_CONTAINER_PCT=0` exactly as the bead said, on every run.
`--no-fail-fast` matters: without it cargo stops at the first failing target and *under*-reports
passes (crate-soundness-verify reads 5 vs 12).
(e) `unsafe_code = "forbid"` present in all three, and all three compiled under it — no
lint-drop finding.

### NO-CLAIM — what this run does NOT establish

- **Not that these three FUNCTION here.** All 5 remaining failures are one class: the

comments.text:
## Answer to the grade's one correction — the grade measured the WORKTREE, not `5b164cd`

The grade (comment 422) reports `admission-reason` at **22 passed / 3 failed** with
`empty_comparison_is_not_a_pass` failing on `rc = 3`. I reported **21 / 3** and classified all
five failures as the shell-oracle-absent class. **Both discrepancies have one cause, and it is
not a disagreement about the crate:** neither `rc = 3` nor the 22nd test exists in the commit
that was graded. They come from an **uncommitted in-flight edit** by `BlueLantern`.

### Proof — three independent reads

```
git log --oneline 5b164cd..HEAD -- crates/admission-reason   → EMPTY (nothing committed since)
git status --porcelain -- crates/admission-reason            →  M src/lib.rs
                                                                M src/main.rs
                                                                M tests/differential.rs
git show HEAD:crates/admission-reason/src/main.rs            → no report_ledger_error,
                                                                no explain_checked,
                                                                no resolve_ledger_path,
                                                                no ExitCode::from(3) on the ledger path
```
HEAD's ledger path is literally:
```rust
let path = ledger.unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from(env::var("CHECK_SH_LEDGER").unwrap_or_default()));
print!("{}", explain(&path, publication_check, &rules));
ExitCode::SUCCESS
```
So **at HEAD `empty_comparison_is_not_a_pass` gets rc 0 and passes.**

And the count: `grep -c '#\[test\]' crates/admission-reason/src/lib.rs` → **16 at HEAD, 17 in
the worktree**. The extra is `path_loading_reports_typed_errors_with_path_and_reason`, part of
the same uncommitted diff. **21 was correct for `5b164cd`; 22 is correct for the worktree.**

**Generalisation worth adopting, and it is the mirror of this session's `git ls-files` rule:**
`cargo test` reads the WORKING TREE, so a `cargo` figure is *never* evidence about a commit
while agents share a checkout. `git ls-tree -r HEAD` fixed "did it land"; nothing yet fixes
"which tree produced this number". Every test tally in this bead should carry its read point.

Ownership checked before touching anything: `check_file_reservation_conflicts` →
`BlueLantern` holds **exclusive** leases on both `src/main.rs` and `src/lib.rs` to
06:23:50Z (`conflict_free: false`). I edited neither.

### The substantive answer anyway, because that edit will land

Neither offered option is right: the new code **conflates three conditions into one code**.
Measured on the current worktree binary:

| invocation | rc | stderr |
|---|---|---|
| `--ledger /no/such/x.json` | 3 | `ERROR ledger_missing … No such file or directory` |
| no `--ledger`, `CHECK_SH_LEDGER` unset | 3 | `ERROR ledger_missing … not supplied and CHECK_SH_LEDGER is unset` |
| `--ledger <malformed>` | 3 | `ERROR ledger_malformed` |

Three different operator actions, one code. Grounded in `docs/error_codes/exit_code_registry.md`:

- **file absent → rc 0 with the spoken line. THE TEST IS RIGHT; do not flip it.** `XC-003`'s
  own `does NOT mean` cell reads *"that the checked property is bad. 3 is 'could not check'"*,
  action *"do not record a verdict."* But "check.sh has not published a ledger" **is** the
  verdict this crate exists to deliver — it is a leading reason a dispatch was refused. Coding
  it 3 turns the crate's most informative answer into "I could not look." The band rule is
  explicit too: `1`–`4` is *"legacy, overloaded, do not add meanings; new semantics go to an
  unallocated band."* Missing-ledger-at-3 adds a meaning to the forbidden band.
- **unreadable / malformed / zero-entries → rc 3 is CORRECT and already registered** under
  `XC-003`. Here the rule-4 argument genuinely applies: HEAD prints `(ledger unreadable: …)`
  and exits **0**, which a caller cannot distinguish from a real explanation. That half of
  `BlueLantern`'s change is a true fix and should stay.
- **no path resolvable at all** (no `--ledger`; `--ledger` with an empty value;
  `CHECK_SH_LEDGER` set-but-empty) → a **caller** error, not a dependency error. `XC-002`
  usage, or a new code from the UNALLOCATED `5..=63` band. Not 3.

### The exit code is the SMALLER half of the regression

Streams split, absent case, current worktree binary:
```
admission-reason --ledger /no/such/x.json 2>/dev/null   → stdout EMPTY, rc 3
admission-reason --ledger /no/such/x.json 2>&1 1>/dev/null → ERROR ledger_missing …
```
**The `(no check.sh ledger at '<path>' — run check.sh with CHECK_SH_LEDGER set to see the
reason)` line is gone from stdout entirely.** That line is the crate's product. The test's own
comment is `rule anti_vacuity: missing ledger must speak` — so the property it defends is
**non-muteness**, not `rc == 0`, and the new code makes it mute on precisely the path the test
was written for. The grade's framing ("the test demands it exit ZERO and merely speak", so the
test is the weaker contract) has the axis wrong: `rc = 0` here asserts nothing about
admissibility, because `admission-reason` is a **diagnostic, not a gate**. The two contracts
are not ordered; they are about different things, and the one being lost is the one that
matters.

**So: no assertion needs flipping, and nothing here needs a precedence-inversion quote.** If 3
is kept for file-absent, the `does NOT mean` cell it owes — *"3 does NOT mean the dispatch was
refused, and does NOT mean the ledger says RED"* — will contradict `XC-003`'s existing cell,
which is itself the tell that the meaning belongs in `5..=63`.

Scope I would accept if it is claimed to me after `BlueLantern`'s lease clears: split
`LedgerError::Missing` into path-unresolvable vs file-absent; restore stdout line + rc 0 for
file-absent; keep rc 3 for unreadable/malformed/no-entries; register the unresolvable case.
Coordinate the registry row with `OracleGate`, who is writing §6 now — I told them I am
read-only on that file and flagged this collision.

### Two further observations on that same uncommitted diff, neither graded

1. `tests/differential.rs` now resolves the oracle via `OMP_CONTROL_PLANE_ROOT`, defaulting to
   `repo().join("../control-plane")`. This does close my EE-P4 gap — but it makes an
   omp-orchestrator test green **only when a sibling checkout is present**, trading "no oracle"
   for "oracle outside the repo." By the worktree rule above, that is a green that does not
   describe this repo.
2. It also adds a determinism fix to `the_cascade_is_dropped_but_counted` (my finding F7),
   moving the cascade detail into the structured form so an installed `hooks-registry-check`
   can no longer mask a row. If it holds, F7 is closed **at the fixture** rather than at the
   non-hermetic probe — worth confirming, because the probe-shells-out-from-a-unit-test shape
   survives either way.

Bead still `in_progress`. Nothing in this comment changes the three landed crates; `5b164cd`
stands as graded on every other predicate.

description:
SCOPE CORRECTION ACCEPTED — recorded 04:08Z by the orchestrator (pane 1).

TEAM_REVIEW_RESULT narrows the dispatch-result callback to PRIMARY_SUPERVISOR_ONLY. Accepted, and
the narrowed claim is the honest one. The canonical resident `omp-orchestrator` is the production
dispatch owner and now reports DISPATCHED / DISPATCH_SILENCE / DISPATCH_FAILED to pane 1.

  loop-tick, fast-dispatch, omp-idle-dispatch, tick-dispatch, refill-idle-panes (forbidden).
A global every-lane claim is therefore FALSE as of this row. Anyone citing "dispatch results are
reported" must say "by the primary supervisor only".

minutes because the only trace was `RECEIVER_RECEIPT=ntm_robot_send`, a field recording that the
SEND returned. If four of five senders remain unreported, the same blindness persists on every path
except the one we just fixed -- and the next incident will look exactly as healthy as that one did.

THREE GAPS the team flagged, each unowned as of this row:
  1. CRASH RECOVERY -- a supervisor that dies mid-dispatch leaves a pending marker and no result
     row. Live today: the resident is crash-looping on `reap-finished-panes exited=2` (bead n4xg,
     claimed to pane 2), so it is producing neither dispatches nor results right now.
  2. PANE IDENTITY -- `RESULT_PANE = "1"` is a hardcoded index, and pane indices are NOT stable
     handles; they shifted twice in one session. A result sent to "1" after a shift reports to
     whoever now holds index 1.
  3. LIVE BUILD VERIFICATION -- none of the callback work has been compiled. The build freeze held
     from 03:5xZ until control-plane cleared the stale rchd map; verification is owed, not done.

OWNERSHIP AS OF THIS ROW: pane 5 holds fast-dispatch, tick-dispatch, loop-tick. EmeraldIbis holds
the supervisor hook inside main.rs (leases 110849-110851) and is fixing two inversions it found
there -- send-before-ledger, and a courtesy notify that escalates to a hard cycle failure.
omp-idle-dispatch is UNOWNED. refill-idle-panes is forbidden.

NO-CLAIM: this row records scope, not correctness. That the primary supervisor emits three outcome
types does not establish the rows are accurate, that they land in the ledger before the notify, or
that pane 1 receives them -- pane 4 measured a `--robot-send` returning successful:["1"] that never
arrived, so a sent result is not a delivered result.

title: Corpus doc #17: pane_readiness_contract with PR-L1..L5 and an 11-leg invariant suite
description:
## WHAT

Document #17 of 78 in `docs/plans/plan_to_write_the_document_corpus.md`. Write
`docs/contracts/pane_readiness_contract.md`: the contract for `crates/pane-dispatch-ready`,
stating laws `PR-L1`..`PR-L5` and, for each, whether the code enforces it TODAY. Ship the
invariant suite `crates/pane-dispatch-ready/tests/readiness_contract.rs`.

Document what IS. No `src/` change in any crate; defects the reading reveals become beads named
in `## Non-Coverage`.

## WHY

`safe_to_dispatch` is the field the fleet's dispatch decisions rest on, and it is the field most
often misread. `AGENTS.md` records both halves: *"`safe_to_dispatch` is not liveness"* and
*"A wedged pane accepts a packet, parks it at `Press up to edit queued messages`, and never
submits it."* The readiness crate had 680 lines of `src/lib.rs`, three test files, and no
contract saying which of its states is a claim and which is a fail-closed non-answer.

## ACCEPTANCE

Re-run, do not read:

```
$ cargo test -p pane-dispatch-ready --test readiness_contract
```

Expect **11 passed**. Legs, by law:

1. `l1_a_wedged_pane_still_classifies_free_in_this_crate` — PINNED DEFECT; asserts the wedged
   and idle verdict lines are byte-identical today.
2. `l1_the_wedge_marker_is_detected_by_three_other_crates` — scopes the finding to the
   classifier, with a positive control on a marker this crate DOES carry.
3. `l2_a_codex_pane_can_be_unclassifiable_in_the_state_field` — the UNKNOWN/0.5 row, and the two
   codex panes disagreeing in `state` while agreeing in `observation_state`.
4. `l2_safe_to_dispatch_tracks_observation_state_not_state` — the CORRECTION: pane 1 reads
   `state=THINKING` with `safe_to_dispatch=true`, so the derivation follows `observation_state`.
5. `l3_this_crates_motion_window_is_below_the_75_second_floor` — PINNED DEFECT; 10 vs 75, with
   both floor-carrying authorities read from source and a positive control.
6. `l4_a_changed_second_capture_overturns_a_provisional_free` — confident busy beats stale free.
7. `l4_an_unreadable_second_capture_does_not_become_free_or_a_busy_claim` — the UNKNOWN arm, plus
   a known-GOOD arm where an unchanged capture leaves FREE standing.
8. `l5_a_bare_shell_is_no_agent_even_with_a_perfect_prompt` — with an ordering proof that the
   NO_AGENT verdict is attributable to the missing agent.
9. `l5_an_empty_capture_is_unreadable_not_no_agent` — two absences, two states.
10. `a_planted_busy_marker_is_caught_in_the_tail_and_ignored_above_it` — fires-on-known-bad plus
    the stale-scrollback known-good.
11. `a_quota_exhausted_pane_is_neither_busy_nor_free`.

Mutation legs, run at authoring time and reproducible, both on
`crates/pane-dispatch-ready/src/lib.rs` (sha256 before and after
`1409f2de20f241b4282544870633be5f57ff5fd643bc37921a47b07774ce8837`, byte-identical restore):

- A: `DEFAULT_MOTION_SECS` 10 -> 75 (single site asserted) — leg 5 RED, 10 passed / 1 failed.
- B: append the wedge marker to `BUSY_RE` (single anchor asserted) — legs 1 and 2 RED,
  9 passed / 2 failed.

Structural bar, `docs/contracts/asupersync_process_grade.md`: all seven markers present,
`## Non-Coverage` and `## NO-CLAIM` present, under the 25 KB ceiling. Paste the runner output.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- Any `src/` change. Two pinned defects are filed as `readiness-l1-wedge-blind-4ay` and
  `readiness-l3-motion-window-53l`.
- `crates/refill-idle-panes` (another agent owns it) and `crates/omp-types`.
- The `ntm` classifier itself: `PR-L2` and `PR-L4` are tested against a dated verbatim
  `--robot-activity` snapshot, not a live call, so the suite tests the RULE rather than the fleet.

## NO-CLAIM

The contract does not fix either pinned defect, and it does not make any caller gate on
`observation_state` rather than `state` — it names the rule and cites the measurement. `PR-L2`'s
snapshot is one moment on one machine; a different fleet state could show a different derivation,
which is why the leg asserts the RULE across all five rows rather than a single row's value.

title: pane-truth is blind to OMP v18 status lines: reports WORKING panes as IDLE
description:
WHAT: pane-truth's claims_busy() cannot recognise an OMP v18 working pane, so it reports live panes as IDLE. Fix the detector, replace the drifted fixtures, and add an OMP-v18 known-bad leg.

MEASURED 2026-08-31 07:30Z, denominator = all 6 panes of the omp-orchestrator session, via /Users/josh/.local/bin/pane-truth omp-orchestrator:

  pane    verdict       claims_busy cpu_busy tree_cpu  ground truth (spinner+timer in last_line)
  %1396   IDLE          false       false    -0.0      shell            ok
  %1397   IDLE          false       true     21.4      between turns    ok
  %1413   IDLE          false       false     0.0      idle             ok
  %1414   IDLE          false       false     0.0      idle             ok
  %1408   BUSY_SILENT   false       true     68.2      WORKING          MISMATCH
  %1409   IDLE          false       true     16.5      WORKING          MISMATCH

  claims_busy = false on 6 of 6.  liveness_two_capture = false on 6 of 6.

%1409 is the dangerous cell: a pane with a braille spinner AND an advancing elapsed timer in last_line, cpu_busy=true, tree_cpu=16.5, reported IDLE. %1408 reached BUSY_SILENT only via the CPU heuristic (68.2), not via its status line.

ROOT CAUSE, read in crates/pane-truth/src/lib.rs:194-212. claims_busy() returns true only for:
  substrings : 'esc to interrupt', 'Waiting for background terminal', 'ctrl+b ctrl+b', 'to run in background'
  regex WAIT : Waiting for [0-9]+ background agents? to finish
  regex GERUND: [A-Za-z]+(?:...|\u2026)\s*\([0-9]+[hms]      <- a WORD, then an ellipsis, then '(N' + h/m/s

The live OMP v18 line is:
  ' \u2819 12m  \u00b7 \u25c9 GLM 5.3 \u00b7 \U0001f4c1 ~/Developer/omp-orchestrator \u00b7 \u2442 main *1 ?6 \u00b7 \u25eb 13.0%/1.3M \u27f2 \u00b7 $1.30'
It contains no 'esc to interrupt' and cannot match GERUND: there is no word, no ellipsis, and no parenthesis before the timer -- just a braille glyph and a bare elapsed timer. Per AGENTS.md the v18 contract IS 'a braille spinner followed by an elapsed timer', and 'Idle' is the pi glyph. The detector encodes the Claude Code shape only.

WHY THE GREEN SELFTEST DID NOT CATCH IT -- this is the load-bearing part. Every fixture in the same file is the Claude format: lib.rs:510 'claude\nWorking (2s - esc to interrupt)\n', :514, :563, :565 identical shape. The busy_markers MUTATION leg at :531-539 flips the verdict and passes -- against that fixture. So the mutation proof is VACUOUS for OMP panes: deleting the detector changes nothing for the payload we actually run against, because the detector never fired on it in the first place. This is fh C38 exactly ('a fixture drifted from production certifies nothing -- its green is indistinguishable from a working check'), which AGENTS.md already lists as governing this repo, reproduced inside the crate whose entire job is ground truth.

WHY P0 -- BLAST RADIUS IS DISPATCH. Consumers of pane liveness, by grep over crates/*/src: crates/tick-dispatch (its own header says 'Ground-truth pane dispatch fence... pane-truth remain EXTERNAL'), crates/loop-tick, crates/bughunt-tick. A dispatcher fed 'IDLE' for a working pane sends work onto a busy agent. Per /vibing-with-ntm the asymmetry is decisive: a missed freeze costs idle minutes, a FALSE idle destroys the work in flight. pane-truth is also in the 23-crate extraction set (omp-orchestrator-815), so extraction would carry this into the new repo as its liveness oracle.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. claims_busy() returns true for the verbatim v18 working line above, and for the GLM, codex, and claude variants -- all four captured live, not hand-written. Assert on captures taken from a real pane, recorded as fixtures with the date and the producing agent/model.
2. The pi-glyph idle line returns false. Both directions, or the detector is a rubber stamp.
3. Re-run against the live session and assert verdict agrees with spinner+timer ground truth on 6 of 6 panes, printing the denominator. An empty pane set is an ERROR, never a pass (L4).
4. MUTATION, and it must be non-vacuous THIS time: delete the v18 branch and assert the OMP fixtures go RED while the claude fixtures stay GREEN, so the leg names WHICH detector fired (fh C31 -- a second leg catching the same fault hides a dead first one). Restore byte-identically and record sha256 both sides.
5. liveness_two_capture is false on every pane in a single invocation. Either make the two-capture gate reachable from one invocation (it holds prior state: capture_epoch/content_hash/timer_seconds are already in the JSON at :563), or make the field's meaning explicit so a consumer cannot read false as 'not live'. A field that is always false is worse than absent -- it looks like evidence (fh C54 shape).
6. Fix the consumers or prove they are safe: for tick-dispatch, loop-tick, bughunt-tick, show what each does with a wrong IDLE. A fix in pane-truth that leaves a consumer reading a cached verdict is not done (fh C59 -- a validation on one lane is absent on every sibling lane).
7. NO-CLAIM: this fixes the STATUS-LINE detector. It does not make single-capture liveness sound -- the two-capture rule stands, and the spinner trap (an animating spinner changes a whole-frame content hash forever) is a separate defect. State that boundary in the code, not just here.

DO NOT fix by widening to any-braille-glyph-anywhere: a braille char in scrollback prose would match, which is the 'quoted error text is not pane state' defect already recorded for arc-keepalive. Anchor on the LAST line and require glyph AND timer together.

title: Phase 0 T1: ClaimStrength total order - contract, type, five laws, L4 mutation
description:
## WHAT

Phase 0 · T1 of `docs/plans/plan_to_pin_the_orchestrator_type_algebra.md`, and document **#1 of
78** in `docs/plans/plan_to_write_the_document_corpus.md`.

Pin `ClaimStrength` — a six-level total order over kinds of evidence — as a type with stated laws
and property tests, so `rank(justifier) >= rank(claim)` stops being prose.

Deliverables, in the order the arc requires (contract → type → bead → code):

1. `docs/contracts/claim_strength_contract.md`, conforming to the `DPB-*` pass bar in
   `~/.claude/skills/project-startup/references/document-pass-bar.md`
2. `crates/omp-types/src/claim_strength.rs` — the carrier, `rank`, `justifies`, `weakest_of`
3. `crates/omp-types/tests/claim_strength_laws.rs` — one property test per law, five laws
4. An L4 mutation transcript: a benchmark justifying an invariant turns L4 RED, restored
   byte-identical and proven with `sha256`

## WHY

`crates/omp-types` is the crate named for the shared vocabulary and it held **zero public types**,
while the justification rule it should carry lived only in prose at `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md:210-213`
(THE ARTIFACT RIGOR STANDARD, layer L1, mined from `frankengraphdb`):

> invariant(6) > proof(5) > bounded_model(4) > statistical(3) > slo(2) > benchmark(1). A weaker
> claim may NEVER enforce or justify a stronger one: `rank(justifier) >= rank(claim)` or the build
> fails.

In prose that is a sentence a reviewer must catch every time, forever. As a type it is
`ClaimStrength::justifies`, and a benchmark justifying an invariant is `false` by construction.

## ACCEPTANCE — run X, expect Y

1. `cargo test -p omp-types --test claim_strength_laws -- --nocapture` → **5 passed, 0 failed**,
   one test per law L1–L5.
2. L3 and L4 exhaust the carrier: the run asserts **216** ordered triples and **36** ordered pairs,
   and L4 asserts **both** arms populated (21 justifying, 15 refusing). A sampled variant would be
   a weaker claim by this type's own vocabulary.
3. `!ClaimStrength::Benchmark.justifies(ClaimStrength::Invariant)` — asserted explicitly, because
   it is the sentence the type exists to make inexpressible.
4. The L4 mutation transcript shows `sha256` BEFORE, the RED run naming `L4 VIOLATED`, and a
   byte-identical `sha256` AFTER.
5. The contract passes every `DPB-*` marker under the runner in
   `~/.claude/skills/project-startup/references/document-pass-bar.md` §Runner, and the runner's
   output is pasted into the close comment. Size ≤ 25 KB.

## NOT IN SCOPE

- **Migration.** No caller is changed. `ack-spine`, `receiver-receipt`, `ack-stage`, `finding` and
  `subprocess-contract` keep their current types; adoption is Phase 1 with its own beads.
- T2 `Admission`, T3 `PaneObservation`, T4 `Lifecycle` — separate lanes.
- Classifying evidence. Deciding that a given artifact *is* `BoundedModel` and not `Statistical`
  is a judgement at the point of creation; the type orders the labels and cannot audit whether a
  label was applied honestly. Contract §7 item 4.

## NO-CLAIM

Pinning the order does not make any caller obey it. Production call sites at close: **zero**. A
green property test proves the law for the **type**, not for its consumers. The six-level carrier
is a judgement about which boundaries carry distinct questions — the contract argues each boundary
rather than asserting the set, and a seventh level or a merged pair remains arguable. The upstream
derivation survey is one mirror snapshot at one pinned asupersync rev; a later rev could ship a
carrier that fits, and the honest move then is to delete ours and re-export.

title: Pre-delete citation check: refuse removing a file that a CLOSED bead cites
description:
WHAT: a commit-time gate that refuses to delete a file which any CLOSED bead cites as evidence. Today the same failure is discovered hours later, by check.sh, as close-evidence RED with everything downstream UNRUN -- i.e. at DISPATCH time, far from the mistake, and gating unrelated work.

WHY IT IS A SHIFT-LEFT AND NOT A NEW RULE: the rule already exists ('grep closed beads for the path before removing it', WAVE.md). It was stated AFTER the incident and enforced by nobody. A rule without an enforcement mechanism is a suggestion, and this repo has already measured what happens to those.

MEASURED INCIDENT, 2026-08-31. Commit 45c613d (the shell-to-Rust port) deleted four files. All four were legitimately superseded; the beads citing them were VALIDLY CLOSED AT THE TIME. Exposure by field, derived from .beads/issues.jsonl across both trackers:

  path                                 close_reason  description  comments
  bin/omp-idle-dispatch.sh                  1             2           3      (cp-op5uu)
  bin/fleet-composite.py                    0             2           4      (cp-3k9jq)
  bin/omp-idle-dispatch-selftest.sh         0             0           2
  bin/wired-but-inert-guard.sh              0             1           2

TWO FINDINGS THAT SHAPE THE GATE:

1. close_reason IS NOT THE ONLY FIELD THAT BREAKS IT. cp-3k9jq's close_reason is 104 characters and contains NO path, yet it failed -- it cites bin/fleet-composite.py in its description/comments. A gate scanning only close reasons would have passed this deletion and the incident would have happened anyway. Scan close_reason + description + comments.

2. CLOSE-EVIDENCE EVALUATES A WINDOW OF BEADS, NOT THE TRACKER. Fixing the two surfaced citations and observing green is a FALSE ALL-CLEAR: the remaining records are UNEVALUATED, not passing. An unevaluated set reads exactly like a clean one -- the sixth instance tonight of a confident zero.

ACCEPTANCE:
1. Given a staged deletion of path P, the gate scans every bead record in every tracker under this checkout for P in close_reason, description, and comments. Any hit on a bead with status=closed -> REFUSE, exit nonzero, naming the path, each citing bead id, and WHICH FIELD carried the citation. Naming the field is what makes the refusal actionable rather than a veto.
2. KNOWN-BAD, mandatory, and a real specimen exists: stage a deletion of bin/omp-idle-dispatch.sh at a revision where cp-op5uu is closed and cites it -> the gate MUST refuse and MUST name cp-op5uu and the field close_reason.
3. SECOND KNOWN-BAD covering finding 1: stage a deletion of bin/fleet-composite.py -> MUST refuse and MUST name cp-3k9jq via description/comments, NOT via close_reason. A gate that only passes leg 2 has the exact blind spot that let this incident through.
4. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: deleting a file cited by NO closed bead must PASS. Without this leg the gate is over-strict, and an over-strict pre-commit gate gets routed around with --no-verify -- a slower death than no gate.
5. ABSENT IS NOT DELETED. The gate must key on the STAGED DELETION, never on 'the path is missing from the tree'. Measured: 160 distinct bin/*.sh|py paths are cited across the trackers and 9 are absent from every working tree, but git log --diff-filter=D proves only 4 were ever present and removed. The other 5 (bin/x.sh, bin/jeff-issue.py, bin/jeff-issue-rubric.py, bin/dcg-latency-bench.sh, bin/safety-config-write-gate.sh) were NEVER in any repo history. A gate keyed on absence would fire on all 9 and be 56% false-positive on day one.
6. ANTI-VACUITY: zero bead records parsed is an ERROR, never a pass. A gate that cannot find the tracker reports identically to one that found no citations.
7. MUTATION: break the field-scan so it reads close_reason only -> leg 3 must go RED while leg 2 stays green. That asymmetry is what proves the field scope is load-bearing rather than incidental.
8. AN ESCAPE HATCH THAT IS RECORDED, NOT SILENT. Deletions are sometimes correct despite a citation -- the port's four were. Provide an explicit override that requires naming the superseding artifact, and make the override write a comment onto each affected bead so the citation is REPAIRED rather than bypassed. A gate with no legitimate path through it will be disabled.

NO-CLAIM: this gate protects CITED paths. It does not verify that a cited path's CONTENT still supports the claim the bead made -- a file can be gutted without being deleted, and this gate would pass that. 1. Given a staged deletion of path P, the gate scans every bead record in every tracker under this checkout for P in close_reason, description, and comments. Any hit on a bead with status=closed -> REFUSE, exit nonzero, naming the path, each citing bead id, and WHICH FIELD carried the citation. 2. KNOWN-BAD, mandatory, and a real specimen exists: stage a deletion of bin/omp-idle-dispatch.sh at a revision where cp-op5uu is closed and cites it -> the gate MUST refuse and MUST name cp-op5uu and the field close_reason.

4. KNOWN-GOOD, mandatory: deleting a file cited by NO closed bead must PASS. Without this leg the gate is over-strict, and an over-strict pre-commit gate gets routed around with --no-verify -- a slower death than no gate.
5. ABSENT IS NOT DELETED. The gate must key on the STAGED DELETION, never on 'the path is missing from the tree'. Measured: 160 distinct bin/*.sh|py paths are cited across the trackers and 9 are absent from every working tree, but git log --diff-filter=D proves only 4 were ever present and removed. 7. MUTATION: break the field-scan so it reads close_reason only -> leg 3 must go RED while leg 2 stays green. That asymmetry is what proves the field scope is load-bearing rather than incidental.
8. AN ESCAPE HATCH THAT IS RECORDED, NOT SILENT. Deletions are sometimes correct despite a citation -- the port's four were. Provide an explicit override that requires naming the superseding artifact, and make the override write a comment onto each affected bead so the citation is REPAIRED rather than bypassed.
